These are good and very addicting. I used store brand shortening instead of crisco but I dont think it hurt them any.  Easy to make, will make these again.

they are pretty good. a bit too sweet for our taste. remember to let it sit for a while on the baking sheet for a while, or they might crumble. overall, these resemble maringue type cookies, and we were expecting a heartier taste. but they are definetely very easy to make! thank you for the recipe.

I wish I could rate these higher but I found them to be very plain tasting...kinda floury and doughy. I didn't find them to be too sweet like a previous reviewer. I followed the recipe exactly and they were very easy to make. I used my 1/2 tablespoon to scoop out balls of dough. I baked mine for about 12 minutes. It made 36 cookies. My mother enjoyed the slightly crisp outside with the soft inside. Perhaps, they're a cookie for Mothers! Made for 1-2-3 hit wonders.
i reallly enjoyed these little gems!!!i think next time as i am sure there will be a next tine i may add the mini chocolate chips(because i love chcolate)
A great little cookie and so easy to do in the food processor - I had to use butter as we do not have Crisco here in Australia . Made and enjoyed for ZWT 111.

I reduced the sugar to 3/4 cup.  It was the only change I made.  I got only 30 cookies.  They bake near 12-13 minutes.  I love the taste of the cookies with the pecans.  For me, no need to add chocolate.  Thanks Kim :)  Made for Zaar Star Game

These are very rich, delicate and delicious cookies! They are wonderful with a cup of coffee. They melt in your mouth. I only got about 30 cookies and had to bake them about 13 minutes. They would be a great cookie for holiday trays. Thanks for sharing.

Another winner from Kim127!  First of all, they are so easy to make (just one bowl).  I also yielded 30 cookies, which were light and not to sweet.  I didn't have pecans on hand (like I thought), so I substituted chopped walnuts.  Very good, and perfect with a cup of coffee.  Thanks, Kim, for the great recipe, and thanks, Lainey, for the recommendation.  Made for I Recommend Tag Game.
Even though I thought they were a little too sweet, my boys and hubby loved them. Maybe I needed a cup of strong coffee on the side!:)  Made for Bevy Tag.

I'm not leaving any stars for this recipe, simply because I screwed up making them. I never have Crisco in the house, so I tried making these with softened butter. While they were easy to make and tasted great, the texture difference caused by using the butter was quite noticeable. They looked good when coming out of the oven, but deflated as they cooled... eventually becoming thin as wafers and super-delicate. I'll have to make these again when I actually have the Crisco on hand.

I really don't know where to start with these cookies. Not only are they the simplest cookie i have made they are one of the best tasting. My family absolutely loves them. I will definitely make these again.
This is an awesome cookie.  So moist.  Great tasting.  A recipe to keep!  Thanks for the great recipe.

These were good, but I wish I had added cinnamon to them. I added chocolate chips, and without I feel like they would have been sort of flavorless. Very nice texture, very cheesecake-like, soft and chewy. I burned the bottoms of one batch, and that only added to the texture!

Yuuuummmmy!  Parmesan, butter and rice... what a wonderful combination.  This was so easy and got thumbs up from everyone here.  I didn't have any parsley but the guys never missed it.  This will definitley be a side dish we'll have often.  Thanks, MizzNezz!

I`ve made this dish a few times now & its always a hit,its a recipe that leaves you room to fiddle with ie. adding garlic or other herbs etc.I love all your recipes MizzNezz....keep up the great work.
Bubble

This was lovely!  I cut down on the butter by half and didn't add the parsley {I forgot}.  Also, just mixed room temp butter and cheese right into the hot rice.  Perfect elegant side dish with no effort.
This was wonderful.  I did add minced garlic to the butter and sauteed and browned at once.  What could be better than Parmesan rice with butter and garlic... mmmm.  Thanks!
Fabulous!  I didn't have parm cheese so substituted asiago...wonderful recipe.  Very flavorful.
Very good, my family loved it.  I cut the butter in half too, and it was still very good.
This was good...but needed some salt and pepper. My rice-lover gobbled it up!
Delish! Hubby asked what kind of cheese I used and our daughter says "parmesan" you sure can taste it. I said good, you're supposed too. LoL! :)

We all enjoyed it but everyone felt there was "something missing". I think the suggestions of adding garlic and/or salt & pepper are probably good ones. A great basic recipe though. BTW, if you have to grate your cheese by hand, leave LOTS of time to do so! LOL! Thanks for sharing MizzNezz!
So easy and so tasty. A real winner with this family. Thanks.
Very good rice dish, and I have been trying to eat more fish lately, so this went very well with it. Thank you for a simple yet delicious dish. :)
it's like risotto, but without any effort-- what's not to like??

Good and simple.  I cooked my rice in chicken broth like I always do and used fresh grated parmesan. No salt needed with the broth.  I also just stirred in the butter, did not melt it separately.  When it was done it still tasted like it needed just a little something, so I stirred in a small bit of fresh lemon juice and it really brought out the flaver.
Excellent - I had some leftover brown basmati rice and needed a quick and easy recipe. With the leftovers from this we added chopped up grilled onions and peppers. Yummy
This was so yummy!  My kids liked it too, and that's a feat!  What a great alternative to the everyday, boring rice side dish!  Thanks MizzNezz, I'll use this again and again.
Great rice, only thing I would change would be decrease the amt. of butter, we thought it was on the greasy side. Served this with recipe#85259 and recipe#78938

I've been making a dish just like this for eons except I use a bit less butter and just stir in the butter and parmesan cheese on the top of the rice once it's done.  Add some salt and pepper and my 2 and 4 year old are in heaven!
Very good.  I would recommend reducing the butter to 1/4 cup. Very rich dish even with the reduced amount.

I needed a side dish for dinner and had rice leftover from the night before.  I reheated the rice with a little water so it wouldn't dry out and then added the melted butter, a parmesan romano blend and used dried fried parsley.  We all thought it was ok but weren't "wow"ed lke we thought we would be.  I will follow the recipe to a T next time and adjust my rating accordingly.

I made this as a side dish to smoked sausage for dinner one night.  It was easy and delicious!  This reheats well in the microwave the next day too.  Thanks for posting, I'll definitely be making this dish again!

Yummy!  I added the stick of butter to the water before boiling.  Came out nice and creamy!  Made this to go alongside recipe #50878  Thanks Mizz for reminding me that i can make real rice that's super simple!
Very good!  I added a little garlic to ours and served with 40 clove chicken.  Would make a great side for many dishes!  Thanks a bunch this is a keeper
This was a great side dish...I served with Hamburger Diane #384790 and it was perfect...What a great dinner for a rainy Thursday night!

Yummmm..This was a very easy and tasty side dish to my pan grilled hamburger patty.  I searched for a quick rice dish and thought your recipe sounded good.  I scaled the recipe down to 2 servings and only had minute rice, cooked the rice (2 servings) per instructions and followed the rest of your recipe as posted.  I enjoyed this very much and will have it often, thanks so much for posting.
Great side dish for our pork tenderloin tonight but would go with lots of things. Thank you for posting.

Very good!!!! Love it, love it, love it!!!  Made this tonight to go along with Salmon patties and broccoli.  I did however add a very large clove of garlic that I browned in the butter.  Will definitely be making this again...thanks for sharing!!

This is great. I made rice using Recipe #39269 and then added the rice to the melted butter and mixed in the parm. cheese. I added a little salt and pepper and it's the perfect side dish! It's a keeper I'll use often. Thanks!
Tasty and easy!  I browned the butter and added garlic.  Thank you!
this is really good, but for us a bit greasy.  That's an easy fix, next time I will cut back on the butter.  thanks for sharing.
This dip will please everyone.  It's simple to prepare too.  I made it in the morning and put in the refrigerator to allow the flavor to meld. Thanks for sharing, dienia bennett.
This was a good veggie dip for our Super Bowl snacking.

I was looking for a crock pot recipe similar to my grandmothers and this is very close. My grandma used the water the beans soaked in and different measurements for the molasses and brown sugar but other then that it's very close... But I doubt my grandma cooked hers in a crock pot. It's hot in the house so I wanted to just use a crock pot. First time making it I made it with salt pork and it took 6 hour, I am trying it again today but with bacon so we will see. thanks for sharing!

Super-sweet, so portions need to be small, but the smell of these cooking alone is worth 10 stars! These are fabulous mixed into plain yogurt or oatmeal, and they would probably go nicely as a topping over some plain vanilla ice cream. Thanks for posting! Made for The Hot Pink Panthers for ZWT9
My family makes this same recipe, but instead of pretzels we use Chex cereal, either way, YUM!

I printed this recipe over a year ago and finally had the opportunity to make it.  Everyone who tastes it comments on how much they like it (and of course wanting the recipe).  My husband cannot stay out of it!  Very simple to make!  You could even do this with Chex cereal, popcorn, or anything else similar.  I also thought it tasted better after it sat for a couple of days.  But either way, very good.
Very good and very easy.  My kids ask to make it themselves, its that easy.  I use less oil than stated and still taste great.

I've made this a dozen times but without the lemon pepper, we used dill. I think the small round pretzels are the best because they hold the tasty stuff better. They do taste better on day 2 or 3 if you can save some for later. My sister also started making it with regular oil and some butter buds, I think about a Tablespoon or so.

Like other reviewers, I let this mix sit a few days.  It still seemed a tad oily, so just before serving, I put it in a brown grocery bag, shook it around, and let it absorb any excess oil.  Personally I thought this mix was too salty, but it was heartily eaten by guests.  I followed a reviewer's suggestion of adding chex cereal to it as well (50/50 mix).

I make a similar recipe, except I use the small pretzel twist , spicy ranch packet, colemans dry mustard, garlic powder, lemon pepper & canola oil. I eye ball the measurements then I  mix in a very large bowl , pour onto a parchment lined baking sheet to dry for about an hour then I store them in an " UTZ" pretzel container that I purchased from SAMS. My husband loves these little guys and he lets me know when the stash is getting low lol....

I think this is a wonderful, filling soup.  Great for lunch.  Very easy, too.  Prepackaged coleslaw mix makes this a breeze!  I added some chicken boullion to the 4 cups of water and then just decreased the salt.  Thanx for the great recipe.  I'll make this again.

I absolutely loved this soup! My family loved it so much they had to have 2 and 3 servings each. I just switched some of the veggies: 1 cup diced celery, 1 medium diced onion, 1 diced sweet potato, 1 can green beans, and I added cilantro and sriracha sauce at the end. YUM! mmm mmm mmmmm ~Thanks!!

This made for a lovely dinner on a very warm Australian night.
I made nearly almost to the origninal recipe, my problem being I could not fine tamarind so I used lemon juice instead, which worked well although it did tend to seperate and so I had to blitz it a bit to get it back to a normal sauce (the blitzing worked well)
But in the end it worked well, and was enjoyed by all.

Awesome recipe.  It deserves 5 stars for that incredible sauce alone!  I did change things around though- only because I wanted to make the dish into a Thai bento bowl.  I left out the tomatoes and eggs, and added some brown rice instead.  Also, instead of boiling the chicken, I diced 2 breasts and stir-fried the pieces in a bit of peanut oil.  the chicken was great, but I think fried tofu would taste awesome in this sauce as well..  Thanks for sharing. [Reviewed for PLEASE REVIEW MY RECIPE]
We really enjoyed this recipe.  To make it easier, I just shredded store-bought rotisserie chicken.  The sauce is divine!
This is a wonderful salad, especially for a hot evening. We all enjoyed this very much. I will make it again. Thanks for sharing the recipe.
Fantastic recipe! The gnocchi were super light. Excellent directions. A little time consuming stuffing one by one,but worth the effort. Delicious.

This is really tasty, although I did make a few changes.  I adjusted this down to half for 6 skinless boneless chicken thighs, I substituted white wine for the red, and I used water instead of chicken broth - it was definitley a great dish.

Very tasty and will be making it again. Made a couple modifications because of what I had on hand. Did not have mushrooms and fines herbes. In place of herbs, used poultry seasoning and dried parsley. Could not find Knorr leek soup mix; used Knorr vegetable soup mix instead (has leek listed in ingredients on label). Everything else was the same as written in recipe. Served over rice. Delicious and hearty yet pretty healthy.
We loved this recipe!  So easy and tasty!  I used stuffing mix instead of breadcrumbs.  A keeper in this house Thanks Recipe Fairy ; )

I found these to be "tough".  Would like to know from others how the recipe worked for them.  I even refrigerated them to firm up the butter before baking.  The flavor is fine but I'm not too pleased with the texture.  Perhaps I overworked them.  Was looking for a lighter texture.
Made this tonight for dinner, it was very good and filling.

These are tasty treats.  Used my abundance of fresh tomatoes whose flavor really came through on these sandwiches.  Bacon and tomato with an added twist.  Felt like the pumpernickel overwhelmed these somewhat, but the chef notes that other breads could be subbed.  Personally, I think a ciabatta would really enhance this sandwich better.  Thanks for the suggestion Ms. Jack in my recipe search forum.  :)

how can you go wrong with all these great ingredients, we loved these and I look forward to making them again soon, the only change I made was I doubled the recipe and I'm glad I did, my DS and GF came over and they all went fast, thanks for sharing Mrs. Jack!

Wow, soooooooo good. I used the full 8 oz cream cheese about 1/2 lb bacon and added extra horseradish to mine. Then I spread on little cocktail bread. I love these and my sisters did too. We took them on our little vacation and had us a picnic. They are like a BLT with a little twist. Next time I think I may add a tiny amount of sour cream to thin them a bit to make it spread easier.

I made about half this recipe and altered it a little (I can't help myself) but it was delicious.  My husband doesn't like chard, but he loved this.  My dinner guests asked for the recipe.  I did add some fresh dill, and used white cheddar. Even though it was great, I'm sure gruyere would be much better.  I cooked it at 250 for 2 hours or more. Will make this even when my voluminous chard crop is reduced to frozen chunks in freezer bags!

Loved it!  Not only was it a fun recipe to make but it was absolutely delicious.  I followed the directions using gruyere but also did equal parts shredded parm.  I good hearty side, would be a good replacement for stuffing too.

excellent, tasty and wonderful. the only change I made to this was accidental, I used rosemary bread, and I think it added to the flavors.  I also made this ahead and froze it. I cooked it to the just before the point of putting it in the oven for 1 1/2 hours, and froze it for a couple weeks, as we didn't need it for the company I had it planned for. It survived the freezing just fine, and was an incredibly tasty meal.  the only downside might be holding yourself to a serving. we couldn't! I will definately use this for my frozen chard this winter when our fresh chard is gone!
Very tasty!  i don't care for chard, so wanted to dress it up a bit, and this was just the thing.

Oh, this was sublime!  Instead of the chard, I used the musroom duxelles from my recipe #457210 (that I had previously frozen)...and used gruyere cheese as fontina was not available.  Once the mushrooms had thawed out, I used some of the mushroom liquid and mixed it in with some homemade chicken broth for more of an earthier taste!   I made this dish up ahead of time and took it over to my girlfriend's place and finished off the cooking there.  Do watch what you are paring this dish with as it is really rich in taste...a little serving does go a long way.  We had this served with pork tenderloin, baby potatoes and garden salad!  As for the taste, it was absolutely nummy goodness.  Keep in mind, 4 cups of liquid would equal the amount you would need for a onion soup.  I used 3 cups and could possible have used a bit less.  Kudos on such a find...your directions were spot on as well, so again, thanks!!!

Great recipe, especially if you have left over bread to use up, as it lifts humble ingredients to another level.  I agree this would make a good replacement for stuffing too. We ate it as a side to roast chicken and it was so juicy that no further gravy was needed.
Made these for a sick neighbor with kids to feed.  Everyone loved it.  The second pan for my family didn't last long, either.  Different, delicious.  Thanks for posting.
These were great! Used light cream cheese and light cheddar. My husband doesn't like "light" anything and ate every bite of his dinner. Thanks!
I used the sauce from recipe #54909, and made a few changes...adding mushrooms, celery and green peppers in place of the spinach.  These were awesome. Thanks!

Mmmm... These enchiladas are delicious! Actually, I joined Zaar after making these three times so I could post the review, and I tell about this recipe to anybody who will listen.  The texture and the blend of flavors are just perfect, and the leftovers are as good the next day. Thanks.
These were amazing. Definitely going into my regular menu.

Very good! I made it the first night, and my family liked it so much, that we made it the next night for company. I doubled the recipe the second time, and added one pound of chicken in place of another pound of ground turkey. I also added peppers, and black beans. It was excellent. Thanks!

I honestly would not change a thing! I did find that for the absolute best results, you can broil the enchiladas for 4 minutes after adding the cheese for a nicely baked and browned cheese finish. These are amazing and our neighbors stole the recipe they loved it so much!!!!!!!

Great recipe! I even got my fiancee who hates spinach to eat these and he enjoyed them a lot! You can't really taste the spinach in them or tell that it's ground turkey.. but they sure are good! Next time I'll use reduced fat cream cheese to make it a little healthier. It made so much filling that I ran out room in the pan for more tortillas. Next time I'll put in a larger pan. Thanks for the recipe Kittencal!

We really enjoyed this recipe. It is definitely not a "typical" enchilada. It was really delicious, very filling, easy to make, and healthy too! I will definitely add this to my list of regular recipes!

I have made this dish three times now, and each time was a hit!  Two of the times I had no picante sauce but plenty of salsa; it substituted nicely.  I've also doubled the recipe with no problem.   Next, I'm going to make the filling and freeze for when I want it soon.  I serve guacamole with it everytime.    As far as healthy though- I don't think so, the cheddar and the cream cheese, even reduced fat, make this a yummy comfort food.

I made many changes to this recipe to suit my diet/available ingredients but I wanted to give major props for this recipe giving me inspiration! It was delicious & a great way to use up spinach, too! Thanks so much for sharing.

These were fantastic! I followed the recipe and added in some diced green chili's to kick it up a notch. We will make this again. It made 9 rolled enchiladas which we topped with sour cream, lettuce, and black olives.
Delicious!    My family loved it.  It's a great way to incorporate vegies in a classic Mexican fav.   Will be making again and again. Thanks for another great recipe Kittencal!

I made this with left-over turkey from Thanksgiving instead of the ground turkey.  The enchiladas were delicious and everyone agreed it was a great use of the leftovers.  Will keep this one in mind for after Christmas too!!
Everone loved this.  I made it exactly as written, except to use whole wheat tortillas.
Easy, tastes great

I have to admit that while I was making these I was very skeptical...cream cheese sounded really weird and I wasn't sure there would be enough flavor but these were absolutely delicious.  My kids gobbled them up and they hate spinach! The flavors were great and they are very filling.  Excellent recipe.
This is an excellent recipe! My husband was a little scared of the spinach, but absolutely loved it. This is going in our "make again" file.
I thought this was very good, but my hubby was not crazy about it.  It is VERY rich!  Thanks so much for sharing!  :O)

We absolutely loved the filling of these enchiladas.  I actually only had 5 oz. cream cheese, and it still worked out wonderfully.  Using an enchilada sauce recipe in place of the picante sauce, ours had a really nice kick, too.  I never would have thought of adding spinach, but it was great.  Thanks Kitten!
Wow these are very tasty! I will be making these again and again. I used ww tortillas and frontera salsa for some kick. Yum!

I really liked the combination of ground turkey (couldn't tell - the filling was so rich and flavorful), spinach, tomatoes, and seasonings.  This is a great switch up from regular enchiladas.  I struggled with the rating as my DH, son, and I loved them but my 3 daughters turned up their noses at it - decided I couldn't penalize the recipe because of my picky eaters :)

Great recipe! I added a huge jalapeno with the onions and garlic. I also threw in some chopped cilantro and rolled with WW tortillas. This makes a lot which is perfect...we have a delicious lunch for a couple days.
We will definitely be making these again!  I used enchilada sauce instead of picante sauce and added a can of green chilies. I used 4ozs of low fat cream cheese becuase that is what I had left.

Excellent!  I deconstructed the enchiladas and made this into a casserole.  I lined the pan with white corn tortillas and topped with half the filling.  Added another layer of tortillas and the second half of filling.  Finished with one last layer of tortillas and topped them with the remaining picante sauce and the cheese.  Put in the oven until it was warmed through and the cheese was melted.  Used the recommended toppings and it made for an excellent dinner.  Thanks for sharing, Kitten!
deliscious
These were good. I used green sauce as the topping because I ran out of red.

I was looking for a chiffon cake & knew I had to make this one after reading the recipe intro.  What a wonderful story & thanks for sharing it!  We loved the prominent lemon flavor.  Quite often it's only just a hint of lemon in something like this, but not here!  I frosted it with a basic chocolate frosting & a sprinkle of coconut but next time I'll make a lemon cream cheese frosting instead to compliment the lemon cake.  What a winner this is!  It baked up perfectly in the 45 minutes stated.  The instructions don't suggest hanging the cake upside down but when it started to sink I turned it over & hung it on a bottle of Worcesterschire sauce & it cooled without sinking further.  We really enjoyed this cake.  Thanks for sharing, Chilicat!  Made for New Kids on the Block tag game.

Normally when I want ribs at home I buy Kettle Cooked back ribs that already come in bar-b-que sauce.  Since I couldn't find them, I decided to buy fresh ribs and find a recipe at home.  I've never made ribs before, but these turned out great!  They take very little effort and come out very saucy.  In, fact I only made about half the sauce and they were still excellent.  I didn't have liquid smoke, but knew that I still wanted that smokey flavour, so I just added about a tablespoon of Bullseye Smokey Bar-B-Que sauce.  I will definitely be making these again!

These ribs are absolutely wonderful.  So easy to make.  I put my ribs in the crockpot until they were done, then put the sauce on and broiled as directed.  Taste like Applebee's.  My DH said he would serve these to anyone.  Thanks so much for the yummy recipe.
I cant believe anyone finds that boiled ribs are very good ....all the good flavor is now in the water
Boiling extracts flavour, roasting or broiling condenses flavour, that's why we make chicken stock with all the leftover chicken we don't eat!
Easy, very tender, and consistently perfect.  I will never use another rib recipe or bbq sauce recipe again.

This is a VERY NICE thousand island dressing! I especially liked it because it uses salsa instead of ketchup. I was able to adapt it to the South Beach Diet by using baby dill pickles. I also used green olives but I think black would have been better.

Yum!  I would like a little more mint in mine so I will make another batch of syrup with triple the mint.  I think the ratio of espresso to milk is spot on.  I made mine sugar free with stevia (instead of sugar) and sugar free hot cocoa (but note that you will use only 1 T of sugar free cocoa instead of 3T regular cocoa due to the decreased volume)!  UPDATE:  I made this again today with the leftover syrup.  If you follow the instructions, you will end up with almost 2.5 cups of liquid which we find is enough for 2 people - so if you are making this for just 1 person, make sure you have a mighty big mug!!! (Most mugs only accommodate 8oz or 12oz).
What a fab smoothie! I haven't made a smoothie w/o banana in a while, and this was refreshing, light, wonderfully flavored. Great invention- a keeper!!

Wow!! A terrific recipe! I scaled this down to use 1 avocado as there are only two of us. I made it in the morning and kept it in the fridge all day before serving it at supper time. It's true, the flavours come out so much better over time. A great blend, and simple to whip up in my food prcessor.
I'll be making this one again, thanks for posting!

This is a great breakfast bread ... as it is not very sweet. I loved it right out of the oven because it was so light and fluffy. The next day it is a bit more dense. This was great for us as DH doesn't like it super sweet and I do - so I drizzled mine with a powdered sugar and orange juice mix. The orange flavor is very subtle.
it was alright there is something missing idk  what it is ?

We loved this recipe. The flavors all blended quite well.

We look forward to having this dish again.
My mother is still raving about these & it's been 2 weeks! Incredibly easy & tasy. Would recommend to others!

This was easy to make, though the chicken ended up being very very mild, and I couldn't really tasty any of the flavours like the lemon or honey. It was just very light tasting for some reason, which was nice, but not quite what I was expecting. I'll have to play around with the ingredient amounts next time around. Thanks!

This was very easy to make and had all of the ingredients on hand. The taste is very light- not a strong lemon or honey flavor. I used minced garlic instead of sliced and chicken broth in place of the water. Good taste and easy weeknight dinner
This had very subtle flavors considering the ingredients.  My family liked it, and I will be making it again.  Thank  you for posting.
This was just ok for us. I didn't really like the sweet and sour taste so much. I don't really know what i was expecting. We didn't finish it. sorry this didn't work I usually love Ramsey's stuff

I enjoyed it. Following these directions, the sauce was strong, but the taste of the chicken was light as others have said. I may try using thicker slices of lemon and timing the honey a bit different. This video of Ramsay cooking this dish does it slightly differently:

http://youtu.be/mARkUax2jg0

DELICIOUS!!!!  I was a bit skeptical when I read some of the reviews because my family like bold flavors but I was very happy how this turned out!  It was so quick and easy I had dinner done in no time!  My modifications where I used chicken breasts that I flattened out and adjusted the cooking time a bit so the meat would not get over cooked I also just sprinkled thyme since a Tbsp sounded like a bit much.  The sauce it made was very tasty and I served it over rice.  Definatley going to Pin this one!
This was a great from scratch version.  I used pretty thick slices of bread and had to double the amount of coating.  I also used some dijon mustard, per our taste.  Great recipe!!!!!
I have been on the hunt for what appears to be the reasonable way to prepare this for my husband. This is the ONLY recipe that sounds right! I will try this and get back to you. Thank You.
Does the trick in a pinch
Really good bread.   Added some cranberries to recipe.  I will make it again.

This was great.  I am always looking for recipes for cabbage and this one is a keeper.  The mixed flavors of the cabbage, pork and potatoes was wonderful.  I will have to take your word that it tastes better as leftovers because in my house there has yet to be any.
This was super yummy!  A perfect dish for fall.  Thanks for posting.
Really good.  I used some leftover pork tenderloin instead of chops, and added another onion to the recipe.  I didn't have cream of celery so I used cream of mushroom soup.  A great winter dish!

I think the recipe turned out just like it should - a nice creamy sauce, baked pork chop and potatoes and cabbage that taste something like a scalloped potato recipe.  My hubby enjoyed it and said he'd definately have it another time.

Very good recipe!  I didn't have Cream of Celery soup so had to substitute with Cream of Mushroom.  Next time I will use the Celery but we loved it even without it.  The left-over cabbage and potatoes were yummy as a side dish with another meal.  Thanks so much for posting, Kathy228!  M. Joan
tasty and tender.  omitted onions, salt, pepper.  added rosemary and carrots.  used cream of mushroom and 2 cans of evap milk.  Great flavor!!  served with sugar butter acorn squash.
Delicous!  Cooked for New Years day dinner, very easy and comforting. May even be better warmed up next day. Will make again.
I had this recipe when my kids were little and they loved it.  Somehow over the years it got lost.  Thanks so much for bringing it back.
Followed this recipe exactly. Was the worst food I ever put in my mouth. Threw it out. A fried bologna sandwich would have been better.

Used 5 chops, 1/2 a Napa cabbage, cream of asparagus soup with 1/2 and 1/2 not milk. While browning last chop I started onions, took chop out added a can of mushrooms. Finished as directions stated. Yummy!!! Grilled asparagus as a side with no salad. Try it you will like it!

Excellent recipe!  There are no words to express how good these porkchops was. I did let them simmer in my skillet alittle longer so they would be tender. I also used bacon grease in place of the butter(about 3Tbs) 
I also made Carla's recipe #109716  for rice to go along with this porkchop recipe. Another excellent dish! 
Thanks Carla for sharing your recipes!!

I have never made a curry so good, and on the first try! My husband are three pork chops like he had been starved for the last week. I am sharing this one with my Mom even. Thanks a bunch for a great, adn easy recipe!

A keeper! This recipe is absolutely wonderful. I scaled the recipe down for two people (two pork chops) and the flavor was outstanding. Wow! We moved from Cincinnati to Kansas a few years ago and this is an incredible recipe. VERY similar to Skyline. My husband and 11-year-old daughter were impressed and my husband actually thought this was better than Skyline! The only change that I would insist on is not to add onions to the chili. Real Cincinnati chili doesn't have chopped onions in the chili but they are put raw on top of the chili at serving time along with cheese, etc. I used a little onion powder instead instead of chopped onions and it was great. I also added a little more salt (1/2 to 1 tsp.) and used a pressure cooker (for 1/2 an hour) to cook it faster since the family was hungry and couldn't wait 2-3 hours.  Cincinnati chili is supposed to be a little "watery" anyway.  We ate it right away and it was great.  I'm so excited - now we can stop shipping cans of Skyline in from Cincinnati! I had heard of, but never had, Cincinnati Chili. I also knew that there were strong opinions about the "best" CC.

Having looked through the many CC recipes and reviews on Zaar, I zeroed in on Debbie R's and, with my fingers crossed, gave it a try. (FYI: I tripled this, but otherwise, followed it precisely.)

It was super-easy to make -- mostly it takes a few hours to simmer -- and the results were fantastic. Although It's totally unlike the many Tex-Mex chilis with which I am familiar (CIncinnati Chili is more like a meat sauce than a stew), me and the other NY'ers who had never had CC all adored it -- especially the three- and four- and five-way versions. It was fun listening to people try to guess the spices as they tasted it.

BUT I happened to serve two Cincinnatians and they thought this was superb! (Both asked for extra hot sauce -- so keep the Tabasco out with the other condiments.)

(I served this with Recipe #170772 for dessert, which everyone adored too.)

Thank you, KelBel!

Oh this was so good!  You are so right - the boiling of the meat is the key.  I spoke with our local Hard Times Cafe and they confirmed that the hot/boiling water is the secret! This is the best Cincinnati chili recipe I've come across, but as a long-time Cincinnati resident I have to tell you that you have the "ways" all wrong.<br/><br/>3 way - spaghetti, chili, cheese<br/>4 way - spaghetti, beans or onions, cheese<br/>5 way - spaghetti, chili, beans, onions, cheese<br/><br/>Oyster crackers have nothing to do with "ways". I have never made Cincinnati Chili until today. My husband mentioned it a few months ago so I wanted to make it. I had read all of the reviews before I tackled this recipe. Some mentioned that the cloves and cinnamon are too strong. I use cinnamon sticks in the ubiquitous Vietnamese noodles, pho. Cinnamon powder is put in a cloth spice bag and discard when done. So I put in 2 2" cinnamon sticks and 1 T of whole cloves in a spice bag. You can wrap the cloves in a coffee filter, wrap completely and tie in kitchen twine. Since I grind my own beef, I simply slide the freshly ground meat into the boiling water, stir with a wooden spoon. Or like someone suggested, use the stick blender to break up the meat. I skipped the onion since quite a few folks from Cincinnati said onion is a "way", not in the chili itself. I used 1 1/2 Tablespoons of raw cacao powder and 1/2 T of butter instead of the 1/2 oz. unsweetened chocolate. I used the same measurement for the rest of the ingredients. Once done, discard the clove bag and cinnamon sticks. My husband loved it with raw chopped onion and shredded cheddar cheese. He said it is a keeper.

These were very easy to make, but a little too subtle with the orange flavor. Next time I will include some zest and use the oj to make a powdered sugar glaze. Thanks!

I agree with jshorten - these are way too subtle in flavor. Next time I will try her suggestions...or at least add more spices! But this is a very easy recipe and the results look very nice - just need more of a flavor boost.
Had this tonight for our tv snack. Was very simple to make and I also added a few extra berries, and some sweetner.
I, too, needed some honey in my smoothie for breakfast.  Delicious.
Really Good! I added OJ because it did need something sweet in it. My husband & son really enjoyed it!

This was excellent.  Easy to prepare with outstanding results.  Company-worthy!  Thanks so much for sharing.  My pork loin was just over 2 pounds and it fed 5 people so if you're cooking for more than 5, adjust accordingly.

Thanks so much, Paula, for a great slaw! I'm a great fan of 'yams' so this recipe was just right for me, & I particularly liked the 'Day 2' part of it, giving me another meal without my having to think about what to do! Will definitely be keeping hold of this recipe! [Tagged, made & reviewed in the Aus/NZ Recipe Swap #27]

Day 2 was a big hit and day 1 was good, too.  The 1.5 pounds of sweet potatoes (3 medium) made a lot. I would cut back to 1 pound (2 sweet potatoes) next time.  Thanks for two new healthy and easy meals.

What a terrific salad Paula. I love sweet potatoes and lime and ginger, this was tailor made just for me...so thank you my dear. The dish was quick and very easy to throw together, using ingredients I always have at home. What a great way to get my vitamins.

Day 1 the slaw was crisp and oh so flavorful, loved the addition of the walnuts and green onions to the mix, it was perfect. The dressing was the bomb. So much flavor. I will be making this for other salads as well, can't wait to try it on fruit salad.

Day 2 was just as good as day 1. The only change to your recipe was to use savory pork tenderloin in place of the chicken. What a treat, I can't wait to make this again. Thank you so much for posting this treasure.
This made a terrific lunch. I have to admit I went straight to day 2. I had no idea you could eat sweet potatoes raw! This opens up a whole new world for me. The salad was both tangy and sweet.

This was a great recipe. I added just a bit of extra dressing on day one and my husband loved it. I liked day two even more than day one. (Although we discovered that the hubs doesn't care for hoisin . :-/ ) I would say that my best advice is to take it easy with this recipe to make sure that your digestive system is really prepared to handle that much raw potato.

Great recipe for ease of prep, accessible ingredients and overall convenience.  I used 6 boneless chicken breasts instead of the thighs -- so the chicken itself was a little dry (not the fault of the recipe.)  The sauce was very good, but it's subtle.  There's no real power punch of spiciness, despite using hot salsa.  Fresh cilantro and crushed peanuts for garnishes were key.  I might salt the chicken next time prior to crocking it.  Overall this was lovely to come home to after a chilly evening at the ball park, but a couple eaters commented that it could have been spicier.
This is simply DELICIOUS! Ingredients sounded a bit strange, but the result was a delicious, creamy sauce. We ate with P4's Recipe #52025, which was a delicious combination. Thanks for sharing, Jen!

This was pretty good--this recipe is posted several times in different variations--but this is the best.  If you want Thai flavor, definately use Fish Sauce instead of Soy Sauce.  I would also salt the chicken a little before cooking and add a little more peanut butter to the sauce at the end to freshen the flavor and thicken a bit.  My family loves Thai food and this was a quick and easy close to Thai food approximation.

I was truly skeptical that salsa would do the trick for Thai food but it did!  I grilled the chicken on my George Forman as per an other reviewer on a similar recipe and mixed it all in with the sauce.  I used both soy and fish sauce and would definitely recommend the fish sauce.  We served it over rice.  The picky kids wouldn't eat it but they don't count.  I am giving it a 3 because the sauce was really a bit rich by the end of the meal.  I will try and tweak it and resubmit next time.  Over all it had good Thai-ish flavour for a fast meal on a week night!
I added almond extract to put inbetween an almond cake I made. (67231) It was light and perfect!

My favorite icing. Have everyone wanting the recipe. I have used it for cupcakes in the past and today I'll try it on cake. What I do differently is mix the sugar with the cream cheese first and then slowly add it to the cool whip so the cool whip doesn't go flat. This should be made shortly before it is served because it does go flat and forms a rubber-like surface by the next day. Great for coloring, and super fluffy-whipped

Wonderful Frosting!!Very Easy to make and tasted great with the jello cake(recipe #23480) that I made!! The combo was wonderful together!! Wasn't too sweet & the jello cake is moist & light!! Will use again on my jello cakes!! The frosting didn't go flat either, and keeps great in the fridge. Was worried it wouldn't be good but trust me the combo of both made everyone enjoy it and asked how frosting was made!! Thanks for posting grandma!!
Thanks for posting a great recipe.  I used this with Kittencal's recipe #121323.  This was the perfect frosting for it.  Thanks again.

I used this on top of a super moist and fudgy chocolate cake, it was fantastic!  I hate frostings that are over powering or too rich, then I can't taste the cake!  I only had an 8oz. container of cool whip, but I think that's the perfect amount.  I added in a little more powdered sugar and 1 cup of toasted coconut. Will def. be making this again!

Amazing! I used this in a three-layer yellow cake with strawberry filling. I spread this frosting along with the strawberry filling on each layer, then frosted the entire cake. I added 1/2 teaspoon vanilla to this and used lite Cool Whip and cream cheese. My boyfriend raved about the cake and ate two slices in one sitting! I wish I made more frosting for my leftover strawberries so I had something exquisite to dip them in. Thanks for a keeper!

Great! Easy and quick!
I put this on a coconut cake and got great reviews.
Thank you.

This is a fantastic frosting.  I used it with cake #69630 for a baby shower.  Everyone raved over it.  They loved it because it wasn't so sweet.  It was also very light and creamy.  Thanks for such a wonderful recipe.
YUMMY! This is a great dish. Easy to make and a great kid pleaser! Will definitely be making this one again.

I  eat Cool Whip like a snack, so adding cream cheese is a big plus for me. However, my husband does not share the same taste BUT he loved this frosting and asked where I bought it! (and I'll never tell)  This frosting was simple, quick, and easy. This will be 'my secret' frosting and definitely a keeper! Be sure the cream cheese is soft so it blends well with the sugar and when the Cool Whip is folded in. If I could give this 10 stars I would!  For me, this is THE perfect frosting!

I just made this and it turned out wonderful. I am a little worried though because I made it today which is Wednesday, so I could use it on my fourth of July cake. Great recipe even my pickey son liked it. Thanks, this is a keeper.

Very tasty alternative to "ordinary" pizza. Only 2 small leftover portions remaining!  THANKS!

The introduction to this recipe, I just HAD to try it! Thank You Bama for recipe! This one was a pleaser to EVERYONE in our family. and let me tell you..... this just does not happen very often in our household. Out of 5 children we only have one that is not a picky eater. this was very easy and very good...we all enjoyed it.

My boys really enjoyed this.  It was simple and tasty.   I might layer the meat and cheese next time just for added gooey-ness.  Thank you for sharing!

really enjoyed it, and it was SUPER easy to make. Next time I'm going to try more of a mexician flavour and add black beans, tomatoes, corn & chillies, and instead of tomato sauce...salsa. Great recipe!

Delish!! I made a few adjustments to reduce the bulk since I was only serving 3 people: one pound of Italian sausage (no ground chuck), half the pizza sauce (we don't like tons of sauce), and just two kinds of cheese I had on hand (mozzarella and Parmesan). The crust was glorious, the aroma was delectable, and the taste was spectacular. I've had this recipe for years but never made it until now. I was really pleased and will make this part of my pizza/calzone repertoire. Thanks so much for the recipe. I sent the recipe to two people while I was still eating it.
This is a rich drink, I omitted the steamed milk and topped it off with Cool Whip topping, you need a sweet tooth for this, it is very sweet, thanks for sharing hon!...Kitten

I knew I would love this as I just love cinnamon, simple to make with my coffee maker too so I'm sure I will be making this often. I used recipe #37023 for the syrup as it's hard to come by here without paying a small fortune. Thanks for posting Bev!

This is an old family fav. when it's really hot out.  We use all the same ingredients but the olives and onions.  And, before they started selling the rotisserie chickens everywhere we used to poach our chicken breasts in some stock.  Great recipe!

Truly a gem that made for a nice breakfast.  For the fruit, I used pineapple, and banana, and for the cereal I used some honey oat granola cereal.  So easy, so quick.  The flavors were nice, though using the honey granola cereal bought out the honey flavor.  That's a good thing. Enjoyed this very much.  Made for PRMR Tag.

I made this using mangoes as my tropical fruit. I cut the recipe in half and had one serving as directed. I mixed the 2nd serving all together and took it to work with me. Delicious. Made for Veggie Swap 62.

I really liked the crystallized ginger in this recipe and enjoyed the combination very much.  Definitely reminds me of Spring and Summer with the tropicaliness.  I used kiwi, oranges, mango, canteloupe, pineapple, strawberries, and blackberries.  I thought the fresh pineapple made for the best taste.  Sprinkled some granola and crystallized ginger over the top as well.  Made it for Please Review My Recipe.  Thank you ellie, for a keeper.

Dojemi- I recently made this same recipe from "The Best American Recipes 2004-2005" (originally cited from "The Way We Cook" by Sheryl Julian and Julie Riven- cook, Arlene Jacobs). Thanks for posting!

I tried this and it came out nice and crispy. we all enjoyed it a lot, including my 1.5 yr old daughter. 
I used the mayo, mustard, lime juice combo as a dipping sauce to this and it was awesome. Thanks for the recipe. I will definitely do this many more times.

What a great recipe!  Don't overcook the asparagus as that crispy coating with the crunch of asparagus is great!  ...and definitely, thick asparagus is the key.  We'll make this often.  Thank you, Dojemi.
I had a lot of extra asparagus and used this to take an appetizer to a birthday party.  It was a relatively easy and quick recipe that everyone liked.

This was good, easy to make and nice flavour. Maybe need abit more garlic, onion and salt. It is tasty but a little plain needs something extra maybe some capsicum, peas, tomato or mushrooms some other vegetables. Thankyou for posting.

Fantastic S'more type of cookie!!!!  I made 1/2 of the recipe and using my cookie scoop, I got 22 cookies.  These take a little extra time compared to most cookies but well worth it.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.  Made for win in the football pool!!

Great cookies!  I like that the graham crackers crumbs cut the sweetness a little.  Used fun-sized candy bars and cut each square in half.  I used my cookie scoop for these and got 40 cookies.  Made for week 1 win in the Football Pool 2012-13.

I used this recipe as a guide subsituting the turkey carcass and leftover turkey in place of chicken and chicken stock.  The seasoning was perfect and drew raves from my Katrina evacuee crowd.  Thanks!

These steaks are totally awesome. I didn`t have to make them because I`ve been served these many times in your home canarygirl. They are also very tasty when served with roasted red peppers. What a great way to us thinly sliced round steaks!  Tons of flavor for very few ingredients.  I served with a horseradish mayo dip.  Will try it on sandwiches next time.

I used this as a marinade for some venison steaks.  Threw everything in a plastic container and froze it.  Decided to go camping and threw this in the cooler. We loved it.  We are going to make it again and see if we can't tweak it a bit to make it outstanding!  I served it over a bed of rice and we all appreciated the homemade sauce instead of canned or jarred sauce.  I especially like the absence of MSG!  Thanks Nimz!

Excellent and so easy to make! I also used some mushrooms and I substitude the rice vinegar with plain wine vinegar cause I didn't had any. Its a total keeper! Now I'll never going to buy any jarred sauce again. Thanks Nimz!

Great, great recipe, & a very tasty veggie dish! Used a couple of ingredients I'd never used before, but that's what makes Zaar such a great site ~ I'm always learning, about cooking as well as about my own tastes in food! Thanks much for sharing this very satisfying dish!
I made this with Vidalias instead of green onions. Also, I used low sodium soy sauce. It was very easy to prepare, and went well with meatloaf- thanks for a great side dish.
Very nice sauce for vegetables.  I had to boost it with a bit more of everything, but it was simple and flavorful.  I also added a can of sliced water chestnuts.  Thanks for sharing!

This is very nice, and simple to put together.  I left out the peppers, as I couldn't find any in the store today.  So I put in extra broccoli and carrots.  Very quick to get from the chopping board to the table.  Thanks, Nimz!
Made for ZWT 4.
I used different veggies. The sauce was great!

Simple yet very tasty salad.  I didn't use any oil just Balsamic vinegar and it was delcious

Okie-Dokie!  This TASTED wonderful, but I will make some adjustments next time!  First of all, I used 1/2 cup hazelnuts instead of cashews; and the sugar/cinnamon/nut mixture made enough to put together 3 or 4 of these rolls! YUM!  Thanks Nonnie!  You concocted a wonderful dessert!

Oh I'm so glad I came upon this recipe.  I knew I would like it immensely as I also love datefilled cookies. I cut the recipe in 1/2 as I really didn't need 48 cookies, although I did read your directions about being able to freeze them as well.  These will make a lovely addition for holiday trays.  Thanks for this keeper Johnny!!!

My family loved this cookie! The recipe is easy to use. I doubled the amount of raisin filling in each cookie and gently pressed the top cookie layer over the filling. The cookies really do increase in size, so give plenty of room when placing on baking sheet. Make lots because they disappear quickly!

I had 3 large field mushrooms which I have just devoured for lunch and throughly enjoyed.  I did have to sub diced ham of the bone for the bacon and grilled (broiled) at a lower temperature to make sure the mushrooms would cook through.  Thank you Mandy for scrumptious mushroom recipe.  Made for Newest ZAAR Tag Winter 07.

I used 1/4 teaspoon of Tabasco in case DS wouldn't like it too spicy.  But I should have used 1/2 teaspoon cause anyway he didn't like the mushrooms (don't know why).  But we loved them.  5 minutes and they were done with a nice color.  Thanks Mandy.  Made for Beverage tag.

We loved these! I made these on request of my DD, and will have to make them again. I couldn't take pictures, they were gone too fast! Unfortunately i forgot the chives, with it it would've tasted even better... Made for ZWT4, Tastebud Tickling Travellers

OMG!!  So delicious!!  I used sliced mushrooms (baby bellas, white button and shiitake) as that is what I had.  I mounded them in a foil packet and topped with the rest of the ingredients.  Grilled for about 10 minutes and served with some grilled steaks.  What a perfect combination!  The hot sauce is a great idea!  Made for the Babes of ZWT4.

Yummy!  I love mushrooms.  I used wild mushrooms along with brown mushrooms.  This were soooo good.  I served these over perogies.  Thank you.  Will make again.  (Made and reviewed for NZ/Aus recipe Swap #21 Oct. 2008).

Excellent!  Yes delicate and buttery and so delicious, just what I expect from an Andypandy recipe. The flavorings so compliment making this an extraordinary cherry loaf- a loaf that will be used for coffee hours, tea and bake sales and when having friends in for coffee and dessert. Yes it's that good! Have always said there is nothing like a 'grandma recipe' and thank you for sharing one of yours.
This is a really unique and delicious salad. I tried it from Olive Garden's web site and saw it was listed on here already. Delicious!

This was fairly quick to put together and I really enjoyed it.  I left out the broccoli for personal preference and had to add a lot more milk (I used 2% milk) because it was just too thick.  I used the chicken and mushroom soup as suggested which I really like and I used 6 slices of bacon (just because I love bacon)  I will probably add some red pepper flakes to kick it up a bit next time and maybe some parmesan cheese.  All in all it will make a good lunch for the week.  Made for Spring PAC 2014
OMG!  These are wonderful...it helps that I adore bananas & vanilla yogurt.  My kids also loved these and they cooked up very quickly for a nice weekend breakfast.  Thanks for the post.  ZWT 2007

These were just superb.  Loved the yogurt maple syrup topping.  We'll be have lots of these on the weekends now. 
Thank you.

I made these for Little Miss (DD) for breakfast and she yummed it all up. Little Miss said she loved the bite size pancakes, I told her they were pikelets and she wouldn't believe me. She loved the banana topping. Thank you Mandy from Oz - *Made for Zaar World Tour 4*

These are awesome!  I used lemon flavored honey (all I had on hand) with really good results.  I used skim milk & vinegar because my buttermilk was not fit to use anymore.  My girls loved these.  We did use 3/4 cup white, 1 cup wheat flour, but the texture is light enough, I'll use more wheat flout next time.  These work really well for dropping large Michican blueberries into them on the griddle, because their fluffiness keeps the blueberries encased in batter, rather than sticking all over when you flip the pancakes.  The beaten egg whites are a great way to lighten up the texture!  I did find that it is necessary to spread the batter out a little bit when dropping on the griddle, or they are gooey in the middle, but not too much, or you knock the air out of the egg whites.  Made for Kid friendly tag.
This dish reminds me of one my mom made for us as kids, so I just had to try it. This is a little differant than my mom made, but it is delicious! Thanks! I'll be making this again!
The taste was okay, But the preparation was horrible, I kept having to add more flour because I could not get strips I only got balls. I would suggest you never even try to make this!

This is one of the many fine cookies my Norwegian Grandma used to make for us. Tebrod 'Tea-Bread'. You use a rolling pin to roll out the whole lump of dough into a thick slab and then cut into strips with a knife. She also decorated them with colored sugar sprinkles and chocolate sprinkles. A very simple and yummy treat. She taught me how to do them when I was 5 yrs old. (with help, of course!) ;)

Excellent way to serve watermelon!  I made this for our Labor Day party and everyone loved and the ladies wanted the recipe.  It was a refreshing complement to our traditional heavy potato salad and baked beans that accompany our burgers and hot dogs.

Still tastes great, but looks a little rough:-)

Thanks Laurie

This recipe is a total mouth explosion of flavor!  I thought I would share them with my family, but decided I would keep them all to myself. (I still don't plan on sharing!)

loved this!!! last week I made them exactly as recipe written. this week instead of eggplant, I used roasted pureed zucchini, squash & carrots. it was just as good!!! I'll be fixing these on a regular basis.

I made this summery salad to take to my grandmother's for lunch.  We both enjoyed it very much.  Great flavors, it is reminiscent of other Mediterranean salads I have made before, but this time using farro as the base.  While you need to set aside quite a bit of time to make this salad (mostly owing to the soaking and the simmering of the farro),  it is quite easy to make.  We had a lot of leftovers and the salad held up well the next day with an extra little splash of red wine vinegar.  I'll make this again.  Thanks!

This is a ten star recipe, thanks for sharing!
We are casein free so I used about a cup and 1/4 of cashew paste (leftover from making cashew milk) with a seperate 1/2 cup of warm water to bloom the yeast. I cut the yeast back to 1 tablespoon (candida scares me) used 1 cup of arrowroot to replace 1 of the cups of tapioca (tapioca binds with and removes calcium) and raw apple cider vinegar instead of the lemon juice. I baked it in an 8 inch cake pan because I was using it for stuffing. It turned out extremely well. The texture is like a really good sour dough bread and the taste is divine. I will use this recipe for foccocia, stuffing and subs from now on. 
Thanks again.

This recipe sounded real good and the reviews were good so I decided to try it. However, I now disagree with the 5 star review. I found this soup very lacking in flavor and the parmesan cheese did not blend very well and would get clumpy on your spoon. I gave it 2 stars just because it was edible!

Thank you so much for posting this.. I had made it before from the magazine and lost track of it.  I seem to remember adding more seasonings than called for, but it really is a wonderfull and easy soup. Got to have a crusty bread for dipping.

This was very good and easy to make. I followed the recipe as written other then I used a can of crushed tomatoes instead of diced tomatoes. I also used 1/2 cup of parmesan cheese. My kids loved this. Will be making again.
This is a wonderful recipe! It is very filling and tasty. My husband said he would give it 10 stars out of 5. It is very easy to make. I will definately make this again and again.

This is really good! I love how light and refreshing it is, with the lemon juice and fresh grated rind highlighting the flavour. I used a few drops of stevia liquid instead of sugar, as I usually do with dressings and vinagrettes that call for sweetening. Omitted salt, as we were having grilled ham and cheese sandwiches to accompany the coleslaw, and what a complement they were to each other! Best thanks for this recipe.
This is one of our family staples. I was attracted to it because of the title, thinking, would it delight him? It did!

This was wonderful, then men went crzy over it, I pureed the cottage cheese because the would have reacted badly if they knew it was in there. but thats the only thing i changed. It was a hit. It served 12 easily with the other casseroles. Thanks so much for posting. Its a keeper.

I gave this 5 stars. I make a dish very close to this it is Creamy Noodles N' Beef Casserole. The recipe I use microwaves for 6-7 minutes then another 6-7 minutes. I couldn't believe how fast our 6 year old ate this AND then asked for seconds! DH loved it as well.... I am renaming this dish in our house to My Boys' Delight. Delicious! In my opinion, anything with cream cheese in it is a winner. This is a perfect recipe for serving a crowd.

This was pretty good.  My only complaint is that the sour cream/cream cheese taste is a little overpowering. Overall, a very good recipe.

I think these will be a regular for X-mas baking for me (although not the only time I will make them).  Thanks for the recipe!

Although these ingredients may not seem appealing to some people, the end results are surprisingly wonderful!   The soup is pleasantly mild and has a subtle sweet flavor to it.   The only thing I added was some chopped onions.  I used fat free half and half to cut some fat.  Thanx for posting this yummy creamy chowder!

This is a very delicious filling chowder, perfect this time of year for warming up little cold tummies. I too initially found this recipe at Wal-Mart and was skeptical about the combination of ingredients, however was pleasantly surprised and wouldn't change anything. I prefer to garnish with fresh dill. Thank you for posting this recipe here, I have been looking for this exact recipe for the past couple years. I have tried other variations and none are quite this good. Thanks again!
Pretty good.  I had to add a little greek seasoning because it was a tad bland for my tastes, but overall good.  It made a lot and was a healthy eat.

This recipe is amazing!! It is as good or better than skipper's. I halved the amount of clams because I wanted to test the recipe and originally was only going to make a half batch. But as I was cooking, the flavors were so good, I decided to make a full batch and I did use pre-sliced package Bacon, so there were six slices to fill in anywhere there might have been a clam or two missing. But I really didn't notice anything missing at all because it was just so good!! I did sub heavy cream for half half because that's what I had on hand. Just for fun, I added a little corn. I don't think I'll ever need to look for another clam chowder recipe. I will make this again and again. After making this a dozen times (this and Jakes Etouffee are my favorite recipes) I've posted a few improvements. The recipe doesn't call for it but add the shallot with the tomato and Parmesan to the sauce. More importantly, I doubled the amount of dry ingredients for covering the shrimp. As you toss them in the flour mixture and set them aside they become damp looking again. When you finish coating them, toss them a second time. This results in very nicely crispy shrimp and helps retain the Parmesan and pepper flavors in the batter.

C.F. shrimp scampi is one of my two favorites on the menu, so I was excited to try this recipe. There definitely is lemon juice in the authentic version, so I added this to the sauce. Be careful to only add a very little at the end. This recipe calls for adding the already cooked shrimp to the sauce prior to serving. Next time I won’t do this as it ruins the crispy texture of the light shrimp coating and renders it mushy. Instead, keep the shrimp warm and serve it on the side of the plate like they do at C.F. I also AGREE about doubling the Dry ingredients ...HERE'S a TIP; Instead Of doubling with ALL flour. .I Suggest Using the Amount of flour suggested then USE SAME AMOUNT Of Cornstarch ......The Cornstarch Keeps the crunchy...without the Floury Taste :)..And I've read all the reviews posted. ..You could even use JUST cornstarch. .which that's what I Do...Also as far as the lemon taste..Whenever Your making ANY Creamy sauce...You add the Lemon as a squirt of freshness right before serving...you Never add lemon DURING the Cooking Process Bkuz of the acid..the lemon Either tends to Cook the shrimp faster and gets rubbery. .SO what Yiu wud do Is Use Lemon ZEST...in the Sauce making ..this will give the lemon flavor the recipe is missing without compromising the dish..then Chop fresh basil and a squeeze of lemon before serving...this should help..
