You get a more potent lemon taste if the rind is grated into the sugar and rubber together with your fingers. Thanks for posting.P.S. with the changes mentioned above they are now better than our Tim Hortons (so agree with other reviewer!!!!)
This was delicious! Thanks for the recipe!

This was excellent -- and got lots of totally unsolicited compliments at the two Christmas parties I took them to! As suggested by several people, I let the grated lemon rind macerate (that's prolly the wrong word, ah well) in the sugar for a while before incorporating into the mix. Also, I used fresh cranberries, and dredged them in flour before folding into the batter. Turned out lovely, and the glaze was nice!

Wonderful!!  Great lemony taste.  Doesn't really need the nuts, I liked them, but I liked the lemon and cranberry tastes best, and the glaze is great too - make with fresh squeezed lemon!  I made these to take to a get together tonight, and I'm glad I made mini muffins for them and loaves for me, because when I get home I have a mini loaf for now and a mini loaf for the freezer.  Thanks for a great recipe!

Thanks for sharing this delicious recipe! I halved the recipe, used a cup of fresh cranberries instead of dried, and omitted the nuts. I baked it for about 35-40 min. I also topped it with a simple lemon icing instead of the glaze: 3 tbsp butter, 1.5 cups icing sugar, and 1.5 tbsp lemon juice. This will be made often!

I was really hoping for an outstanding taste, from all the reviews. I normally make this with fresh cranberries, but didn't have any, so that was my reason for trying this recipe. It's not bad, just not as wonderful as all the reviews. Also, the glaze didn't look anything like the pictures. All I can think of is that maybe it should have been confectioner's sugar?? That's what I've always used in the past, but since the recipe didn't state conf., I used regular. Not a success.
I used fresh cranberries and didn't include the nuts. Very good. Very lemony ?

Can't say anything except that this was the best loaf!  My husband raved over it and I must say it was really good.<br/>I did use fresh cranberries instead of dried and the combination of lemon and tart cranberry was just right.<br/>Highly recommend this one!

First, I had a 20 oz. bag of fresh cranberries (I had previously frozen ) so I used them all and just snipped them in half with a scissors. Then I used all the zest from 1 large lemon, approx. 2-3 Tbls. and then juiced it. So I put the 3 Tbls. as called for, into the batter. This left me with about an 1/8 C of juice for the glaze, which probably would have been perfect. BUT I made up the difference with bottled lemon juice --and THAT was my mistake. It was sooo lemony! As in pucker power! I actually had to drizzle a little icing on each slice when serving. But it was bursting with flavor and disappeared in no time :) I will definitely make this again -and the same way- EXCEPT that I will use whatever amount of juice the one lemon gives, and NOT add any bottled. Then I'm sure it will be 5+ stars worthy! I made 1 large loaf for right now and 3 small ones for the freezer. (It's always nice to have things on hand for when the kids visit. )

Tried this recipe with dried blueberries instead of dried cranberries it turned out great! I have tried fresh blueberry in recipes and the bread breaks up so much, with the dried blueberry it stayed together better. I like lemon and blueberry together and orange and cranberry together

Decided to make muffins instead. Followed another reviewers suggestion and used 1 cup of fresh cranberries (chopped after measuring). Drizzled with lemon glaze and added a sprinkling of sugared zest to the tops. Very pretty and tasty.
This was made for the Diabetic Tag Game in TOTM.  It made a very filling brunch dish for DH and me.  I substituted mushrooms for the zucchini.  Delicious and filling.  Thanks Nan for posting.

I make several different breakfast frittata's and this one is different (in a good way) & tasty.  I increased the bacon abit & used olive oil for the margarine.  Threw in some green onions, jalapeno & a couple sliced fresh mushrooms.  I cut back the tomatoes and glad I did because I think it would have overpowered the flavours for us otherwise.  Nice change to our normal breakfast recipes, thanks for sharing.

Easy recipe to put together.  Had some "bite" to it with the cayenne.  I would leave the sugar out of the basting sauce next time, though.  Didn't care for the sweet edge.  Cooked mine indoors on the Foreman Grill, but will try again during the outdoor grilling season.  Made for Fall 2009 My 3 Chefs game.

I made this last night. It was delicious. Although. Even though I do tend to love things with a spicy hot bite... This was just a tad over the top. I will make this again but cut the cayenne back to a half of a teaspoon, VErrry delicious any way even being too hot.
Amazing! It's alot like Tradtional Mole sauce, very rich and unexpected but with a lovely finish
yummy!

This is a great recipe.  I'm not a big fan of biscotti but had to make something for our coffeehouse party.  It was a huge hit!  It is pretty simple and everyone raved about homemade biscotti and the yummy taste.  Thanks!
I cut down on the cinnamon to one teaspoon so as allow the honey flavour to come through. I also added a cup of toasted pecan pieces. Really good biscotti - thanks for posting!

Yum, yum, yum!  I followed the recipe exactly and it was delicious. I used an orange blossom honey and the flavor came thru even w/ three teaspoons of cinnamon and the rolled oats gave it a great texture.  I'm looking forward to having one w/ my coffee in the morning.  Definite will be making this again!  Thanks for sharing the recipe, carolreu!

I was looking for a nutfree biscotti recipe that was would have crunch.  I made this twice and it was a real hit.  They seems to get better after a few days - the honey flavor gets stronger.   The only changes I made was to add more flour as i shaped them and I divided the dough into four sections to make smaller biscotti.  For a little interest, I added 1/2 T. of anise seed and dribbled a light anise glaze over finished cookies.
Exccellent, I was sure the kids would hate it, but they LOVED IT!! And I feel good giving them such a healthy treat!
I wasn't a big fan of these, but when I gave them away, everyone else loved them.  Mine turned out a bit too crumbly--I am not sure why...

The cookies were crumbly when I was slicing them.I also reduced the cinnaon by 2 teaspoons, and I had only half a cup of honey,so I added a little sugar to make up for the sweetness.I am thinking maybe that is why the cookies were a little crumbly.My two year old just nibbled away at them though.That says a lot-the recipe is very good.

Just made these tonight. I substituted 1 cup of white whole wheat flour. They have a nice flavor - not very sweet, but hearty and healthy tasting. I wish mine had turned out a bit crisper...they just wouldn't do it! They're definitely firm, just not totally dry like I like. Oh well, I'll keep trying. Nice recipe - thank you!
My husband said this reminded him of one of the Jaeger Schnitzel dinners he had on our recent trip to Germany. I guess that says it all. Made for Maommy Diva's Cook A Thon. :)

WOW, this was delish! I used chicken breasts and it turned out great. I used S&P and lightly dusted with flour before browning. I placed them in a baking dish and followed the rest of the recipe with a couple small changes.  I used chicken stock and added some Kitchen Bouquet, to darken up the sauce. Then I baked for 40 minutes @  350°F. It was divine and gobbled up, even the kids loved it. I served with buttered parsley noodles.  Made for Mommyy Diva's Cook-a-thon! Fight Like A Girl MD!

Delicious! Easy and quick to make. I would give 10 stars if I could! I used chicken breast and dusted with flour before browning, doubled the mushrooms and used chicken stock and light cream. I didn't use ham. It was flavorful enough for us. Served with rice but would be great with pasta or potatoes too. This is definitely keeper! My husband loved it! Thank you so much Mommy Diva for excellent recipe.
Made for Mommy Diva's Cook-a-thon! Fight Like A Girl!

Wonderful dish! The only thing about it we did not like had nothing to do with the recipe. The pork I used was the correct cut of meat but was tough and leathery. Bad butcher. I will definitely be making this again (and again) because we loved the sauce!
I did have to make one change. I had ham set aside and when it came time to start dinner found that DH had made a sandwich or two with it. At 6pm I wasn't going to the store so I used thick cut bacon sliced in to lardons. It was great! Next time I would boil the sauce to thicken it up some. I use 35% cream and it can take a boil without separating. Scrumptious sauce though and I'm thinking that it would be awesome to use as a topping for steaks. Thanks for posting Chelle and keep on FIGHTING LIKE A GIRL!!!!
This was really good over our spaetzli and pork chops (we breaded them with Italian bread crumbs and parmesan cheese). The prep time was about twice the 30 minutes stated though.
I am so grateful that this is a pork recipe Hubby hates veal but I love it. Thanks again!
THANK YOU!!! My mom has been searching for this recipe for AGES! She found it in a women's magazine years ago and misplaced it. Definitely making these this year for a party!

Looking for a recipe to use some leftover steak.  I found that 1 lb of meat easily did 4 wraps.  We don't like real creamy dishes so I cut back the cream cheese mixture, substituted feta for blue cheese & sour cream for milk.  Cut back the bacon abit also.  For the greens I used chopped romaine & some leftover cooked vegys.  Wanted to serve warm so I heated meat, built the wraps, sprinkled with cheddar & baked @ 350F for about 15 min.  Very yummy & a great way to serve up leftovers in a new & tasty dish.  Thanks for sharing.

This turned out better than I thought! I used purple onions (not sure why they were purple, and I'm not even sure if they're what you call "sweet onions"!) and garlic powder, but like yogi, I couldn't really taste the garlic. Next time I'll probably reduce the honey, but otherwise, this recipe is great! Thanks Sharon, this was really easy.

This is a nice change from other ordinary spreads. I love the sweet and salty, but would reduce if not omit the honey next time. A glass of red wine and great crusty bread served with this spread made my dinner tonight!  Thank you for sharing :)

This turned out very nicely.  The flavor was more sweet than I expected (from the honey and sweet onions?) and I couldn't taste much garlic.  I will definitely make this again, though next time try more garlic and maybe less honey or regular onions, though I'm sure other people will love the sweetness of it.

Yum-za!  I have made this twice, the first time following the recipe exactly and the second time with the following changes:  I used 2 Tablespoons olive oil with the onions and garlic.  Also, I turned the oven to 375 and baked it one hour so the onions got slightly browned.  These changes resulted in better flavor.  I found that I absolutely loved this on buttered French bread.  Thanks for posting this, I haven't seen another one like it.

What a sweet and flavorful spread! Made without the honey and am so glad I did as the onions turn very sweet with the roasting. Was very tasty on roast beef sandwiches and am already planning on using the remaining on grilled veggies. Thanks for the post.
I really enjoyed this sauce!  The flavors balanced well, I used water instead of stock and only about 1/2 a cup as I used it as a pizza sauce.  I will be making this again, thanks for sharing!

WOW.. some in-you-face-flavours here ! DH made this for dinner tonight and we enjoyed it over pasta. I'm not certain about this serving more than 2-3 people, I went back for seconds and DH had beaten me to it and there was none left. My standard sized blender was only about 1/5th full at most, the total ingedients not adding up to a huge amount... so next time we will definiately be doubling the recipe. I had homemade vegetable stock in the freezer but DH didn't find it so he used the water option instead... and he used a pinch of sugar and a decent amount of red pepper flakes. The result was a spicy, garlic-y tomato sauce with hints of onion in the mix... quite strong tasting but FULL of flavour. Please see my rating system: 5 excellent stars for pleasing DH who declared that we must definiately save this recipe as he enjoyed it very much. High praise indeed from the Pasta Fanatic. If you are not overly keen on onion. garlic or pepper flakes then this recipe might be too strong for your tastes, but if like us, you appreciate these in spades, then this IS a recipe that you will enjoy as much as we did.  Made for Pick-a-Chef Autumn 2008, Thanks!

My DS's loved this-but could someone PLEASE tell my DH to stop picking at the jellybeans! Used salted cocktail peanuts since we enjoy salty/sweet combo.
Thanks for another great one Shirl(J)831!

Sooooo delicious, I love that zippy tang from the lemon. I kept exactly to the ingredients with one adjustment, I doubled the oregano. I pounded the chicken first and I cooked it in the oven for about forty mins, (I don't have a slow cooker). Had it with broccoli and basmati rice. Thanks, this will be a regular!!

Outstanding! I made this for dinner tonight, and was rushed so I too made it in the oven rather than in the crockpot (30 mins covered at 325F, then remove cover, baste, and 10 more mins uncovered). I used 3 garlic cloves and about 1/4 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice. The flavour was excellent, tangy and garlicky, and the chicken was very tender and moist. It was quite straightforward to prepare and I will definitely make this for my family again; they loved it.
This was very good .. I was short on time so I made it on the stovetop.. very easy, another keeper!

Easy preparation and wonderful flavor.  I used a cut up fryer instead of only chicken breasts and it turned out great.  I also cooked it in the oven, covered for 40 minutes and uncovered the last 10-15 minutes.  Used more garlic than called for because the garlic cloves were small and we just like garlic.  I served it with roasted potatoes and steamed asparagus.  A delicious meal we will have again.
I just love crockpot recipes. This was very easy and tasty. I make this on Girl Guides night so I can have an earily dinner. It is a nice change from sweet and sour recipes, but I do like them too.
Very good taste for very little effort! I followed another reviewer's cooking method and baked uncovered at 325 F for 30 minutes, then uncovered for 10 minutes. This one's a keeper.

Another tasty low carb dish that has been added to my weekly rotation. I did sub olive oil for the butter but it didn't seem to make a difference in taste. Prepared this over the stove top in 20 minutes served with green salad and sauteed artichokes. Thanks for a great recipe
Outstanding! I did add a little more water(2/3 cup) but other than that I followed the recipe exactly. Very easy to prepare and the flavor was perfect. I will definately be making this often.

Hi Kitina;
Made this for dinner last nite.  Tender, meat fell off the bone, had a delightful and nice lemony taste.
I did add more garlic as we love the garlic flavor.
Thanks for sharing this great recipe.
Will be making it again as my DW will only eat Chicken Breasts.
"Uncle Bill"

Wow, this was SO good!!!  As soon as I finished my plateful I wanted some more (and I am not a big fan of chicken!).  I served it over rice with a side of green beans.  The flavor was just amazing...I wish I could give it more than 5 stars.  I used three huge chicken breasts so I upped each ingredient just a smidge.  Thank you very much for this great recipe - I will be making it many more times!

This recipe was very easy to do.  I did follow the directions exactly.  After running two chicken breasts through the seasoning bowl however - there wasn't any seasonings left.  So I sprinkled seasonings over the chicken as it was browning in the pan.  I thickened the juices a bit when dinner was ready for some real tasty gravy.  A very yummy recipe! :)

I would give this 100 stars if I could.  It was moist, flavorful and scrumptious, exactly what you want chicken to taste like.  The sauce was so tastey, I could have drank it â˜º.  I did make extra sauce, I added and extra 1/2 cup of water and 2 tablespoons of lemon juice.  So total water was 3/4c and 5T lemon juice.  It was very lemony (we love lemon flavored in our family) 
OH I forgot to mention that I made it in the oven as pp mentioned I cooked covered for 35 minutes and uncovered for 15 minutes (I had huge pieces of chicken breasts), temp 350 
I think we will be serving this once a week for a long time.  
BTW, I made this with side dish Lemony Rice Pilaf Recipe #16512 
Thank you for posting this recipes.
Fran 
Illinois
This was fabulous!  I used boneless, skinless chicken which I know can tend to get dry in the crockpot if you are not careful, but it turned out great!  The sauce was divine!

I cooked only two breast, but didn't decrease the sauce and it was just enough.  As one chef mentioned, the sauce is so darn good it's drinkable.  Since we're already puckered, kitina,  we're all blowing lemon kisses your way!

Giving this 1 star because, well......I think just submitting a recipe deserves it.  Honestly I didn't like it at all.  There wasn't enough sauce to cover anything and it was thin as could be.  Maybe it's just me but I was expecting more of a sweet lemon taste and this was just pucker power, so I added about  1/4 cup of brown sugar and a can of crushed pineapple (I ran out of lemon juice - only had enough to double the recipe).  I won't be making this again.

One of my son's favorites. Prepared as directed but doubled the water, lemon juice, garlic & bouillion so we'd have more sauce. Chicken breasts were so tender & juicy that they fell apart so we shredded & served over rice with the sauce.

This was great. I too added my own spin.

I season salted and peppered both sides of the chicken then placed in an olive oiled glass baking dish, 

Then I melted the butter and added the parsley, garlic, lemon and water and poored it on top.

I am not an oregano fan so I skipped it.

Baked at 325 covered for 30 then uncovered for 10.

Super simple.

Delicious and tender.

There was plenty of sauce, I may even cut it down to 1 T of butter next time.

Very nice.
Really good chicken!  Lots of flavour for sure but maybe a little too tangy.

A slow cooker recipe with a difference -- I had come to the conclusion slow cooker recipes meant a stew like dinner.  I was concerned at the start when there was not a lot of liquid in the pot.  Still, I went ahead.  The result is terrific!!!  Tasty chicken and a light 'jus' in the bottom of the pot.  All who had lunch with us today enjoyed the dish.  I will change nothing next time we make this one.
Great flavor,simple and quick.Yum!
This recipe is so easy and every time I make it I hear, "This is the BEST chicken I've ever had." So moist and flavorful, it's perfect for every day dining or as the protein to a special meal.

Turned out great!  We loved the sauce, which I thickened up with a slurry of cornstarch.  I had thought it may be too lemony so reduced the lemon by a 1/2 Tablespoon, but it would have been fine with the 3 Tbsp.  Next time I make it, I will use the full amount of lemon juice.  Thanks for a yummy and simple recipe.
I followed the recipe exactly except I used a can of chicken broth instead of the water I did double the recipe. I like a lot of broth and the chicken was falling apart. Such a good flavor!

Great simple quinoa recipe!  I don't care for onions so left them out.  The seasonings in this were very mild, making it a nice side dish for the spicy grilled chicken I served it with.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

Another great way to use Jell-o! We used the raspberry flavor and the color came out nice and bright and the crunch is similar to butter-toffee popcorn. I DO think this is a 2-person job and you have to be very attentive that you take it out of the oven right away because it burns easily! I am looking forward to trying different flavors!
i made these for my christmas gift baskets i use cherry the colors came out bright and beautiful and the flavor great

This was delicious. I made a few goofs but they turned out to be fine. I misread the directions and added the bluberries to the cream mixture, But tasting the two in one bite makes me think I will do it this way from now on. The only other thing I did different was we assembled them in individual glasses because I was worried the angel food cake would get too soggy, taking in to consideration, we have three strawberry desserts in our fridge to eat due to this swap! Any ways the flavor was wonderful with the almond extract coming through nicely. Thanks Happy Harry!

Four stars for the flavor of the coating and moistness of the chicken. I used Reduced Fat Cheez-It crackers. I did have quite a bit of coating left over even though I pressed it onto the tenders. There is also no oven temp listed, so I baked the tenders as I always do which is 400 degrees for 10 minutes per side.
Great Cookie!!  Made them this week for St. Paddy's day - a huge hit.  I iced them with some Bailey's and icing sugar for an extra punch.

Gee, maybe saying how big the cookies should be when we put them in the oven would help. I did 1 large tablespoon each and they took 20 minutes to cook. More Bailey's would be better, can't even taste it. Had to make my own cake flour. Dumb to use it. Sorry but, there are better recipes for these cookies out there.
I love this.  I found it a great recipe to bring to a potluck.
If you like eggplant or quiche, you will LOVE this.  I did. easy to make and super tasty!

We made this casserole for dinner tonight and liked it.  It is not difficult to prepare and worked well as a weeknight meal.  I served with an arugula salad with feta cheese and pomegranate-infused balsamic vinegar (purchased at Fustinis in Traverse City).  I liked that this had a subtle spicy flavor.  While we liked it, we didn't love it.  Thanks for a quick, easy, veggie meal.
Yum! This is so so so good! I left out the cilantro because I don't care for it, everything else was the same. I'll be making this again for sure! Thank you!

WOW!  I was completely suprised.  This was just like a quiche without the crust.  Used everything to exact measurements, but I think I will use a white or yellow onion next time as it was a little overpowering with the red onion.  Thanks!

Delicious! I followed the recipe exact except I could not find fresh cilantro this time of year in Alaska so I used dried. Even my husband who doesn't care for eggplant ate it and liked it. Easy to put together, wonderful blend of flavors. Another winner!

Wow!  A great new way to fix eggplant!  Those fresh herbs and feta really give this casserole spectacular flavor.  My eggplants were the very long, slender chinese eggplants, so I used 3 of them for this recipe.  I may have gone a little heavier on the feta ;)  but otherwise followed the recipe exactly.  Thanx for posting this.  It's a real keeper!
Wonderful Eggplant recipe and I love cilantro so this was great for me, you can really taste the flavour. Thanks for posting!

I'm a great fan of the combination of eggplant and tomatoes, but this was a new and unusual combination of seasonings for me. It was truly declicious. (I used canned diced tomatores rather than stewed, but I doubt that changed the taste experience much.)

Very good! I liked it. It was easy to prepare. The taste reminded me of dish my mom use to make.It was nice to eat warm, but even better cold. 
When warm the taste of onion is little bit overpowering, but I didn't  mind, because I like onions.
Day after, eating it cold, it was much better, since all flavors just blended wonderfully.
And it's very nice looking dish, too.

I enjoyed this a lot - it's very flavourful and a great combo of ingredients. It was nice and easy to make and the directions were spot on. This isn't quite 5 star for me because personally I felt it was a little too tomatoey. I couldn't find stewed tomatoes so used regular canned (as previous reviewers have) and, while I don't think this would really have affected the taste, I wonder if I shouldn't have drained them first as it was very watery and, as I say, a bit overpowering. I'll probably make this again but I'll be making a couple of amendments. Thanks Engrossed!

This is the first time I have tried eggplant and I must say that this is a fantastic dish!  I did add four eggs instead of three as it didn't seem like it would be enough to cover - I am glad that I did.  Other than that I didn't change anything, although next time I think I will add some garlic to this very Italian tasting dish.  Thanks for making my first time eating eggplant a less scary prospect!

Very tasty, and very easy to put together.  My husband forgot to buy the Feta at the store, so I used a combination of mozzarella and parmesan.  Definitely would have been better with the Feta, but it was still tasty.  I would not categorize this as a main dish, but if you added grilled chicken strips or something like that, it could serve as a meal.  I think the key ingredient is the fresh cilantro.  It adds such a wonderfully bright flavor!

I couldn't wait to review this! I have an odd-take on this dish. First, I used lowfat ingredients and had to sub with dried herbs which I would easily do again. More interesting: I actually found this dish to be good served immediately.. but *outstanding* when chilled and served as a cold-salad of sorts the following day! What a great side dish for a warm-summer evening to jazz up a grilled chicken.
Brought this to a collaborative supper with our neighbors, and we all enjoyed it very much.  I did saute the onions a little to soften them first.  Great combination of herbs and spices!

Oh boy this was good!  I used fresh tomatoes roughly cut and omitted the cilantro, did not have.  This dish kind of reminded me of frittata, but without so much egg.  I was a bit leery of the spice mixture, but it was really good. Be careful with the sage, it can overpower a dish

Outstanding dish!!  When I told my DH we were having eggplant for dinner, he said (with a sly grin) "I'm allergic to eggplant"......NOT!!  He just THOUGHT he didn't like eggplant until he tried this wonderful dish.  A perfect blend of flavors. I can't wait to make it again, it was thoroughly enjoyed!
Deliscious dish, only a little moisty for me, left in the oven almost one hour. Thank you for post.

Pretty tasty way to make eggplant!  I loved all the fresh herbs and spices.  It reminds me a lot of a frittata with the egg baking on top.  Very light and fresh!  I added a jalapeno to spice it up and my boyfriend loved it!  It did take awhile to get the egg mixture to set...probably at least an hour.

Loved the mix of flavors and a wonderful way to use the frozen, breaded eggplant slices I already have in my freezer! I also precooked the onions a bit first. Even using petite diced canned tomatoes, it was wonderful! Will definately make again!

This was really good!  I am not a fan of cilantro so I omitted and I used a can of crushed tomatoes, everything else I kept the same and it was awesome.  I did think it was a little heavy on the onion but it was still great.  Thanks for posting!

Although I didn't add the cilantro this time, I felt this was a great GF dish.  I "fried" the eggplant in  the oven at 450 degrees after spritzing the slices with oil and putting them on parchement paper.  If you cook the casserole covered for more time (I did 40 minutes), then the onions are not crunchy.
Miss Annie, my DH and I really loved your french toast! I put it in the fridge overnight and it turned out wonderful. I used red rasberry preserves and milk. Scrumptious! Thanks!

Fantabulous!  Used blackberry jam and whole milk, and made it the night before.  Nice crisp crust on the top, and tender underneath.  Not too soggy, not too eggy.  It was awesome.  We had it with maple syrup over the top.  Mmmmmm.  Thank you!
Excellent! Thank you! (I used Garbanzo Beans/Chick Peas instead of beans due to lack of, & it was awesome!)
These are very good!  I sprinkled with cinnamon and sugar before baking.

These were delicious and filling.  I love stuffed peppers and love to find all kinds of alternatives to the traditional version.  This was perfect and very easy to make.  I added a little cumin to the stuffing mixture, but otherwise followed the recipe as written.  The peppers were nicely cooked but still had a slight crunch, which I like.  Great recipe; thanx!

Almost without exception, when I see ice included in a recipe like this, I'll exclude it, & I did this time, too ~ For me, that just gives the drink a more intense flavor, & the frozen fruit & sherbet gave it a great chill! The only other thing I did was to use an extra half can of the nectar, & had A VERY, VERY NICE TASTING SMOOTHIE! [Tagged, made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in the current Pick-A-Chef]
This recipe clone is from Top Secret Recipes Sodas, Smoothies, Spirits, & Shakes by Todd Wilbur: topsecretrecipes.com

I also saw this recipe in NY Times, and I made it for Thanksgiving this year. Fabulous! I substituted chanterelles for crimini mushrooms, garlic paste for the chopped garlic, and added a cipollini onion to the shallot but otherwise used the stated ingredients. I baked my squash at 400 for about 50 minutes. I laid out my rolls directly on the parchment sheet so I wouldn't break them transferring them from the counter to the sheet, and I was glad I did. I baked my rolls at 375 instead of 400 because that's what the pastry dough package said -- probably a mistake, try it at 400 so the pastry dough doesn't underbake. (Even at 375 it was still pretty good, though.)

This recipe would probably be terrific made with other cheese and vegetable fillings, and DH wants me to try it with beef one of these days. I'm sure I'll make it again this winter just to make the day seem more like a holiday...

I was looking for a vegetarian dish to serve at Thanksgiving this year.  I wanted something special for my vegetarian daughter to enjoy.  This wellington was superb.  Even non-vegetarians. raved about it.  It looks beautiful and fit the bill as something out of the ordinary for a holiday meal.  I'm making this again as part of our Christmas dinner.
I have made this several times and it is always a hit. I even made smaller sized ones for a large gathering once. Oh they freeze well too!
Delicious and easy.

I love this recipe and use to have it memorized.  I probably have the My Great Recipes recipe card stashed somewhere...  Anyway, thanks for posting.  I have even made it several times by substituting the lb of sausage for a lb of fresh mushrooms.

I love Goya Champuru.   The recipe was great although I did make some changes.   I do not enjoy spam so just used the bacon instead.   I only used 4 eggs and they were way too many.  When you make this recipe, and you should,  use probably 2-3 eggs.  It helps if you add them slowly.

I really enjoyed the flavour of these and will be making them regularly for summer BBQ's. Tonight I served them with lots of vegetables instead of on buns. They hold together very well and were moist and tasty.

These were quite tasty. I halved the recipe and it worked out fine. I thought they were nice and moist and had good flavor. I keep a list of burger recipes (I don't like just plain meat) and this one will go on it!

These were very good, though I altered it a bit. I used 2 lbs of beef but left the seasonings the same - I like really flavorful burgers. I also added about 1 tsp of montreal steak seasoning. 
I think the BBQ sauce keeps the burgers moist. I served these on whole-wheat buns, with Recipe #39478 & Recipe #66644.

These were very good.  We altered the recipe as we only wanted to make 2 burgers.  We used 1/8 tsp of the garlic pwr, salt and pepper.  As for the bbq sauce, I tried to use only a little bit - about 1/16 of a cup.  They turned out wonderful and we can't wait to make them again!

These were good and easy to make. I only had a pound of hamburger so cut the recipe. I made five burgers with the pound of meat. I used 1/8 cup of bbq sauce and 1/4 teaspoon of everything else. We all enjoyed these. They were really moist.
Beautiful cake but was not as sweet as my husband would've lliked it to be.
Very good cake, but I couldn't taste the lime flavor that much. Maybe increasing the zest or juice would help.

Really good and simple to make. I followed it exactly using Fritos and it was so yummy. 

Thanx

I`ve made this using maning of my prepared jams like these
Hot As Hell Habanero Zucchini Jelly Recipe #95424 &
Spicy Pepper Plum Jam Recipe #100538. Always a big hit!
Have been making these for years with crackers, but tried them with corn tortilla chips tonight.  YUM!  Thanks for the idea.

Just a great little simple appetizer anyone can do. I made this for the ZWTII and I will definetly make it again!
I just couldn't decide on Red or Green pepper Jelly!
Love this recipe . .  that's why I made the jelly.   I used crackers.  We had as appetizer last night.

I make this often for work as its easy to grab when we have a minute but to make it easier to transport and eat I mix the softened cream cheese with the jelly and blend on low with the hand mixer for a minute....fabulous and easy.
A must have around here for a quick snack ! 5 star snack !

I canned a ton of jars of Hot as Hell Habanero Zucchini Jelly (Recipe=95424) and served this as an appetizer.  Half like the Carr's water crackers and half liked the Fritos the best.  A truly simple, outstanding appetizer!
YUM! Its  a keeper! :)
This was a great salad.  I served with tuna steaks.  It looked beautiful and will be a nice company salad.
My huaband loved this salad, especially the dressing.

I will admit I didn't create the entire recipe as I didn't have the mushrooms but this will be made in its entirety at some point in the future.
I made the rosemary dressing with (as you guessed) more garlic and another teaspoon of red wine vinegar (I love vinegar). This was such a nice change from the usual dressing and I was able to use some of my fresh rosemary from the garden! Thanks for a great recipe.
This was a nice change of pace and looks so pretty.  I too used extra garlic but had to use dry rosemary as I didn't have the fresh.   It still worked out wonderfully.

very good!!! I would change the dressing a bit next time. Not as much olive oil and way more vinegar. I used balsamic. Other than that, this recipe is a keeper!! Great to go alongside any grilled meat.

I really enjoyed this salad.It looked very attractive and impressive. The only changeI made was to the dressing. I added some more vinegar and a little bit of sugar to it. Thanks Yooper for a great recipe.

Delicious, perfect salad with a really nice grilled flavor from the mushrooms and peppers. I was skeptical of the dressing until it was combined with all of the vegetables- soooooo delish. A definite keeper- thanks yooper!
Tasty!

Very flavorful sandwiches! I loved the bright flavor of the broiled tomatoes with the deeper flavor of the beef.  Next time, I think I will try cooking the beef differently, maybe doing it on the grill or not slicing it before cooking. Thanks for sharing!  Made for ZWT3

outstanding.  I used tender venison, and it was wonderful. The allspice really lifts it from a regular sandwich meat.

Also did use the sesame yogurt sauce, yumm

I made this in a large pot on top of the stove, I used chicken broth in place of water and did a few amount adjustments, we like spicy so I added in a heaping tablespoonful of crushed chili flakes, we really enjoyed this soup and I will make it again soon, this was made for kittencalskitchen forum tag game, thanks Dorit!

Delicious! My DH and I loved this recipe. I used poblano peppers and 1 green bell pepper and vegetable stock. I'm sorry I didn't get a photo, but the cream curdled a bit. I left it for a minute and look what happened! Even though it didn't look that great, it was still wonderful! Thank you Julie! Oh, and I didn't peel all the skin off, and it was fine.

The flavor of this is so yummy! I couldn't stop eating it! It did seem like a strange side dish, though, and I plan on adding chicken next time for a main dish. I added a bit of corn starch at the very end to thicken it even more. I'll definitely make it again! I served it with Recipe#127295 and Recipe#17126.

Yes, this is the best recipe out there for mac and cheese.  This is exactly exactly what I do but I beat 3 eggs into the milk and pour it over b/c I like a little bit of the custardy texture.  It's perfect, especially with the super-crusty top.  The best!

This was one of my recipes I choose for PAC and I'm so glad I did.  The taste was outstanding and so simple to make.  I halved the reciew for the 2 of us, and it still made a lot.  I also had to put aluminum foil over it at the 40 minute mark because the top was browning too quickly.  I didn't turn the oven up to the 400 degree mark, because it was done and crunchy on top at the 45 minute mark.  Excellent dish that I'll make again.  Thanks Chia

Delicious and so easy! My ds made this for dinner tonight using both the American and Cheddar and we all enjoyed it very much. Thanks for sharing this keeper which we will be having on a regular basis at our house!

This is definately easy to put together.  I cooked it at 375 degrees for 45 minutes and it was plenty crusty.  If I cooked it any longer it would have been to hard.  I think I might try making this again and reducing the temperature to 350 degrees.  I will also increase the cayenne next time around.  I did use the combination of processed and cheddar cheese.  The processed cheese helps to give the creamy texture to mac n cheese.

Sorry to give such a low rating, but I really didn't like it. I've never made homemade mac n' cheese and I've never had it baked at all, so I guess maybe I just didn't know what to expect. I remember my grandpa making mac n' cheese when I was a kid, and he always used Velveeta instead of American and I think a milder cheddar; it always came out richer and creamier and cheesier than this turned out for me and while I liked the spiciness of the cayenne (used a little over 1/4 tsp actually), I didn't care for the bite of the extra-sharp cheddar in this. Didn't care for the texture of the top layer either. To me, it was almost like uncooked pasta when it got all  hard and crunchy. Again, sorry, it was worth a try, just turned out it wasn't for us.

The three stars are for the lovely crust, but the flavor was bland. I'm learning that if I don't make a roux, the cheese disappears into the milk and is never heard from again! I even used an extra cup of cheese (I used all extra sharp white cheddar) and we could still barely taste it. I'm going to combine this cooking technique (but cut the time to an hour total since some parts were too crunchy) with a roux-based sauce--I hate to use the extra pot but it's worth it to not lose all that cheese and to have the creamy texture.

If you like mac and cheese that is creamy and moist you may not like this recipe. This is pure macaroni and cheese with just enough milk to hold it all together and with a nice crusty cheese top. If you prefer the creamy type of mac and cheese find a recipe that starts with a white sauce, there are plenty of them out there.

This is one of the best mac and cheese dishes that I have had.  I have been searching for so long for the homeade mac and cheese that I remember as a kid, but all the ones that start with a white sauce first don't taste right, so I figured I would give this a shot!  And I am so glad that I did!  Pure cheesy/pasta goodness!!  I may play around a bit with the cheeses, but not much -- great job!
This was really good! I cut the recipe in half. But still not like Great Grammy's recipe but close. Left out the cayenne pepper... it browned nicely on top but not on the bottom..

This dish is a national treasure all by it's self. Too delishious for words to describe it.
jmeyerc
Really greasy!  So much so, that we couldn't eat it.

I was looking for a recipe that had a crunchy crust with a creamy center. I cooked the macaroni 9 minutes until it was el dente. To ensure a creamy center I mixed the butter and 1 C. Milk with the macaroni mixture. Baking was 40 minutes. I did not increase the temperature. The leftovers was a little drier but still delicious.

We loved the crust on the top of this macaroni but my BF ( who is the mac n cheese lover in the house) found the inside to be very dry and bland.  I guess we like a creamier mac n cheese... We ended up eating the very top layer with our meal... which was very yummy!  Very easy to prepare but we will probably never make it again.  Thanks for posting!!!

Delicious, I made it for my husbands birthday party and everyone loved it.  Now whenever my parents come to visit my dad asks for it, it makes me happy to have found something that I can give him to make him happy!

Really good mac and cheese. I made it for my nieces and they loved it! I used nonfat milk and all sharp cheddar cheese, and the only things I would change for next time is not to bake it the last 20 min. and  to up the milk and cayenne. But I definitely loved it and will make it again.

This is a very easy and delicious family-pleasing casserole.  I followed the recipe exactly as written, but used a 15 oz drained can of corn, not 11 oz.  I garnished with some parsley.  Thanx for a great casserole.  I'll make this again.
A nice variation on a ham/potato casserole.  I didn't have corn, so used frozen peas(which I thawed out) and really liked the combination. This dish is now on my "comfort food" list.

Excellent dish!  And so easy.  I had some fresh asparagus tips so used it instead of the corn.  I  sauteed my onions with the asparagus tips before adding to the rest of the mixture.  Didn't add any salt either and it came out great.  I will definitely use this recipe again, and next time I'll try using Land o Lakes Fat Free Half & Half to lower the fat.  Thanks for a great recipe!!
Ar

Loved this soup, and could detect the deeper flavor from using bone-in chicken breasts.  If Step 3 had  been clearer about the type of pressure release to be used, I would have given 5 stars; normally, when additional cooking is needed, a quick release should be used (following the recommendation of the p.c. manufacturer). Great soup!  This worked very well in a Kuhn-Rikon 5-Liter pressure braiser. Made for Name That Ingredient tag game.
Great soup.  I will use heavy cream next time.  I like my chowders very creamy.  Thanks for<br/>sharing!

easy recipe to follow, and came together very quickly. I used olives I had brined myself, and they were lovely and crisp. Didn't have tarragon vinegar, and only half a cup of sour cream. AND I bought Salmon by mistake, still, it turned out brilliantly, and I enjoyed a serving last night with just a big slice of toasted turkish bread. was yum :)

I hate this recipe because it is so good I ate the whole thing! I simply could not pass up on the wonderful glazed skin , I even had trouble leaving the bones!  The hen was fall off the bones tender &  moist  The flavor was heaven;y. I cut the recipe in half doing only 1 hen for the two of us and it worked perfectly.  The only change I made was to cook the hen for 25 minutes without the glaze and then basted the hen with the glaze and continued baking for a further 25 minutes.   Chuck this is a winner Thanks for sharing

This is a wonderful! The sauce is simple yet amazing. Hard to beat that! A big hit in this house and a keeper. 
Thank you for sharing this recipe!

I was cooking 8 hens so you can imagine I had to increase the sauce.  I had two big trays full of hens lol....  I basted them a couple of times but I don't think it was necessary.  They looked wonderful and everyone thot they were great.  My son ate 3 halves.  thanks for posting this Chuck...
Lee

Occasionally one just has to try a new combination of ingredients. I hesitated on the chili powder but went with the recipe as printed. The flavor was fantastic. They were juicy, moist and so incredibly good. Made for an impressive meal.
Chuck....made these yesterday...awsome, really 10 stars!!!I didn't have honey so I used maple syrup....what a great taste....this is surely a keeper...thanks Chuck

I agree with all of the other reviews.   This is juicy and flavorful.   I fixed this for our Easter dinner and we all loved it.   I've got leftovers that I can't wait to dig into.   I'm thinking that next time I make it though I will inject the breasts with some of the wonderful sauce to get even more of it's flavor into the meat.

Made this tonight for dinner and it came out great. Me and my DH enjoyed it immensely. For orange juice, I used a real orange and then lined bottom of casserole dish with 4 orange slices.  Thanks will make again.

Oh my god this was soooo good! My boyfriend usually doesnt have a big appetite so I only made one hen for the two of us, and he was looking for seconds! I also added orange slices to the bottom of the pan as someone suggested, and it came out great!  The hardest part was cutting out the backbone and the little bones, but it was worth the time! Thanks for the recipe I will definately make this again!
I made this for Christmas dinner and it turned out fabulous.  It was easy to make, everyone loved and it made a nice presentation.  Thanks!

very good...i had to adjust for a family of 5.  i baked with skin side down for 15 min. vs. 6-8 and increased final baking time to 60 minutes; basted half-way through, again.  easy to prepare and family loved it.

Now, I have made many recipes from recipezaar.  This is the only one that has compelled me to write a review for!  I absolutely loved this dish.  My husband was so impressed.  I might have to make this once a week now.  A Very tasty meal!
Fantastic. Very interesting list of ingredients, that blended so well with each other. Served this with Savory Rice and 'so Simple' Cauliflower Mash Thanks Chuck!

We just made this as part of a Thanksgiving dinner for two. The hens were amazingly moist and delicious. We usually roast them whole, but this made a much tastier meal. The honey and orange worked very well with the chili powder -- we used ancho chilis and really loved the zip!
These were good but they seemed to be missing something. I'm an herb girl so next time I'll add some herbs to it.

An absolute winner!!  I love how easy it is to prepare. I used orange concentrate and prepared the hens in the am and cooked them for dinner later.  Served with green beans, corn and tomatoes  and wild rice, it made a terrific presentation as well as a great tasting meal.  Thanks for the post Chuck.
Yes, it's juicy!  I've been baking these hens for over 20 years and couldn't overcome the dryness of the white meat. Honey and chili go great together, and they look gorgeously brown.

Very good. A lot of messy work to cut the hens in half, but they looked great all browned and crispy on the outside. I baked them for 45 minutes and they were slightly dry, so next time I'd decrease the cooking time by 5 or 10 minutes or use a meat thermometer to be sure. The chili butter had nice subtle flavor... next time I'd add onion powder and some minced garlic for a little extra flavor. Thanks for a nice dinner!
Very simple, and makes a nice presentation. A little bland for my taste, but that can be easily remedied next time. Adding to my recipe box!
Nice glazed skin.  Just a wonderful recipe to make.

Very nice!  We had this for dinner tonight.  After baking the hens, I had a bit of glaze left over in the pan, which I boiled down a bit & slathered on each piece before serving.  My dh said he's not a huge fan of cornish hens, so I will make this again with chicken.  But I really enjoyed it.  Thank you very much for sharing.

Outstanding recipe!!! I add more to the basting sauce because I love chili powder. The taste is OUT OF THIS WORLD!!!!You've got to boil the sauce down after the hens are done and use it to eat with them!

Excellent. This was my first time making cornish hen and i am glad i chose this recipe. The only thing i did was add some peppers and onions while baking. This mixture was absolutely delicious and i will be using this often! Thanks so much for sharing

I gave this recipe to my sister yesterday and she called me back today to tell me how wonderful it was. She said she will be making this one over and over again. She also mentioned that she thought it would be just as good as chicken breasts w/bone. Big thumbs up with her husband who is a major picky eater. Thanks Chuck!

I use this recipe and my cornish hens were perfect. I made them for my parents and it was the first time that they had it and they really liked it.  I left out the chili powder and used rosemary and thyme instead
so yummy!
These were so good! The skin looked so great! It was nice and brown and so yummy and crispy! The meat was so juicy. We will have this again! Thanks!
Delicious!   I baked 3 hens in a 9x13 pan and found that it took the same amount of time.

I made this recipe for dinner tonight and it was delicious.  So quick, easy and inexpensive.  I used the juice from 1 large orange....about 7 tablespoons and placed orange slices underneath hens.  I will definitely add this recipe to my collection.  Thanks Chuck!

Great recipe. Best one I have found for Cornish Hens. They came out moist and tasty. This is  a keeper. Good combination of flavors. Thanks

Bruce
This was my first time making Cornish Hens and it was sooo good.  Very juicy and moist.  Had a hard time cutting the hens in half but definately worth the time.
what a shame I didn't make more !!  So juicy and very tasty
Very good, but a bit greasy.  Great flavor and easy to prepare. Next time I will cut down on the butter.

YUMMY!!!  Not only is it EASY...but fabulously TASTY!!! Someone else had mentioned that it lacked herbs or flavor...so I added 2 large cloves of minced garlic [per someone else's suggestion] to the mixture and it was scrumptious. I also put salt and pepper on the hens directly prior to baking.  Not at all greasy! Thank you!!

Oh, my...not that you needed another review, but this is FANTASTIC!!!! I haven't been a huge fan of cornish games, but this has maybe converted me....goes well with my mushroom barley risotto, which I hope to post within the next day or two... Thanks SO much, Chuck!!!
This is an awesome recipe.  My husband loved it!! and he is a picky eater.  He went on and on about how wonderful the game hen tasted.  Thank you!
Very good, juice and tender...next time I will marinate for extra flavor!

This was a delicious recipe for cornish hens. The only difficult thing was splitting the hens but other than that they were super easy to make. They turned out perfect for our Christmas dinner and my family loved them. Thanks!

I made this recipe for Thanksgiving. And again today, New Year's Day. Both times, I didn't have all of the ingredients at home, so I improvised. Both times I substituted maple syrup for the honey. The first time I used apple juice for orange. And this time grape juice. Both times the birds came out scruptious!!!
I baked 15 mins. skin down, 45 skin up. And I basted every 10 minutes. Thanks Chuck for a delish, easy recipe...De Jur, L.A.
We didn't care for the seasoning.

This is a great recipe! Very easy, but no one will ever know going by the taste and the presentation. I put 2 thin orange slices under each half of hen, and used about 2 tablespoons of the juice from the remaining orange. Both times I have fixed it, it has come out amazing. I'm not a fan of chili powder, so I was very surprised at how wonderful I thought this dish was.
Excellent, the only thing I changed. Was after I washed and dried the Cornish Hens I had season the hens. But other than that this is a very good recipe.

I thought this was really good.  It wasn't as difficult as I thought to cut then hens in half.  I didn't remove the back bone....just cooked it as is and there was no problem.  I really hate the taste of chili, so I didn't think I would like this, with the chili powder, but I made it exactly as is and it was great.  There was no chili taste at all.  The only thing I would do differently next time is to make double the sauce or (like someone else said), inject the meat with the sauce.  It's so good, but I don't eat the skin and that's where all the flavor was...on the outside of the skin.  Maybe if the skin got crispy, I would eat it, but it wasn't.  Extra sauce to spread inside the chicken would do the trick though!
very tasty! My husband and I like our poultry more salty, and this recipe is pretty sweet. but worth a try for me, and very good!!!
This was a good recipe, nice flavor and extremely easy.  It wasn't my favorite but it was tasty.  I will make again.  Thanks

Sorry, but I didn't care for the flavor of the sauce.  I could taste the chili powder and it just didn't taste right.  I was surprised that one of my kids ate it - other didn't, but she's very picky.  Chicken cooked up nice and was very juicy, but the taste wasn't for me....

Excellent recipe. This was my first time making cornish game hens and they came out perfectly. I added garlic and basil to basting sauce and used remaining to dip in...so yummy! I also cooked on orange slices as suggested. Will definetly make again!!!
We really tried to like these, but there was something missing. The hens DID come out juicy, though, but way too bland.

I would recommend adding 2-3 more teaspoons of chili powder to the liquid mixture. Also, the mixture did not leech very well beyond the skin, but for that, I can provide another solution or reccomendation. 
Oh, the drippings mixture makes an excellant dipping sauce for teared chicken pieces.
This was good. It was simple to make and flavorful. Thanks Chuck in Killbuck for sharing. Made for Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup tag.

This is a great recipe!!  So easy to do, I love it!  I had to sub in Emeril's Original Essence instead of chili powder.  It was very good, my wife even liked it and she doesn't like anything I make, lol!!  Thanks again for sharing!

Delicious! I made it for Xmas dinner. I did change it slightly....I sprinkled the salt and pepper directly onto the hens and marinated it in the butter/paprika/orange juice/ honey sauce for 12 hours. Then I basted it with extra sauce I made on the side, in which I added basil and Rosemary, every 10 minutes when baking. easy and delicious!
Quite enjoyed this recipe.  Haven't had Cornish game hens for a long time so this was a nice treat!  I would do this one again!!

Wow was easy and good...I get so tired of figuring out what to fix for dinner..my husband is extra picky..and he was most enthusiastic about this recipe. I wondered after I fixed it if sauce would also be good on chicken..as it is so easy and tasty.

The next morning after having the hens for dinner..he said he would eat leftovers for breakfast!
Couldn't believe I was hearing that from such a picky man!

The birds were very juicy and had a nice mild flavor.  The recipe deserves 5 stars.  This was my first experience with Cornish game hens and probably my last.  They tasted just like chicken. I guess I expected a slightly different flavor.  For the money, chicken is a better alternative.

WOW!  This was the first time I have EVER made cornish hens and they turned our fantastic.  This recipe is named appropriately, because they did turn out juicy.  I follow the "sauce" recipe and that turned out great.  I did add a few things.  I salt & peppered the hens on both sides and place sliced onion and garlic on top, as the skin side was placed down.  When I flipped them, i made sure the onion and garlic was underneath as they cooked. The "sauce" isn't over powering, which is why I like this reciped so much.  Thanks for posting this wonderful keeper!
My family loved this. I didn't have any orange juice though so I used lemon juice, worked great. Made extra sauce for dipping. Thank you for sharing
I can't believe that I have forgotten to rate this recipe!  I've made it three times now and love it every time. If you make it don't change a thing!

The sauce was great.  I took the other reviewers advice and doubled the sauce recipe.  We served this over rice with some of the sauce poured on top,  my family liked it a lot.  Next time I think I'll marinate the hens for a few hours because all the flavor was on the outside.

Per some other reviews, marinated all day, and also added garlic and some dried herbs.  Very easy and tasty.  Will try on the grill next time.  For those that commented on it being difficult to split the hens, use kitchen shears, super easy.  Have to giggle at those that don't like cornish hens but like chicken, the cornish hens you buy in the grocery store are just immature broiler chickens.
I used real butter instead of the recommended margarine, and added a little orange marmalade and cinnamon. Awesome!!

I had invited a longtime friend for dinner and decided to try this recipe for the first time...this has to be one of the best dinners I have ever made i was somewhat stunned as to how good the hens tasted...I tried cooking the hens for half hour skin down and turning them over, basting them and cooking for another half hour...fantastic...

This recipe is fantastic! My husband and daughter are both picky eaters, and I was worried they wouldn't like it, but both gobbled it down. Like some others, the only thing I changed was seasoning the hen with salt and pepper rather than putting it in the sauce. It's so easy and delicious, can't go wrong.
Tasty! Recipe was very easy! Quick  and very well liked by the hubby and the kids.
This recipe is amazing!!!!!

The problem with this recipe is that the Hens need to be brined before getting to the recipe. Hens are nothing but poulty and I always brine my poultry before cooking whether I am grilling, frying, roasting or baking. The brining really imparts the flavor all the way through the meat. Pat the Hens dry and then proceed with the recipe.

This has been my go-to reciepe for Cornish Hens for the last 3 years. The flavour is just amazing. You can make it exactly as is and it's easy and wonderful. I've made just a few tweeks after making it so may times. I throw in 2 cloves of garlic while I'm melting the butter, add an additional tbsp of orange juice, and then I marinate the hens in it before cooking (even just for a half hour). LOVE THIS RECIEPE!
How do I cut the hens in half? I'm going to cook this for Christmas and I've only cooked them whole
Delicious! Also works with skinless boneless chicken thighs. I also didn't have any oj on me so I substituted with bottled lemon juice and it turned out great.
Excellent!! Quick to prepare and easy to make. Will definitely do again.
I loved this, but did not have a orange, subbed a big jucy lemon instead, was just over the top!!!! The best game hen ever

I made this recipe for my boyfriend tonight and he agreed that this is the BEST cornish game hen ever!!! I doubled the sauce recipe and basted the chicken every ten minutes. In addition, I seasoned the chicken liberally (garlic powder, salt, pepper, and rosemary). I could eat this all day long. I've also never taken the time to write a food review...so that tells you just how gosh darn good this chicken is!!
Can't wait to make it again with chicken pieces! YUM!

Made this tonight -- AH-MAZING!! Did not change anything, but I did double the sauce because I cooked 3 cornish hens instead of two. Served with mashed sweet potatos and I sauteed string beans in olive oil with salt and pepper. LOVE! Thank you for this delicious recipe! Adding this to my main go to dinners.
Didn't modify the recipe and it was super yummy
I made this for dinner this evening and the sauce was very flavorful. I think however next time I will try cayenne pepper instead of black just to kick it up a notch.
The hens were delicious! Definitely a recipe to make again! Guests were saying, "Yum."

Wonderful recipe!!!!, This was my very first time ever having Cornish hens and my first time ever cooking something like this so I was nervous and really iffy about this, And my husband is very picky with chicken but he loved this!!!.
Delicious! First time my hubby REALLY liked the Cornish Game Hen I prepared.
I tweaked it see my tweak post. It was juicy and a sweet hot. Will do this again!
Quick and tasty way to prepare Cornish Game Hen. Went from intimidated by not knowing a thing about cooking them, to delighted. Perfect for a dinner for two!

GREAT Recipe...I Love it! I added fresh squeezed orange juice and little more honey and sprinkle of brown sugar to the baste. I removed almost all natura juices from baking dish before I started basting. I also used garlic salt and little season salt black pepper and no salt seasonings to my hens when i baked them on both sides before I basted them. I kept turning them too. They are DELICIOUS ??????
I thought the flavor was just ok. The hen looked amazing but the taste did not match. The hen was juicy, and tender. I like chilli, but not really in this recipe.
I made this last night, so very good. Next time will make more sauce and do more than two hens. Easy to make ahead also.

I am surprised to be the first review.  This was a snap to make. I bought a 15 pound turkey on sale last week.  I cooked it using my crockpot which made A LOT of turkey.  I really wanted a traditional dinner but without all the work.  This is also great for lunches.  The cheese adds a nice flavor also. Thanks for sharing.

This 1999 Taste of Home cookbook recipe is a great way to use up your leftover thanksgiving turkey...If you also have leftover gravy you can use it instead of the jarred gravy...Got leftover stuffing? Use that instead of making the stuffing in the recipe...Got leftover veggies? Use those instead of the frozen peas in the recipe...A versatile recipe indeed!

While this recipe was tasty, it probably go into regular rotation at our house. The oregano was too much for my personal taste and the end result was quite dry so I would probably try to boost up the liquid content. That said, the fact that this is a healthy, fibre filled recipe is a huge plus. I added some sundried tomato and kalamata olive veggie sausages. Made for the French leg of ZWT5

Extremely delicious and easy both.   My electric skillet must run hot.   The onions started to brown and double tomato sauce turned into a paste that coated everything.   However, the flavor was excellent, and I'd intentionally do it the same way again.   It was really delightful biting into little bursts of fresh green pepper.   I didn't miss sausage at all.
Very good (although I did miss the sausage). Based on another review, I used lots of creole seasoning instead of the oregano and thyme. Great weeknight meal!

A nice combination and very easy to make! We enjoyed this rice and bean combination with some salmon. It seemed to be lacking in a little something flavor-wise, so I will play around with seasonings next time. Thank you! Made for Susie's World Tour 2018 - Cajun/Creole.
Excellent flavor.  I added a few drops of sesame oil in the frying stages and it gave the sauce a nice perfume.

This wasn't really my taste - I think the combination of flavors was a little "much" for me.  But my husband really liked it, and I'm sure that I'll make it again for him.  I may leave the raisins out next time, as I think it was the combo of sweet & salty that didn't work for me.

I remember the first time I tried this recipe years ago ... I thought, "Now that's the way chicken is supposed to taste!" But I lost the recipe and was ever so delighted to locate it here! I made it again by special request of my DS and the "romance" with the flavors began all over again! 
UPDATE: I made it again tonight, even though I was in a time crunch. I just dredged the chicken with the flour and oregano, then dumped everything in the crock pot. When the whirlwind stopped, dinner was ready! Served over plain cous-cous. Yummy with a capital YUM!

This was quick and lovely !!  Had a BIG bag of chicken breasts -- all at least 8 ounces - far too much for the 2 of us. so cut them in half, and proceeded as directed -- still have enough for another meal.  Lemons, capers, and feta make a delicious sauce, served with left-over saffron rice and fresh broccoli. (Spinach is still on the NO-NO list).  Thanks, Derf, for another "Keeper"!

Great sloppy joe type sandwich with a taste of chili..very easy to prepare.  I toasted buns under the broiler, and then added the meat, topped with Colby/Jack cheese and put back under broiler until cheese melted.  Thanks Geema for this really good recipe.

I tried it and it is GREAT!  It's like having sloppy joe's with a kick.  I'll never go back to plain old SJ's again.  They will just taste to blah!

Thanx for sharing!!

This was very good, although a little too tomatoey for my taste, I think the next time I make it I will only use half of the tomatoes. The seasonings were perfect. I served ours on toasted buns with finely minced onions. Quite tasty!

While I haven't been having too much success with my kids and spicy Mexican cuisine, this sloppy joe recipe was very well-received.  I probably did make it a VERY scant tablepsoon of chili.  Everything blended together nicely and we all liked the addition of cheese and lettuce.

My DD calls these "tacos on a bun" - they were very tasty & a quick and easy meal.  I used ground turkey with great success.  Next time I will use canned crushed tomatoes or smaller diced?  We didn't like the tomato chunks in the meat so much.  Thanks for the post.  ZWT 3

I haven't had Sloppy Joe's in years, and these really hit the spot - a great variation on the classic recipe.  I felt that these would have worked better with crushed tomatoes though - I simmered them for a bit longer (at least 15 minutes) so that the tomatoes would cook in.  Thanks Geema!

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #50*  I also only used 1 cup of Craisins, which was plenty-- any more would have been too sweet.  Made the rest as directed.  Very nice salad, served with salmon burgers.  Nice crisp sensation !  Thanks for posting, Kathy.
The best one yet!!!

I scaled this back for 4 serves (which was plenty for 3 of us as our only side and still a little left over).  I only used 2 teaspoons of oil in the cooked couscous and that was plenty to separate it and then stir int he rest of the ingredients as per recipe, though I did use parsley instead of coriander/cilantro as we don't really care for the taste of it and the lemon added a really refreshing taste.  Thank you Kiwi Kathy, made for Aussie/Kiwi Recipe Swap #66 July 2012.
Very tasty recipe. I used half the amount for cranberries and pine nuts. Great side dish for barbecue.

Oh-h-h so good! The smell while they were baking was so tempting! I used Splenda brown sugar blend and Sunmaid's Tropical dried fruit mix (which I soaked in hot water for 10 minutes). The wholewheat flour gives it a good texture, and the orange zest really adds to the flavor. Can't wait for the coffee to finish brewing.
Thanks for another winner Kittencal - Carole in Orlando

Kit - you have got another winning muffin recipe here!!  Loved loved loved them!!  Made as is, except I added my frozen cranberries without thawing them...  rolled them in a bit of flour (so they wouldn't sink to the bottom) and added them to the mix.  Also used low-fat milk.  Can't wait to make them again!  thanks Kit!

These are delicious!  However, I got 20 muffins instead of 12, and next time I will reduce my oven temp to 375Â°F because these got done in 18 minutes and the bottoms were already a bit too dark.  I still have lots of cranberries left so I will probably be making these again within the next couple weeks!

Five stars -- all the way!!!  You must have a direct line to the "recipe Gods"!!!  These muffins sounded good -- and I needed muffins for the weekend - so decided to give these a try.  Oh my -- fabulous.  I did use the Splenda as suggested (hubby is diabetic) -- and it worked beautifuly.  For those who need to use the sugar substitute, it's always good to know that it works well in a recipe.  I really wanted to do the cranberries -- but I didn't have any -- but had a couple packages of blueberrie in the freezer that I needed to use. I don't know how the cranberries could be any better -- but I'm so looking forward to trying them.  The orange zest is, in my opinion what takes these muffins over the top.  I'm sure the orang juice helps.  And it's great to know that we're using the whole wheat flour!!!  I got 14 muffins out of the batch.  And I'm freezing all but two of them -- so I have them to take to my son's house over the weekend.  Thanks, Kitten -- a total blast again!!!

Delicious muffins!  I made them with blueberries since I had some to use up.  Although I cut the sugar in half, I still found them quite sweet, possibly because of the blueberries.  I will make them next time with cranberries and I still find them very sweet, will cut back on the sugar a bit more.  Otherwise, they are just wonderful.  I baked them in memory of CoolMonday.
These were really good and pretty simple to make! :D Thanks!
My DD Tinkerbell_16 made these for me and they were very good. I love the crispiness on the outside and moist in the inside. Great recipe!

Awesome muffins. I love the combination of flour and whole wheat. I used only 1 tsp of vanilla, a misread on my part and they turned out very nicely. I used fresh cranberries. This is not an overly sweet muffin but a very excellent breakfast muffin. Mine baked up in 20 minutes. I got exactly 12 very nice shaped muffins. Thanks Kitten for a recipe that will get alot of mileage at our home!
These were pretty good and easy to make. mine did make 18 muffins though. I didn't have cranberries, so I used blueberries. I didn't think these were too sweet at all.
These are so good!  Next time I may sprinkle some granulated sugar on them before baking to make them even prettier.  This recipe is a keeper and I will definately make again.  Thank you for sharing.

Very yum.  I used veg oil instead of butter (just being lazy), also added 1 1/2 cups frozen cranberries, which I didn't defrost.  For me, 20 was more than enough (18 was likely best) and I got 12 regular and 12 mini muffins from the batter.  Will make again for sure, as they were tender and moist, but may sprinkle with brown sugar next time.  Thanks

These were moist and delicious. I subbed dried cranberries that I soaked in the oj for 30 minutes. They came out perfect, healthy and and not too sweet. My sons who usually don't like anything whole wheat really enjoyed them. Thanks Kitten!
I look forward to Thanksgiving every year because that means I can get all the ingredients to make these muffins! They are DELISH! Thank you so much for sharing them!

Super!!!  Easy to make.   The only thing I did different is I pre-heated the oven to 400, then turned down to 375 because with a dark baking tin, muffins tend to burn.  I baked for 23 minutes and they were perfect!  I also cut the cranberries in half to spread them more evenly throughout the muffins.  What a great combination of sweet and tart...great with coffee!  Thanks Kitten for a wonderful recipe!

I love these, reduced the brown sugar by 1/4 cup, used whole wheat flour once and now use all white flour.  Forgot to put the OJ in one time and they were fine without it.  I'm keeping a bag of frozen cranberries to make more.  I do spray my paper liners because they tend to stick.  Now I did depart from Kittencal's recipe because I decided I wanted a streusel topping and found a nice oatmeal one as follows:  1-1/4 cups old fashioned oats, 1 tablespoon white whole wheat flour (use any), 1/3 cup brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, 4 tablespoons cold butter, cut into chunks; 1 tablespoon honey - worked with my fingers but will try softened butter and a fork, then work in the oatmeal and honey.  I saved out 2 cranberry halves to put in with the streusel on top, cut side up is prettier.  Next time I am going to end with sprinkling with a little sparkley baker's sugar.  Am also going to try some cut up candied orange peel I made, lots of little variations you can do.

Looks like this is the Lays chips recipe from their Tangy Carolina BBQ flavor. Original calls for everything you listed, except 1/3 c spicy brown mustard, and it's only cooked on high for 3-4 minutes, or until the sauce is reduced by 1/3 - stirring occasionally. Salt and pepper to taste at the end. Very yummy recipe, to me, it is very tangy and a little taste of spice.
I'm from Maryland and have been to a few pig roasts in Raleigh, NC.  I fell in love with the Carolina BBQ tangy sauce.  This is just what I was looking for and it was sooo easy to whip up.

This is the best pulled pork BBQ sauce I've ever tasted - I had to cut the cider vinegar in half because it really takes your breath.  Made BBQ for a family event and everyone went nuts over this sauce.

Delicious! I thought it would be too sweet when I first looked at the recipe, but it was just right. The only thing I did differently was to brown the chicken in a frying pan first, instead of in the oven. My kids really liked it. Thanks!
Good! I wasn't sure how it would turn out, but I was pleasantly surprised.  Very interesting taste.
We really liked these served with rice and some dipping sauces. We used a honey mustard sauce, a sweet and sour sauce and a chili garlic sauce. Thanks for posting !
YUM!!! So delicious! I baked them for about an hour to make them extra crunchy! The tofu inside had an awesome consistency and flavor

These were really tasty! I thought the thyme was a little overpowering, so next time I'll cut down a little, but otherwise they were delicious. I didn't freeze them beforehand either, and I think I will try that also. I had to use Multi-Grain cheerios instead of cornflakes b/c that was what I had on hand. Much better than store-bought chik'n nuggets.

No stars just yet. I want to try it one more time to give it a fair shot! Per other reviews, I cut down on thyme, but it was still waaaay too much for me. Will experiment with seasonings and report back!
Yum!!  Eating a giant plate of these right now!  A bit heavy on the thyme for me, too, but still totally awesome!  I love that you get a big crunch from the oven without frying.
Awesome!  Definitely worth the extra time! A+++

These are really outstanding! My only suggestion would be to soak the cut potatos in cold water for at least an hour, even overnight works. This takes out the excess starch and makes them very crispy! Thanks for posting Belgophile.
Add us to the list of satisfied eaters.  Great sauce.

This was excellent as a light dinner dish on a hot summers evening. I used basil in the herbed sauce and added a little seasoned rice vinegar as well as the wine vinegar; the sauce smelt 'powerful' but was delicious on the potatoes. I also added mushrooms to the kebabs and plan to try marinating longer next time. A big hit with the family and definetly destined to become an alltime favourite.
The seasoning blend was perfect for the chicken, very simple but still very tasty.  Thanks

We really liked this! Very easy! I marinated the chicken for a several hours in the fridge (I did end up adding more olive oil to coat everything.) I even cooked the kabobs on my George Foreman grill! I cooked them for 3-4min. I used rice wine vinegar since that was all I had, and I didn't have any fresh herbs, so I used dried ones (about a teaspoon for every "sprig") and it was still delicious. I bet it'd be even better with fresh ones! I served red grapes along side everything. Fabulous, simple summer dinner! We're having it again tonight.

This is a foolproof recipe for an easy and great tasting salad. It doesn't always have to be complicated to be delicious. Serve it with cheesy breadsticks for satisfying meal. Thank you Carolinafan for posting this recipe!
Denmark Neighbors loved it.

I served these little beauties as part of a seafood appy party we hosted to watch the *Eurovision Song Contest* & Icelandic election results Sat nite. Smoked salmon & brie are much-favored here & this combo was a big hit. I used my recipe for recipe #225428 for the mustard component & spooned it generously. Thx for sharing this recipe w/us & our guests. :-)

These were such a snap to put together.  I used a multigrain baguette and added some capers.  I took Twissis advice and served it with her Gravlaxsosa sauce.  Leftovers were served for breakfast with a poched egg on top with some of the sauce.  Excellent combination!

Great recipe! I loved it, stored readily for my lunch the next day at work! I did add some homemade spaghetti sauce over the top just to give it a little extra kick! But I will definitely make this again!!

These are AMAZING rolls! Not yeasty or gummy, these are lovely white rolls with body.  I made the recipe exactly as stated with no problems.  The rolls stayed fresh in a sealed container for 4 days (no more left after that!).  Absolutely fantastic!!!

This recipe makes outstanding rolls. Just remind me next time not to double the recipe. It wasn't a lot of trouble, but it is a lot of dough. I had to halve the double batch to knead it. Oh, and this does go through the horrible sticky mess stage before you get all the flour kneaded in and achieve bread dough. Even the kneaded dough was a bit sticky, but I didn't want to get it too stiff. On the other hand, the rolls rose amazingly in the oven and are light and delicious. Will definitely use this recipe again. Thank you very much for posting it.

These were great! I was in a hurry so I halved the recipe and made the dough in my food processor. I mixed 1/2 cup water with the corn meal, sugar, salt, and oil in a glass measure and microwaved it for 2 1/2 - 3 minutes, then added a few ice cubes to cool it to 110. I added the egg to this slurry and poured it into the running machine, which had the flour and INSTANT yeast in it. The processor made quick work of mixing and kneading, after adjusting the liquid to flour to make a very soft dough. It rose beautifully and baked up light and slightly sweet. Delicious with our chili tonight. Thanks for posting this!

Excellent chicken recipe that truly did have everybody hunched over the table.  I thought I had made enough for leftovers the next day, 12 legs for three of us, but they were all gone.  I followed the recipe exactly.  I did marinate the legs in a large plastic bag because this allowed me to reserve about 1/4 cup of marinade to baste the chicken while it was cooking.  The family has declared this one a keeper!

My dh was very  happy tonight, he loved your wings and kept talking about how wonderful they tasted. He even bragged to the neighbors. They were tender and flavourful and we didn't stop eating until they were all gone. Thanks so much for sharing this lovely meal.

I've made these several times and they are wonderful. Currently my favorite lemon bar. They are lemony not eggy. I never would have thought of the macadamia nuts but they go very well with the lemon and give it a nice texture. The crust is yummy too, shortbread like.
