Very very good casserole. No cream of whatever soup, which is great. This had a nice texture and not all mushy. My roux worked perfectly, not too dark. I didn't use portabella, but regular button mushrooms instead. The portabella would have been much better. I also added some minced garlic with the mushrooms. I also used crushed Ritz crackers in place of the bread crumbs. Overall very good recipe. Made and Reviewed for New Kid on The Block tag - Thanks! :)

I have made this twice now.  Both times for Thanksgiving.  The second time I was making it I wondered why I was doing this again, since it is quite time consuming.  When I tasted it I knew it was worth the extra time.  So much better than the traditional green bean casserole using canned beans and soup.  I did make several changes. I added 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper to the vegetables.  Used panko bread crumbs, but reduced amount to 1 cup.  I also added some shredded parmesan to the bread crumbs for topping.  My family has asked that this be added to our Thanksgiving menu.  Not great for leftovers, I did not think it reheated well.  I do think it is worth the extra effort.  Very tasty dish.

This was a good basic recipe. I made this for my sons band and they enjoyed it but thought I could have used more meat. Next time I would add 1/2 pound sausage and 1/2 pound of ground beef. I did omit the mushrooms as I wasn't sure if they all liked them or not. I also added a lot more cheese then called for. I didnt measure, I just dumped as we love cheese. I thought it could use more seasoning also but the kids didn't say anything about that. Made for Fall PAC 2008.

This was so easy, and turned out so well!  Even my picky eaters loved it...and wanted seconds, too. (they are die-hard fried chicken fanatics, so this is a REAL plus!) The thighs I had were a bit larger than usual, so I had to add another 15 minutes to the bake time.  I had some fresh mushrooms that I needed to use, so while the chicken was baking, I sliced and sauteed the mushrooms with a little butter and garlic, then added the mushroom soup mixture to the frying pan and simmered it until it was reduced to a gravy consistency.  This definitely got a "thumbs-up" and "make it again" from my guys.
Short ribs are not my favourite meat but these turned out very tender and tasty.  This is a very simple recipe to make and the browning of the ribs certainly is necessary.
Delicious and a perfect meal at the end of a long day - just ready and waiting for the noodles to cook! I think browning these under the broiler really added a lot to this dish. Thanks for sharing!

Comfort  Food 4 sure! I only cooked the ribs on low for 6 hours and they were perfect -   I kept them on warm for a whole hour in the crock Pot.  I love the simple easy sauce and will use this on a  fried chop. Thanks Hey Jude for a really good, easy recipe

Hi Judy !  What a great way to prepare short ribs!  The house smelled wonderful as these cooked and we could hardly wait for it to be finished.  Easy to make and your instruction were easy to follow.  Thank you for sharing.   :-)

Had never made short ribs before and picked this dish for our debut. The ribs were tender and saucey but not overpoweringly sweet and we low carbed by using cabbage instead of the noodles, cooked separately. We had about 4.25 lbs and it was barely enough for three hearty eaters, so be warned these go fast! Thanks for a keeper!

This was very rich and flavouful indeed. Unfortunatly the ribs that came with the side of beef we ordered were very fatty. Even though I cut most of the fat off, it was pretty greasy. I refrigerated the leftover sauce so I could enjoy the yummy flavor over the noodles the next day (minus the fat). If I can't find better ribs for next time I will try this with stew beef instead.  Thank you.

Best ribs we've ever tasted! Simple and easy to prepare. No special ingredients to buy. They turned out tender and full of flavour. Sauce was absolutely delicious served over rice! Thank you for sharing this uncomplicated recipe.

Well, this dish got raves from the 3 guys I served it to! I don't eat meat but had to taste the sauce and it was yummy!I served this over buttered noodles with salt and pepper and a little parmesan cheese. Thanks for a delicious dinner I will make again! This goes into the keeper file!

Thesen were so good and we just LOVED the sauce. I made extra since it was so tangy and delicious. I am always very hesitant to use vinegar in anything but this made the meal! This is a definte keeper. Thank you, Jude! :-)

Man oh man was this good!  I added one clove of garlic with the onion and two shakes of cayenne pepper to the sauce.  This is the only way I plan to make short ribs from now on.  It only took 6.5 hours on low to cook.  I might try doubling the sauce next time, requested from my boyfriend.  I served this with rice.  Delicious!  Thanks Jude.

Very yummy.  Don't skip the broiling step!!  We ended up with almost a cup of fat in the broiler pan; I can't imagine what all the fat would have done to the sauce in the crockpot.  I made this meal low-carb by using sugar-free ketchup and splenda brown sugar blend, and I served it with low-carb pasta and green beans.  My husband loved it and told me the recipe was a definite keeper.

My husband really loved this.  I however did not like it at all.  I would have given it a much lower rating but he gave it 5 stars.  I didn't find the sauce had any depth of flavour...it was just sweet and vinegary, but didn't taste that special to me.  I think it's probably just my taste though.  Thanks, it was still nice to try something new.

Yummmmmmm......with a capital Y!  Both my husband and I loved it!  I didn't have quite enough ketchup for the sauce so I substituted chili sauce for the remaining amount.  It added a delightful bit of sweetness, though I'm sure the original sauce was quite tasty.  The meat literally fell off the bones and the sauce was heavy enough to coat the egg noodles really well.  Great as leftovers for lunch the next day!
I was pretty underwhelmed.  Nothing very wrong with it, but lacked any excitement.  Needs something to give it kick.
The family loved this! The recipe tasted like it had an Asian flair, kind of a sweet/sour thing,  so I decided to serve it over rice instead of noodles. Yummy!
These are yummy and easy to make. They are so good this time of year with the fresh vegetables available. I will make again! Thanks for sharing.

This is a different corn recipe.  When i went to make it I found out my cream cheese had gone bad so I subbed margarine for it.  I hope to try it again soon with the cream cheese as I know it would change the taste.  It has a spicy flavor made this way.  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.
Yummy corn. I love street corn and this was a really easy variation. It wasn't the prettiest corn....lol....but really good. Thanks Sofie for sharing. Made for Culinary Quest 2.
easy yummy served with http://www.food.com/recipe/easy-chili-size-178011/review?lrc=true good lunch cherry bombers

I served it over rice and alongside some buttered broccoli.  Great easy dinner!

I made this tonight. I served it atop a pile of delicious whipped potatoes, and it was quite delicious. A very nice meal.... I omitted nothing, but the optional mushrooms, as I had none. Clear five stars for an easy to prepare, tasty gluten free bread with very nice texture. I didn't look properly at the directions, so I used 1 whole egg accidentally instead of 2 egg whites, but that didn't seem to matter - maybe because I used rice milk which is more watery than moo-milk. The bread doesn't dry out, slices and freezes well and works with different kinds of gluten free flour mixes (I've already tried two). This will definitely be a keeper! Thanks so much for posting!
This was bread has an outstanding texture.  It isn't heavy, slices and freezes well.  I used a whole egg in place of the egg whites without a problem.  I got 14 to 15 slices.

I reduce the oil to 1/4 cup and increase the baking temp to 400 degrees Fahrenheit (for the same amount of time).  This gives me a crisper crust, and an inside that is less mushy.  I also finally found a smaller than standard loaf pan here in the states (a regular 9x5 is way too big), and then I slice and freeze whatever I'm not using that day.  It defrosts in the microwave well if I'm in a hurry.  My recipe now has lots of modifications but I give this 4 stars because it was a great base for me to get started with!  (Note, I have found that what kind of gluten free flour you use makes a huge difference in the moisture content and texture, so my changes might not work at all well for you, but if you try this with your flours and you need to reduce the moisture content, maybe this will help.)

This bread truly is excellent! It has a very nice texture, somewhat moist, but still sliceable and firm enough to hold toppings. A wonderful breakfast bread.
I made half the recipe baking the dough in two oven-proof round ramekins, which turned out nicely and reduced the baking time to 40 minutes.
Since I didnt want to throw away the yolk, I used the whole egg, reducing the oil accordingly. That worked out well. Next time I might use applesauce in place of the oil just to see how it goes. Also I think I will reduce the sugar as it was a tad too sweet for me.
THANK YOU SO MUCH for sharing this lovely recipe with us, Kate! Its a keeper for sure.

The only thing I would change, is to put the sesame seeds IN the batter instead of on top.  I will be making this again!

Awesome recipe for Gluten Free Buckwheat Bread. I baked my first gluten free bread and turned out very well done and delicious. I have used the recipe posted by katew as it posted. Thank you for the recipe.

Very easy to make. I went ahead and completely removed the orange sections from the membranes, which was tedious, but when I added them in at the end, they broke up into nice little orange chunks. I also used Grand Marnier, and it turned out absolutely fantastic! The sauce is sweet, but not overpowering, and the flavors of the oranges and the cranberries fit together perfectly!

One of the nice things about have a lot of bags of frozen cranberries year round is that I can make recipes like this anytime I like! Made this one as given, although I did add the Grand Marnier earlier so that the alcohol would cook off, leaving just the great flavor behind! Absolutely wonderful sauce, & a recipe that's a keeper, for sure! Thanks for sharing it!  [Made & reviewed for one of my adopted chefs in this Spring's Pick A Chef event]

Very good, not overly sweet. I did substitute 1 cup agave syrup for the sugar (i was out of sugar!). I also used fresh grated beets. It did need frosting and was more a "grownup" cake in that is was rich but not so sweet.

I am so glad to be the first reviewer for this yummy recipe - AND Susan's first review EVER! I didn't have any evap milk on hand so I used half & half, still came out great! Easy to make and this is definitely a regular dessert now at our house.  I served this with Lee Lee's Famous Chocolate Sauce(recipe #19678)and the combo was unbelievable!  Great recipe, Susan.  Welcome to 'Zaar!

i used half & half rather than whole milk and it's really quite tasty.  if you eat it right away, it pretty much tastes like chocolate soft-serve.  not sure how it will be after it freezes/hardens.  definitely easy enough to make though!

This is exactly the recipe I use, except I like a lot more sauce, so I use 2 lbs of grape jelly and 2 16oz bottles of chili sauce for this amount of meat. You can also substitute 2 large shallots for the onion if you want a subtler flavor.

I made these last night with steack and grilled zucchini...Yum! I made a few changes, I used bacon instead of pepperoni and added thin sliced green onions and finely chopped red pepper...thanks for the great recipe !

Great recipe. I changed it a little :) I used vegetarian keilbasa, no milk, vegetable broth instead, no eggs and kept the entire process in one very large cast iron skillet. Additional ingredients were 3 diced cloves of garlic, turmeric, and cumin giving it a little more diverse bent. Thank you Pellerin for making my rainy Sunday fun!
Made this for PAC Fall 2007.  This was very good and made a wonderful side dish.  I think next time I will try it with a pepper cheese.  Thanks Lainey for a great spinach dish.

Nice and cheesey!   I cooked it on low for the 4 hours.  It stayed moist and creamy.  Since I have to have onions in everything, I added some chopped onions, but otherwise made this as written.  I'll make this again.  Thanx for sharing.
Absolutely delightful, and very easy! Perfect side-dish for sausages, and I'm going to try the leftovers as a filling for a vegetarian lasagne. Thank you!
This was so hearty and delish. I made it for Thanksgiving and have been craving ever since. Will be making it again. I used reduced fat cheddar instead of American cheese.
Love this recipe. I used white cheddar?.make sure the spinach is well drained.  Delicious!

Tasted great, just like what you would think, but it looked weird. My cubed cheese stayed as big globs of orange. I think some of my guests were suspect when they looked at it. Not sure why the picture here looks so wonderful and mine looked so bad. I followed the recipe exactly and cooked it for 4.5 hours on low in my crock pot. Not sure I would make it again for guests, and it's a bit overkill to make as a sidedish for myself. I do look forward to eating the leftovers tomorrow.
This is a good creamy drink.  Not too strong.  Maybe I'll add a little bit or regular rum next time to make it less sweet.  Thanks Mommy Diva :)  Made for Beverage Tag.

Here's another one of those recipes where I was able to substitute lemon pepper for the usual S&P! Made for an enjoyable mid-day meal along with a smoothie & several slices of toasted whole-grain bread! [Made & reviewed in New Kids on the Block tag]

This was very easy to make. I made the rice in my rice maker while I made the dressing part and then just combined it all together! This was a wonderful side for grilled chicken and reheated wonderfully! Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag! :)

Great side salad for grilled chicken. Loved all the fresh dill and red onion. Made as written using brown rice that I cooked last night and then just re-warmed it in the microwave this evening for this recipe. Thanks so much for the post.

This was an excellent side dish with our grilled lemon chicken. Lovely flavor. I did have to substitute dried dill (about 2 teaspoons) because I couldn't find fresh dill anywhere. Made for Every Day is a Holiday tag.

This was yummy! I used basmati rice and cooked it in chicken broth to give it more flavor and it came out really good. It is a little tart, so if you like things sweeter, I would add maybe a pinch of sugar or honey. I will make this again- thanks!

This is delicious! I had to substitute dried dill for the fresh and used a tad bit less of it, but other than that followed the recipe as written. We love it as is, I wouldn't change a thing and won't in the future. Thanks for sharing the recipe Lori Mama! Made for Pick-A-Chef Fall 2011.
Easy to make, has a wonderful consistency and tastes so much better than anything available commercially!
Very easy to make and even easier to eat!! :) I used the vanilla because it was for a teen party but I can't wait to try it with the orange liqueur. I bet that would be fantastic.

I used banana peppers to make these.,.  My daughter helped me make the batch and we had so much fun doing it.  They go together rather quickly and when we dug into the first jar we were thrilled with the results.  They are awesome!  I had some with my tuna sandwich the other night on the side and it tasted so good together!
Great marinade!  I used this over green salad with the  Kozmic Blues Honey Lime dressing #65294.  Also added some carmelized onions, corn and carrots - great - thank you!

I love cheesecake, and I was definately NOT disappointed with this one.  It is fantastic.  I didn't have any mango, so I made 1/2 cup strawberry puree and swirled that in the plain cheesecake mixture.  It was not only tasty, but very pretty to boot!!!  Thanks for the great recipe.
wonderful and easy to fix  even my picky eaters liked it

We all loved this recipe! I stirred all the pasta into the sauce, chopped it up some, and added 8 oz cream cheese to it. Awesome!
Yuck. This is for kid's with ruined taste buds. The deal breaker is the 2 cups of ricotta. We threw it in the compost immediately. Wasteful and expensive. If you like pablum tho, this maybe for you!

wow Sylvie, this is a wonderful way to serve fish, soo delicious and easy. I made this tonight and my husband said it was great.   I/m not a great cook so when he says he likes something....especially if it is easy to make, I am happy.

After I uncovered it, I gave it a stir and did add to the baking time (uncovered) to thicken it up a bit. Thanks for sharing this simple, tasty recipe!

This was so easy to put together!  What a huge help on for a busy day!  It was too cheesy for us, so next time I will only put the mozzarella on top- and none mixed in.  I will also add more seasonings and maybe some mushrooms.  Since there are only 2 of us, I split the dish into 2 casseroles. It turned out that one casserole is enough for 3 meals for us! Thanks for sharing this easy recipe!

Sylvie,This is a very tasty fish recipe,I of course used large crappie filets.But it worked really well.I did bake them in the oven though, because my hubby wasn't here to help me with the grill, and I am not good at the grill,but I can't see where that could have made any difference in the taste,they were very good.I had fried potatoes and made a salad and had garlic bread.This made a very satisfying dinner.Thanks for this recipe,Darlene

This is a great way to make a horse cake. I made this for my granddaughters birthday. I used a marshmallow, cut in half, for the eye with a brown M&M stuck to it with frosting. This was a very pretty iced tea. The raspberry flavoring is very subtle and tart. I added some sugar and garnished with orange slices. Thanks for sharing.
Just wonderful!! Absolutely an A+ recipe, very simple and easy to make. A definite crowd pleaser! Thanks for the great recipe!!
i love these but i used crushed graham crackers for the crust(with melted butter).

Worked great for us!  We made them round with a biscuit cutter and dusted them with cinnamon sugar.  Delicious!!!!
Very good and easy recipe for leftover stuffing! In fact it's so good, it's worth making a stuffing especially for it. I added garlic powder and thyme to the chops.

New favorite! I served this tonight for the first time. My husband informed me that out of all the Catfish recipes I've made from RecipeZaar...this is the best one! However, instead of topping these with peanut butter cups (in my opinion a really bad choice) I crushed up some homemade peanut butter brittle & sprinkled that over the top ~ RAVES from the neighbors & from my house, too! [Tagged, made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in the current Pick-A-Chef]

We enjoyed this. It did taste like a Chinese or Japanese curry, the sauce was very thick. We subbed tofu for the meat, used less salt and skipped the butter and sugar. The mushrooms were the best part!
This was soooooo yummy!!! thank you for sharing the reciepe, made it for my husbands b-day, and everyone loved it. have a great day!
First time I ever tried to bake a Milk Tart. What a success. Tastes great. Just have patience when making the custard. This recipe rates a 5
Very good. Next time, think I will add some heat to the black bean dip and a layer of chopped olives. Made for Easy Does It! event in Cooking Photos.
VERY tasty and everyone in my family loved it!  I marinated for 8 hours and it was a bit salty, I might cut down marinating time next time I make it--but it will be made again!
These are awesome! Very easy to put together and taste incredible. I got 18 good sized muffins. Combined with the glaze they are a lovely moist treat! I highly recommend this recipe.

These muffins are delicious! I was sceptical about adding the whole 3 1/2 tsp ginger, and they almost tasted too gingery when they were still warm, but now that they've cooled off the flavor is perfect. I wouldn't change a thing. I also got 18 huge muffins, which is great because I know they're going to disappear quickly! Thanks for a keeper, Bev!

Oh my, these were wonderful.  The lemon glaze turned a simply good muffin into something really special.  The kids and I ate the muffins as were made, but I doubled the recipe and added 1 cup of seedless raisins to the second batch for dh, who loved them.  Thanks for a new 'keeper' recipe, with the snow starting to fly in Alberta this week, these really filled the need for a comfort food dessert.
These are very good.  Lemon ginger is one of my favorite combninations.  Perfect for breakfast or snack.

Delicious, tender muffins that are very mild spice-wise.  I got 24 regular sized muffins.  I liked them better before putting the lemon glaze on them!  Oh well.  The glaze made a bit too much, so I have leftovers of it in the fridge.   These are tasty muffins that make the house smell yummy, too!
Fantastic!!!!! MMMMMMM!!!!! I made mine in the paper cups, cuz I had to transport them, but I'm sure they're better without them, so the glaze runs down the side. I'm making these often!

These turned out great, but I made several modifications to make them more healthy.
I used 2 cups whole wheat flou and 3/4 cup white.  I used 1/4 grapeseed oil and 1/4 cup applesauce instead of the butter.  I also reduced the sugar by half.  What resulted was a tender, sweet enough muffin.  Very good!
So tasty!  I did not use the glaze (i am sure it is fabulous though).  I also added about 1/2 cup oat bran and 1/3 cup flax meal.  great flavor!
For us, these muffins were tasty but VERY dry by the next morning.  We did enjoy the flavor.  Next time I would replace some water with oil or perhaps applesauce.  Thanks for posting!

It certainly doesn't get any easier than this quick, yummy chicken dish. We really loved the sweet/ spicy combination of the sauce, and I loved that it goes together so quickly in one pan. There was only two of us eating so I halved the recipe with great results. I used a "medium" salsa instead of the mild because we like a little more spice. Also, because we are not eating much rice these days, I served this over cooked barley. Yummy! Thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe...it is definitely a keeper!
**Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game**

Very yummy! I used regular vanilla pudding mix and served with apple slices as an after school snack. The kids loved it! Very versatile, too. I think it would be great layered with bananas or even alone as a dessert, too. Thanks, Kristen, for a great recipe!

This is a weird one for me to rate.  Personally I'd give it a 3 as I found it only so-so.  I thought it had a weird aftertaste and next time I'd be more inclined to use vanilla yogurt.  That said, my 8 year old loved it and happily ate it up.  So I compromised on a 4.  :)  Thanks for posting.
A delicately flavoured cookie.  I got 26 cookies!! Not too sweet or overwhelming. Nice!

I really liked the flavor of this cookie. However, I feel like it is missing some more "wet" ingredients; perhaps another stick of butter, another egg or a teaspoon or two of vanilla? The dough was very dry and crumbly so I was concerned. The first batch I baked for 15 minutes and it was much too long. They were very brown on the bottom and very dry. The second batch was better, having baked them for just 10 minutes. I will probably make these again because they do have a good taste, but I will try them with more butter and eggs. Thanks for sharing.

These cookies are really good, however not very sweet, but that may be my fault :). Instead of mixing melted white chocolate into the batter I used white chocolate chips, which worked very well, however the batter itself needs a little bit more sugar if you do that. Also, the batter was dry so I added 1 more egg and enough milk to make it nice and wet. I got over 20 cookies, thank you for posting this recipe! Oh and I did not use nut, because they weren't available. :)

You've got a winner here, MNLisaB!  Outstanding comfort food! I made the recipe exactly as written and I wouldn't change a thing.  I'd like to say I would cut the butter amount in half next time, but I probably won't.  It was just too good. Thank you!!

I made this for a dinner party where the theme was "Modern Australian" (fusion). I doubled the recipe, using a 500g bag of defrosted frozen prawns (shrimp) and eyeballing the butter (probably used about half). Ran out of sherry so used about half sherry and half apple juice with a splash of rice wine vinegar. I also cooked the peppers with the mushrooms (briefly) as I didn't want them to be too crunchy. To prepare in advance, I completed up to step 10, slightly undercooking the rice. Then transported everything separately. Put the pot on the stove at the host's place, added a bit more hot stock, and stirred until hot. Threw in the veggies, pinenuts, and coriander (which were room temp and only took a minute to reheat).  Reheated the prawns (which I had refrigerated) in a hot skillet and served on the side (as we had a few seafood haters).  It was a big hit with everyone, especially the kids! (Oddly enough!)

My husband and I both love risotto, so we got excited to see this recipe. I cooked this as a main dish, and it was a little overwhelming. It would probably be better as a side dish to something. The cilantro seemed to be one of the only flavors we tasted. Maybe less cilantro will improve overall flavor.

We loved this! My husband thinks Risotto is bland but this was was far from it and is a keeper! 
I substituted the mushrooms for zucchini and the shrimp for pork stips, but prepared them the same way. The zucchini provides a great colour against the red peppers.

I was torn between 4 and 5 stars. If there was a 4.5 stars, this recipe would get it.  I loved it's inventiveness and the wonderful burst of Asian flavor from the ginger and garlic.  Since I have a mushroom-hater in our family, I substituted asparagus for mushrooms and it turned out great!  Thanks for sharing!

This would get 10 stars if I could go that high. My little family of 3 just demolished a pan of these guys and Boy, are they GOOD!  This recipe also marks the official start of using herbs from my aerogarden.  I added some chives to the chicken filling and, of course, the first cuttings of my cilantro went into this.  I made this pretty much as written except I used manchego cheese, which melted beautifully over the burritoladas and browned up nicely.  I LOVE using grocery store rotisserie chickens in stuff....they're always $4.99 at my store so I always get a lot of 'bang for the buck' out of them.  The rest of the chicken that went into this dish became chicken salad.  Excellent use for a rotisserie chicken!  Cilantro Lovers, you will love this recipe!  This is our new favorite recipe.  Thanks for posting it Sandi and thanks Raquel Pelzel, whoever you are.

Scrumdiddlyumptious!!  I had some tortillas to use up and this just fit the bill.  Very easy and super tasty.  I left out the jalapeno and used Medium Salsa Verde.  The leftover one was just as tasty cold for lunch the next day :)  Thanks, sweetie.
WOW-I loved this recipe!! I used homemade salsa instead of tomatillo sauce-only because I'm a novice. Great flavor and it was a hit! Thanks!
In one word, I would have to say "EXCELLENT"!!!  I did substitute Chunky Med. Salsa for the tomitillo sauce, and we loved it!

I was a bit apprehensive about raw eggplant, so I made half a recipe, to try it out on just me before going ahead and sharing it.  I tried a few bites without the honey then added the honey so I could experience it both ways. I was pleasantly surprised with how much I liked this dish. The amount of honey is so small that it didn't change the flavor substantially but I'd probably add it again.  The one change I'd make would be to use a bit more garlic, because the salad was just a bit bland. However, I'll definitely make it again--it will be a great dish to take with me for lunch.

I have an interest in Raw foods and like to try recipes that I come across on Zaar that sound intriqing...I was pleased to find this as an option from one of my team mates while playing in the ZWT3.  I used 2 fabulous avocados, 3 fat cloves of garlic and a generous amount of the red onion.  I soaked the diced eggplant in a bath of ice cold water with a ton of lemon juice and some sea salt for about 1/2 hour.  I did not have any dulse flakes...so to play with the texture and acidity I ribbon cut a couple of sun-dried tomatoes into the dressing.  I allowed the mixture to sit at room temp for an hour before serving it and LOVED the finished product... it was even better the following day after being chilled when the flavors had been allowed to mingle together...I used the honey to balance the lemon-tart and that sat in the salad mix as well...in my opinion it is key to the dish...
     The raw eggplant is a nice surprise...almost apple like with the way it is treated here, but of course not as crisp. The flavors are wonderful, the dish is different and creative.  Perfect for the summer weather!!  I loved it, Thanks ~Rita~!!

I have a garden full of eggplant so I thought I would try this. Didn't have dulse flakes so left them out. Also used a regular brown onion as I was out of red [and my kids won't eat onion if they know its there]. I only had 2 lemons so made up the rest with a little verjuice which works rather well. The eggplant ends up having a slightly apple like taste. The kids ate it and didn't complain although they weren't singing its praises either. I quite liked it for something different.

The raw eggplant really works well in this salad.  It's a nice blend of textures.  I used a beautiful white eggplant that I got at a local Famer's Market.   Instead of honey, I just sprinkled a little sugar over it.   Thanx for posting this unique and delicious salad!

I love lemon juice, salt, and avocado together; and I love eggplant, so I had to try this.  It is really good!  The first three I mentioned are wonderful, of course, but then there is the addition of two different crispy, crunchy textures.  The eggplant and onions go so nicely in this dish.  After chilling the dish, I totally forgot the honey until I got here and saw it mentioned in the other reviews.  I thought it was great without.  Thanks! Reviewed for the Veg*n Recipe Swap.

This was good. Different but not as I expected as there was no strong flavour from the eggplant being raw. I was trying it because it was a pretty raw recipe. I used less avocado as I only had 1 on hand, 2 pretty big organic (Canadian as opposed to Chinese) garlic cloves, regular cooking onion (I found too strong as usual), less freshly squeezed lemon juice as I had just 1 lemon left, light tasting extra virgin olive oil, no dulce flakes sorry, I added some sea salt for flavour instead, no pepper as I didn't have that either (I am in the house without many spices), but I did add some honey (too bad it was not raw & local as usual) it was still nice for the taste which I tried before and after adding and would recommend it but use raw! Plus the rest of the ingredients. Made for January 2013's Casual Veggie Tag (come join us everyone!)

WOW! So good!  Tastes just like the french drssing my mum used to make, but with WAY less fat, and no raw eggs. The only problem is that this recipe doesn't make very much, so i will double it next time!

This is really delicious. I don't know that it tastes like anything else I can think of. It's dark and rich like sauteed mushrooms or steak, yet a bit crunchy. I am glad you posted this, because the grocery store nearest me is Korean, and I've been seeing long brown "gobo roots" in there for years and wondering, "What is that? Is it really edible? How do I cook it? Am I missing out?" I was missing out, until today. I did find another recipe that said it was OK not to peel it, so I didn't. Be very careful with this: you keep adding damp vegetables and various liquids to hot oil, and it tends to spatter. In any case, yum.
Thanks so much for posting this! I've been served gobo in a different dish twice and I've been looking for recipes! Thank you!

Yum.  We have made this many times and for some reason I keep neglecting to review it.  I love the dark, earthy flavor of burdock, and like Nose, I don't peel it.  I feel that it gives it better flavor and that's where most of the nutrients are anyhow.  The soaking tip is a very good one.  We've also made this a couple of times with chicken, pork or tofu added to make it a main dish.  Yummy!

When I cooked this, my husband was surprised.  I was able to buy the frozen burdock and carrot 'matchsticks' at the Japanese market, then I quickly stir fried then added the season mix.  Easy and tasty!

This will be my contribution to our New Year's gathering. I decided to test your recipe and it tastes just like the okazu I normally go to in town. Now I can eat it anytime I have a craving for it. Thanks!

I discovered gobo last week at a local Japanese market and I had to use it. I just love discovering new ingredients. I found this kinpira recipe and others and I picked this recipe as the one to showcase Japan as we are cooking around the world with 2 friends right now: http://www.196flavors.com/2013/02/19/japan-gobo-kinpira/

I'm not usually a bread baker, & almost passed this recipe up because of all the steps in preparation! However, I'm glad I didn't, because this is a VERY, VERY TASTY bread! Got to admit that I added more raisins than were called for, but that's me ~ I love raisins! You want something different in a loaf of raisin bread? TRY THIS ONE, & I don't think you'll be disappointed! Many thanks for posting!

Very good loaf of bread here! An interesting way of preparing the dough, lots of work, but well worth it. I liked that the raisins were mixed in. Mine didn't roll up very well and separated at the roll. However, this may have been because I used Splenda not sugar. All in all, well worth the time to make.
Very good bread.I used a whole grain flour and added two tablespoons wheat gluten and it came out nice and soft.

Mine looks just like the picture. Lots of cinnamon. it taste like a cinnamon roll. Might be good to add some icing to the top. 
Thanks for sharing!

So tasty! I just had a slice and it's still warm. I love the cinnamon flavour. I used about half of the sugar which seems to have worked fine. I don't think this loaf will last very long!

Amazing bread! I used quick oats as I didn't have rolled and it was fine.  My husband ate 4 pieces tonight with dinner.  Definitely worth the effort and great gift, too!  THanks, pattiday!  Made for Aus/NZ Recipe Swap #14
I make these alot for breakfast with fried eggs. I never thought to add garlic and parsley for a dinner side dish. This was very good. I will do this one again!
I used frozen hash browns added the garlic & parsley and said WOW - Easy tasty breakfast or dinner side dish'  Thanks for posting Mielie

My 8yo daughter and I made these for a Russian project at her school. They were delicious! Very nutty and slightly sweet. They were very easy to make too. For the ground almonds I ground 1 cup sliced almonds with 1 Tbsp. flour in my food processor. Worked perfectly!
I needed a quick salad for dinner and found this one. This was real easy to put together and it tasted good. I made this exactly as written and we all enjoyed this.
This combination is great.  I like to add fennel as well.  I use coconut oil and a little mixed seasoning of whatever I have on hand.  for the salt, a little Real Salt.  Very nice.  Thanks

This was great and I'll make it again! I was a bit skeptical at first because the combo just didn't seem to fit - but it melds together beautifully!  I didn't read the previous review, and may try the coconut oil next time. I'd also like to try this the next time I'm in the States, as the sweet potatoes we get here are so different - they're white and not all that appealing to look at (though the flavor is good!).

This recipe is VERY popular among the Mennonites in Texas and Kansas. We like to serve the verenika with white gravy and tomato juice or strawberry jam. Also, dry cottage cheese is really easy to make at home; bring a gallon of buttermilk to boil and let it cool completely, drain and squeeze dry. By the way, some people call them porogies (not sure of the spelling).

This is Great!!! I was raised on this! Your recipe is entirely correct. Just as we had when we were kids. I was raised in a German, Amish, and Mennonite community. This was a very common meal. Doesn't get any better than this! Thanks for sharing!

Was lucky enough to get this once in a while growing up near the Amish town of Yoder, Kansas back in the 70's. A great place to try it now, is at The Breadbasket German restaurant on Main Street in Newton, KS. They serve verenika every Friday and Saturday night, along with whole loaves of fresh, homemade bread and lots of delicious, locally grown vegetables. We just visited there last weekend..so delicious, it'll make you weak in the knees!!

I made the potato casserole version tonight and it went over well.  I made a vegetarian version (for my daughter) w/ meatless sausage and I used veggie boullion instead of beef. I needed to add more water but I think it was beacuse the veggie sausage soaked some of it up.  I will try again with the other versions!  Thanks!
Good stuff! I made the potato casserole. Easy and filling!
My family fell in love with this pie.  I found it easy to make - the only thing is that I needed a larger pie plate than 9 inch.
I made this for Thanksgiving and everyone loved it.  Easy to make too.  Juanita in Nova Scotia

I just had some of this pie.
HMMMMMMM all yummy and still warm with some whipped topping.
HMMMM HMMMM HMMMMM!!!!!
Just wonderful :)

This is wonderful!  We were scraping the sour cream mixture out of the bowl with apple slices while the pie baked.

I had doubled the recipe to make two pies for a pie auction and ended up keeping one for ourselves!  The auctioned off pie was snatched up in a hurry!

This is the first time I've ever made an apple pie but I love sour cream so I knew I would love this pie. I'm not a great baker so I had a little difficulty making the butter crumble into the topping but other than that the taste was amazing!

I made this pie because I had sour cream and apples to use up before they went belly up!  WOW!  This was sooooo easy and yummy.  DH was practically licking his plate and said to give it 15 stars!  Hee Hee We served it with a bit of cool whip on top but really it could stand on its own.  I'll be making this often.  Thanks for sharing!

Now this is a perfect apple pie for those of us who don't necessarily like apple pie! I added some fresh cranberries to counter the sweetness of the apples. Wonderful, and beautiful on our Thanksgiving dinner table. Thank you!
The pie is an unusual mix of custardy sour cream and apple slices, but boy is it good!!  Nice and easy to make, too.

This was excellent, and smelled wonderful while baking, but I can never leave well enough alone...instead of 3/4 C sugar, I took away 2 T white sugar, and subbed 2 T brown sugar.  I also added a heaping teaspoon of allspice to the sour cream mixture, and 1/2 t allspice to the crumb topping.  I used a nine-inch deepdish crust, and it was the perfect size.

This was a delicious pie!  The only problem I had was with the topping -- didn't end up crumbly, but more like a paste.  Next time I'll use very cold butter and see if that does the trick.  It still worked out fine the way it was -- and the pie was fantastic!  Next time I'll try sliced apples, as it just wasn't the same for DH with the apples diced.  We do get set in our ways :-)  Thanks, Miss Annie, for this wonderful recipe!
Dianne

I used our very own home grown Granny Smith's to make this wonderful pie. I also used half Splenda for the filling, and half brown sugar Sugar Twin for the topping with great results. It was very easy to make, and was a big hit with hubby! Thanks Miss Annie!

This is a very unique apple pie! It was very easy to prepare and was very very tasty!  I added way more than 2 1/2 cups of apples and I also added a handful or more of oatmeal to the topping! This will be made again and again, as my family loved this dearly!

I fixed this recipe for my wife to celebrate the Fourth of July. This was the first time I  fixed an apple pie, and it turned out to be easy to fix and, according to my wife, who has tasted MANY apple pies all her life, it was "outstanding! the best apple pie ever!". However, I have to admit that I used mostly organic ingredients (sour cream, sugar, flour, apples, butter, vanilla extract). I also used Egg Beaters instead of eggs. For the topping, I used 1/4 cup of brown sugar, and 1/4 cup of Turbinado sugar. I didn't use cinnamon at all. I just don't understand why, upon cutting, the pieces wouldn't come out in one whole slice. Thank you for a great recipe! 
   Saulo
This was really good and a nice change from the usual apple pie.  At another reviewer's suggestion, I also added oats to the crumb topping.
Oh MY!  This was insanely delicious!  I will be making this again!!!!!!!!!  Thanks a ton!
Quick to make, a little sweet but delicious!  Used 4 cups of apples to fill the pie plate.  Thank you!
Made this pie the other day and it was a hit!!! I'll be making this apple pie instead of the traditional from now on.
The combination seemed so unusual, I had to try it. It's fantastic! Thanks for posting it!

Definitely unusual! Certainly intriguing! AND, wonderfully tasty, even if I only left the jalapeno in a couple of hours! Had it when a Mexican couple came by, & they LOVED it! Will be making this again! [Made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in this Spring's Pick-A-Chef]

I made this pie for Thanksgiving and my husband and I never got a chance to taste it as it was inhaled by my guests that very night. I will definitely make it again for Christmas and be sure to set aside a piece for each of us. Can't wait to make it again. Thanks for the recipe.
This pie is so amazing!!  It was very easy to make.  It did not last 24 hours in my house every one gobbled it up super quick.
I gave this four and 3/4 stars,and used about 3 c of apples ,was loved by all,and will do again..Enjoyed by all ,thanks for posting,Chef Don Steele
I just made this pie for the second time to try to correct my mistakes from the first go-round.  Fantastic!  I used Granny Smith apples, sliced thinly instead of diced.

I've made this pie several times. It is so moist. I use splenda instead of regular sugar and you can not tell the difference. When ever I am making an apple pie, which is pretty often, I log onto recipezaar and retrieve this receipe. Heck
The Pie is wonderful and easy to prepare

I can't believe I forgot to rate this... I was craving an apple pie since it's getting cooler and I remembered this delicious and creamy pie I made for Thanksgiving last year.  I really love sour cream but really did not know if it belonged in a pie... WOW!!!`When we had our first bite, we just fell in love.  The tangy and creamy sour cream really complimented the sweetness of the apples so well.  I also loved the crumb topping which was reminiscent of an apple crisp.  It was the best of both worlds... I baked my pie in a deep dish 9 in frozen pie crust and it filled it to the brim... Thanks so much for posting this wonderful variation on apple pie!!!

I tried this recipe for Thanksgiving this year. I baked it the day before, and it looked great! However, after letting it cool then refrigerating it until the next day, I have to say, the presentation of this pie wasn't the best. It almost looked curdled, I guess from the sour cream. However, I did like it! I will only make this pie again if I'm serving it soon after it comes out of the oven. Thanks!

I'd like to rate this 3 and a half stars.  The pie was really good but not quite what I was expecting.  It was very creamy on the inside, and the apples were still a bit firm.  I used granny smith and red delicious.  It really was very tasty but not quite what I would choose if I was craving apple pie.  Thanks though... I might make this again if I get in the mood for it.

I've been planning to make this for quite some time and I'm glad I did! Even though the ouside edge was a bit burnt it tasted wonderful. Next time I make it I think I'll use a 10 inch pie dish as I used a 12 inch one and the filling was too spread out. Great recipe!

The flavor was great! I used a shortbread crust instead as I hate rolling out pastry.  I only used 3 granny smiths and had more than enough apples, although I sliced them, I didn't dice them. Super easy to make. Even better the second day. BUT the apples stay crunchy! Just to warn those like me that prefer soft apples in their pie. Not dry, perfect filling!  Loved the vanilla, I added a little extra oh and some nutmeg, but shouldn't have bothered, couldn't taste the nutmeg. I didn't like the topping the night I made the pies but the next day It was all perfectly melded and not too sweet. I suggest letting this pie rest at least 12 hours before eating, just to help with flavors. Super yummy!

This was one of the first pies I have ever baked and I couldn't fiqure out with the list of ingredients how it would taste. I was amazed at what a great flavor it had. As others have mentioned it is better served chilled.
Very unusual taste for an apple pie! Got lots of raves!  Will make again!!  Thank you for listing it!!

Woah. I brought this in to work and it was gone in 20 minutes (and I work at a restaurant where there's plenty of other food around). Even my boss raved about it (yay! and it was his birthday, too!). The only changes I made was decreasing the sugar in the filling to 2 tablespoons, and then spooning homemade caramel over the top. Oh man was that good. Thank you!
20 stars !!!!!!!!!! I have made this several times. It is so easy and it is gone in seconds! If you are not a baker you will think you are after this recipe
Jumpin G Jahosafats, this was awesome!!!  It was gone in no time Christmas day. Next time I make it, I will make 2 so everyone gets their fill!  Loved by the whole famdamily here!

This was so easy to make and very delicious.  I made it 3 times now.  The directions should include the need for a "deep dish" crust and the fact the butter works better melted.
It is almost cheese cake like when done so...delicious.
WOW! Yummy. This was so easy to make and got rave reviews from guests. This will become a regular recipe for me. No changes made to the recipe.

Great Apple pie.  Easy to make with a great taste.  I did not make any changes, used granny smith apples, a deep dish pie shell and  served with ice cream.  I did not even have to cover the crust it came out golden crisp and perfect. My family loved it.   Thank you for the recipe.

Simple, yet delicious and easy. I cut the sugar down, and added extra cinnamon and nutmeg. Based on other reviews, I also added oats to the topping. I made mini pies - they looked better than those sold at the Union Square Farmer's Market - and tasted better too!
Wow - someone stole my grandmother's recipe!!  LOL.  One thing to note - the apples need to be tart - Granny Smith - makes ALL the difference.  Sssshhh, don't let the secret out ;)
A very easy and delicious pie!

This is one of the easiest pies I have ever made. It is delicious!  I will be making this one from here on out.  My husband and I loved it and can't wait to share it with others.  The only thing I was concerned about was that I used homemade sour cream.  It is a bit different so I wasn't sure of the outcome.  Fantastic.  Thanks!
Super easy and super yummy!  Will make this often.  Thanks for sharing.

I made these back along and forgot to review them, so I am doing it now.  This pie was gone in one sitting and I got thumbs up from the whole gang!  Looks like I need to add this to my favorites so I don't lose it!

I had a recipe like this that I got from a cookbook from the Amana Colony, Iowa, but misplaced the book and have been looking for this recipe for ages! It's also good with pears. I also agree that granny smith apples are great in this pie.

If I could give more than 5 stars I would!  This was out of this WORLD!!  Flavor and texture wise it's a cross between a sugar cream and apple pie.
