Good, but needs more tomato sauce and some more seasoning. I doubled the garlic and added 1/2 cup tomato sauce and about 2 teaspoons of Italian seasoning.

Very good, ellie_!  Simple and quick to make,  we enjoyed this for supper last night.  I did leave out the spinach, since the girls won't eat it,  but I upped the amount of tomatoes, using a whole can (410 gr) of chopped tomatoes, and I chopped an onion, starting it off in the oil, and adding the tomatoes and garlic.
A simple comfort food without excessive calories! 

Thank you ellie_!

Made for Vegetarian Swap#14

This was an interesting take on a noodle and cheese recipe. I loved the tomatoes in the recipe and next time will add more and skip the spinach. Also, I like things that have a little spice to them, so next time will add a little kick to it. But all in all a nice lowfat alternative to mac and cheese.

Mmmm, this was soo good!  I made this to take for lunch this week.  I did use part skim ricotta & mozz, which increased the points value, but it was worth it.  I used cherry tomatoes that I quartered, I wouldn't reccomend cutting them so small as they seemed to disappear in the sauce.  The picture doesn't do it justice, try it & you'll like it. Thanks for posting, ellie!

I added the spinach just before serving so that they were just barely wilted.  The kids didnt like it I think it was the texture of the Ricotta.  All the adults had seconds though :D  Thanks for a good little variation.
I used macaroni noodles (as in kraft mac and cheese, lol.) It was great! I loved the complexity of the flavors and the texture was great. Next time I'll make it with spirals and grilled chicken.

The texture of this was weird...sort of clumpy...but that wasn't really a detriment for us.  The flavor was great and I liked how it was a slightly healthier mac-n-cheese option.  Recipe was OK doubled and using canned diced tomatoes saved a little prep time.  Thanks for the great recipe ellie_

5 year old DD loved it, I found it overly sweet. The banana I used was not even fully ripe but I did fry the slices until slightly brown in organic unsalted butter which I think gave it much more flavour and we love banana that way. I used straight from an organic farm fresh eggs where the chickens have space and eat grass sometimes, for the milk I used organic full fat coconut milk, and organic local raw honey which I would reduce if I make this again.
I never put milk in an omelette - Delia taught me that! I switched the oil for butter; very tasty ??

This was very tasty, especially with the vinegar and tarragon on top. Unfortunately the flour didn't stick very well to the leeks, so I found that after frying, the nice browned battered parts of the leeks separated and fell off the leeks themselves. Otherwise, this was a delicious and attractive dish and I will post a photo soon. It really highlights the sweetness and tenderness of the leeks.

I found this soup to have a good vegetable combination, however, very tasteless.  In my opinion it requires some spices to enhance the flavor.  It is somewhat suprising to me that you are a vegetarian foody and would post a recipe such as this without giving it a good tryout yourself.

Very tasty!!  I loved the marinade, not too sweet or salty.  I liked the use of the lemon pepper and garlic powder and I left out the salt since the marinade had soy sauce.  Grill time was perfect.  Will make this easy recipe again!  Made for Photo Tag.
This is just like my Javanese Grandma would may on cool afternoons. The combination of the salty pudding with the sweet brown sugar syrup - just transported me back.
Very nice bar and very easy to do. Perhaps a tad dry but still very easy to eat. I will definitely do these again and you could even do more marbling and use white chocolate too.

A very easy to make and flavoursome meal, and a crockpot recipe that I'll certainly make again.  I doubled the onions and garlic and used a pound and a half of fresh mushrooms, added in step 5, (simply because I love mushrooms and because I never use canned mushrooms).  I used 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup and I also added some dried thyme.  I cooked this on low for 5 hours, then sprinkled on the cheese (a grated tasty cheese) and bacon and turned the crockpot to high, as instructed.  The chicken was fall apart tender and really delicious.  Next time I make this, and I’ll probably wait until winter, I’m going to make it with Julesong’s superb Delmonico's Puree of Portabello Mushroom Soup Recipe #117144 rather than with canned soup.  Thanks, Kitten, for sharing another tasty recipe with really easy to follow instructions!

This was an easy recipe to follow and yet wasn't lacking in flavor.  I served it over rice which the sauce was great over top of and steamed broccoli. This recipe will definitely go in the keep pile. LOL

Very Yummy!  Changes I made:  Fresh baby bella mushrooms, and about 1/2 cup white wine (to clean out the soup can).  Also used velveeta and shredded mexican cheese blend.  Delicious served with white rice.  Thanks Kitz!

I will be celebrating my THIRD Zaar anniversary tomorrow. I wanted to bake a lemon cake and decided to go for this one. I did this today and it turned out so fabulous. I cheated and tasted some of it - I couldn't wait until tomorrow;-)! This cake tastes very good!! Thank you for posting!
The cake was fabulous, especially the lemond curd.  I have never made a cake like this before, but I think I can stop here when it comes to lemon cake.  You won't be sorry.

I served this for a family dinner yesterday with Lasagna Supremo #86623, garlic bread, salad, and Refreshing Strawberry Iced Tea #85243. I was using 9" cake pans, so I ended up having to make 2 recipes of the cake layer portion; 1 recipe isn't enough for pans of that size. At first, I thought the layers weren't lemony enough, but with the addition of the frosting, it turns out they're just right. The lemon curd will give you a jolt at the beginning. Don't eat this if you don't like lemons. I forgot to look for candied violets while at the supermarket, so I just snipped a few pansy blooms from a flower border and placed them in a dollop of frosting in the center of the cake. The dinner guests enjoyed the cake so much, they asked if they could take a few more slices home with them. Ahh, sweet (or tart in this case) success.  :)

I love citrus and this made such a Wonderful cake. I added orange juice into the cake batter and also made Orange curd instead of Lemon. Made the orange cream with half the orange curd and refrigerated for over 3 hours and then used it to fill and top the cake. Put a thin layer of curd on top of the cream leaving a boundary of 1 inch all round the cake. I decorated this ridge with orange wedge slices and orange cream rosettes. Was a super hit. THank you Marie. Delightful recipe. :) Fay

This was a delicious, very lemony cake. I'm glad the cake recipe was a bit forgiving, since I overbeat the batter. I made this in a 10 3/4" springform and then sliced horizontally to make three layers. The cake stayed together nicely and the few broken parts could be glued together nicely with the lemon curd. I used 1/2 of lemon curd between layers before adding whipped cream for frosting to go on top. Great cake. I will try it again as suggested by Fay as an orange cream. Yum!

I have been making this cake for years. Its my favourite cake, Dh requests it at least once a month. I recived this recipe from a chefs school 1 day baking class. I use my own cake recipe and dont add any confectioners sugar.

I was really disappointed in this recipe. I followed the instructions to the letter, and I was surprised when I ended up with a very thick, heavy batter. It was unlike any cake batter I've ever seen, and I wondered if I had done something wrong. I went back over the recipe, and I had done everything exactly as instructed, but it still didn't look right to me. I should have trusted my instincts. After baking, the cake was dense, heavy and DRY. It was practically inedible. I felt terrible because this was a birthday cake. Never again will I make a cake for a special occasion without a test run first.
Sorry, but this did not work for me at all.

This didn't turn out for me the first time at all.  It was very runny.  I tried it again using self-rising flour (or you can add 1 1/2 teaspoons of baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt to regular flour), mixing the dry ingredients, adding 25 minutes to the baking time for a total of 55 minutes, and baking it in a 9x13 pyrex pan.  It still came out of the oven very runny and kind of strange looking, but I refrigerated it overnight and it set up some.  I wish there was a 3 1/2 star rating.  I would definitely give this a 5 for taste and ease, but a 2-3 for needing alterations to the recipe and for appearance.  I gave it 4 because it was so tasty.  I will make it again.

As written this is a three, however, with just a little change it can be a five!!! Do mix all ingredients together including butter, which should be melted, reduce the peaches to one can and you have yourself a yummy, easy-peasy peach cobbler!

I mixed all the ingredients prior to adding them to the peaches. This included the butter, which, as it is summer here, was very soft, but not melted. I also sifted the flour twice to make it nice and fluffy. I cooked it for 40 minutes instead of 25, too. This made it turn out great!

I used 3 1/2 - 15 oz cans of peaches.  I think using smaller cans - may have more juice than just 2 - 28 oz cans.  I cooked it a total of 40 minutes because it looked extremely runny when I checked it at 30 min.  After removing it from the oven and letting it cool off - it still is very juicy.  We had to throw the whole thing away.

Tuna and onions...what a great combination. Overall my DH and I really enjoyed this recipe.  I had no problem making the onion sauce, but needed to add a little more vinegar and sugar to get that sweet/sour taste...about 2 more Tbsp. vinegar and another tsp. sugar.  The method of cooking the tuna was pretty unconventional for me, and it certainly did take longer than the 7 minutes to get the fish to medium rare...more like 12 minutes. Perhaps my steaks were extra thick.  They did continue to cook after removing from the skillet, so perhaps I should have taken them out a minute or two sooner. This is a very good recipe and I'll experiment in the future with other fish.
Thank you.  It was the first time I cooked Tuna steaks.  They came out very good.  Loved the taste of the onions and tuna. I told my sister about it so I had to sent her a copy.
This was very tasy.  A nice combination of ingredients.  Thanks for sharing.

I love tuna and am always looking for new ways to prepare this healthy fish.  The sauce is what makes this dish!  It's absolutely delicious!  As the fish was cooking covered in the wine, I added some broccolini to steam alongside it.  Served this with a side dish of White Bean Pancetta Salad
Recipe #65318

UPDATE:  Rather than sauteeing the steaks in olive oil then adding the wine, I poached the steaks in the wine and added a thinly sliced bulb of fennel for a side dish.  This method really brought out the taste of the bay leaves and wine in the fish.
I loved this recipe.  It is company and special occasion worthy.  I was thinking to give the finished dish a little more color, sprinkle it with paprika. Other than that, no changes are needed.
Very easy to make. Cooking it now. Used balsamic vinegar instead of red. Love balsamic vinegar with onions.
These cookies are a bit too sweet. I may have packed the brown sugar a little harder than I should have.

Delicious! I followed the directions up until  # 4, then I cooked it in a crock pot (I had no need for the string)on high for about 6 hours so it would be done when we got home from church. My shoulder was a little over 5 pounds. This was one of the best meats I've prepared in my crock pot!

It was ages since we'd had lamb, and this Mediterranean-style lamb, with its lemon, oregano, olive oil and garlic was just so wonderfully flavoursome.  I added a few more herbs - rosemary and sage from a nifty grinder that I've been using in nearly every recipe since I bought it. I followed Blessed*One's lead and, after completing step four, cooked this in my crockpot, for about 5 hours.  I also cooked some quarted onions, parsnips and baby carrots with it.  The onions were in the pot for the full time; the parsnips and baby carrots I added part way through, and I added a bit more lemon juice when I added them so that they too were drizzled in lemon juice.  I also doubled the garlic.  Wonderfully flavoursome and SO tender.  We enjoyed this for a small family dinner and everyone LOVED it.  Thank you for sharing this recipe, lindseyclw!

This cooks a long time, but the time to put it together is minimal. It is very good. I made the whole recipe and there is only my husband and me so I froze the leftovers. I'll be curious to see how it tastes reheated.

I doubled this recipe, which called for a lot of the WINE, but it simmered down nicely. I then added water to thin it some. Added some frozen Italian meatballs, and served 6 people easily (over whole wheat spaghetti noodles) with 2-3 servings left. I added fresh cracked pepper & 2 pinches of kosher salt, and I had to add a bit more sugar b/c my canned tomatoes were a bit bitter. Oh, I left out the green peppers b/c I didn't have any! Thanks :)
Very good sauce that I will make again and again.  Definately printer worthy!  Thanks!

I just made my second batch of this GREAT SAUCE. the first was as shown, the second was quadrupled. 
It freezes and thawes without loss of appearance or flavor. I fill sandwich sized zip lock bags, each holds 2 servings. When frozen. I place the bags into a larger bag that is labeled and dated. It's nice to have a freezer full of good stuff for quick meals or unexpected company.Thanx for sharing this great recipe.
Pierre

I made this last week and it was exactly what I was looking for in taste.  Excellent flavor!  I really love red wine added in spaghetti sauces.  The only different thing I did was to put the can of diced tomatoes in the blender first to smooth them out a bit as I have a daughter who's not crazy about chunky tomatos in things.  I also added 1 pound of lean ground beef to make a meat sauce.  This would be great to make a double batch and freeze ahead. Pam
VERY GOOD.  Try using red bell pepper in place of the green pepper for a slight variation.
Great sauce, it takes a while to make but it is worth the wait.  I didn't put a green pepper in because the peppers at the supermarket didn't really look good to me but I will put them in next time.

Very simple and very, very good!
Fantastic sauce!  Will definitely make this again.  Thanks!

I doubled the recipe due to that there were 4 of us.  Overall, they were great, .  The combo of lemon and peppercorns is a must to try.  I guess I estimated the thickness of the potatoes, after 45 minutes, they were'nt done after an hour, they were done, but almost to done, but they were fine.  If you make these, check oven regularly after 45 minutes, depending on the thickness as stated in step 6. These are great potatoes, and is a must tryer. The flavor is something everybody should try.  Made for holiday tag.

Enjoyed the flavors of this recipe very much. I think my "bunch" of basil might have been too small, as it didn't stand out quite as much as I had hoped. I'll add more next time. Made for Every Day Holiday Tag. :)
Yummy recipe! Loved all the mushrooms and the barley is so good for you too! Thanks! Made for ZWT#6 by  a Looney Spoon Phoodie!
Love barley and mushrooms. I did used just button mushrooms and a onion seasoning mix for the chicken bouillon. Thanks. Made for ZWT6

This was easy to prepare, although it took some mixing to get the lumps out of the batter and the frosting mixed in well without using a mixer. But the result was wonderful.  I used a Dark Chocolate Fudge Cake mix with a Chocolate Frosting.  It is so moist and delicious!  Thanks for sharing your recipe Marie!

I have made this several times trying different techniques of mixing it.  The best way I have found for myself is to beat the eggs with a whisk then whisk in the frosting.  Add the oil and milk and lastly the cake mix.  If the cake mix is really lumpy then I have sifted the mix to get the lumps out.  It is a wonderful recipe and the combinations are endless.

I found this loaf a little heavy, almost too moist and with  quite a different  taste.  Too cinnomony for me but my DH liked it very much. I felt the cinnomon taste obliterated the pumpkin/banana and zucchini, even the large amount of vanilla extract did not come through. Another time I would leave the topping off, perhaps that is what made the cinnomon so overwhelming.In any case DH will enjoy it and that is important!
Not one of the best recipes i have made.  I think that the pumpkin and bananas was just too much.

The mixture never thickened up before put in the bread pan. The problem may be the recipe calls for baking powder when most recipes of this type should be baking SODA. I baked mine for an hour and a half, and it stayed the same consistency as the batter.
We made the Curried Chickpea filling. Neither DH nor I liked it very much as it did not have much flavor.  It was also quite watery, not saucy at all.
not so bad you can alter how strong the curry is b
Good mix of flavors, and a great way to stretch a little leftover roast. Our beef was dry, so we added a poblano sour cream. Thanks for posting.

This was served at a recent party.  It is a great party dish as it can be made ahead of time and it is also economical for a large group.  I doubled the recipe for 12 to 14 servings.  The meat was flank steak.  It was cooked in the slow cooker and then shredded.  Some of the broth was poured  over the meat and it chilled overnight.  A combination of thinly sliced red and Vadilla onion was used.  The lettuce was iceburg.  The avocado was added just before serving.  Everyone seemed to enjoy the combination of flavors.  I really enjoyed it because I was able to relax and enjoy the party.
This is an absolutely ingenius dish; my family drools over the smell and spoons in before it's set on the table. Thanks for the great idea; this one's a keeper people!

Glut is one of the oddest recipes you will ever see. But, unlike Twinkies del Mar, it really is a recipe.  Our dad could do a steak like nobody's business and this was just the icing on the cake.
Just don't tell anyone what is in it.
Oh, yum!!  This was SO very good!  I know people might avoid it because of the anchovies, but don't!  Make it tonight, and just keep the ingredients a secret.  I used sherry and added green onions.

Sorry to be the "party pooper" here, but this is one of those "coconut" recipes - either you like it or you don't. I didn't. However, my 2 picky kids who don't eat anything both did. I used sherry, and most of a 1.58oz tube of anchovy paste (minus about 1 T that I had used before). I also used 1/2 tsp. garlic powder because I was out of fresh garlic. I urge everyone to try this. I get the impression that if it's for you, it will be positively heavenly!

This is very good.  I made it as shown, but I used light sour cream.  I also added several generous grinds of black pepper, and several tablespoons of milk at the end to thin it out a bit.  The anchovies are not optional.  Don't be afraid; you won't really know they're in there, but the sauce will suffer if they are not.
I like the flavor profile, however I found it too thick.  Making again I would add more sherry or brandy to thin it out a bit.  I found it needed a little salt and pepper really helped.

This was a tasty dish, but I had a tiny problem with it... :-(  I arranged the raw eggplant, zukes and mushrooms in the baking dish and then followed the directions as written (including using some of my hoarded Splenda).  This is delicious tasting, but the raw vegetable release a tremendous amount of water while cooking and the dish was literally swimming in veggie juice!  I served this up with a slotted spoon and we had this over rice and pasta (depending on who was doing the eating).  I will absolutely make this again next time, but I think I'm going to saute all the veggies first, then reduce the baking time.

I took a few liberties with your recipe. I cut out the tomatoe juice, changed the stock from beef to chicken and increased the stock  to make up for cutting out the tomatoe juice and it was super.  Is'nt it amazing how many people are afraid to use 30 cloves of garlic?  It is the natural source of wellness!  Thanks!!!!

I changed recipe slightley. I added the can of tomatoes with its juce instead of fresh tomatoes. Have never used so much garlic but thought Id try the right amount. IT was fabulous even my hubby loved it so told him after eating how many cloves  He said I should reply to say how great it was. And many thanks.!!

Just made this for dinner--fiance doesn't really like soup but I love it, so I'm always looking for good GARLICKY soups to make, because he LOVES garlic! Like Bergy, I replaced the tomato sauce with chicken broth and used all chicken broth instead of beef broth. I think I used about 30 cloves of garlic. I'm serving this with pasta shells stuffed with ricotta, zucchini, spinach and garlic with tomato sauce. This soup is perfectly seasoned and satisfying. Thanks for posting!!

I love the flavor that this soup has!  I had to make a double-batch because I just couldn't get enough of it!  I didn't make any changes or substitutions, I liked it as is.  Thank you for this yummy recipe!

Am sorry but you cant call this soup an onion soup it would be more apt it it was called tomatoe soup with garlic and onion. I made this soup exactly as it except I used chicken stock cubes. T he garlic was perfect but i had to add alot of salt and fresh black peper. The end result was like a chunky very wet pasta sauce. I am sorry but I wouldnt be making this soup again.
Blah! I love garlic, but this was too much. And it was really a tomato soup, not an onion soup.
It was delicious! I used about 30-32 cloves of garlic, low-sodium V8 for the tomato juice, and added a sprinkling of dill and oregano. Will definitely be making this one again!

It was far too runny, like a pasta sauce as someone mentioned before, though that could very well have been my own fault! I ommited the onions and used tinned tomatos but stuck to the recipe otherwise. It smelt amazing as it was cooking, you can never have too much garlic I think! I'll probably give it another shot though, it has potential.

Fantastic soup!  I followed the recipe except added a shot of vodka at the end. I donâ€™t care for vodka except in pasta sauce and now this soup. I used shredded swiss cheese. Canâ€™t wait for summer tomatoes and will make and share this often.  Thanks!
Loved this on our corn yesterday.  I used my light spread and didn't roll in a log, but it was great!
Mmmmmm.  This was really good.  I used minced garlic from a jar instead of the powder and I used a mix of parmesan and mozzarella.  The people at the party I brought it to loved it.

Definitely a five star.  I prepared with no changes.  One guest didn't bother with crackers and ate it with a fork. She liked artichoke very much; she is from Cuba and she says they don't have them there.
This was liked, but not a 5 star wonder for our family. Missing something.  Followed recipe as written.
Terrible. Please don't waist your time and ingredients. Take these ingredients and add it to a recipe that requires proofing of the dough.

My girls LOVE this bread. We replaced the canola oil with coconut oil and think I used 1/4c of honey. They love to eat it it with butter and cinnamon or peanut butter. Texture is a lot like a corn bread and it's very sweet.

I am so dissapointed. This does not take 2 cups of flour. It was soup until i added 3 more cups of flour. Then do i let it raise. It has yeast in it. It says to put in bread oan and bake?? So want to tey the flavor. It is my first time trying a bread with Dandyline flower In it. Someone one needs to correct the errors. Will let you see after i raise and bake it. Hope it still has a chance!!!

The end result of how I cooked this was off the charts fabulous.  BUT there is no way in the world I am cooking any green, especially tender swiss chard, for 1 hour or more.  SO, I boiled the wheat berries in salted water until *almost* cooked, then drained them.  I sauteed the onion (no leeks), stems, added all the rest except the leaves.  I let that cook until the liquid absorbed, getting the crusty bottom.  THEN I added the leaves & stirred them in until wilted & served.  I would add more pomegranate molasses next time.  This is a super yummy combo that we ate & ate & ate & ate....then it was gone.  :(  Made for Sun & Spice Tag 2.2013.
Turned out great!  I've been trying new recipes for DH and this one was so good.

Oh my stars, Kaarin this was a winner with us. Such simple everyday ingredients turns into comfort food sumpreme. I scaled the recipe down to 2 serving besides that I followed the recipe. This recipe is thick, creamy, smooth, silky with just the right amount of chocolate. It tasted like an imported French chocolate pudding that DH is addicted to except much much more better. This pudding tasted more rich and decadent then it really is. All I can say is no more French pudding for us and hello Chocolate Blanc Mange! Thank you for sharing this recipe.

Ibought this magazine years ago when i came out, and this was our dessert of choice for many months. Alas, my magazine has been lost for years now, and I am thrilld to have this recipe again. Chocolaty and not too sweet, it still delivers a great kick to your sweet tooth.

This was delicious.  I was looking for a way to use up the spinach and canned tomatoes I had in the freezer, and all I had to buy for this recipe was the ricotta and the pasta.

It took me like 15 minutes to get it ready for the oven, not counting the cook time for the pasta.

The only change I made was to the tomato sauce.  I added a little chicken stock and chopped onion.

The only change I will make next time is to add salt to the spinach-cheese mixture and to double the sauce.

But I will definitely make this again.

Thanks for posting it!
This was great and very comforting too! I cut it in 1/2 - but now wish I didn't! I also then did a little more pasta, otherwise followed exactly. It's a keeper - thank you.

We loved this recipe. It was a less-labor-intensive and less-caloric way to make something that tasted very much like lasagna. I added a bit of parsley and garlic to the ricotta and spinach mixture, but it was otherwise made as posted.

Really delicious.  I was tempted to add a chopped onion, but refrained from doing so.  The sauce was rich, and thick and tasted most wonderfully of garlic and basil.  I served it over linguine and we were all immensely satisfied.  I will try it again with onion.

For the ease of this, it was wonderful! I added  some ground sirloin and I served it over Cappellini. I guess it is romantic, it packs some heat! :) Thank you ms.susan!!! Made during ZWT3 by a Floozie - Remembering Amy.

I loved this delicious, simple sauce.  I confess, I make a very similar sauce, but I don't add water and I cook it only 15 minutes, so my herbs (either thyme or basil) permeate the tomato sauce.  This sauce was just as nice, and maybe the chili flakes get a longer time to settle in as a dominant flavor. This is like an Arabiatta Sauce - very nice!

I made this for DH and it met with an ok response. I used piri piri in the absence of chili flakes and that did pack a punch so he wasn't complaining there, he just said that other recipes I have tried tasted even better, so I think that it's a case of we are spoiled by Zaar and getting rather choosey.  The good news it that DH said he wouldn't mind to have this again. And from the Pasta Fanatic that's not bad going. Please see my rating system: This one gets a lovely 4 stars. Thanks!
Wonderful sauce! I love the garlicky flavor. My kitchen smelled great while this was cooking!

This is a very tasty sauce. It gets 5 stars here as my husbands comment was "I don't like tomato sauce but this is your best attempt so far". He seems to think it needs meat in it. I, on the other hand, love tomato sauce and I agree that this is one of my best attempts. I did decrease the pepper flakes as I have 2 people here who do not like anything too hot. You are so right that it smells delicious. How can you go wrong with garlic and basil. Mmmm.
Thanks Susan for a great recipe!

This was very good and easy to make, tasting mellow yet fresh.  I added some sauteed onion to the sauce, as per another reviewer's suggestion.  I loved the little bite provided by the chili flakes.  Served with spaghetti squash and Tofu Nut Balls (Recipe #29671).

This was delicious, and very easy to make. I added some Italian Sausage, which was very good. It is quite spicy, though; we served a different sauce to our small children. I will most definately make this again.

GREAT TASTING SAUCE, & just the thing for my son & his wife who are wanna be vegetarians! Made up a double batch &, after tasting it for myself, sent it home with them! Almost reduced the amount of chili flakes, but am glad that I didn't ~ The taste was just right! [Made & reviewed for one of my adoptees for this Spring's Pick-A-Chef]
Amazing sauce. Will be making this again for sure.

Great and easy recipe! I added a can of mushrooms as well because I had them on hand and liked the flavor, and since I didn't measure chili flakes, I think I put in a little too much, but that was my fault. Overall, loved the sauce and will make again! Thanks for sharing...

We really enjoyed this fast and easy sauce.  I only used 1 tsp of the chili flakes as I used 3 hot Italian sausage in to bring the heat up a wee bit more. I also cut the salt down too (personal preference). Will be making this alot for our pasta.  Thank you for sharing.
This is a really great recipe. I used the pressure cooker and caned chickpeas. This is a quick and easy, delicious comfort food.

5 Stars, I am in love!  This reminded me of a superb complexly layered pea soup, that is completely different from my other chicken standards. I am not sure I even did the recipe correctly.  I used 2 large skinless chicken breasts and grated fresh ginger with the given measurements.  I startd from dried garbanzo beans, which required an 8-hour soak, plus 30 minutes to shell the beans after cooking; I spared myself the extra salt, but the slowest chopper in the Western Hemisphere would be better off rinsing and draining canned garbanzo beans instead, I think.  I used the pressure cooker, and let the press.ure come down naturally.  Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

Five gold stars! What a delicious dish -- the chickpeas are soft and creamy yet still maintain their integrity; the chicken is juicy and tender; the sauce has such a velvety finish from the butter. I was so enamored of the taste and texture of the sauce that I skipped adding the cornstarch slurry; otherwise followed instructions to the letter. Truly a terrific dish, Nasseh!

I changed the ingredients a bit here, used chicken instead of beef (that's what we had for sunday dinner yesterday!) used carrots instead of the peppers, left out the whiskey (the kids are rowdy enough lol)but did the rest and it was a definate hit!!  Beats bubble & squeak any day of the week! (which is what i usually do with the left overs!)

I made this recipe for a few people and it was a big hit.  I used my pressure cooker and the flavors were terrific.  Make sure not to serve this with any powerful side dishes, the flavors of this are subtle.  I followed the recipe rather closely but with the following adjustments:

-I did not remove the skins of the chickpeas, maybe that was suggested to let the chickpeas absorb more flavor?  But I didn't want to do it and it still tasted great.
-I browned the chicken before cooking it in the pressure cooker, which is usually recommended to help "lock in" the flavors.
-I added some frozen spinach to the pot after pressure cooking - added to the recipe without overpowering the flavors and looked gorgeous.

Made this tonight. I'm caring for my twin grandbabies and handicapped husband. I just didn't have time to cook anything tonight that was long and drawn out....this was fast and so delicious!!! Thank you!
This is very good. I used blackberry jelly instead of preserves.  My pkg. of Good Seasons was a 1 oz.  pkg. so I guessed on the 2/3 oz. measurement
Made for Christmas dinner to top a salad of romaine, dried cranberries, mandarin oranges, toasted almonds, feta, and rice sticks. . .everyone loved it.  Thanks!

I was surprised at how good and easy this recipe is.  I did double the amount of raspberry preserves; unfortunately, I could drink this stuff!  May never buy ordinary bottled dressings again.<br/><br/>Thank you!
Oh, my, this is good!  It reminds me of the pies my mother and grandmother used to make.  I used Appleydapply's Recipe #243072  for the crust.  Thanks for recreating a memory for me.
Flavors are great.  I love shrimp and  I will be making this again.  [made for recipe swap #19 Aug '08]
Simple & delicious.  I squashed up the tomatoes right in the pan instead of dirtying up another bowl.  Worked great.  Thank you for a fabulous recipe!

this is SO easy + great flavours too. just made it ahead for tomorrows dinner & will be making it several times over. thanks for the great recipe! i'm not a premium member so haven't been able to email you - but thanks for the photos and great reviews :)

At the time of this review, Sprout 13 is a fairly new member, with one recipe posted....and this is it.  Well all I can say is, Sprout if your other recipes are as good as this one, please post them soon.  Sprout 13 may call this comfort food, but I'd happily serve this dish to company.  We had this with roasties and green veggies as suggested.

This is excellent. I hadn't baked tofu "dry" (ie. not in a casserole or something) before, and it turned out great. The mushroom gravy is wonderful. I made very minor additions - added some garlic powder to the tofu, and Bragg's aminos to the gravy. Yummy! I hope you post more recipes soon!

This turned out really tasty and was pretty easy to make as well. Served it over oven baked potatoes with baked garlic.  Yumm.  It all went perfectly together.  Thanks for submitting this great recipe.  It's a nice new way for me to prepare tofu.  I was surprised that it called for silken tofu, and not firm, but it worked great.  We will make again for sure!
Very good. I added some garlic powder to the gravy.  I have struggled to find main dish tofu recipes that I really like, but this was great.
WOW!! This is SO good. And easy! Wonderful comfort food. Mmmm. I could make this several times a week.

This was great! My first experience with silken tofu. I have to admit (though it worked out) I think i would use firm tofu next time. The gravy was perfect though! I can see making that for a good many things!
This made a yummy lunch today! I halved the recipe and used firm toful. I enjoyed the flavors and liked the way the tofu baked up nice and crispy! Thanks! Made for PAC.
Yum.  Easy, quick and tasty.  I will definitely make this again.

I used sesame oil (to marinate the tofu) and sesame seeds with the mushrooms.  I think it gave it some nice extra flavor.  I must admit that it was way too thick, although it may be due to the fact that I used soy milk instead of regular milk.  I also recommend making sure the tofu is really dry, as mine fell apart.  I think the flavoring was nice though, and I'll probably give it another shot with the proper ingredients because it was so easy...

This was good comfort food. I was a little skeptical that the tofu would crisp up in 35 minutes, so cut mine into 6 slabs instead of 4.  The sauce came together quickly and I used diced baby portabellas instead of white button mushrooms.  I subbed in soy milk. My sauce did end up a bit too thick, so thinned it out a bit before serving.  It was tasty and comforting. I would make this again. Thank you.

Like others i added a garlic, i didn't have any yogurt so i used sour cream and it was still really tasty! I also added a little bit of vegetarian worcestershire sauce.  Thanks for the recipe I will be using it often!

Tai I just fixed this for supper tonite as the kids and I like breakfast for dinner.  I was not WW for us though and that made for a richer more calorie laden casserole that we all loved!  I used regular shredded cheddar, bisquick clone (12648) from zaar, 2% milk and real eggs to make a cup...Popped some refrigerated cinnamon rolls in while it was baking and had that with some cold applesauce.  Kids were dividing up portions to "save" for breakfast ont he run in the morning.  Thanks for a super recipe anytime of the day!

this was soooo great!!!  it smelled so good when it was cooking and is going to be breakfast and lunch in this house!  i didnt have any egg substitute so i used a cup of raw eggs, about 4 large eggs, and alot more cheese, probably 3 cups or more, but it was great!!!!  will definetly make it again!! thank you very much!

I made this casserole for dinner, (In our household we like breakfast any time of day!). I used turkey bacon in place of ham. This took about 10 minutes  longer to cook than than the recipe said. It was pretty tasty.

I made this last night so I'd have breakfast for the week. I substituted 10 pieces of crispy turkey bacon for the ham, but used everything else as called for. This was very easy to make. I found it a little bland for my personal tastes, I added some garlic salt, red pepper flakes, and hot sauce, but I feel like it probably needed a bit more. Overall, however, this was good and I will definitely make it again. It's also quite filling- it's been 2 hrs since breakfast and I'm not hungry again yet. Thanks for sharing.

I was looking for something to make ahead for my week day breakfasts on the go.  I had made a similar dish before and it was really bland, so I jazzed this one up with seasonings at every step.<br/>I used pork sausage (on hand) and added sage and garlic, then cooked bell peppers and onion separately seasoned with oregano, s&p and chili flakes. The potatoes had their own seasoning.<br/> To the Bisquick, I added ancho chili powder (just a little), paprika and s&p. Baked it in a smaller pan for thickness 40 min. When cooled, divided into six pcs and put them into the freezer. Pull one out for breakfast, microwave 1min 30sec, mabe add a little pica de gallo.

Very simple recipe to make.  The muffins came out very moist.  I made these with just vegetable oil as almond oil is very expensive in the NE, as almond oil has an almond flavoring in it I did add almond extract to the vegetable oil.

I have had these in my cookbook a while, looking forward to trying them, and I made them this morning for breakfast. I didn't especially care for them. They looked very appetizing, and there wasn't any one thing about them that I didn't like, they were just so-so. The chocolate part of the batter was very stiff due to the addition of the cocoa powder and it just didn't seem right and didn't marble well. They just didn't have a good taste to me. I used all vegetable oil and a bit of almond extract. The  kids were excited with the marble effect, but no one even finished one. I would not make them again. They were attractive, though!

This was a good tasty frosting. It had the right amount a vanilla flavor. We used it for frosting sugar cookies. The only thing I would do differently is to cream the sugar a bit first because mine was not as warm as I would have liked and so I had to beat it a lot to get rid of the lumps.

Made this soup tonight and it is delicious. I soaked the beans. Cooked for 35 min and then letting pot sit for 10min before I let pressure release. I used spinach because I couldn’t find escarole. The broth is rich and tasty. Adding the sherry vinegar made the soup bright tasting. Highly recommend. I’m sure if you want to make this vegan you can add smoked paprika instead of the chorizo. But please make it with chorizo. This is truly amazing. So flavorful. I’m keeping this in the rotation.

Wow - these were terrific pancakes!  Just loved the nutty flavor and texture of the whole wheat and the cinnamon/honey was a perfect sweetner.  The great thing about these pancakes was they had a hearty taste but were not heavy and dense at all.  Loved these - thanks for sharing your recipe!  Made for Fall Pick-A-Chef 2011

Too much garlic for me.  
I would use some of the garlic and parsley in the boiling pasta.

I cooked the garlic very slowly and it got very mellow and yummy.  My favorite way to have pasta.  Not a very good thing to cook for a date tho, lol.  I added mushrooms the last time I made it, with great results.

Love Garlic and this recipe is so perfect for garlic lovers.  I did add a couple of chopped mushrooms but elsewise made the recipe as stated. Sy lvie this is an easy to make super recipe - Thanks for posting

Fabulous!  I made this with whole wheat spaghetti and the fresh basil as suggested and I've received requests to make it again already.  I used fresh garlic and for my family there is no such thing as too much.  This is one of my favorites.
So easy and very tasty.  I used a little more garlic and added some fresh brocoli and tossed with the pasta.  Then I cut some grape tomatoes in half and added them and it was excellent.

DH had this for dinner tonight and said he'd have liked a little MORE garlic in this LOL. Garlic lover or what? !!! He knows my rating system and is rather critial when it comes to rating his all time favourite Main course: PASTA ! He gave it 4 stars and said he'd like this every now and again. So, here's to what probably is an above average recipe rated severely by the Pasta Master! Thanks !

I loved it, my DH liked it but would only give it 4 stars. I sauted some chicken in the pan first, then cooked the sauce. It got up all the tasty little bits from the chicken. Then I cut the chicken and served it on top. We also added some julienned sun dried tomatoes to the top. I think next time I am going to try it with even more garlic. MMMM thanks for a great recipe.
Delicious! I think I like this better than Tomato sauce. It was SO easy, and so quick!
Used all butter and added 2 chicken bullion cubes. Wonderful, we all devoured it thanks!

Very tasty and quick to make! I did brown the butter and garlic-it added to the flavors, IMHO. Really delicious, Sylvie! Nice flavors to accompany baked chicken. Thanks for posting will make this again!
Easy and tasty. Next time I am going to add sundried tomatoes, mushrooms & peas and serve it with a grilled chicken breast. Thanks for a quick meal idea.
Yum!  I have added a can of petite diced tomatoes with the juice to this, both ways are wonderful!

This is a unique and delicious salad!  I used red delicious and braeburn apples and the parmesan cheese option.  The dressing is terrific and the sweet/tart flavor combines well with the sweet crunchy apples and the salty bacon.  This made a quick and easy lunch that I really enjoyed - thanks for sharing!

I used blue cheese and golden  delicious and they weren't quite sweet (or tart) enough to make this fabulous.  Will make it again tomorrow night with different apples and may re-do my review!  I also think that raisins might be a nice addition to this salad.  Made for Football tag.

I just loved this salad!!!  I only used granny smith apples, as thats what we like and  is what I had on hand.  Then made the rest as written, opting for the parmesan cheese.  Will definitely be making this again, thanks for sharing FloridaNative.  Made for Pot Luck tag.

I used a spring mix for the greens and parmesan for the cheese.  This has a nice tartness making it a wonderful salad.  I also liked the fact that there is a minimal amount of oil in the dressing.  I think that adding toasted walnuts would be a real flavor boost.  Made for *PAC Spring 2009*

AMAZING!!!  The dressing is divine - I make it all the time and I always haev the ingredients on hand!  Instead of bacon, I used bacon bits and instead of the blue cheese, I used reduced fat feta to make it healthier.  SOOO good!

Alrighty!!!  I often eat a "variation of this", but it doesn't include the basil.  Today, I tried this for lunch specifically as posted...only I halved it 'cus it's only me.  This is wonderful, easy, and with ingredients always at hand.  Wonder why I never thought of the basil before, but it made the dish, and I'll never omit it again.  Thanks!
This was exactly what I was looking for! I used half basil and half Italian parsley. Added some pepper at the table. A great, economical meal!!!

I used the jar minced garlic and it worked good.  This is a quick and easy recipe to prepare and have along with any kind of meat or fish really, and it's easy on the budget!  We loved the flavors of the garlic and cheese along with the oil.  I have made this a few times and it's great!  We really like it with the fresh chopped basil, and I have even sauteed mushrooms and onions and added those.  Yummie!

This is the best!! My sister sent me the link and I am so greatfull. My hubby is picky but he loved it. I did add some sliced chicken breast to add some substance.. He has to have some kinda something in it.. LOL.. Anyways.. Thanks.. Will use over  and over..

Delicious! I added a little of the pasta water to make it seem creamy and help the parmesan to really melt in. I used capellini instead of spaghetti and it was perfect. Quick, easy, and a real kid and crowd pleaser!
yum! had this with recipe #107997 and LOVED IT! i didn't have any fresh parsley or basil on hand, so i used crushed red pepper. yum!

My DH has been under the weather and kept talking about the Garlic Spaghetti his italian grandma used to make for him when he was sick.  This was great. He said it was almost like hers.  I cooked the garlic slowly to let the flavor develop and mellow and then added some canned mushrooms.  I also added some pasta water and salt and pepper.
I thought this was good, my boyfriend said it was bland.  It was super quick and easy and I'll probably make it again. Thanks for posting.

I made this for dinner last night & it was GREAT!!  I forgot about the basil/parsley, but I didn't miss it.  Will definately make this again.  Very simple & easy to make & good tasting, the best kind of recipes! :)  Thanks for the good post!
Simple and delicious, we loved this side dish with our Chicken Piccata.  My friends agree it's a keeper and it is a dish that can be shared with many types of meat, chicken and seafood.  Loved it!
My new favorite spaghetti sauce! This tastes just like a scampi sauce at an excellent italian restuarant in NJ we go to. So easy to make and it tastes awesome!
This is very good and so simple! I like to make this on nights where I don't feel like putting a whole lot of effort into cooking but still want something good and homemade! Thanks for posting!
If you love garlic this recipie hits the spot.  Awesome
Simple to prepare and delicious too!

My children really love pasta and ask for it often, and since it's such a kid pleaser we have it at least twice a week, and sometimes for lunch!  I don't add the basil for the kids.  A keeper at our house!

this is so scrumptious!!  my only changes/additions were to use angel hair pasta, flat-leaf parsley and added salt and pepper. great side for italian dishes, i paired this with stuffed bell peppers!  thanks for a great recipe, sylvie!

Simple to whip together and great flavors. I used fresh Italian parsley instead of basil, and Asiago cheese instead of Parmesan (personal preference). I served this alongside Pork Chops w/ Mushroom Madeira Sauce (from the Food Network). It went well together! Thanks for posting!

This was amazingly good!  My family does not like spaghetti... especially DH and myself.  But all of us loved this!  I'm so happy to find this, I've always mourned having this cheap dish and now I can serve it!

This was just ok for me.. I thought it was going to be more flavourful then it was so I was a bit disappointed.  I used 3/4 box speghetti and tons of parmesan to give it more flavour.  It was really easy to whip up but I don't think this is a keeper for me.

My boyfriend hates tomatoes, so he doesn't typically like spaghetti. So I tried making this recipe instead. He loves greesy foods. So he loved this recipe. It is a very plain tasting. So what you should do to help it out is add a meat, and salt and pepper. It has alot of butter, so I would use less buter and less olive oil. I will be making this again.

Tomato sauce has its moments but it is usually way too thick (people add paste, no wonder). I usually add that by adding generous amounts of red wine. But what seemed to provide the most flavor to this was the Parmesan.

I found this recipe today...I'm amazed at the reviews saying this has little flavor. Most of the other recipes I've found for this sauce use a clove or two of garlic...this one uses a half cup...where does the flavor go? Excellent. We cooked the 'sauce' with jumbo shrimp and added a few sun-dried tomatoes. Will certainly make this meal again.
I made it and thought it was delicious!
This was almost perfect. I added a ton of sweet onions and some cheub tomatoes. That made all the difference in the world!!!! Also, i let it cook very slowly on low heat, which added to the flavor.

this is a great dish! Might I suggest an addition though? Get a few boneless chicken thighs (about 5) and cook till brown with some Salt & pepper and olive oil ( about 5-7 minutes each side on a high flame) then remove the chicken from the pan and stir in about a tablespoon of Italian Seasoning and 2 chopped garlic cloves until fragrant stirring not to burn the garlic, then add half a cup of chicken broth and reduce by half (about 5 minutes) then add in a tablespoon of butter and melt it through. Add the chicken back to the pan and spoon the sauce over top, then put the chicken on top of the pasta and this makes a GREAT meal :)

DH and I really enjoyed this recipe.  I flattened the chicken so it would cook evenly.  I spooned the glaze over the chicken and sprinkled some hot pepper flakes on top.  Thanks for an easy and tasty recipe.
It is really delicious! Just a little suggstion; amount lemon juice can be increased. Thanks a lot!
Yummy! I modified it 2 ways - first, added a bit of chili pepper oil for a bit of kick and flavor; second, left the skins on the pepper - more smoky flavor that way. Cheers!

I made just a couple of changes to this soup based on some comments I read on a different site that had this recipe.  I used vegetable broth in place of water and only 3 cups instead of 4.  I also added more curry powder than called for.<br/>This was a nice thick rich soup and tasted even better when I drizzled a little olive oil on my serving.  <br/>Very nice, I would recommend this recipe.
This is amazing!  It is so good and sooo easy to make.  Thanks for a keeper in my cookbook!
I tried this for my 4 year old who loves pasta and cheese, it was a hit with the family! Very easy to make!

This was pretty good. I liked the addition of the parmesan cheese.  I think I would have preferred stirring the sauce and the noodles together rather than pouring it on top.  I will try it again that way.  Thanks for the recipe!!
I have tried several bistec encebollado recipes and this is by far my favorite.  Will be making it again tonight!
Very good recipe.  Thank you for posting it.  My whole family enjoyed it very much.
this is by far the best bistec encebollado i've ever tasted it was very easy to prepare and the taste was outstanding...thanks!!
Delicious - and quick and easy.

This had great flavor. I followed the recipe exactly, except I substituted lime juice for the vinegar.  The lime juice was a bit strong for my husband, but I liked it.  I used thin cut ribeye steaks, and pounded them down to 1/4 thickness. So Good! I will be making this again and again. Thank you for the recipe!!

I have made this today with a temp of 48* outside....and it is true...after 2 hours....I even had neighbors come over and ask what I was fixing.....I always have baking powdered biscuits with this meal.....
The only change I do....is my kids like chopped tomatoes and a TON of different spices.....I love this recipe and it will stay in my recipe box for generations to come!!
This is the best beef stew! Easy and delicious, what could be better than that? The aroma and flavor is amazing. Yum!!

Delicious!!  This was ridiculously easy to put together and smelled incredible the whole day.  My DSs were bugging me for hours about when dinner was happening.  Absolute perfect comfort food.  Thanks so much for the recipe!

I got the recipe from my husband's Grandmother and have made it for years. It's the best stew and so easy. I also like to add celery and if you don't have tomato soup you can use tomato sauce and about 1/2 can of water and you can use cornstarch in the place of tapioca.
Comfort food! This is the only beef stew recipe ever I make now. Its cooking right now, and smells amazing in here, even though it has 2 hours to go.

Great Cake! I have made this for years. One thing I do different is I add 1oz of rum to the batter and a small drizzle of rum into the sauce to give it a little kick try it is is really gooooooooooooood!
Excellent cake! Might also be good if apples were added to the batter.

This is the same recipe for a bakery called "Big Mama's" that was shown one the Foodnetwork. I was so happy to be able to get the recipe online because it sure looked good. The chef gave all the ingredients with the exception of the flour and buttermilk. This cake is very moist and rich and has somewhat of a Southern quality to it. This is going to become one of my regulars to sell now. I'll add some vanilla flavoring to my caramel sauce and make another small tweak to make it my own. It definitely worth sharing and making for others to enjoy.
I am so very glad that I found this recipe. This cake was very moist and delicious. My family really enjoyed it and they all wanted the recipe. I will continue to use this recipe over and over again.

Amazing!

Aside from skipping the banana due to my daughter's sudden dislike of the fruit, I used all of the ingredients. It was a big hit with her. I included the banana & the strawberries (frozen) & opted out of the ice cubes since it was already pretty thick & chilled! I did, however, add almost another 1/4 cup of the juice! GREAT TASTING SMOOTHIE ~ Thanks for sharing! [Tagged, made & reviewed in This Round's On Me!]

Another wonderful smoothie from JanuaryBride. We enjoyed this tasty treat very much. I did use the banana, strawberry, pineapple and kiwi options, am I ever glad that I did. What a great way to get our daily fruit.

This was delicious - and I could make it with what I had on hand.  I forgot to add the pineapple juice, but it was fine without it.  I didn't have a banana, and I used about 2 t of sugar in place of the artificial sweetener.  I could have used 1 t I think, as it was sweet enough naturally.  Thanks for a great recipe!
This was yummy!!! I made this recipe just as it is written and added a splash of orange juice. I let my son taste it and he loved it also. I will definitely be making this again.

I really enjoyed this smoothie. I added the banana and wanted to add some frozen strawberries, but someone had eaten them all - no matter. It was great, as written. I did add a squirt of honey, to suit my taste. This was very refreshing, JanuaryBride. Thanks for sharing!

5 stars of yum from here!   I reduced the recipe to make 1 TBS rub for two salmon filets,  I used hot smoked paprika and cayenne instead of the red pepper flakes. This mix might be intended but it will be a great seasoning for anything fauna or flora. I skipped the pepper flakes and added 1/4 tsp of chayenne. I could practically feel my arteries clogging, but I couldn't resist. This is one yummy snack. I used 100% pure Maine maple syrup.

Wow, this was tasty.  I used Smart Balance Light for the butter and real maple syrup.  I halved the recipe using about half of a 1lb beef summer sausage. I drizzled some butter/syrup onto the slices after they were done  Thanks for sharing Michelle_My_Belle! :)  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.

Tried this variation today to switch it up a bit with our regular Sunday cook-out. This dish has now replaced them all! Everything I've made in the past seems mediocre. Can't wait to see what you come up with next!
A very nice pea salad! Alot of flavors! I halved the recipe. Thanks!

Very good!  It reminds me of the Hot Pockets.  Instead of making the pastry, I used the jumbo refrigerator biscuits and flattened each one out and filled as directed. I'm sure i'll be making these again!

This recipe turned out really tasty, but "fantabulous" is still not a word.

Really delicious recipe.  I did add two boiled eggs to it, I just like them!  It is fantabulous of you to share!! I believe it is on its way of being a word, there are 31 fantabulous recipes on Recipezaar!!!! Thanks for sharing.

This was FANTABULOUS!!!!   I LOVED the brown mustard in this!  I usually have a "go to" German Potato Salad recipe that I use, but I wanted something different this time.  And, it was a hit at the cookout I went to.  Thank you Niki S for posting this recipe.
Really, really good! Went great with my German Bratwurst tonight!

This was AWESOME!!! Fantabulous is an understatement in my book. I tripled the recipe easily, for I served this at a recent baby shower and all the ladies loved it! This is my new keeper for a german potato salad. Thank you for posting!
Absolutely perfect.  I put in a little less sugar because I don't like it to taste as sweet, but it turned out great.  This is a keeper.

This was awesome! We really like this a lot.  Although, I drained off most (certainly not all) of the fat, reduced the sugar a smidge and reduced the flour a bit to make up for the smaller amt of fat.   It turned out lovely.

Delicious chocolate sauce! I served this with French vanilla ice cream. Really good and easy! Thanks for sharing. Made for Gimme 5 tag.
This was very, very good. Great consistency and taste.
Yep, it's fast, it's easy, it's a winner!!!  I used dark choc instead of unsweetened but it was still fab.  A pressie for you...made for the 12 Days of Christmas Aussie Swap 12/08. :)

YUM, yum, YUM, yum!!!  Did I say YUM??!!  Syd this is wonderfully smooth and tasty sauce.  I used it warmed in a small crockpot and served with fresh pineapple, apples and strawberries. Oh my, Syd!! This is a fantastic sauce. I will use it later today as a topping for brownies, but of course had to taste test after making! The corn syrup does the trick and the smoothness is just fantastic. I know that this will be a hit. I made 1/4 of the recipe which worked fine. Made for PRMR

Fresh and yummy! I did not have fresh basil so I used some fresh oregano and a little dried basil. Loved the extra vinegar that I garnished the dish with. Gave it that zing that is so often missing in 'diet' foods!

Surprising hit with my family!! I tried green chilies since I had no olives & added a pinch of sugar with the chilie powder. Good for a change.. Surely a keeper!

Really tastey and filling.  I made this in two stages. First I made the meat mixture the night before and the corn meal topping the night I served it, then I put it together and put it in the oven. Absolutely loved this! My husband loved it as well.  I put the leftovers through the blender, and my baby daughter loved it as well! Will definitely be making this again!

This is the BEST casserole I have ever made.  I made enough to have leftovers only there weren't any!  Next time I am going to double the cornbread topping. It was absolutely fantastic. Really yummy. Just the right amount of spices for me. I used corn fresh from the cob that I froze last week -- delicious. My husband had THIRDS! Thanks.

loved it!!!!

Mm, mm, mmm! These were easy to make and tasted delicious. I brought them to my sister's house when we went to visit and when she had company everyone liked them. I added an extra handful of marshmallows.

I split 2 wholemeal/wholegrain rolls and the DM and I thoroughly enjoyed this for lunch today. A wonderful foodstuff: as most supermarkets now carry Jasmine and Basmati rice, it is to be hoped Black (Forbidden) Rice, too, will become widely available. Apart from its striking color and taste, it should be noted that the rice is chock-full of antioxidants, and a good amount of high quality protein as well.  I buy it online from Lotus Foods and they have a particularly nice recipe on their package. But this is a good, all purpose procedure. I like to saute the rice lightly in a little ghee, clarified butter, canola or peanut oil before adding the water.
Way too much water.  I would use 1 cup black rice and 1.5 cup water next time...

I use 1.5 cups of liquid to 1 cup of rice.  This rice does not absorb liquids and puff up like other rice varieties, so I find 2 cups of liquid makes it a wet mess.  I have to cook it for an hour.  Also, add salt unless you are using bouillion cubes or Better Than Bouillon concentrate (what I use instead of canned stock).  I always add spices and raisons/dried fruit and onions and nuts - what ever you want for a sweet rice or a savory rice.  And I make a ton of it and then freeze it in small containers.  It freezes well, so I can include this easily into a 30 minute weeknight meal.

I quite agree with Hiromi and jashley1000: Use 1.5 parts water to one part rice. Cooking rice can be a moving target because it can retain different amounts of water depending on how old and/or dried out it is. You can always add water, but I found the recommended ration 2 to 1 water to rice to produce rice that was too mushy. If you get stuck with mushy rice, you can always heat in the oven at a slow temp to dry it out, but better to get it right first time around.
