best rolls I have ever smelt/eaten
These are fantastic!  They disappear quick so be sure to make lots of them.

These are so good! I made them to go with soup, I started them too late so instead we ate them for a snack last night. I will be making these often, they are so easy and yummy! Thanks P.B. & Jayne for a great roll recipe!

I used regular button mushrooms and made about 16.  This would be great on a buffet as even when at room temp they were very tasty.  Instead of baking I put on foil on indirect heat on the hot grill for about 20 minutes total.  This is a keeper!!

I served these with pesto tortellini and grilled salmon, as a side dish, rather than appetizer. They have a nice flavour and the ricotta makes them very creamy. I probably wouldn't hollow them out next time and just pile the stuffing on top, as they went very flat in the oven, which I assume was because of taking the whole stem and gills out. Thanks for sharing! :)

All I can say is Wow!!! They are sooo delicious!! Instead of big mushrooms I used bunch of small ones and did not change anything else. I love all kinds of stuffed mushrooms and this is a first time I've made them myself. I could not stop eating. The filling is full of flavor and very creamy. I added extra mozzarella cheese on top in the last 3 minutes of cooking. I will make this recipe often! Thank you for a great treat!
I can not put into words how much we loved these mushrooms, I passed the recipe on to family! I used the regular button mushrooms, also. They were creamy and delicious.  Thanks for sharing!
Very, very good!  Made these tonight and they were loved by all!
I fixed these for Super Bowl Sunday to go with our Spaghetti with Red Clam sauce. They were outstanding!
I fixed these as a side dish with Recipe #23425 and they were fabulous.  All we added was salt but otherwise we followed as written.  Thanks for an easy, tasty recipe!

The Mushrooms were great Wildflour.  We did have a lot of left over stuffing mix as the 10 button stuffing mushrooms were in various sizes.  I will try and get more than 10 next time or try larger mushrooms.  Otherwise a great recipe.  They were our appetizer and they were very easy to prepare.

Thank you for posting Wildflour! These were delicious. They were pretty easy to make although it took me more that 10 minutes preparation.  There was a lot of "stuffing" left over so I could make two cookie sheets full and I'll make another batch tomorrow. Very yummy. Everyone enjoyed. Best right out of the oven for sharpest flavors. Enjoy them they are great. ChefDLH

I cut the filling in half, and still had 12 large mushrooms full of the cheese mixture.  I also added a couple of garlic gloves, because it's all better with garlic.  Easy to put together, flavor was great, will definitely save this one to do again.

Love the 'shrooms. I am a pesto lover and am always looking for new pesto recipes. I used portabello mushrooms. (as they are my favorite) I wasn't sure about the ricotta with everything else but it was perfect. I too added a little bit of sea salt. Will be making again for Christmas Eve.
What a great side dish, appetizer, anytime dish.  I didn't have ricotta and used whipped cottage cheese and greek yogurt instead.
So Easy, So Good!

this is a tasty roll! iv'e made it many times, when i have a few left over which is rare, i cut them in cubes and bake them on a cookie sheet in the oven for 5 min. then i let them cool on a plate. i put them in a ziplock bag and save for soup or salad as croutons.

These rolls are delicious!  I made them last night to go with beef stew and they were a perfect accompaniment.  It was very easy to throw the ingredients in the bread machine and shaping and baking was no problem.  I did have to bake longer than 30 minutes ~ about 40 to get them as brown as I like.  They smelled delish when baking.  Thanks for posting!

I must admit,my dough was very sticky and hard to work with,but that has everything to do with my machine and nothing to do with the recipe.I just used a LOT of extra flour and had to work fast while shaping them.I made some into rolls and made one little loaf.It was worth persevering.The end results were fantastic.They were light and fluffy and smelt delicious.
UPDATE:These are some of the most popular rolls that I make,and are constantly requested.They turn out perfectly every time,and it never ceases to amaze us just how soft and delicious these are.Thanks for a lovely recipe.

I took these to a BBQ and they were gone in no time flat. The hostess even hid some in the freezer for later consumption. :)
The dough formed a perfect ball in the BM, though was a little sticky coming out of the pan. Working with it on a floured surface solved that and it was really easy to form into balls. Thank you for a unique and very tasty recipe!

I really wanted to love these but I just don't.  I made these 3 days ago and only 6 of the 24 rolls have been eaten.  The texture isn't what I was expecting and wasn't what I was looking for when I set out to find a recipe to go with my spaghetti dinner.  These are heavier than I had anticipated, not the light fluffy I thought they would be.

These were wonderful, we had them with baked ziti and a salad so we had plenty left over, the recipe really makes a large amount. I decided to use the leftover rolls as my "bread" in my stuffing recipe and boy did that pay off, everyone loved that too. Thank you for sharing such a great recipe.We will make this over and over again.

Made these rolls to serve at our 4th of July barbeque and what a hit.  They rose so nice and baked up with a yummy crusty outside and so light and airy on the inside and the parm on the crust made for a great flavor sensation.  They only thing I did different was add some wheat gluten to the mix for extra rise.  I'll be using these again specially when serving Italian food.  Thanks so much for posting.

I thought these were pretty and had a nice texture.  They were a little too sweet for us, but would be better paired with breakfast/ brunch instead. I liked that the recipe was for 6 muffins and utilized yogurt.  I used greek yogurt and fat free mayo with good results.  Made for PAC 2014.
These ones took us a little bit longer to make as there is a little bit more work involved in it.  The taste however is fully worth it in the end.  We really had a great weekend making all of these.

Bergy, Thank you for posting this, This is definitely a Five Star recipe. I made it last night and the taste was "MARVELOUS". My boyfriend Marvin loved this so much, he took the rest of the leftovers home with him. I will have to fix this again real soon and I won't tell my boyfriend Marvin, so at least I can have some leftover. Thanks again. Melody
Bergy, Love this recipe!!! It was excellent. I posted a few photos for you. Thanks for sharing. Lisa
These were very good. Made for Chinese New Year Dimsum for my Red Hat group. Couldn't find leaves and didn't want to use foil so parchment paper worked well. Can always trust Bergy's recipes!

These are......well they're.........hm, whats the word? AWESOME!!! If I had any less self control I would have eaten them ALL at once. I could eat these for breakfast, lunch and dinner. I do not see a time when I will not want to eat these. Now I just need to find a place to get bamboo leaves! THANK YOU FOR THIS RECIPE!!!!!
UPDATE: I made these with a Japanese twist. I did not mix the chicken/mushroom mixture into the flavored cooked rice, instead I "stuffed" the bundles. Thanks again Bergy, I love you (and your recipes)!

I made this for an appy for dinner guests and it was a huge hit! I used fresh chives from my garden, and added a little garlic, served it with pita crisps.
Thanks for posting!

I used dijon mustard in this--that's French, isn't it? Had it for breakfast on a bagel. I had a half-block of cream cheese to use up, so just made half a recipe, but still have some left for tomorrow--yippee! It's savory with just a bit of sharpness and the sprouts add a nice crunch.
The chives in my garden were going crazy, so I'm glad I found this recipe.  The flavor of chives really shines is this spread.  I served this with crackers.  Very enjoyable and elegant for company.

Really great guacamole and so simple to make!  My avocados were not too ripe so this came out a little chunkier than anticipated, but still good.  I did leave out the cilantro (can't stand the stuff!).  Will make again!!  Made for PAC Spring 2011.
Fresh peaches are in season and the Spring lamb chops are fresh.  They are are a perfect blend on an early summer evening.

This was UNBELIEVABLY good!!! I would give it 10 stars if I could. We had this for Easter dinner, and I think I ate a pound of it all by myself (and I'm not a fan of red meat)! David baked the 3-1/2 lb brisket in a foil-covered pan at 250 degrees for 5 hrs, then topped it with the BBQ sauce (made same amount as for larger brisket and used every last drop!) and baked it uncovered for another hour to carmelize it. I should mention that David marinated the meat for 24 hrs in the seasoning as well as Natural Pecan-Flavored Liquid Smoke in a vacuum-sealed bag (Food Saver). The meat was tender, juicy, falling apart, and melt-in-your-mouth YUMMY!!! Much to my delight, it made even better sandwiches the next day. OUTSTANDING recipe, WI Cheesehead. Thank you so much!

This recipe is sooooo good and sooooo simple. I cooked the brisket in the oven, followed the recipe exactly, and it turned out amazing. I served it for several friends and had them all requesting the recipe. Trust me. This one is really good.

This is a very nice salad that I think everyone will like.  All of the flavors blend well together.  I used sugar snap beans in place of both the green beans and peas and I did not blanch anything.  The flavors and textures were just right after sitting for 6 to 8 hours.  I also didn't add any water and the vegetables did provide their own.  The more I ate this, the better I liked it.  Made for PAC, Spring 2012.

I am only rating the filling, cuz I cannot have nuts, but the filling was incredible! LOL  I drizzled Chocolate Fudge Sundae sauce (recipe #45027)over the top, and it was soo good!  Thanks!

This was fantastic!  The crust really gave this pie that extra kick...the contrast of the pecans in the crust was really delicious.
The filling had just the right peanut butter flavor, although it was a little bit rich...can't eat too big of a slice!  But overall, this was a real winner!  Thanks for the recipe.

OOOOOH! This is one rich pie! I ran out of graham cracker crumbs and had to use 1/2 cup oreo cookie crumbs to make up the difference but it was still great. Just remember to keep it chilled right until serving time as it tends to not stay as firm.I garnished this with a dap of whipped cream and a scoop of creamy peanut butter. Thanks for posting!

Wow, this was a fantastic chicken dish!  We really enjoyed the flavors the prosciutto and cheese imparted to the chicken.  My dh doesn't like parmesan cheese, so I subbed colby jack for the parm.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly.  I served this with marinated tomatoes, green beans and french bread.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

Another winner from Charmie!!! Was just perfect! With a substitution of white wine for the chicken stock--very, very flavorful! Made for PAC 07.
Thx for this delicious entree!

Substantial & satisfying, this bread is full of hearty flavor and makes a most excellent slice of toast! I kneaded the dough in my KitchenAid stand mixer and baked the loaf at 350° for 35 minutes. This turned out to be an excellent bread. It's a hearty whole-grain bread with the added interest of the sesame seeds. Toast from this loaf is to die for!

You just have to love the simple recipes! This was delicious. My husband mmmm'd his way thrugh dinner again. When he does that, it's usually a 5 star recipe. I took your suggestion and served a mushroom pilaf and green beans with it. :)

Excellent!! I'm not normally a lover of Swiss cheese, but all of these ingredients were wonderful together. I made this with Recipe #121513 and Recipe #61267 and this is the best dinner I've had on the tour so far. Thanks so much Charmie! This will be repeated often. Made for ZWT4.

excellent!!  made as written with the exception of seasoning the flour with salt, pepper and cayenne and garnishing with fresh parsley.  this is a yummy keeper recipe!  served with Recipe#69186 and Recipe#88634!
Easy to make.  I made it ahead of time then popped it in the oven for 10 min.   I used chicken tenders and it came out great!  Juicy with great flavor.  I served it with creamed spinach and risotto.

Whaaat?  I never reviewed this?  I must have made this a dozen times, and it is fabulous every time.  Elegant looking, and oh so delicious.  Whenever I'm trying to impress, I make this recipe.  It is so easy, goes together in minutes, and everyone absolutely loves it.  My favorite!
This was fabulous!!  I made it with the Cod.  My husband and I both loved it!
These were really good burgers.  I made them using by on dry onion soup mix and the rest was pretty much as directed.  I also cooked them on my George Foreman Grill instead of in the oven.

This was a really nice recipe.  I think the directions could be a little clearer regarding step #1. I chose to consider this an oversight & go with the ingredients listed.  It turned out to be very well recieved. Made, enjoyed & reviewed for Pick-A-Chef Spring 2008.

3 1/2 stars! This was a good chicken recipe, though not as special as I had thought it would be. I thought the beer made the bacon a little too soggy, and would probably finish it in the oven next time. Overall made a great dinner entree for the family. Made for PAC spring '11

Based on Chef Jean's review, I decided to change the cooking method a bit. I placed 1/4 cup beer in a casserole dish with a rack, and after searing the bacon wrapped breasts in the frypan, I placed them onto the rack and baked at 350F for about 20-30 minutes. We couldn't really taste the beer (perhaps if I covered the pan, but then the bacon would not be crispy), but the chicken was fabulous. I left out the 'magic seasoning' as I have never heard of it. Just need to figure out how to get the beer flavor without the bacon getting soggy. Overall a nice recipe. Made for PRMR.

This chicken dish is wonderful and flavorful! That said, based on other reviews, I also made a couple of changes. I used essence, in place of the Paul Prudhomme's, as it is what was on hand. I reduced this, for only 1 huge breast. I did NOT heat my cast iron skillet to high, perhaps medium high, cooking on each sides for approximately 5 minutes. I finished the breast in the oven, due to size, adding the beer, and cooking at 350 for about 20 minutes, flipping once throughout the 20 minutes, to keep the bacon kinda crispy. The flavor imparted by the beer is tasty, as is the dry rub AND the bacon (I used applewood smoked.) Thanks so much for sharing, purple raider.

These were so yummy, a bit like an apricot health bar in taste. Very easy & very quick to make. 
I actually didnt have coconut milk but substituted by using Creamy Coconut Milk Recipe #26714 by mielhollinger, and they turned out fantastic.
They didn't last long here, but I think (actually I know) I made the balls a little too big because I only got 20.
DH would like them again to take to work and everyone loved them.
Great recipe Jubes, and I will be making these again.

These are quick, easy and so delicious. I live on the other side of the world now and these so reminded me of Aussie health bars, we can not get anything like it here in Switzerland. My whole family loved them and I had to ask them not eat them all as I want to take a few to mum's so that they can all try them,  I know they will absolutely love these. I made as is but found I needed quite a bit more coconut milk than stated but that is neither here nor there. A super recipe Jubes I will be hanging onto this one as it gives me a little taste of home that is so healthy too. :)
Made a tiny boo boo today. Okaaaaayyyyy, so maybe it was a really BIG one, but nothing a little martini couldn't take care of.

I made this for my Valentine's Day/anniversary meal. The day didn't turn out exactly as I had planned, but this dish was fabulous. OH LESLIE!!!! These potatoes are SINFUL!!!! But soooo good!!!!! Awesome!!  Everyone will ask for the recipe!!!

Oh my these were good! I made a 9x9 pan and if I had made more, we would have eaten them too! So creamy, and gruyere was the perfect choice! I also had to add about 20 of additional cooking time. Thank You for sharing. Made for ZWT4

Wow!  We enjoyed these so much.  The creamy cheesy texture just melted in your mouth.  I did add some bacon bits to the top layer. These were absolutely delicious!  We had my brother over for dinner and he had three helpings!  I made them just as written and wouldn't change a thing!

Very good potatoes that are not diet friendly but taste great! I sliced the potatoes by hand so some of my slices were thicker than others and had to bake a bit longer. Awesome! I made these with a russet potato and cut the recipe back to 2 servings. Now I wish that I'd made the whole recipe. These truly are decadent! So easy and yummy. Reviewed for ZWT7- THese potatoes were so good- creamy and cheesey- delicious. I couldn't get red potatoes so used nadine potatoes instead. Used freshly grated nutmeg and ground pepper for this dish. Photo also to be posted
From a cook to cooks, this is a wonderful recipe. It is not dense as some au gratin potatoes can be; it is not light but a delight to all who partake.
What an awesome recipe!  Make as written and wouldn't change a thing.

I have to say that this is by far the best tasting cheesecake I have ever tasted! The crust was so delicious and the cheesecake had just enough lime flavor as to not overpower but add a nice zest. This was a truly amazing dessert!! Thanks for posting!!
Kids like ranch dressing so this was a new way to get some cabbage into their diet.

quite yummy if you are a ranch lover!

I wiill be making these again & often, Thank you MaeEast.

No big thing, but there seems to be a step missing between 5 & 6, the one that has me cutting the dough into a dozen cookies! Thank you for that recipe.  It is true that it is quick, easy and delicious. I did not have enough because everybody wanted a second bowl. It is a keeper.

Oh boy, this is yummy stuff!  I had originally tagged this in the Games forum but someone beat me to it.  I wasn't going to let that stop me from making this recipe!  I pulsed the peppers in the food processor.  I also added just a bit of cayenne pepper, we like our pepper spreads with some kick to it. Just made this for a group gathering I'm having in a day or so, & it is gonna be an OUTSTANDING spread for finger food! I've never before used the red bells for anything other than a fresh salad, but this recipe takes them to a whole other level!! Thanks for sharing it!

This turned out AWESOME!

Dh says 5 stars for sure.  I made this using dry lemon-flavored drink mix, ie Chrystal Light.  He's the lemon fan so they were made just for him.  I made popsicle molds of small paper cups and wooden popsicle sticks I found at the local crafts store.  Just peel off the cups when ready to serve.

In the words of a 3 and a half year old "Mmmm, this is yummy, Mommy!" I agree. Thanks for a great, versatile recipe!
Such a good healthy alternative.  My preschooler loves these.

excellent! i used spanish style rice. no celery. 4 peppers instead of 6, was just for my husband and i. thanks! :)

This was easy and delicious.  My granddaughter loved making them.  We used bathroom cups because that's what we had.  I used the vanilla yogurt too.  Now her mother is asking for the recipt.

My three boys absolutely loved these. Doubled the recipe, using a 12 oz. frozen 100% juice pomegranate cherry blend, and since I used plain yogurt, added 1/4 cup sugar. With vanilla yogurt, no extra sweetner would have been necessary, also would depend on the type of juice used. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I doubled the recipe and froze them in plastic cups. They're awesome. I used Welch's 100% Orange Pineapple juice and vanilla yogurt as suggested by others and half cup sugar. other then I followed the directions just doubled the recipe as not to waste the juice or yogurt. These are awesome my kids love them.
I used orange juice and doubled the recipe.  I ended up with an Orange Julius like mix, and had a cup leftover to drink.  Tasty!
Very, very good.  My son loves these.  He likes tangy/sour things, so using plain yogurt and juice concentrate without added sugar works perfectly for us.  Thank you for posting!
These are great!  I use 100% (organic) juice and can feel great about giving this wholesome treat to my toddler-who loves it!  Thanks Serendipity Elizabeth....

Easy and basic no-frills deviled eggs.  These are great to take to potlucks because they generally will please everyone.... even the picky eaters.  Sprinkled with paprika, they make a lovely presentation, too!  Thanx for posting Bobby's recipe!
great eggs  made em for the 4th

I made these when I was visiting my new boyfriend in wi. Marie not knowing he didn't like oatmeal. So I got to eat them  all myself the best cookie I ever ate thank you for the recipe. I just added 2 tea of pumpkin pie spice  in place of the cloves and cinnamon. Was awesomee

These cookies are Excellent.

Very good.  Simmering the raisins give them a very sweet taste.  I felt that they could have used a little more oatmeal though.  Next time, I think I'll add 1/2 cup more.  Thanks, Marie, for another great recipe.
This receipe is amazing!  Even our friends that are not big oatmeal raisin cookie fans love them!  They turn out so nice and moist.  Thanks for the great receipe!

I've made these for 40+ years (compliments of my old tried & true 1964 Betty Crocker Cooky Book)and love how they always turn out.

Well, the smell of Oatmeal raisin cookies warms the air in my home as the temperature drops to -48 degrees F outside. I followed the recipe exactly however I did add semi sweet mini chocolate chips to the last third of the dough so that my little one would eat them. Instead of dropping a teaspoon full on the parchment lined cookie sheet(like I was suppose to after re- reading the recipe before writing my comment) I used a rounded tablespoon. This review is from my husband , I don't like oatmeal raisin cookies , but he loves them, so I made them for him.

These are the first oatmeal cookies I have baked that I liked. My only suggestion would be to make sure you boil the raisins WAY ahead of time to give them time to cool. I poured the raisin liquid in the cream mixture immediately after it finished and it melted the cream mixture and the cookies were terrible. I did let them cool for the second batch (the next day when I was a little more alert) and they went off without a hitch. Also, it didn't specify quick-cooking oats or the regular kind, but quick-cooking works great. Great recipe!

These are the BEST oatmeal cookies I have ever made.  The raisins reminds me of Mom's homemade raisin pie, the spices fills the house with such a wonderful aroma, and this is one recipe I am going to keep forever.

Good, but these are more "cake-like" than I prefer.  Nice flavors.  I added a few extra raisins and nuts with great results.  I guess I prefer the recipes that call for butter instead of shortening.  Thanks for sharing!

Well, I never can leave well enough alone! These are great cookies! So, the second time I made them, I subbed dried blueberries (DH & 2 sons) don't like raisins. Hi! I thought I'd throw in my 2 cents (or, ok, there are no "pennies" in NZ so maybe I'll throw in my 5 cents worth ;)). My husband is a kiwi and left NZ to marry me and move to the USA where we now live with our 2 sons. I haven't been able to find anything like malt biscuits in the grocery shop but I did manange to find a store in the SF Bay Area (CA, USA) that sells kiwi foods so we pick up the malt biscuits there. You might want to try graham crackers, I haven't tried it but they might be similar. If you want details to the shop email me at ocean413@yahoo.com. Here is the way I made the lolly cake...and my kiwi hubby put his stamp of approval on it. Enjoy...they are YUMMY! :)

The above recipe is perfect, if you need a USA Conversion version of the Lolly Cake, here it is:

7 TBSP butter, melted
1 pkt malt biscuits, crushed
1/2 c sweetened condensed milk
2.5 c mini marshmallows 
finely chopped coconut

Mix together butter, biscuits, condensed milk and marshmallows. Sprinkle coconut onto wax paper, shape dough into a log and roll in coconut. Fold wax paper aroung log and refrigerate until firm (a couple hours usually) and then slice into rounds.

Have a nice day!
Tiffany :)

I recommend actually measuring the lemon juice.  I used 1/2 of what I thought was a medium lemon, but the lemon flavor was VERY strong, so I suspect I used too much.  Still, the flavors were delightful together, and I'll definitely make these again being more careful with the amount of lemon juice.

Wonderful combination of spices.  It was pretty AND tasty and the directions easy to follow.  Thanks Bev for a great recipe that I'll be using often.  I'd bought some Herbs de Provence and had never used it before but I will be using it a lot from now on.
I made these to go along with our Easter dinner this year.  They came out wonderfully and the spices were just perfect.  I will make these again with roasts etc.  They were delicious!
Good basic potato recipe.  Thanks.
Absolutely gorgeous! Have made these twice now both times with recipe#28199. Simply stunning. Thank you!

The lemon juice gave this dish a brightness that really highlighted the flavor of the herbes de provence. Simple, delicious, and a bit out of the ordinary. This will be my go-to potato dish. I might also try this with roasted potatoes -- I think the crunch of the potatoes will add another wonderful level to the dish.

I made these to have with our special steak dinner and they were awesome!  I sprinkled with Rosemary for the herb and proceeded with the recipe, but baked them in the oven sprinkled with a little olive oil.  We loved them!  They had such great flavor and was the perfect side dish to our meal for Valentine's Day.  Thanks for sharing!  Mike

I've made these every week for a month now and love them.  This is my daughter's new favorite potato recipe.  Giving them only 4 stars and 5 with some modifications.  I wedge the potatoes and then saute them longer (15 mins) until golden brown on all three sides.  My husband said, "how do you get them crispy on the outside and smooshy good on the inside?"
Scrumptious! I cooked them a bit longer than just heating through and they turned out like roasted potatoes.
Oh, these taters are so yummy!
Wonderful, easy, cooked potatoes longer in oil and butter to get some crispness.

This was quick and easy to make (I reduced it to one serving) and surprisingly good - I'm not usually a a tofu eater. The chocolate tofu mix is very rich and has a bit of a tang - kind of like frozen yogurt. Two things that I found conflicting - Tofu comes in firm, medium, silken and soft - I did see one silken medium but that was it, no firm silken,  so I went with the silken  I served this over 3 berry blend as suggested,  which was a nice combination. Also, why call for dark chocolate and then add sugar? I used Fran's Bittersweet Chocolate. My DD who is lactose intolerant  liked it even though she doesn't care for very rich things - she thought it would be good with cake. Thanks Lynn for taking me outside my normal cooking zone. Made for the Comfort Cafe Recipe of the Day July 09
Very easy to make.  It has an unusual texture that I am not used to.  It is very chocolately. Made for the Summer Comfort Cafe.
Simple to put together. I used frozen fruit. I really enjoyed this. I have been looking for more ways to use tofu and the berries are healthy as well. Made for Comfort Cafe Jan. 2010

This was the yummiest white clam sauce I have ever had, too!!  However, if you're a saucy person, there might not be enough for your tastes, you might even consider doubling the recipe.  For example, I followed the recipe exactly, and it gave barely enough sauce for two people; the recipe says it's for four.  This is easily fixed though, it tastes delicious, and that's what counts!

A very simple and delicious sauce - much better than most restaurant sauces I've had.  I used two 6oz cans minced clams and one 10oz can whole baby clams instead.  Plenty of clams in every bite!  Serve with plenty of fresh grated parmesan cheese on top.  Yum!
I also sauted 3/4 cup of mushrooms along with the garlic and parsley, turned out wonderful.  My family has already asked me to make it again.

The "BEST" I have ever had, and I have had my share!  This was truly authentic and every bite had me going back for another!  My guests loved it too and we give it 5 plus stars for flavor, appearance and ease of preparation!

I think this is the first time I have made polenta and had it turn out great! I usually do something wrong, and end up with a disaster.  This was so good, I loved it after it was grilled!  I used half beef stock, and half chicken stock, because I already had both open and needed to use it up, and I ended up using about a cup more than the recipe called for.   After it had finish grilling, I let it stand for a couple of minutes while it firmed back up, then served it.  Delicious!  Made for ZWT7 - Italy.
I used vegetable stock and did use a little more than called for. This was delicious with Recipe#457226(Spiced Butter). Thanks! Made for Zaar World Tour 2011-Italy by one of the Food.Commandos!

This is really lovely...I tried some baked in the oven, and some fried...both were great, but the fried just had the edge..nice and crisp around the edges, but smooth and soft in the middle..simply delicious!!!
Don't leave out the rosemary...it really does make it!
Made for 123 Hits.

Loved This!  I was worried that 4 cans of clams was going to be too much, so I used 2 cans plus one 8oz bottle of clam juice, after it was made I realized the 4 cans would have been fine.  I used a chardonnay for the wine and cooked per directions.  I wanted the sauce a tiny bit thicker, so I added 1 t cornstarch to 1 t cold water and mixed it in.  I will make this one often, thanks Marie!

Loved this recipe!  We made it for dinner this evening but modified it a bit to reduce the fat and calories... Specifically, we nixed the 2Tbs of butter and replaced the heavy cream with half&half.  It was excellent.

This was awesome. I followed the recipe almost to a T but made some minor adjustments based on reviewers' advice to increase the amount of sauce and to thicken it slightly. Adjustments: 1. Added finely minced onion (about 1/2 small onion) to butter/oil until softened. (I think next time I will sautee the onions w/ a small portion of butter for a min, then add the rest of the oil/butter, etc).  2. After onions were soft and I gave the parsley/garlic a min or two to cook in, I stirred in a mix of 2 tbsp of flour whisked with a little of the cream (used half/half not heavy) until a smooth mixture. 3. To increase amount of sauce, I doubled all ingredients EXCEPT the amount of clams (there were plenty - perfect amount), cream:  about 14 oz of half/half (instead of 16), about 4ish cloves garlic (I think 6 would have been overpowering). This will be a new family fav! I might try it with a little less butter and low fat dairy next time to lower the calories/fat and see if it's still as delicious as this was!

I have never really tried my hand at cooking before and not only is this recipe completely simple to follow, it doesn't take long and it is incredibly delicious! I followed it exactly and loved every bit of it!
Thank you so much, Marie! You are the reason I joined food.com!
Loved it!  Glad this recipe doesn't skimp on clams!

The sauce did not come out creamy. Used 4 cans of clams (6.5oz ) The liquid was about about 2cups. Was this too much. I followed the instructions. When you simmer do I leave it at medium heat or lower the temperature?

I make a thin roux with the butter and oil first or the sauce is too funny. I add grated lemon rind, lemon pepper and dill. I make this every Christmas Eve. This is something my family looks forward to every year.

For a low-sugar muffin these are quite good.  I used reconstituted powdered milk and fresh blueberries.  The flour was 3/4 cup of whole wheat pastry flour and 1 cup white flour. For the allspice, I used Recipe #145505.  The muffins had a nice crust outside and moist center.  They were done in 20 minutes.

I used only sugar so 6 tbs.  I used thawed frozen blueberries, whole milk.  I cooked them 22 minutes just to be sure they were ok.  They're crispy but moist inside.  So yummy!  Thanks Annacia :)  Made for Holiday Tag.

darn these are yummy. Update, made them again and the only thing i changed this time was to cut the oil to 2 tbs and add 2 tbs applesauce.  They were still moist and delicious, sighs..will probably eat them al today so wont be diabetic friendly for me :D
I followed Boomette's review and used 6 tbs. of sugar only and 1/2 tsp salt. These were tasty muffins and moist to boot. Made for Rookie Tag Game 2013.

We just made this recipe to break in our new smoker/grill and it was fantastic.  We left out the celery seeds because we didn't have them, and omitted the Tabasco because we thought the other ingredients would give it enough zing. We were right.  They were spicy, but not TOO hot and very juicy.  We're adding this to the recipe book!
Yes, this was delicious - we had it with pasta, absolutely beautiful. We were also wicked and used butter instead of virgin olive oil - silky smooth and delicious little variation!

If I could give it a 6 I would!!  This recipe is simple and can be thrown together at the last minute.  Ribs usually take hours, if not days to marinate properly but not these!  Max 30 mins on the stove and you're good to go.  They fall off the bone and melt in your mouth.  My kids love them and several friends have tried this recipe since I found it and all LOVE it!  Thank you, thank you!

Excellent rib recipe! These ribs couldn't be easier to make, and were so tender and juicy. I followed the other reviewer's advice and simmered in the stockpot for 30 minutes, followed by a 45 minute bake in the oven. I was out of barbeque sauce so I made my own for this recipe. It was all so delicious and my home smelled amazing all night! Reheated for lunch today and everyone was commenting on how great they looked and smelled. Will be making this recipe a lot... Thanks for sharing! Should also mention this was the first time I'd ever made ribs

Didn't have time yesterday to do this in the crockpot.  Used a stovetop method & it worked very well.  Came together quickly.  The only things I did differently to the recipe were add a tablespoon of chicken base to the potato water and add some granulated garlic to the seasoning.  I cooked the onion with the ground beef before adding.  Next time will also add some diced celery.  I like a really thick soup, so next time will start with 4 C. water and add if/as needed.  This is a simple, delicious, inexpensive meal that we will enjoy many times in the future.

The flavor was really good. It's kinda like Hamburger Helper (but soup) and the Velveeta makes it taste so much better. The potatoes were really good in this. I cut mine real small and accidentally cooked on high 6 hrs and they came out so tender, but not mashed. I didn't measure the spices but I know I used more like a tablespoon of onion salt. I let the onion cook in the crock as directed and they came out very tender. I too like a thicker soup so I will also start out with less H2O next time. Thank you for a yummy and different soup!
This was good but rich rich rich!  I'm pretty sure it's 5 pounds to the thighs but it is fantastic for filling you up on a cold winter night.
This was a VERY NICE PINK drink! It had a bit too much of a vodka flavor for me though. Made for Maynia Tag.
Another wonderful Cocktail. I had this ... after  I had your Recipe #203705. Very *nice* Thanks for sharing. I love these PINK drinks! Cheers ~V
Delicious!  I love the fusion liqueur ~ but I'm afraid this one was a little too strong for me ; )  Thanks again, Mommy Diva!

Very good salsa!  I love the fact that you use dried chili peppers, I have tons of these at home.  Normally I reconstitute them in hot water when cooking, but grinding them to a powder works wonderfully here.  The cumin adds a good bite as well.  I did the whole thing in the food processor and just pulsed the tomatoes in there until I got a good, chunky texture.  Thanks for a great salsa!
best salsa ive had in quite awhile!!

Definitely delicious with a sneaky hidden "kick" in the after-bite.  I just re-read the recipe, and COMPLETELY missed the part about draining the tomatoes, so mine was a bit watery, but we didn't care!!!   I added about five garlic cloves (we love garlic), and it was really potent, but not so much that the other flavors don't shine, too.    I ground up some coriander--in place of the cilantro.   That gave a bit of a lemon bit, but not too much like you get with cilantro (which we are NOT very big on).

I would like to suggest that you put the ingredients in the SAME order as they are called out in the step-by-step instructions.  It just makes it easier to navigate (and I'm at the point where I kin youse awl the help navergatin' as I kin git!).   

We tried it "as is", but I was thinking to add a dash of lemon or lime juice to get that "tang" that's so good, too.   Will let you know how that turns out.

*Made for PAC Spring 2007*
Had the neighbors over for "happy hour" and I served this wonderful Salsa.  Excellent flavor.  Everyone thoroughly enjoyed this, Rockin Robyn.  I HIGHLY recommend this recipe to everyone.
What a nice mix of flavors! I used cremini mushrooms. Thanks! Made by a Looney Spoon Phoodie for ZWT#6.

Great flavor!  I used the lemon juice since I do not like heat and dark rye bread.  I would just use a splash of lemon juice next time since mixed with the cheese it gave it a stronger 'bite'.  I used crimini mushrooms and also mixed a little parsley and dill in when sautéing.  Made for Rookie Recipe Review Tag contest win.

This was really good!  I took it upon myself to remove the seeds from the peppers, and I'm glad I did.  I think it would be too hot if I had left them in.  I didn't end up putting the marinade on mushrooms, so I can't comment there, but the meat was fantastic!  Very tender and full of flavour.  I only marinaded it for about 1.5 hours, and it was enough.  Great recipe - thanks!!
We love this recipe!  The spices and cocoa make the sauce especially good.  Thanks for posting!

I love a good chili, and this one's a real keeper.  The honey, cocoa and oregano in the sauce makes it taste completely unique- I love it.  I also added two chopped serrano peppers because I just can't make a chili without it being devilishly hot.  The feta and olives were also the perfect finish.  I actually left out the noodles completely though, and just served the chili with pita chips like one would serve a traditional chili with crackers.
I ate this alot growing up and dining out in so cal. It is so good and I have a pan of it in the oven even as I am typing. For a pretty presentation, spoon it into a corn husk before serving.
This made a nice lunch with a spring mix salad. I cut it down to 1 serving,using wheat sub rolls. Easy, directions are good, quick! Thanks Karen!

It was good. I modified it a little. In the future I would use a little less coconut milk. I added a little more soy and lime juice. I also added bean sprouts and cilantro, and substituted the onion for a little onion powder (not a huge fan of it). I had to substitute chili paste for another ingredient I didn't have. But overall I was happy, lol.

Wow, I really enjoyed this recipe.  I have never thought about combining navy bean soup and onion soup together.  I didn't need to adjust anything to make this tasty...I did use canned beans because I didn't have the time to soak the beans. It turned out great.
I added a bit of onion and 1 1/2 cups shredded sharp cheddar to the soup mixture.  Yummy.  I will certainly make again.

This was one of the BEST casseroles I've made in awhile!!! I added sliced mushrooms and 5 slices swiss cheese. The rest I followed exactly. It was VERY VERY good! A MUST TRY recipe!! TY Stacy!!Oh, and after I uncovered it, I only baked it 5 minutes longer, and it came out PERFECT! :)
This was good. I added some mushrooms, chopped onions and cheddar cheese. Very yummy, thanks!
Nummies...
Very tasty, Stacy! It reminds me of an old Chicken Divan recipe, but without the curry (which is perfect, because I don't like curry powder). Loved the crunchy stuffing mix too. Thanks for posting!
I added 3 tblsp of dried minced onions to the soup mix. Very good. I might try mushrooms in it next time.

This casserole is delicious!  I served this to my neighbors tonight and they raved over it!  I doubled the recipe just to be sure I had left overs and it doubled nicely.  I wondered about the lemon juice, but was pleasantly surprised.  The citrusy taste was not overpowering and you could not taste specific lemon flavor, but just the tang.  Sent some home with the neighbors at their request!  I prepared as directed by the recipe, except I used fresh broccoli and steamed it for just 2-3 minutes first.  Delicious and easy!  Thanks Stacky5LRC!  Its a keeper!

We must have very different taste buds at our house.  This casserole seems to have way too much mayonaise mixture and too little broccoli.  We also thought the lemon was too tangy and just didn't go well with the rest of the ingredients.  I followed the recipe EXACTLY but our dinner became a disaster-sorry...

I made this for a get-together and everyone was going back for seconds and thirds! Yay!  Anyway, I ended up adding more stuffing to the chicken layers because I love stuffing.  I also made twice the ammount of broccoli because I love broccoli and I read in one of the reviews that there wasnt enough.  Finally, I have a crazy oven that apparently gets too hot because the stuffing layer on the top got way too brown even though I only uncovered the dish for 15 minutes. No one minded.  Thanks for the recipe--Ive had this casserole at a church potluck before and Ive been looking for the recipe ever since! :D
My favorite "go to" recipe for this dish but have found that a layer of shredded cheddar cheese over top (before adding the stuffing layer) really makes this dish even more special.
Doubled the recipe and didn't add the salt and for my family of 5 there was none left, no kidding. Definitely a keeper.

This was an easy, enjoyable dinner. When I dished it up for my mother, she initially said, "oh, you gave a lot," but she had no problem polishing off all I served her!  I didn't add cheese, but I think it would have been good.  It was fine just as it was though.  Thanks for posting!
This is now my new favorite Chicken baked dish ever!!  Only change I made was that I shredded my chicken.  Thanks Stacky!!!
Great recipe! Finished it in two nights - just the two of us. Thanks so much.

This is very good.  I did make one substitution - I don't like to use cream soups... I used a chicken gravy made with 1/4 stick of butter, 1/4 cup flour (make a reux) and added 14 oz. chicken broth.  I then added the mayo and a little broccoli juice and lemon.  This has appeared on my table twice in the last two weeks.  It's that good.  Thanks for sharing.
Very tasty, super easy recipe.  Thanks.

My family is the fussiest there is when it comes to casseroles - and they have begged me to make this again!  It was really good.  The crispy stuffing really adds a great texture, and the flavor was wonderful!
Wow!  I did add more broccoli (14 oz.) and used only 1/2 cup of mayonnaise with 1/4 cup sour cream.  Awesome taste!  Thanks for posting!

This was really delicious. The reason for four stars instead of five is that the lemon tasted just a little bit strange to me (though my boyfriend didn't notice it). The stuffing also stayed really hard and crunchy on the top, which we didn't mind, but next time, I think I'd either use seasoned bread crumbs or crunch up the stuffing so it's smaller. The only change I made to the recipe was to use lowfat mayo and soup, and I added some cheddar cheese. I will definitely make this again. Thanks for posting!
I just made this for supper and I was very disappointed.I did not like anything about this dish.It was very runny and it tasted awful.

This was so delicious we had it for 2 nights in a row!  My DH thought it was the greatest and my DS's give it 2 thumbs up too.  I think it deserves more than 5!  Awesome recipe and perfect just the way it is posted.  Will make many times in the future!  Becky

I could not bring myself to make the recipe as directed with 57 grams of fat per person.  So I cut the mayo in half and used Lite Mayo.  I also cut the butter in half and added a little chicken broth.  The resulting dish was wonderful, so it's hard to imagine ever making it the other way.  I hope others might give it a try in the lightened version, because it's a great basic recipe!

This is really good!  I used light mayo and the fat free cream of chicken soup.  But I guess I added some fat back in -- I had some shredded cheddar I needed to use, so layered it with the chicken and broccoli.  I also used a box of Stove Top Stuffing in place of the seasoned stuffing mix.  The box was only 6 oz. -- and not the 8 oz. the recipe called for, but it was plenty and really tasty.  I made this for the Cookathon in Memory of Stacky5.  I wished I had had the chance to thank her for sharing this wonderful recipe.

This is one of the best casseroles that I have tried lately.  Even my DH liked it and he claims he hates chicken.  I didn't boil my chicken, I sauteed it in a little butter and sprinkled lightly with seasoned salt instead.  I left out the lemon juice because I didn't have a lemon on hand.  I used melted butter instead of oleo and Stove Top Chicken flavored stuffing mix.  I also added a handful of shredded cheddar cheese on top of the soup mixture.  This was delicious and my DH has asked for the leftovers in his lunch tomorrow - so this is definitely a winner!
Excellent chicken casserole!
Great!
we loved this!
This is real good! Made this about 3 weeks ago and last night my 5 yr old was asking for this again! So Im making it tonight. Thanks for a keeper
I used cream of broccoli soup instead and sprinkled a little cheddar on top of the broccoli layer.  We enjoyed it!

Fantastic, easy recipe for a cold winter's night!  We made it even easier but not cooking the broccoli or chicken first... chicken was nicely cooked and broccoli kept a bit of a crunch.  Will be making often!

Yum!  I was worried about boiling the chicken breasts for so long...thought they would be tough.  But I made this the way the recipe said to, and my chicken was SO GOOD...falling apart.  I was able to just pull it apart with a fork.  I used fresh broccoli and steamed it, and accidentally used cream of mushroom instead of chicken, but it turned out great.  Will be making again soon!  Thanks for the great recipe!

This was very good and pretty easy to make too. The entire family said that I am to make it again (not the not asking part? LOL). I forgot to add in the lemon juice but it didn't make a difference. Was great without it.
I had some cooked chopped chicken already done in the freezer and I used fresh broccoli instead of frozen.  Very yummy.

This was quite good and I think it will be a standard when I need an easy meal, but I did I make a couple changes for ease and health.  I chopped and sauteed my chicken (to save time) and used light sour cream in place of mayo to reduce the calories (approx 200 cal less per 1/4 recipe serving), with no loss of flavor.

This is excellent!  I've tried MANY broccoli casseroles in my day, including the one I grew up eating.  However, this is by far the best broccoli casserole ever and my family (including 2 young boys) loves it!  I have thrown out all the others in my recipe box and will make this from now on!

My family loved this!  They couldn't get enough of this yummy casserole.  I didn't cook the chicken or broccoli first.  I just mixed everything up, poured it in the casserole and topped it with the stuffing mixture.  It was so simple this way.  I added a cup of shredded mozzarella cheese and some garlic powder.  I left the salt out completely since I didn't boil the chicken.

I made this last night for guests, and everyone loved it! It's definitely a keeper. Instead of cutting up the breast meat, I left them whole. The next time I'll cut them in half because they were huge and no one except a teenager could eat a whole breast. I followed what other reviewers did and just let the chicken cook in the oven and just put the broccoli in frozen, but because I tripled this recipe, the cooking time took longer. That's my fault though for not realizing I'd need extra cooking time. Because I was using whole breasts, I didn't care for the two layers of chicken. The next time I'll just layer as follows: Chicken, broccoli, soup mixture and then stuffing mix. For the broccoli juice, since I didn't cook the broccoli first, I used chicken broth. I also left out the lemon juice, as many reviewers did, but I think I'll add it in the next time. I think it'll give it just a touch of tang. I also tripled the stuffing mix, but next time I won't do that. I ended up only using 1/2 the final amount because it covered the whole dish, which is what I think the main intent was anyway. Also, the stuffing mix was pretty salty, so next time I might even use less, or something else altogether...it's a lot of butter mixed in with the stuffing mix. I also used low fat mayonnaise and it worked out well. The other thing I did that I didn't realize would be a problem was that instead of covering the casserole with aluminum foil, I used the lid of the roasting pan I used, which left a dome of space between the top of the casserole and the lid. The result was that the very top layer of the stuffing mixture burned slightly. Next time I'll use foil so I can take it off the last 15 minutes for browning per the directions. But, despite my mistakes, the chicken was sooooo moist and tender, and other than the stuffing mixture, was not salty at all. It was absolutely delicious and I'll definitely add this to my recipes to make again.
Oh, this was good stuff!  I think what makes this so different from other casseroles is that it's not heavily sauced - such a welcome change!  Thanks so much for sharing  :)
Great combination of ingredients.   Made for Name that ingredient.

I have probably made this a dozen times in the past year. My tweaks include a layer of mild cheddar. About 1/3-1/2 cup of the broth made from boiling the chicken added to soup mix to add moisture. I also use skinned dark meat (legs/thighs) and I do not pre-cook the broccoli. It is still cooked enough after baking but still has a little crunch to it. A little modification to our taste but overall this is one of our favorites!
Always searching for new rice recipes and saw this one and tried it. Everyone really liked it!  I didn't add the cilantro, personal preference, but it was delicious without it too!

I omitted the salt.  I made buttermilk with 2% milk and vinegar.  It was very easy to do these pancakes.  The taste of banana is great.  I served mine with maple syrup and whipped cream.  Thanks Acerast :)  Made for Newest Zaar tag

Fantastic. Perfectly light and fluffy pannie w/the great taste of banana coming through nicely. I sifted the ingredients as indicated and used real buttermilk which resulted in a real filling pannie that DH only needed 3 to get his fill. I used a 1/3 cup measurer which made them quite large.
Thanks for this great keeper Ace.
Made for Recipetag in KK's forum~

Wonderful. I've never made banana pancakes til I had 1 lonely banana left. So I tried this recipe. I used brown sugar instead of white and evaporated milk instead of buttermilk. My kids were both back for seconds before I had a chance to finish my first one. Perfect pancakes. Thanks.
Used 2% instead of buttermilk and it turned out great!!
This pasta dish is wonderful!  I made a cheese sauce using part Velveeta and American cheese.  It was a delicious meal.  Thanks for sharing this soon to be repeated meal!

PAC2008 My baby did a great job with this recipe.  So simple to put together, very nutritious and tastes great.  I used a blend of velveeta and mozzerella as that I what I had bought prior to PAC.  This turned out so good.  WIll be making on rotation for pasta nights.
Thank you.
Nice and easy, loved by 2 yr old and husband! Added more vegetables and made my own cheese sauce. Great taste, thanks!
What a great recipe, this came out wonderful, thank you. I used a 2lb roast and omitted the onion soup mix because of allergies,and it still tasted great. Thank you.
Tastes like you died and went to garlic and cheese heaven!

This is a snap to put together and the house smelled like Heaven when I got home from teaching on a cold, rainy day in the desert (which we don't often get here in Arizona!).  I added a pound of baby carrots and thickened the delicious gravy with some corn starch at the end. The meat was wonderfully tender and tasty.  Served with homemade mashed potatoes and hot french bread.  My 14 year old and DH asked for seconds - I'm glad it was a big roast so we can have it again tonight!  Thanks so much Shawn C for a new way to prepare pot roast that I know we will enjoy many times again!

This was wonderful!  I forgot to use the bouillon cube, but it was still very flavorful.  I used Cream of Chicken Soup instead of the Cream of Mushroom Soup.  I added fresh thinly sliced sweet potatoes during the last 3 hours of cooking.

This was excellent!  I used cream of chx as I was out of cream of mushroom and instead of the broth and bouillion i used 1 can water and 2 t. beef base ( i like McCormick's brand found at Costco.  This was such a great roast, very moist and flavorful.  The gravy made in the pot was perfect.  Next time I'll do as other commented and add carrots and sliced mushrooms. TY!

This turned out beautifully - my husband actually ate pretty much the whole roast - it was falling apart and so tender.  I didn't have the onion and mushroom soup mix so i used some french onion soup mix and some of the "cream of anything soup" mix from hillbillyhousewife, with water - and seared the roast before i put it in the crockpot - then scraped off the brownings with some water and added that to the crockpot as well instead of beef broth and bouillon, which i also didn't have.  It still turned out great!  And the gravy was delicious - i had some on a bun with the gravy to dip it in and it was probably the best beef dip i have had in a very long time!

This is a quick meal to throw together with items you have on hand in your pantry. Cooking in a crockpot makes meat more tender and enhances the flavor. Thicken gravy with water and cornstarch. Removed the roast to a cutting board and turned the crockpot up to high for 15 minutes.  While gravy is thickening, this gives you enough time to slice beef and cook a vegetables.  Thanks for posting!

We prepared this recipe for dinner guests using a sirloin tip roast.  It cooked for 4 hours and it was so tender that it fell apart, but with the gravy it served up fine.  We'll make it again with a chuck roast, but I can't believe that it would be tastier.  It was excellent with garlic mashed potatoes and brussel sprouts with mushrooms.  Thanks for sharing!
This was a fantastic! I didn't do anything to the recipe, made it just like it said. We had it for sunday dinner and it was commented on how good it was by everyone. Thanks!

Awesome!  I used a larger roast (5 1/2 lbs), 2 envelopes of onion soup mix, 1 can of cream of mushroom, 1 can of cream of mushroom with garlic, 1 can of beef broth, and 1/2 soup can of water.  It was done earlier than expected in my crock pot.  I turned it down to low after 4 hours and it was done an hour later.  Thanks for a great recipe!!

This was so easy and good... I used fat-free mushroom soup and low sodium beef broth.  I left it on low for 7-8 hrs.  Served it with glazed carrots and a salad.  Thanks so much for sharing.  We will have this again soon!!

This was great!  We didn't have the Onion Mushroom Soup packet so we just used the plain Onion Mix instead.  Still came out fabulous!Mashed potatoes compliments this well.  Even the kids loved it! Thank you.
Great pot roast, I added some crushed garlic on the meat, then thinned the gravy a little with red wine at the end!  Loved the taste, leftover gravy was delicious on meatloaf a few days later.
This was the best roast ever! I don't think I'll go back to my "old" way of preparing a pot roast again. Thanks for sharing.

I thought this was the best ever!  Thanks so much for posting this recipe!  I wanted more gravy though, so I doubled the broth, soup mix and cream soup.  It turned out very tender and extremely tasty!  Will definatly be making this again and again.  I served this with mashed potatoes (the gravy went Great with them!) and green beans.
No doubt about it, this is the best pot roast we have ever had. It was absolutely delicious. The only addition I made was to add about 1/2 cup of red wine. Thanks for a great recipe Shawn

This is one of the easiest roast recipes that I have ever tried.  I teach simple cooking...and this is great!  The taste is wonderful, and the meat is extremely tender. My 3 year old son even said "mmmm, this is good!"
Simple!!!!  Meat came out tender & tasty...perfect! Will make again!!

What a simple way to make a great dinner.  I substituted onion soup mix for the mush/onion soup mix.  It was delicious.  It may be the most tender roast I have ever cooked, and my husband said it was the best he had ever eaten. Thanks for sharing such a great crock pot recipe.

EXCELLENT !!!! Love the fact you didn't have to defrost the roast ahead of time. I cut up the roast and put it over open faced buns and pour the sauce over the top.. I spread creamy horseradish over the buns before adding the meat.. Have made this numerous times and will definitely keep this under my "favorite" recipes. Thanks
This is a good recipe from Bon Appetit 1997.

My husband is so impressed with this recipe I just want to thank-you for making me the cooking star!!! The gravy the recipe makes is so wonderful over mashed potatoes!! Thanks for posting this recipe!  Love the fact that the roast can go in frozen too!  My house smells wonderful!!!

This was so easy and delicious. I added potatoes and carrots to mine and also thickened the sause with corn starch. The meat was so tender. I will definitely be making this again. Thank you for sharing!!

I've made this several times in the crock, but yesterday we had a chuck roast that was too big.  I put it in an oven-safe ceramide dutch oven, doubled the recipe to match the size of the roast, and baked covered at 250*.  It went in at 10:00, registered 180* internal temp when we got home at 2:30.  Was fabulous by the time dinner was served at 6:00.

If I have to do this variation again I won't be so concerned about defrosting the roast prior to baking.

Thanks for sharing!!!

Falling apart tender & very tasty. I couldn't decide which pot roast recipe I wanted to make so I combined 3 of them, but mostly based it on this recipe. I dissolved 2 tsp beef base in 1 cup coffee + 1/2 cup marsala wine + 1/4 cup soy sauce in place of the canned beef broth and added vegetables for a one-pot meal (2 sweet potatoes, sliced thin & 1 cup each coarsely chopped carrots, celery, onion, & mushrooms). I also added 4 cloves of minced garlic & subbed cream of asparagus for the cream of mushroom. I know I very much unsimplified this recipe, but it still came together very quickly and tasted excellent. Thanks for providing a good basis for dinner tonight; I'll try this more as is next time. But since I made so many changes and this came out so well I'm considering posting my version from tonight as a seperate recipe and making it that way on a more regular basis.

I've found my new standard pot roast recipe- but this pot roast is anything but standard!  My gravy was a little watery, but never fear, I skimmed the gravy of fat and simmered with 2 tbs cornstarch and water and it was perfect.  This was a hit with DH over mashed potatoes along with hot french bread.  Thank you- Thank you!!

This was served for Sunday dinner.  The flavor was good, but the meat was a tad dry (5lb at 8 hours).  I added carrots and they were too salty, probably from the onion soup mix, but had a great roasted flavor.  The resulting gravy was also good.
Made for supper tonight.  The flavor was excellent although my roast was somewhat tough even though I cooked it all day in the crock pot.  I'll try again with a better roast.  Thanks!
Very simple, tender and tasty!  Made as directed.  Thanks, Shawn!

We just replaced our old crockpot and had to tell you how wonderful this recipe is. We added quartered potatoes, butternut squash, carrots, because we had to use them. Thank you for sharing this wonderful meal. I'm editing my original review to give you the 5-star deserved rating--operator error :) We are still enjoying this recipe; I have used frozen chuck roast & added 2 hours. thanks again, shawn!

Just plain, PERFECT ! I will make this again and again and again.  I salt & peppered the roast, seared it, then deglazed with a cream of Celery, a can of water and two cubes of beef bouillon because I had no beef broth, and the soup mix. Then I poured it over the roast and cubed potatoes.  Mmmmmm mmmmm!

I've tried a few different versions of pot roast in the crock pot that didn't even come close to this awesome recipe that I'll make again and again. Having so much of that yummy gravy really makes this. I also seared the pot roast first after reading that great tip in reviews, and I think it added some nice flavor. Thank you for an easy but fabulous winner!

Browned a chuck roast first, then deglazed the pan with about 1/2-3/4 red wine and added to the soup mix also added half of a finely chopped fresh jalapeno to give it just a little kick (bland food never makes it in my house) - tender, juicy and no leftovers, will have to make a larger roast next time :)

This is sooooo super simple and delicious.  My husband loved it, and so did my 3 year old daughter...her brothers didnt....but they dont like much anyways.  It is tender and tasty!!  I will definitely make this again and again!!!  The next day its even BETTER.

This was a good basic recipe. I did add more spices as it wasn't quite flavorful enough for us. I added garlic powder, 4 cloves of garlic, sicilon salt and pepper. I also thickened up the gravy just a bit. My roast was frozen and I cooked it on high for 5 hours. Thanks for a great dinner that we will make again.
Roast was excellent.  4 stars as the gravy had too strong of a beef flavor, a little overpowering.

This was sooo good!  I didn't have beef broth so I used chicken broth and a beef bouillon cube.  Then I thickened the gravy with a little cornstarch and water at the end.  Not quite as good as my mom's, but a close second!

I have never made pot roast before andI had no idea what to buy so I ended up with a bottom round roast.  I followed the recipe exactly except I added some garlic into the mix as well as some potatoes and carrots.

the veggies and the gravy were fantastic. to die for actually. I didn't thicken it as some may have suggested but it was still a medium thickness.

the meat was a little bland and a little tough but it may have been not quite the right cut for this recipe.  I also had to cut it in half to fit it in my crock pot so maybe that had something to do with it?

Thank yo so much for the recipe!

Really good recipe!  The meat was a little tough (will have to try a different cut next time), but it was great overall.  I added some sliced onions, carrots, and a little big of garlic to the roast about halfway through.  Will make again but will add more veggies to the roast.  Thanks!

Nov. 21, 2008 I had an Angus roast that I thought I would have time to do in the oven yesterday. But plans changed and I found this while looking for something else to do with it. I had a 2+ pound roast and exactly 6 hours. I had homemade soup mix in a jar and just dumped a bunch in and skipped the bouillon because I dumped in more soup mix that I ment to. Because my roast was small it was done a little earlier. I think Angus is more tender but this was melt in your mouth. My DH, who is not a meat lover and thinks meat has a funny texture when done in a crock pot, had seconds and he raved as he ate. He said this was the best meat that I've ever done in the crockpot. I will defiantly be making this again but using a larger roast. Besides ususally having everything on hand, I like that I could do this with a frozen roast. I'm pretty bad about taking things out to thaw ahead of time. Thanks for a great recipe. I'm looking forward to having the left overs for lunch today.

I'm making this again for a neighbor and wanted to add that soup mix I use is Recipe #24952.
WOW! This is a good pot roast, and soo easy! It makes a lot of gravy too.  I put the roast in frozen and it took about 10 hours. Thanks for a great meal!

This is delicious!!!  Everyone in my family enjoyed it, including my husband who doesn't like most pot roast (for some reason he keeps calling it stew).  The meat was so tender, and the gravy - perfect.  I used Lipton's golden onion soup mix because I couldn't find onion mushroom.  This is my favorite recipe of all time.  Thank you so much!!!

This was good and easy to make. I followed the recipe as written other then I couldn't find onion mushroom soup so used just onion soup mix. I added some carrots in the crock also. We enjoyed this but we thought the gravy could have used a bit more spices.

This is the way I make my pot roast, too, except I substitute half a can of red wine for an equal part of the broth and usually use short ribs.  I think this is the ultimate in comfort food. I have made this a few times since finding it on here, husband and I love it, meat falls apart and tastes amazing and also makes a lot of gravy too for rice which I love! Never any leftovers no matter how big of a roast I get. Thanks for sharing an amazing, easy, and delicious recipe!
This makes the BEST Beef Gravy EVER! So yummy. I've made it several times and it just makes me want to like the plate when I'm done.
Couldn't be better. Remind your guy what a fabulous cook you are!
This is the only way to make a tasty, tender roast. I was looking for a way to make this from frozen, and this fit the bill. Thanx so much, I will be using this recipe from now on.

Hubby and I tried this recipe on a whim.  Awesome!  He couldn't get over how tender the meat was, even though it was put in the crock pot frozen.  In fact, it was so good, I'm making it again tomorrow night!

I've tried several different pot roast recipes and this is by far my favorite. It was extremely easy had great taste.  I've made this several times now and have stopped looking for a pot roast recipe.  This is it!

Great flavor though lots of salt.  I will use the substitutes that Kitchenwitchway suggested next time to cut down on the salt.
My husband and daughter both agree this was the best roast I ever made.  The gravy was very flavorful.  Thank you!

I give this 10 thumbs up - My husband, 3 kids and myself love it. no hassles, it was perfect. I followed everything and I added carrots, potatoes, mushrooms, onion, thyme & rosemary... made it with green beans.  THIS IS A KEEPER...  will make again soon... thanks for posting... =)

A really nice roast beef dinner that is so easy to prepare. I used regular onion soup mix as that is all I had on hand but would like to try this with the mushroom onion soup mix too. Turned out great!  Just the kind of easy and delicious recipe I was looking for.

This was good! The only thing I did different was used a can of low sodium broth.
Excellent!  My husband said it was awesome!  Guess I will be making this again based on that comment!  Thanks for the recipe!

If I could give it more than five stars I would.  De-li-cious!  The only thing I added was carrots and celery.  I put everything in the crock that night.  When I woke up, it was ready. Super simple and super delicious! I'm definitely an amatuer at making pot roast as this recipe was my 2nd attempt at making the dish. Made this for my boyfriend from Basel, Switzerland and he LOVED it. Will definitely make it again, thank you for the great recipe!

I made this for photo tag and I liked the nice change for standard broccoli. I made half the amount listed and that was plenty. I also used low-fat sour cream and pine nuts instead of cashews.

Used Splenda instead of the sugar and added a extra egg and a 1/2 cup of crunchy peanut butter delish will be making again!

This was great! I like my brownies chewy and gooey and that's exactly what these were. I made two small changes to the recipe. I subbed coconut oil for the butter because I wanted it to be nondairy. I also replaced the nuts with chocolate chips which made it even more intensely chocolate flavored. Quick to make and everyone loved them. These are replacing my previous top brownie recipe.
To die for!  Really good authentic chinese dish!!  Its worth trying.  Will put this on my regular meal rotation.  Thanks for posting!

Excellent Dish!  I made as directed except I used a red onion instead of a green onion.  We served over rice.   The sauce is very nice and very spicy which is what we like.  Thanks shygirl.  Made for Fall PAC 2008.
10 stars all the way!  love love the flavors of chili and oyster sauce together! Truly exquisite! Thanks girl!

Hi Shygirl, I made this for a gathering and it was a hit. I love that it is easy to do do.  But can you please clarify the amount of garlic please?  I could not tell if you meant 1 clove or 1 whole head of garlic.  Since I like garlic so I used 1 entired head/7 cloves and the shrimp was very garlicky which was still great but if just wanted to know the exact amount for future references.  Thanks in advance.

I cut the serving size to just 1 serving, which really made two servings.  My DD and I both enjoyed this for breakfast.  This would be great to make for a brunch dish.   I used Pepperidge Farms Brown Sugar Cinnamon Swirl bread.  Made for Spring PAC 2008.  Thanks Hamre for a great recipe.

I had intended to add some cinnamon sugar to the top of it before I baked it, however since my DH had seen me making it yesterday, and I left the directions out on the counter . . . he baked it himself. They also dove into it without taking a photo of  it completed. So my photo is only of one piece as the loaf was pretty mutilated in the feeding frenzy. LOL! I too used Pepperidge Farms Brown Sugar Cinnamon Swirl bread. Made for Zaar Chef Alphabet Soup tag '2009.
Too much wet to dry. Too much sugar. Made it inedible.
Very good.  I used roughly cut frozen spinach, which worked fine.

Has potential, but didn't come out quite like I hoped.  2lbs. of spinach seemed like a lot, and I ended up using about 8oz, which might be why.  I also found I liked the texture better when pureed in the blender immediately before serving.  Next time I will try more spinach and less coconut milk.

My family loved this recipe, it is  our new favourite steak meal.  
I seared  the steaks on a hot indoor cast iron grill for a couple of minutes each side then put them in a fairly hot oven for 6 minutes. Then I added the juices from the steaks to the gravy.  

It's so hard to find a meal that all of my family will happily eat...this one is a keeper!

We enjoyed the flavours.  I have a recipe I already enjoy for brandy mushrooms but wanted to find something different to serve with our rib-eye steaks.  I had some port so this recipe caught my eye and it worked out well for us.  I didn't have shallots so I used green onions.  I was alittle short on mushrooms so I increased the sauce abit to make up for more volume for a group I was serving.  This is a definate keeper & will be added as a regular in our household, thanks for sharing.
These are delicious and healthy! I'm doing as suggested, and leaving the batter in the 'fridge as I make a few at a time. Thanks, CongoGirl! Made for PAC Fall '09.
Love this recipe,, great tasting and love that you can keep some batter in fridge for later... I added strawberries one time, banana another time...thank you for the recipe

We enjoyed this soup with some crusty onion bread.  The flavor of the soup is delightful, and the texture was not stringy, like some cheese soups (I did use Cheddar cheese, even though the cheese was not specified).  The recipe ingredients went together effortlessly without a lot of intesive work, and the finished dish was irresistibly good.  Thanks, Mimi, for sharing a recipe that I will make again!
delicious

I'm not sure what I might have done wrong here--I followed directions exactly. Everything looked great until I added the cheese, then when the cheese melted, the soup seemed to curdle/separate, and it was a gloppy mess that I could barely get down (as much as I love onions & cheese!). I used sharp cheddar--maybe that was it? Or was it something with the milk (which seemed fine)? I won't rate it b/c the mistake could have been on my part.

Easy, cheesey, and tummy-warming.  I used sweet onions and used smoked paprika instead of regular.  That really added to the flavor.  Next time I would also add some thyme or parsley to pick up the flavor just a bit.  Thanx for an easy yummy soup!

I don't have to make this again to know I love it!  I love "The Splendid Table" and all of her recipes.  Quite often I make the dressing and use it on steamed, new potatoes tossed with fresh herbs and baby lettuce from my garden.  Fabulous Post!

These are a real treat and very easy!  I subbed honey for the corn syrup, though.  Everything else as written.  I made mine a little too big, and got only 32 instead of 48.  They spread out a lot.  I think these would be good with chopped dried cherries, also, and maybe pecans.

YUMMY WONDERFUL CHEWY NUTTY TANGY CARMELLY DELIGHT! WOW these are a new favorite. Oh so easy and super tasty. I did use cashews in place of pistachios which worked out great. Mine spread out into eachother but it didn't affect the flavor...I think I may just try spreading it all out on a pan instead of trying to make individual cookies next time. Made for 1-2-3 hit wonders.

This cake is excellent. However, the bourbon is bitter and overpowering. If I make it again, I'll cut the bourbon to 1/4 cup, or leave it out entirely. The cake itself is moist and quite good (after you scrape the filling off!)

To be perfectly honest, I am not a mustard person. The only place that I tolerate it is on McDonalds Cheeseburgers. But for some reason, I decided that I would just HAVE to try this recipe to broaden my horizons.  I am glad I did!  The chicken comes out so moist and juicy and the mustard flavor doesn't overpower like it usually does in most recipes.  Even my boyfriend liked it and made suggestions on what to serve it with NEXT time.  Thanks so much for helping me add another great recipe to the list that I make on a regular basis!

We loved this chicken.  Dipping the chicken in the mustard sauce was a bit different from other like recipes.  The addition of the Worcestershire to the mustard mellowed the sauce.  The chicken was very moist.  The dish was very tasty, and it made a nice presentation.  Thanks for sharing your recipe.  I will definately use this one again!

Marvelous! Bold flavors, but not overpowering. I really enjoyed this...it's just the type flavors I look for in a dish. Very complimentary and very much enjoyed by all. Thanks for a keeper - this one is going into the monthly rotation!

I love making p.b. cookies with the chocolate kisses on top.  These did not disappoint.  Used the chocolate kisses filled with p.b.  You can never have enough chocolate and p.b....Thanks Klyn...
Made for Springs PAC 08'

Delicious! Peanut butter cookies are one of my family's favorite cookies and they loved these.  These cookies are quick and easy to make and are soft and chewy.  I used extra-crunchy peanut butter and didn't use the chocolate kisses.  This made 30 cookies. Thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe.
*Made for Adopt A Tag II*
Great Cookie! I used chocolatechips instead of the kisses,and the only problem I had was NOT eating the dough before I could get them in the oven! Thanks Klyn!

Delicious and perfectly soft!  I am not a fan of the crispy version of Peanut Butter Cookies so these really fit the bill.  First bite out of the oven....soft, warm and heavenly.  My husband said, "well done honey, well done".  Enough said!

I ended up adding wayyy more peanut butter, a little of both sugars and vinila to get it to taste not like cardboard. They were soft and im currently trying a single cookie in the oven until i get the batter right. not going to lie i might just eat the batter cause that is Y U M M Y

Everyone loved this one...even though I wasn't paying attention and had 3 lbs. of chicken breasts! So, I could have used another can of onion rings - it was still delicious and I'm sure will be even more so if I use 2 cans for my 3 lbs. chicken next time.  I will not double the butter mixture, however - there was plenty for this amount of chicken.  It was some of the moistest, juiciest chicken I have ever had - definite keeper!

I've had this recipe before and lost it and was so excited to come across it again.  I love this chicken and fried onions give it a different taste.  One can easily adjust the ingredients to fit the amount of servings they need.  AND it's quick and easy - my favorite.
Loved this recipe for two reasons - sooo easy and my 2 year old even loved it. 5 stars!!!

Easy no fuss recipe that produced a very tasty and moist chicken breast.  I had some difficulty getting the onions to adhere to the breast during the preparation but just piled the onions on and tossed the dish in the oven.  We all enjoyed the dinner.
I served this for some friends, and all you could hear from them was MMMMMM! I usually add a little hot sauce in this to give it more of a spicy kick.

We all loved this one Karen. Easy enough so the kids could help make it which is always fun for them. The chicken was quite moist and tender with a wonderful flavor. Perfect for a no-fuss simple family meal. Thanks for posting.

I've been wanting to make this chicken for a while with the can of French fried onion rings that I had in my freezer. I added in some minced fresh garlic, salt and pepper along with the other ingredients to the melted butter. If anyone is searching for a quick chicken dish that is very tasty, then this one one to try, I served this with mashed taters, we absolutely loved it! Thanks Karen for another winner!...Kitten:)
