Simply wonderful and so easy to do.  This can be whipped quickly with ingredients I usually have on hand then, while it cooks, relax or finish the rest of the meal.  Served it with a Carrot/Raisin salad and we had a very nice, tasty meal!  Thanks!

I wondered what recipe would prompt me to write my first review- before the dinner dishes have been cleaned no less, AND THIS ONE IS IT!  Wow - great recipe! Never in a million years did I ever imagine my family would be bummed out because there weren't any second helpings of poultry - lol!  I will make extra next time. Followed it exactly, except that I pounded the breasts and needed to cook them for only 30 minutes. 
Thanks for posting this Karen.
Loved the crunchy texture & moist inside. Was just a little salty for us. Next time will try it with no salt butter. Thanks!

I've made this twice now, and I love it!  The onion coating is unique and flavorful.  The crispy texture reminds me of fried chicken, but this tastes better.  It was very easy to make, and the butter/margarine mixture clings well to help make the coating stick.  I pounded my chicken breasts flat, so they only needed 30 minutes at 350 degrees.  I've used both butter and margarine.  The butter might have been greasier than the margarine I used last night.  I will happily make this over and over again.  Yum!

Very tasty! Prep was almost too simple. I cut the recipe to make only 2 servings with no problems. The chicken came out moist and the mustard and onion flavors combine for a great taste, not overwhelming but not too subtle. Will be making this again.

Wow!  What a keeper!  Halved the recipe in an 11 x 17 pyrex dish and turned out perfect in 45 min.  Juicy moist chicken with just the right spice.  Oh yeah, used WalMart brand ingredients, too, instead of the name brands.  Perfect!!  Thanks, Karen!

I added 1 c, coconut to this recipe and we had it for dinner with rice and steamed veggies. It was YUMMY...I would definitely make it again. There are no leftovers.  I used Costco chicken tenders and they worked out great.

Delicious chicken! Hubby and son said it was yummy! Added a clove of minced garlic to the butter mixture and fresh ground black pepper and 2 tablespoons of flour to the onions. I laid the chicken on a wire rack sprayed with Pam over a foil-lined cookie sheet and it made for easy clean-up and helped keep the bottom crispy. The mustard flavor was very mellow so don't worry if you are wondering if it will be too strong, it's not. I bake my chicken at 400 degrees for 45 minutes and it was nice and crispy, like oven-fried chicken. Served with broccoli cheese rice and steamed veggie blend (carrots, broccoli, cauliflower, zucchini and yellow squash). Will make this again , thanks!

5 stars all the way.  I reduced the butter to 5 T., and used panko in combination with the crispy onions.  I halved the chicken breasts horizontally and seasoned them with granulated garlic, dried basil, pepper and a tiny bit of salt before running them through the butter/mustard/worcestershire.  The only thing that made us sad about this recipe is that we didn't have MORE!  Will definitely make this again - thanks for a winner!

Very flavorful and moist.  I subbed ground turkey for the beef, and it still stayed moist.  I loved the tomatoes in this, and I usually don't like doing "freeform" meatloaf, but this worked great and gave more surface for the sauce.

This is the real deal!  We used to sell derby pies as a fundraiser for my high school band, and I have been searching for "the recipe" ever since then.  Every other recipe that I had tried left the custard part a little curdled and lacking flavor.  Not this one!   It produces a perfectly smooth, delicious filling no matter how many or how few chocolate chips and nuts you add (I often omit the nuts for my nut-hating friends).  Thank you!
EXCELLENT!  The Bourbon was still evident in the sauce but I found that enjoyable!  Very easy and the house smelled WONDERFUL while it was cooking!

Made the little meatballs and used the crockpot allowing me to spend extra time in the garden. The aroma alone worth a five. Only had one of those small mini bottles of bourbon - not much but certainly aged! Seemed to be just fine. Put on at noon and they were done for supper. Wonderful to walk in and supper ready to put on the table.

These are great and made for a quick, easy meal.  I used some frozen IKEA meatballs and cooked on the stove top.  These have quite a sweet and sourish taste and if you really wanted to I believe you could easily add a packet of frozen chinese vegetables.  Served on rice.

I made mine using homemade meatballs,and my beloved Jack Daniels,cooking on top of the stove.It really couldn't have been easier or tastier-they are delicious!!Absolutely no need to change a thing about this recipe,it's spot on!
I will definately be making this again!!
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

This was great!  I did the stove top method and it was easy as could be.  I didn't have any bourbon so I used Jack Daniels, like another reivewer did.  It was very tasty and the Jack wasn't too strong.  I served along with mashed potatoes.  Great supper.  Thanks so much for sharing!

Oh my goodness, Sarah_Jayne! These are fantastic. I really had to stop myself from eating all of these!! lol These are the thing to take to a party, that's for sure. I do think you can taste the bourbon slightly, but that's what makes them SO good. I used the crock pot method and I found that 8 hours was going to be way too long for mine. I shut mine off at about 6 hours. If you are going to make these for a party, I suggest you double the recipe because they will be gone very fast! Thanks for sharing!

I made these for an office luncheon and they were GREAT!
They were practically falling over each other to get at them for seconds.  I've already given the recipe out to 3 of my co workers. The other great thing is I made them in my crock pot and my house smelled fantastic. Thank you for an easy recipe and a great addition to my recipe box!
Great recipe! Quick, easy and a real crowd pleaser.

This is super easy and good!!  The sauce thickens into a very rich and sweet glaze.  I like the hint of bourbon.  I halved the sauce ingredients for 24 meatballs.  This is a great recipe for a quick appetizer for last minute guests!!!
LOVED this sauce!! These are so easy to make too. I wouldn't change a thing.
This was good, but not the best appetizer meatball recipe we've had.  I didn't have bourbon, so I subbed Jack Daniels.  My husband was disappointed that I used his favorite for just an okay recipe.

I made this in the crockpot and it smelled amazing as it simmered away but found as it cooked that the sauce just too sugary sweet for my liking.  I threw in about 1/3 cup of prepared medium heat salsa to the mix and it made all the difference!  I ended up with spicey sweet meatballs that I would make again!

better than anything ive ever done w meatballs!
i was barely able to get them from the pot to the plate! had to throw several people out of my kitchen and hide all the forks! no joke!
making these again tonight for MNFootball!!!! very excited.. just like the rest of them.
GOOO RAVENS! :)

These were a hit at an adult halloween party we threw recently (30 people). I followed the recipe exactly(croc pot version)  and was afraid that they'd be a failure because they smelled quite "drunken". I thought the bourbon really was going to be too strong, but it turned out to balance well with the other ingredients once done cooking. I guess I expected these to turn out more like a sweet/sour meatball, but who am I to complain, every last meatball was devoured!
These went fast at a jewelry party I had and am now doubling the recipe for a birthday party as a request. So easy and very delicious. I used home made meatballs.

I made this with frozen meatballs in a crockpot.  It's sooooooo good!!  This recipe is going in my permanent file :-)  I used Southern Comfort and chopped up one each red, yellow and orange bell pepper and added it.  It turned out perfect and was a hit with all my friends.

Holy Smokes these are good. I used a 6lb bag of Costco Meatballs (The ones at Sam's Club are too fatty). Increased the Brown Sugar & Ketchup to 3 Cups and the Southern Comfort (a must) to 1 1/2 Cup. I saw another version of this recipe and they call for 2-3 hours on high in a Crockpot. Mine cooks odd and the sauce breaks down if you cook things to long or high so I cooked these on the stove first stirring ever so often then transferred them to the crockpot. Everyone devoured them. I wish I had more. Thanks for the great tip. I think next time I will try with Turkey Meatballs so they are a little healthier and I like the idea of adding the diced bell peppers. May also switch the Ketchup to "Homade Chili Sauce" http://www.saffola.com/chili.htm. I usually make their Candied Meatballs but these are better.

I normally make my meatballs with grape jelly, but I wanted to try something new for a work pot luck.  I did not change a single thing, only doubled everything, and these came out absolutely perfect.  There wasn't a single one left, and I was told many people came back to look for more. I might try them with Chili Sauce next time, but that's because I have an unfortunate tendency to buy the strangest things in bulk at the big box stores.
I made these for an Irish Themed Pot Luck and they were a big hit...everyone wanted a copy of this recipe!! I made a batch at home and my kids cleaned the out 4 dozen within 10 minutes!!

I was looking for a quick crock pot recipe one day and came across this.  I was skeptical to try it thinking that the sauce just didn't sound like it could have that much flavor.  I tried it anyway and boy am I glad I did!  I did add a bit of garlic and onion powder to the sauce.  I also had to use a 14 ounce can of tomato sauce as I was out of ketchup.  This recipe still was outstanding!  I served mine over cooked rice.  Yummy!
These were great! Thanks for the share!
Exactly why are we cooking ALREADY COOKED meatballs for 8-12 hours ???? Seems way beyond over kill.

Great Recipe I made it a meal by adding some red pepper flakes and chopped peanuts serving over spaghetti. Used Trader Joe's frozen meatballs (2 packages) which were great Kind of an Asian take on the recipe. Would have also added fresh cilantro if I had it. The bourbon really cooks down and it very mild Yum!
Awesome recipe! A real crown pleaser! I often increase the sauce amounts and I only cook these for about 4 hours on low since the meatballs are already cooked. Yummy!!

I have been cooking these for years with 7-up or Sprite instead of the bourbon. I increase liquid to 1 cup also. As for why you cook meatballs that long even though they are already cooked is that the meatball absorbs the flavor and thickens the sauce, mingles or marries the flavors. My family asks for them on special occasions all the time. It is a favorite for holiday parties. I am definitely trying the bourbon.
Because it takes me that long to get home from work. :)

Pretty good. Even though I simmered the sauce for 5 mins and cooked in slow cooker for over an hour, the sauce was still a bit runny. Added some Sweet Baby Ray's hickory and brown sugar to kick the flavor up a notch.
These drunken meatballs were great! I doubled the batch and used 2 x everything. Next time I would maybe just use 1.5 cups ketchup or it can get a bit ketchupy. Easy and so flavor-full!

I stumbled upon this recipe a few mths ago & have made oodles of variations..Replacing bourbon with Southern Comfort, Cherry Vodka, Dr. Pepper, Cherry Cola, White Grape Juice Pretty much whatever liquor/soda/juice I already had in cabinet or fridge! I've always made homemade meatballs when making this recipe. I imagine frozen would taste great too! It's just your personal preference..That's what I love about sharing recipes back & forth..It allows each & e'ry one of us to experiment & tweak ingredients & preparation to suit our lifestyles & tastebuds! Thanks again for sharing this recipe! It DEFINITELY will ALWAYS be one of my top "Go-to" recipes for numerous reasons!

These were wonderful.  We are HUGE fans of grilled shrimp but had not tried anything like this.  To make it simplier, we did not use skewers.  THese were gobbled down in no time.  Definately  a keeper!!!

Amazing, spicy little bites of joy! YUM YUM! Used a grill basket and 2 chipotle peppers- and a little of the adobo they are packed in. I mixed the sauce in a ziploc bag and added the shrimp and smooshed it around a little. I also added 1/4'd a green pepper and onion to the bag and threw them into the basket for an easy side. YUM! Next time I will add some cherry tomatoes to the mix. GREAT recipe! Thankx for sharing it CHIA!

We loved this wonderful and simple recipe! The chipotle marinade was perfect! Just the right amount of heat! I used the George Forman Rotisserie and skewers for half of the shrimp and the basket for the remaining shrimp! Great Recipe! Thanks Chia!

5 star all the way- I used the chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, alder smoked salt. and for the cilantro I used fresh frozen cilantro cubes.  These prawns were very flavorful but not take your head off hot. I put a few mushrooms on the skewers between the prawns  Thanks Chia for a lovely dinner

AWESOME!!!

I made these Friday night and they were a HUGE success at our party.  They had just the right amount of heat.  I also used 2 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce adding a little of the sauce in the marinade.  I also added Hickory smoked salt.

I am already looking forward to our next seafood grill party!!

We tried this tonight, and we enjoyed the flavor of it, but we wish it were more intense. Maybe we didn't leave it in the marinade it the marinade long enough. Also, I think using larger shrimp would be better for this so we're going to try again next week. We do love the flavor though, so I will update my review when we try again! Thanks!
Changed and added a lot but this was GREAT.  didn't have cilantro and added vinegar and honey to the marinade.  just brushed it on during grilling.  spicy and delicious.  thanks for this recipe!
WOW!! This was a hit with my somewhat picky family. It's often hard to find a meal that they all like, but this one was perfect! Served it with rice pilaf and mixed veggies.

I have to thank you for making my morning breakfast so easy, so quick, so cute and so simply wonderful! This is the fastest breakfast I think I have ever been able to make for myself:-)) Thanks a bunch for the goodie goodie crunch!
Filler and canned meat do not go together well.

This makes a delicious casserole of baked beans. We had this as the main part of a vegetarian meal. It would also be good as a side dish. I chopped a red onion and left it in the dish rather than removing it and omitted the final tbsp of olive oil. Made for Newest Zaar Tag.

Excellent beans!  Served with crusty bread and fresh grated parmesan, these make a wonderful meal or side dish.  I think next time I will add diced tomatoes in their juice instead of puree.  The sage and garlic is awesome

I'm very sorry but I can't leave any stars for this recipe. I tried it first with the unconverted rice the recipe calls for, then with minute rice and then with medium grain rice. All 3 attempts failed turning out very soupy.
Maybe the ingredients are just listed wrong.

I made these for christmas and they are so good.  Everyone liked them.  I did freeze some after the holidays and I liked them better not frozen.  They are going on my cookie list for next year. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
Loved, loved, loved this drink. It is perfect for sipping, not too heavy and not too huge of an alcohol hit. So tasty I sipped two! Made for Phot Tag game.

Be careful of this one.  You will be bombed quickly on this.  Great taste.  I added frozen cranberries to the presentation along with a sugar rimmed glass and tied a bell with silver ribbon to the glass stem.  Looked great for my Christmas party.
Thanks.

An easy & quick snack or light meal. I used whole-wheat pitas, and added some turkey pepperoni to DH's portion. I brush a little olive oil on the pitas, as I think it makes them a bit crisper. Thanks for the recipe!!
Very good pizza but was a little too sweet so would cut down the sugar next time.  We cooked it on the KJ which gave it great flavor.  Used Recipe #70165 for the crust.
Excellent pizza!! I used this with "Quick Beer Pizza Dough" #387067 and skipped the onion. Really good. I really liked the fresh spinach and the veggies. Colorful and tasty!

Made this last night- it's wonderful. Not as sour as a real sourdough, but with much more flavor than a normal white bread. And the crust! The crust was terrific. Crispy, light... I have to go now and make another loaf.
Could have used time & temp info.Think 375 for 45 min.would do.Also use a full size bread pan.We liked this so much & it did have that sourdough taste!
We realy loved this. Have never made or tried sour dough bread. Will definately try again. Had problem with riseing. Found out never used enough yeast. My pkt, must be smaller than yours.
Oh this was a keeper! Thanks for such a simple recipie! I used wheat beer and it gave the bread a delicious flavor. I agree that the crust was terrific!

made this the other night gfreat flavor a little dry but that is probably because the machine cooked too long.  I am going to try it again and do the baking myself.  I also added cheese wow what a flavor
Really enjoyed the texture of this bread. I baked it in a pan instead of the breadmaker, and it really raised the last time. Good flavor, but I had trouble detecting a sourdough flavor.

This bread is fantastic! One of the better bread machine recipes I have come across on Zaar. Yup, a six star recipe.
I used a good quality stout [Coopers Stout, an Aussie brand] and used stone ground wholemeal flour for the flour.
The bread - a 1 kg loaf - rose wonderfully on the Basic Rapid cycle of my bread machine, smelled absolutely scrumptious and cut really well. I don't know how it keeps - we polished it off in one sitting.
Excellent recipe Kimmie - I have you have more like it!

I have been making this bread now for several weeks since I found the recipe.
This bread is out of this world!  I make all of my bread for my family in my two Zojirushi's, and have been doing so for a long time.  This is definitely one of the best breads I have ever made.  My family is asking for it constantly.
Thank you...thank you.....
Bailey
I'm cooking impaired and this was so easy to make!  I took into the office for our morning meeting and it was a hit!

I went to a Tastefully Simple party and tried their beer bread which was fabulous.  I wanted to make my own with wheat flour and no additives, so I checked this site.  I made mine with no water, subbing it for the beer.  It can out wonderfully, and just as good as the one I had at the party!  My husband loved it with the dips I made!  Thank you for an excellent recipe!
Beautiful Loaf, Fabulous Recipe..easy as pie...er...bread! :) Thanks!

I love Beer Bread and this recipe made the best loaf yet.  It was not too strong (beer flavor) and the consistency of the bread was great.  It stays together very well when slicing.  Excellent recipe, thanks!

This is an absolutely awesome recipe.  I've tried other "beer-type" recipes in the past, but this one wins hands-down.  I did find the dough to be pretty sticky (pulled it out of breadmaker and formed it into a french-type loaf), but other than that, the taste was superb -- especially on day two!  Thanks for submitting this award-winner in my book!

This is a wonderful bread. It's dense, soft, and has a good beer flavor that only gets better with age. I've made this twice - once using butter instead of oil. They were both delicious, with the butter loaf having a crisper crust, and the oil having a wonderful melt-in-your-mouth soft one.

I too did not think this tasted like sourdough, but it was the MOST delicious bread I've ever had from a bread machine.  It was also the first time I had tried a recipe instead of a pre-made mix too.  It was superb and the color of the bread was perfect.  I used the Basic bread setting on my bread machine and a medium colored crust and it was golden brown with a perfectly soft textured center.  I just made it last night and am making another loaf today.  Thanks for the awesome recipe!
Although this did not taste like sourdough to me, I'm giving it five stars because it tasted so good!  Thank you for sharing.

I agree with those commenting that this is the best thing their bread-machine has produced. It's light and fluffy, but dense, and has an unbelievable crust. 

I suggest two modifications however: substitute one TB of honey for one sugar to enhance the color, and warm up the flat beer/water before adding it to enlarge your finished bread.

This is one of those few bread recipes to look exactly like the picture. thanks for the recipe, cheers

You need to re-do the serving size, because I ate the whole loaf.  Never mind, I don't want to think about how many calories that was!!

To die for - thank you!!

This is one of the BEST breads EVER! Makes huge loaves. The crust is absolutely amazing!
I've made this two days in a row now. It does need extra flour. It's a pretty sticky dough. 
I did make two minor changes. Less sugar and I added cracked pepper.
Also mixed the dough in my machine. Took out and set in my bread pan & to let it rise for about 45 minutes. 
Baked @ 375 for about 35 minutes. I buttered right out of the oven for a 'softer' loaf and left one un-buttered for a crusty crust.
Either way, delicious!
Yummy and will get made many times in my house.

This is a very nice bread - I do not have a bread makers so I mixed all the ingredients, let it rise for an hour, punch downs, another hour rise and then baked at 430* (I was baking other things) for about 20 min.  Worked well. My problem was I had an odd amount of dough - to much for one loaf pan and to little for two.  I made muffins with the extra that did not fit in my normal size loaf pan.

I used Red Stripe Beer and got a nice beer flavor - great for tuna melts!

I used this recipe because I was attempting to make my own bread bowls for clam chowder. I halved the dough and made two round loaves from each batch. Baked them @ 375 for 35 minutes. They were  fantastic!!! The bread just melted in your mouth when scooped out with the soup and I enjoyed the density and flavor of it! My family loved it so much that I made another batch the very next day! Thanks so much!
I followed the recipe exactly as written.  The bread turned out perfect.  Very tasty.  This recipe is a keeper.

WoW!! This was a delicious bread recipe.   It will be going into "My Favorite Zaar Recipe Cookbook" :)
Texture was perfect!
Thank you so much for sharing the recipe!

Very good. I wouldn't call it sour dough-like, but I don't know what you would call it. It has more flavor then a normal white bread.  I mixed the ingredients in my stand mixer, let the dough rise, pounded it down and let it rise again and baked it off in a mini loaf pan. Wonderful bread will make a again. Another recipezaar favorite.
My husband the sourdough king loved how fast and tasty this bread was to make. Actually all he did was the eating but still loved it. Thanks.

Sooo good.   Have made it 3 times in a week and everyone who tastes it, likes it  - A LOT! I use the Dough setting and make buns.  Took me forever to find it again so I could comment (forgot the sourdough part) Don't know how sourdough-y it is but IS Yumm-O  Thanks so much.
This bread turns out really well.  I definitely echo the sentiment that it's not really "sourdough-like," but rather a white bread with a kick.  It's great for sandwiches and toast!

This bread is so great! I too didn't pick up any sourdough, but the flavor of the beer comes right through, it is so delicious! We made this to cube it with our five cheese champagne fondue. What did I do with the other half we didn't use? I made Texas Toast with it the next day- absolutely perfect! Just like the Texas Toast my boyfriends grandfather makes! So thankful to have found this recipe!

We are another group who didn't pick up a big sourdough flavor with this one. Note the five star rating though, this was a great, tasty, flexible, light and airy loaf of bread- and we will be making it again. Thanks KimmieOh!
This bread is the best. and it looks just like its picture. yummy
This great bread and it makes really good toast.

I have tried all kinds of bread recipes for my ABM and this one is everyone's favourite bread!  I wouldn't call it sourdough flavoured, just beer bread, but a perfect one I can even cook right in the bread maker, which I never normally do. It comes out perfect! I warm the beer in the microwave, by the way.  Thanks for the fantastic recipe!  It is a keeper for sure!

This one is a keeper! I agree it doesn't really taste like sourdough nor is it your typical beer bread but it makes a great tasting loaf of bread. So far I have tried Michelob AmberBock and Guiness Draught (not Guiness Stout) with great results. Made exactly as written for the bread machine. Thanks for sharing!!
I made this when I was on a low-carb diet and it was wonderful.  Great when those cravings for "real pizza" sets in.

I liked this "pizza", however next time I will try to mop up some of the zucchini's water moisture with paper towels before making the crust, because it was a little watery. Leftovers were better, and less watery. Thanks for posting your recipe!
i had a problem with watery zucchini, but i liked eating the end result anyway. i used a lot less cheese to be more healthy, thanks for a great idea!

My husband was putting together pizza for dinner, and I was in a debate of "do I, don't I".  I am a competitive bodybuilder and must limit carbs and calories.  What a treat it was to find this fantastic idea - I used it right away and made up my own crust.  I just had 3 zucchini and it worked out fine.  I also actually omitted the sauce and cheese.  I really just used your crust idea.  I topped with ground beef, soy bacon bits, red onion and loads of rosemary out of the garden.  I also put rosemary in with the crust.  Broiled that up nicely and then topped with some fresh tomatoes.  Very satisfying!  I know I will be making this crust and topping with what's on hand at least once a week.  Thanks VERY much!!

I am on a grain-restricted diet and made this last night for dinner. This really gave me my pizza-fix. Great idea using the zucchini. It compliments the pizza sauce & cheese nicely. In order to get the water out of the zucchini I shredded them on paper towels and then tossed it around a little bit and dabbed it with additional paper towels. It seemed to do the trick. I also added a little parmesan cheese and garlic powder to the shreds with the egg. The "crust" held together nicely and was a good base for the toppings. Of course we couldn't eat this with our hands like "standard" pizza but other than that it sure did hit the spot. Thanks for posting!
This was delicious. Wonderful recipe. I will make again and again. I did add garlic, oregano, basil and approx 1/2 c parmesan cheese the the crust. YUM!!!!
yummo, I topped this with turkey pepperoni, a sliced jalapeno, some sliced red pepper and sweet onion.  I didn't miss the crust at all.

Great recipe however I salted the zucchini first and let it 'sweat' for 15 minutes and then wrung out as much of the water as I could.
Eliminates the watery problem you have with zucchini.
Love the taste but the crust did not make a crust, it's too watery to hold together.  I think this would make a better casserole dish if it were tweaked.  5 star flavor & 1 star crust.

This is a great recipe with changes.  First, put a little salt on the shredded zucchini and let sit for about 15 minutes.  Then take a clean cotton towel, put the zucchini in it and wring it out as hard as you can.  Proceed with recipe except add some mozzarella cheese into the crust and heat the pizza stone, then oil the stone before spreading the crust ingredients on it.  You can also make your own low-er carb pizza sauce without sugar.  A really yummy supper!

It tasted great, just would be great if it were crispy. I think I'll make a lasagna version of this. I did was tdayberry did and added garlic powder and oregano. Any I won't be using my metal perforated pizza pan. It was really messy. use a stone or a cookie sheet. maybe it would've been crispy.

I think the trick to this meal must be in the curry sauce because although I cut the recipe in half (luckily, because I was nervous about wasting 4 cans of chickpeas) I followed it exactly. My husband had to use the better part of a tub of sour cream and struggled through it. I have to say though I have had little success with cooking India so this could just be me. Nonetheless, I won't make this again :(  I would love it if the author posted the brand name of curry and specified the flavour (red, yellow, or green) he used. Thanks!

I thought this was great! I used powdered garam marsala (1 tbs) instead of the curry paste since I already had it on hand. Maybe the other reviewer used Thai curry paste instead of the Indian curry since they mentioned that it came in red, yellow, and green.

This turned out delicious.  I used Patak's Hot Curry Paste and added a about 1/2 tsp of Garam Masala.  It is 90 miles to the nearest Indian resaurant, so it's hard to compare it with authentic cuisine made by experienced chefs, but this satisfied our craving wonderfully.

Wow!  This is a lot of fun and the flavors are completely unexpected.  I substituted turkey for chicken and strawberries in place of the grapes.  This is a recipe you can play with the ingredients a bit and have it still taste terrific.  Thank you for sharing!  Reviewed for A Day in Bargain Basement 2011.
I had all the ingredients, it was easy to prepare.  I needed to add more sugar.  Maybe my lime was too tart?  I toasted almonds to add.  It was light and pretty good.

Real treat for diabetics. Made as posted and I enjoyed it very much. I'll be making this more often when Summer finally gets here. Thanks for posting your Grandma's recipes. Made for PAC Spring 2011 ~ORPHANAGE~

I must admit that I was confused by the instructions in this recipe.  I added everything to the BBQ sauce when ready and served it on Hoagie buns and also on Baguette. It was difficult to eat, we had to use a knife and fork. The sauce was delicious the meat a little tough. All said the flavor was nice, a good use of contest ingredients.  Good luck in the contest.

THESE ARE GREAT SANDWICHES ~ I used a sharp cheddar along with some shredded chicken breast that I had on hand & these went together in no time at all! These, along with a potato soup, & we had a very tasty lunch! Thanks for sharing! [Tagged, made & reviewed as part of my Lunchtime Sandwich theme in My-3-Chefs]

I'm always looking for healthy snacks to feed the family and this caught my eye.  I made it as directed and then tried it before putting it into dessert cups.  I decided to add 3 more peaches -- it still had all the protein benefits of tofu, but with a fruitier taste.  I like the way the honey enhanced the dish without making it too "sugary" sweet.  This is really good and I can't wait to serve it to my daughter-in-law, who is a vegetarian and always looking for new and delicious recipes.

Made exactly as given, & when I took it to a park-wide potluck last week, it was gone in no time at all! Absolutely delicious, & I'll be making it again before the end of the year! Great, great spread! Thanks for sharing it! [Tagged & made in Please Review My Recipe]

I loved this dip. I made it for our Football Sunday get together and it was fabulous. I didn't change a thing and I don't think I will for the future either.  It is perfect how it is.  I will be making this again.  I love mushrooms and this hits the spot.

I made this for a party last week and then again for a party this week.  At both parties people raved about this dip and asked for the recipe!  It's a delicious change from the ubiquitous hot artichoke and spinach dips.  Thanks for sharing!

This was really tasty. I made it for lunch to serve on bread and it went down a treat with the rest of the family. I only had about 6oz cream cheese so I added about 1/4 cup grated cheddar cheese to the mixture. Thanks!
Yummy!  I love mushrooms and this dip did not disappoint!  It was a hit at the party too.  Very easy & very tasty!
made this for christmas eve treat everyone loved it ! will make it again exactly as described.

Made this as a Thanksgiving appetizer.  It was very tasty but too "cream cheesy" to me.  I think you are onto something here but I think I'll fiddle with the recipe... More mushrooms, less cream cheese, a little white wine and more garlic? Thanks for posting!

This has really good flavour & I love that it is CHOCK FULL of chicken & vegetables.  I did 1/2 a batch in an 8" square pan & just used water in place of the chicken stock - other than that, I followed the recipe.  Very hearty wintery meal!  For some reasons, the leftovers turned a very odd grayish colour but my husband gobbled them up & said it tasted even better than it did straight out of the oven.

These were great!  I made these with another "spread" recipe and had them both on party rye rounds.  I thought these had fantastic flavor with little kick!  I might try broiling them next time to make the spread hot and bubbly!  But they were great cold for a summer BBQ!  Thank you!
I mixed up a small amount of this spread and served on grilled panini style bread with a salad.  We liked the spread and found it flavorful.  Thank you for sharing your recipe.  Reviewed for ZWT3.

Delish! I wanted this as a dip -- not a spread -- so I drained, but did not rinse or pat dry the peppers. I simply chucked everything in the food processor and buzzed until smooth-ish. To thin the mixture a bit, I also added three teaspoons of the brine the peppers had been in. Did not have sharp cheddar on hand, so used 6 ounces of grated colby and 2 ounces of grated parmesan. Also used a full teaspoon (or a bit more) of worcestershire. Made and thoroughly enjoyed for Zaar World Tour Zingo.

Mmmm! This is wonderful with crackers. I used a HeAPinG tablespoon of the Horseradish as suggested in the recipe and I love the bite it gave this spread. I tried some on baguette slices under the broiler and that was wonderful too! Thanks for another keeper BKW!
Very easy, very fast, VERY YUMMY!

Someone gave me this recipe ages ago, and I didn't realize it was on here.  I have no contact with this person, and really wanted to find my copy of this recipe, and decided to check here, and I'm thrilled.  This is excellent.  The cherries are a "must", but I did omit the almonds and it was just as good.  So so glad I found this again.

Yummy! Extremely easy to make. Don't worry if you forget about it in the crock pot as I did. It cooked an extra four or five hours. I jumped out of bed, had me a cup of it. Put the remaining in the fridge. The kids heated it in the microwave and enjoyed it the next day. Thanks for sharing. Made for My 3 Chefs 2009

What a great hot cider Nicole. Excellent fruit flavor and spice balance.  We really enjoyed this tasty treat.  I used peach nectar and apple cider, cara cara oranges and fresh ground ginger, cinnamon and nutmeg. So easy to make, just perfect for our cold fall weather. It smelled as good cooking as it tasted, thank you so much for sharing your recipe. Made for My 3 Chefs/09 :)

This, obviously, was a very popular recipe this year for My-3-Chefs!  I can only add my praise, as well.  The spice was right on with the peach nectar and apple cider.  The taste was very mellow and holidayish!  Thnx for sharing your recipe, Nicole.  Made for My-3-Chefs 2009.

This was a great recipe!  Quick to make and the steak was so moist and flavorful!  I did use one box of Liptons Onion soup mix which was too envelopes because I thought 8 ounces was to much at least for our family.Thanks Jen!

This was a great-tasting, meat-and-potatoes kind of meal. My three guys loved it. I used several New York strip steaks that I had on hand and they turned out wonderful. I've never made steaks this way, but I will do so again!

I don't know if I made it wrong (I don't think I did) or what, but it just didn't turn out.  I was expecting great things and was disappointed.  The steak itself was alright, but the "sauce" and veggies weren't so great.

I used leftover slices of beef frozen, a few strip (chuck) steaks(small ones)and no potatoes. I  wanted to serve this over noodles and rice.
I made my own dry soup mix using dried chopped onions and Sysco beef base with a little cornstarch mixed in. I also didn't use as much A-1 Sauce. We love the taste but it is too much saltiness for us with the onion soup mix too. I probably used 3 tsps of A-1 sauce.
I used 4 ozs. of water also. It was still fantastic the next day, the flavors were more intense. I also sprayed Pam in the baking pan before putting in the vegies and meat and the sauce. Thanks for posting!

Delicious!  I thought I had cream of celery but did not so I had to use cream of chicken and it still worked fine.  After an hour and a half my veggies were not quite as soft as I would have liked so I'll leave them in a bit longer next time, I'm pretty sure that's due to the high altitude.  We really loved this dish and will make again and again.  Thanks Jen!
great for busy nights, teenage son can put together and have ready for us when we get home from games.
This was great chicken!  My kids raved about it and wanted it again the next night.  We will be making this often. Thanks for sharing!
I loved the crispiness of the french fried onions. My husband was not as happy with his, he's picky. Very flavorful. Thank you Kitten!
very good.  and only requires one dish!

We really enjoyed this.
Left out the olives I'm not a big fan.
Easy to make and quick.
Posted for Fall PAC 2009.
Thanks.

Delicious quick and easy chili. I used left over ground turkey. I also left out the olives mainly because I didn't notice I needed them, and didn't have any in stock. I used red and white kidney beans as that was what I had on hand and skipped the cilantro since I don't care for that herb. Made for Potluck Tag.

Enjoyed this seeing it was a good night to cook this...damp and rainy.  I did leave out the black olives, used some northern beans that I had on hand, and subbed green peppers for the yellow peppers.  Very flavorful chili, and with some potato stuffing.

I halved the quantities on this salt recipe as I already have lots of my own blends!! It was easy to make and I was fascinated by the mixture of the ingredients. It was a 5 star salt until I added the juniper berries; let me explain, I am not a big gin lover & I thought they overpowered the other ingredients just a wee bit!! So it was a 4 star recipe WITH the juniper berries. However, I made up ANOTHER batch WITHOUT the juniper berries and it was very much 5 star recipe again for me!! I do like juniper berries in cooking - I use them in terrines, pates, chutneys and with venison - but, in this salt mix, I just thought they overpowered the other gorgeous ingredients such as the chipotle pepper and smoked paprika! (It is just personal taste I must point out.) I used the salt mix in my scrambled eggs this morning and LOVED the subtle smoky flavours - very good indeed! So, Rita, THANKS for a superb mix - I am a herbs and spices fanatic, and this was truly a superb mix, which is VERY much a keeper for me. FT:-)

This is an easy recipe that produces a winner!!! Instead of baking though I browned the chicken breasts in the electric skillet then glazed with the BBQ sauce, topped with the bacon & cheese. I turned it down to a simmer & covered.(Too hot of a day for the oven) We were surprised at the  wonderful smokey taste. I have made it several times since. Good job!!!

Sorry it has taken so long for me to post a review on your chicken recipe. :(  I have made this a couple of times now, and it is a nice way to make chicken breast with ease.  I love chicken, cheese and bacon, so with this dish, I get it all together.  Did not change anything and comes out wonderful every time. :o)

Yummy, yummy! Areal hit at dinner tonight. I loved that blend of flavors. Very easy to prepare and looked great on the plate. Thank-you for I recipe that will be used often in our house. Next time I think that I will cook the bacon slightly less.

Simple and yummy! This was recommended to me by my friend (Melanie In Winnipeg) and we just loved it. I used Bobbie Q Sauce recipe#59772 for the sauce and fresh green onions from my garden. Thanks for posting this delicious recipe!
This was good. I used honey bbq sauce and left out the green onions. Next time I will try and find a milder tasting bbq sauce. I'll be making this again.

Isn't this the best chicken recipe ever?  A local restaurant here makes this, using mozzerella cheese and adds mushroom...this is our favourite chicken dish, serve it up with cheesey garlic potatoes, garlic bread, seasoned green beans and a salad...YUM!

WONDERFUL!!! I work at Chili's, and we actually serve this EXACT dish at the resturaunt, only they call it "Monterey Chicken" Well, I gave this one a shot, the only change I made was to 86 the onions, and use colby-jack instead of cheddar, but it was awesome. Thank you for posting this recipe!! LOVE IT!
FABULOUS!  This was sooo easy and so good!  The only change I made was leaving off the green onions.  Will make this again!

Fantastic recipe.  I baked the chicken with BBQ sauce for about 30 minutes.  Drained off the liquid, covered the chicken with more BBQ sauce, the bacon and a slab of sharp cheddar cheese.  Placed under the broiler to slightly brown the cheese.  Served on toasted Kaiser rolls.  My son wants to know how soon I will make this again.  You won't be dissappointed.  I also put the precooked bacon on a plate with paper towels and cooked again in the micro for about 30 seconds to get rid of more grease.
sorry forgot to add my stars
My significant other said to give this recipe a five star rating, and this is to become his favorite chicken....so it sounds like a keeper to me...

I really did not expect this to be SO GOOD! I was looking for something quick to make for a busy night, something which the kids might actually eat. This was a big surprise. I'm not a BBQ sauce lover, but the combination of the sauce with bacon (I used crumbled bacon) and cheese in the oven produces a fantastic result. Chicken was moist and flavorful and the family gobbled it down. I also had some great leftovers for lunch the next day. Thanks, Wende, we really enjoyed it!
Delicious, quick and versatile = one very good recipe.  Thanks for sharing.

This was a very tasty dish. The combination of barbecue sauce, cheese and bacon was out of this world. Like some other reviewers I used crumbled bacon. I may try this with montery jack cheese next time.
Sooo good! I used Diana's Hickory Smoked BBQ Sauce which complimented the bacon very nicely. I didn't have green onions, so I subbed chives instead and it tasted just fine.
Absolutely delicious is all that I can say!  I used a combination of shredded mozzarella and cheddar cheese. Thanks a bunch Wende for sharing. Katherine
Very yummy chicken!  Left out the onions because we don't care for them.  Wonderful, fast and super easy!

This recipe was quite good and everyone liked it.  The only thing I will change next time will be covering it to keep the chicken more moist.  I think it turned out a little dry.  Maybe because I used cutlets instead of whole breats.  Will try again.  It is definitely a keeper though.  Thanks!  YUM!
This was great - can't go wrong with barbecue sauce, bacon and cheese! I pounded the breasts flat before cooking and baked for about 30 minutes.  Leftovers made a yummy sandwich the next day.

Wow! This was really good! DH rated it a 5 star and I agree with him. This was easy to prepare. Also looks great plated. I cook them on the BBQ and they came out excellent. I served some of the barbecue sauce on the side. This will be made again. Thanks, Wende for posting.

Tried this over the weekend and the whole family enjoyed it.  Reminded me of when I was a kid; my mom used to take halfed potatoes with skins on, put grids on them with a knife (score them) and bake in oven until almost done, them top with the same toppings as this recipe (bbq sauce, bacon then cheddar) and then broil for a few minutes.  Brought back childhood memories!  Sometimes the bacon can be a little greasy and cause smoke in oven! But very yummy none the less!

This was a easy and flavorful chicken dish. We thought it would also make a great chicken sandwich. It's a keeper.

Thanks Wende. 

Bullwinkle.
Loved it, fast and easy too.  Was even good as leftovers and I think would be fantastic on a sandwich.

Just awesome! I've had this dish at Chili's countless times and always wanted to make it. Used recipe number 59772 for my sauce and grilled the chicken instead of baking. Very flavorful. Can't wait to make it again!
Yum! Quick and easy and delicious!! Thanks :)
This was delicious! Easy, quick, and a real crowd pleaser. I served it with make ahead baked potatoes, peas, salad and garlic bread. I'll be making this often. Thank you, Wende
This was even better than it sounds, believe it or not.  It couldn't be easier or more delicious.  You've got to try this recipe!  Delish, love it love it love it.
This was great and sooo easy!!! One of my kids declared it his favorite chicken dish!

This was very good, a nice change of pace, but not one of my favorites. It was a little on the salty side, but perhaps I used too much bacon or maybe the brand I used was real salty. I wish I would have seen the suggestion to add tomatoes that would have probably made it a 5 star recipe. On a side note, I don't think the nutritional facts includes all of the ingredients so it may not be as low in calories as it appears to be. It was a very easy recipe. 
This tasted better on the second day. Thanks for sharing this recipe.
I was short on time so instead of using boneless skinless breasts, I used frozen microwavable breaded chicken patties. It turned out great. Made the entire dish in the microwave.
Quick, easy to make.  A keeper.
This was so simple and had a supreme taste.  I am not a fan of bbq sauce as a rule but I used cattleman's classic and the flavors went very well together.

Wow - these were really good.  Both my husband and I loved them.  I made them with fat free cheddar cheese and turkey bacon to try and make it a little healthier.  I'm adding this recipe to my collection.  Thanks for posting!
My entire family really liked this. It was really fast and easy too.
Fast and easy. Defintely something to make at the last minute.
When adding the cheddar cheese we also topped each piece of chicken with a tbsp of mild tomato salsa. It was wonderful. We will certainly make it again.
Very Yummy!! Great change from regular bbq chicken, but still just as easy!
Made this tonight for dinner,hubby said this is a definate repeat! Super easy to make,and really tasty! pattiecakes7

Really simple and tasty! I cooked my chicken on the George Forman Grill first then covered it in the bbq sauce, bacon and cheese and put it under a low broiler for a few minutes. It was perfect! I really think the green onions add something to the dish. Always happy to find something new to do with chicken!
My boyfriend really liked this dish.  Thanks for sharing.

My hubby asked me to make this and I expected to not like it because I thought the BBQ sauce would be overpowereing, but it was really very good. I seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper, garlic powder, italian seasoning, savory and thyme before adding the BBQ sauce, I used cheddar and montery jack cheese, and I added fresh tomato and sour cream to the green onion when serving.  Delicious!
This was really good and very quick and easy to make. I used hickory/brown sugar barbecue sauce and colby/jack cheese and it was delicious!

Fantastic, but I believe those nutrition facts only include the bare chicken! The cheese, the sauce and the bacon bring it up to 197.43 calories & 8.14g fat (for 4 oz. of chicken or about half of a normal size breast.) Still decent in calorie totals and for the yummy taste and juicy texture...5 stars!
very good and easy recipe for any quick meal.
Easy and tasty!
These were good but my family and I didn't find them to be something we would make again.  Thanks for sharing.
Very good recipe!  I grilled mine and then finished them in the oven.  Served them with some oven baked potato wedges.
These were so good!! They'd also taste good on a bun as a sandwich. Thanks for sharing!
Great recipe!!  Love the bacon and cheese with the bbq sauce.  Have done it several times including using grilled chicken and it's always wonderful
Not bad- just wasn't what I was looking for - maybe the bbq sauce I used wasn't good for this.

This recipe has great flavour. I don't know if I did something wrong but my chicken came out very tough. I think next time I will brown it in the skillet and then transfer to the oven. I love the way the flavours all enhance one another. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
AWESOME!!!!!!!!!!!! Totally easy and fantastic flavor, I've made these several times! forgot to review until now..... Thanks for the great recipe Wende

Absolutely wonderful, just as expected! I didn't have any onions, which was fine. I used real bacon bits and that worked well. I used 5 chicken breasts cut in half and layered in a 9x9 pan; they just fit in one layer. It took 35 minutes at 375degrees. 'Sweet Baby Rays' bbq sauce is the best! (Buy at any U.S. grocery store!)

This was a very tasty and moist way to cook chicken breasts..I ended up doubling the recipe and glad I did everyone went back for seconds..the only thing I did was used real bacon bits instead of the bacon strips. Thanks Wende!! Will be making again!!

What else can you add to the many wonderful reviews this recipe has got. It was delicious and oh so easy to make. I could not buy BBQ sauce where I am, I know unbelievable, but the local stores don't stock it and I did not want to have to drive to a more international supermarket, so I had to make my own which added extra cooking time, but well worth it, so yummy. I also used fresh bacon, cut it into strips and cooked it. It was fabulous and my whole family raved. Thanks for posting.
My husband and I really enjoyed this.  It was very tasty and it was fast and easy to make which is a relief after working all day.
A GUY PLEASER RECIPE!  Easy!  We used the precooked crumbled bacon.  MMMMM Thanks!

My BF is a huge fan of barbeque sauce... he could eat it on anything.  So of course he loved this dish.  I am quite picky when it comes it sauce and the bottled sauce I had on hand was way too sweet for my tastes.  I really did not like the combination of cheese, sauce and bacon at all... but that is not the fault of the recipe, but rather my choice in sauce.  I did love the simplicity of the recipe and how fork tender the breasts were...  We may try this one again with some homemade sauce sometime... thanks for sharing!

Really Good!  I can't believe how fork tender the chicken comes out.  I did not have bacon, but I did have reduced fat real bacon bits and that worked out just great!  Thanks for a quick and tasty go-to dinner!
This is a good family recipe.  Both DH DD loved this.  Easy hands-off dinner.  TY

Really good dish.  It's a dish that's probably only as good as the BBQ sauce you choose to use so make sure to use one you know you love.  The combo of the BBQ sauce, bacon and cheese was really yummy.  It was also very easy to prepare.  I used bacon bits and it worked great.  I also doubled the green onions.  Thanks for a nice quick chicken dish.
WOW, we loved this recipe.  The flavors are FANTASTIC on this.  Used my homemade barbecue sauce.  The chicken came out so very tender.  This will certainly become one of our favorite chicken dishes.

Great flavor!  I like that it is a new twist on chicken.  I pounded out my chicken breasts and used regular bacon which I cooked with the chicken.  Easy directions.  I added a bit of liquid smoke to my barbecue sauce too.
Very good and so easy!
YUM!!!! We had a Zaar Day today. I served this with Recipe #10090 & Recipe #39478. WONDERFUL combination. Thanks for a great recipe. UPDATE 8/25/08 I love this recipe, I've made it many many times.

This was GREAT! I followed ChristinaCeline and made the White Potato Salad (no mustard) recipe & Baked Beans recipe. It was a hit! Anything w/BBQ sauce and bacon my husband is all over...Thank you for an awesome recipe!

This was such a simple recipe and so yummy.  We really enjoyed it....made as posted, probably didn't use quite enough cheese.   The green onion really gave it a nice flavor.  Will be used often, on those "I don't feel like cooking" nights!

Thanks for posting!
Yummy! I used regular bacon, cooked it first, then put it on the chicken with the cheese to warm it back up. I left out the green onion, kids won't eat them. Easy, fast and family friendly. Thanks!
Excellent! My girlfriend hates green onions, but she loved it on this recipe... they truly do give it a nice flavor.

Yummy!!!  We thought this was amazing!  The BBQ sauce made the chicken really moist and tender after cooking!  We cut chicken breasts in half and cooked at 375 for 30 minutes.  It was the perfect cooking time.  Like some of the other reviewers we too added the green onion at the end.  This quick and easy recipe will be one that we will make often!  Thanks so much Wende!

Well, I forgot the bacon and green onion, but even so, I liked this.  DD didn't care as much for it, but I think it was more the flavor of the BBQ Sauce, Recipe #19023.  I liked the sauce and the chicken was jucy and tender.  Thanks for an easy, tasty meal.
Delicious!  We loved these.  I served these with oven fries and a salad.  Thank you for posting.

Tasty dish.  I served it with garlic mashed potatoes, corn, and garlic bread.  I seasoned the chicken with a cajun seasoning before browning on both sides and then put it into the oven.  I used Cattleman's BBQ sauce.  DD (15) said that the dish looked un-natural, but she might have been showing off for her boyfriend - she said it wasn't bad after being forced to eat it for dinner.  Everyone else liked it.  DH might try a variation of this on his grill.  It is definitely a man meal.

Great! I grilled the chicken on the Foreman grill. I put BBQ sauce on it, grated some cheddar cheese on it, sprinkled some real bacon pieces on it and microwaved it til cheese melted. Very Tasty! Thanks Wende for the recipe!

tasty recipe!  this is a keeper for sure.  i loved the combination of bbq sauce, bacon and cheese.  i did make some changes.  i used thin cut pork chops cuz that's what i had, i cooked the pork in a pan ahead of time, i made a mixture of bbq sauce and dijon mustard, i added some serrano pepper slices after the sauce before the bacon, i used peppered thick cut bacon, and topped it all off with pico de gallo and sliced green onions.  served with spanish rice and green chile pull apart bread.  dh couldn't stop raving about how awesome it was!!  definite keeper in my book.  will make often.  great make ahead dish. thanks a lot!

Please look at this rating as a 4 1/2 stars. Everyone in our family rated it either 4 or 5 stars but the 4 stars won out by a single vote.  I made a vegetarian version for the non-meat eaters using quorn cutlets in place of the chicken breast and temph bacon.  I just put the still frozen BBQ covered quorn cutlets in the oven at the same time as the chicken breasts.  The Quorn didn't dry out that way and everything took the same amount to time to cook.
Easy and Simple!  Had all things on hand.  Made for guests and everyone gobbled it up!
Pure awesomeness.  I made this on the stovetop too.  I used sauteed yellow onion just because my weird fiance has a hatred of green onions.
It does sound excellent however there is no possible way it is only 1.5 grams of fat - even just using one bacon strip divided in quarters!

Outrageously good and easy!  As recommended I used Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ Sauce which was perfect.  I used one 8 oz. pkg. (2 cups) of Cheddar Jack Cheese and approximately 3 slices of pre-cooked bacon per breast of chicken.  I did served the sliced scallions on the side so everyone had a preference as to using them or not.  Thanks Wende for a keeper in our house!
Great easy recipe that my kids loved.  I had the crumbled bacon so we used that instead of strips which made it easier for my kids ( 4 and 6) to eat.
Beautiful presentation!  Good flavor.  I left off the green onions, but I think I will add them next time for another layer of flavor..

Great recipe, especially since it uses  a small # of ingredients that I had on hand. I made the chicken on the grill and my husband and I were happy with the results. I  coated the chicken in BBQ sauce, grilled them for 5 minutes on each side, then added the additional sauce, bacon, and cheese and let them go a few more minutes until the cheese was melted.
Doesn't get much easier than this, but very tasty!!!  Flavors work great with each other.  Perfect for a weeknight meal.

I cannot put into words how delicious this was. I will make this over and over again. The barbecue sauce that I used was the Dr. Pepper kind. Seriously, this recipe was out of this world. Thanks so much for posting!!
My favorite way to cook chicken!  I don't normally add the green onions because I never have them lying around and it still tastes awesome!!
My boyfriend loved this!!! Didn't use the green onions and added mushrooms.  Was wonderful! Thanks so much for sharing!!!!
Yummy!  Used tex-mex cheese.  Had no green onion so used tomato and avocado.  Cooked the whole thing in the electric frying pan.  Excellent quick, easy.
This is so delicious!  We used Sweet Baby Ray's barbecue sauce.  This is a keeper! Thanks!
Great topped with fresh pico de gallo and sour cream! We made these on the stove top with Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce.

SO DELICIOUS!! I used HP BBQ sauce the first time, but and the vinegar taste was a little strong.  Used a milder, sweeter sauce next time and it was absolutely amazing!!  Served with Betsy502's Recipe#56807 ~ great combo.
Great change from the humdrum. And delicious too!

Really unexpectedly nice. I wish there was more direction in relation to the times. This is what I determined: Bake chicken firstly for 20-25 minutes and then with cheese for 4-8 minutes. I made it with the bacon and it was nice but it's not really necessary for this dish, it's like eating steak and chicken, do you really need the chicken in that dish? no. Really nice and simple; a great bbq dish without tasting like you're at a cookout.

Here's how I made it.  Baked frozen breasts for 50 minutes at 375 (topped with a little sauce).  Then added more sauce, bacon bits and put it back in the oven until the cheese melted.  Topped with the onion.  Served it with homemade mashed red skinned potato salad and my kids and husband loved it!

I have had this two ways, the way as stated and grilled.  I prefer the grilled way.  It is so much better.  You grill the chicken with the bbq sauce and then add extra when you put in the oven to melt the cheese.  We cooked the bacon in the skillet to get it nice a crunchy and didn't top it until the chicken came out of the oven. Super YUMMY!
The calorie count is off by almst 3:1. By my calculation, this is over 500 cals.

We really enjoyed this, but since I changed it quite a bit, I wouldn't necessarily give any stars (turned out about 4*, though). I did a C.O.R.N. of sauces using a combination of Bulls Eye BBQ, Bulls Eye BBQ that had been "doctored" for another recipe, homemade Catalina dressing, homemade balsamic-mustard dressing, and Kraft Honey Mustard dressing to total 1 1/2 c. for the 6 chicken breasts I was using. I baked at 375 for 30 min. before adding the cheese (mild cheddar) and bacon. I only had about 3 1/2 pieces of bacon and I chopped them before cooking to make bacon bits. I served this with Recipe #65427 and some crescent rolls (which were the reason for changing the oven temperature).
Delicious!  Will make this again. :)
Love this, make it often.  I also use this as a filling for potato skins...try it!
This was just okay. It was easy to make, but just didn't do a lot for us.
Recipe is a good idea.I used homemade tomato mushroom sauce instead of BBQ sauce also used half cheddar and half mozzarella cheese.You can also sub cooked sausage rounds for the bacon.
YUM! This is great stuff. Left out the green onions & used low-fat cheese, but otherwise followed exactly. Thanks for sharing -- it's a keeper!
My boyfriend and I made this last night as the main dish of our Sunday dinner. It was so easy to make, and so delicious! We will definitely be making it again.
This is so yummy.  I used recipe#19023 for the bbq sauce.  Thanks Wende :)  Made for All you can cook buffet

This was really delish.  I used 4 large bone in chicken breasts, covered them with bbq and then covered the pan with foil and baked at 350 for 45 minutes.  I removed the foil, added more bbq, topped with bacon bits and shredded cheddar and baked for an addition 10 minutes or so uncovered.  My son and husband thought this was fantastic and they are strictly drumstick and thigh guys!  I also thought this was very good, very moist - the green onions where a nice addition.
This sounded great but I found it a little bland... something was lacking.  I added some sour cream after cooking.  Wouldn't bother making again.
This is a simple and good dinner. Perfect meal for a weekday when you don't have a lot of time.
Very good and made for some very tender chicken. We will definitely be having this again - so easy to make!

Made this with pork chops.  I left out the bacon since I'm trying to watch the calories, but I did put some sautéed onions over it.... It was delish.  Served a small serving of brown rice and a big salad.  I will definitely make this again and try with chicken breasts.
This is a must try.  It was simply delicious.  So quick and easy too.  Thanks for posting such a lovely recipe.

Delicious, but super, super rich and salty. I will probably cut back on the bacon and barbecue sauce next time. I recommend adding fresh diced tomatoes on top along with the green onion; they gave it a nice burst of flavor.

I seasoned the chicken prior to adding sauce with seasoning salt and pepper and it came out perfect!  I didn't have bacon so I just used cheese, chives, and some sun dried tomato for the topping.  My boyfriend gave it 4 thumbs up...counting his toes lol

My husband enjoyed these, but overall they were too bland.   Definitely need something more in the spice department.    However, I do think this is a great recipe for a new cook or busy mom as it is definitely a step above drive-thru, but for us we probably won't make it as written again.

Using the same ingredients minus the green onions I cooked this a bit differently and it turned out fantastic! This is my whole families new favorite chicken dish! I used chicken tenderloins rather than chicken breasts and rubbed them all with hickory barbecue sauce in a mixing bowl. Use the same amount of tenderloins as bacon strips. I used 14, which was the same amount as one standard package of bacon. Cut each bacon strip in half and wrap each half over each side of each tenderloin, leaving a gap between the bacon halves. This allows you to cut the chicken in the center with a fork and have a half strip of bacon in every bite. Cook on a pan at 350 for 30 min then take out and turn the over off. Sprinkle chedder cheese over each tenderloin and put back into the oven for 5 min. Don't turn the oven back on for the remaining 5 minutes. I served it with cottage cheese and avacado. So so delicious and perfectly moist!
Very good! I did season the chicken breast with seasoning salt before I put the bbq sauce on. Will make again, thanks for the recipe.
We used Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce & turkey bacon. Even my super picky 7 year old daughter loved it! And so easy!
I have prepared this with Honey BBQ sauce and with Kraft Bold. I prefer the Honey. It compliments the bacon and cheese perfectly. This is so easy and SOOOO good. Give it a try.

Great flavor, changed a few things. Seasoned the chicken with poultry seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, and pepper. Browned them in a pan with butter and evoo. Spread Baby Rays Ray's Honey B B Q sauce over them. Baked 10 minutes, added Boars Head 3 pepper cheese over top, followed with some low salt bacon strips, and returned to a turned off oven for 5 minutes. They had a nice touch of smoke from the bacon, a little heat from the cheese, and a tad of sweetness from the B B Q Sauce. The better half and I both enjoyed these very much, will make again. Simple and easy! Thanks Wende.
Easy and Good. Minus the green onions. Thanks for posting.
Pretty good! Added seasoned salt and seared it in my cast iron pan first then did everything else as directed.
My daughters and I loved this delicious recipe. Will definitely be adding this to our weekly meals.

This lovely dish is a great way to serve up tomatoes.  I used red cherry tomatoes.  Love the combination of the blue cheese  dressing with the tomatoes.  Very pretty dish too....nice presentation.  You did it again, Scoutie.

I loved the taste of this, but my dressing wasn't thick enough.  I think I'd whisk it or use an immersion blender to get the dressing thicker....it dripped off my yummy tomatoes.  But have no fear, a big slice of french bread took care of all the dressing that dripped off!  The combination of flavors is perfect!  Thanks for sharing.  Made for PRMR tag.

I'm surprised this recipe hasn't been reviewed previously as it has common ingredients and is a quick meal to prepare. Even better it tastes good and my 3 year old ate it with gusto. 
I used the Australian mountain pepper instead of ordinary pepper, and pasta spirals for the pasta. Otherwise the recipe was made as written. The olives provide a nice salty touch which often is lacking with cream based pasta sauces. Thanks Char!

I have a confession to make.  I don't really like summer squash - I just keep buying it because it's always on sale at my grocery store.  So, I offer my congratulations: this is the only squash recipe I have ever really enjoyed.  So thank you!  My adjustments were slight - the only important change was that I sliced my squash into 1/8 of an inch slices, since I prefer them that way.  But thanks for a recipe that will keep me from suffering through my squash impulse-buys in the future!
I added a little more garlic and some seasoning salt, but otherwise followed the recipe.  The cheese makes a wonderful addition.

I really liked this recipe, I'm always trying to find ways to get my little guy to eat veggies. He loved it. I did this recipe on the girll. I have one of those grillers for veggies so they don't fall thru the BBQ grill. I used the same ingrdients but I put olive oil with the mix so the veggies wouldn't stick. Thanks!!

A meal in itself!  Delicious.  We had this last night along with some fresh lima beans and baked tomatoes.  I made no changes to the ingredients and amounts, but did alter the prep slightly:  I sliced the vegetables thinner (1/4") and did not cover the pan, allowing the juices to evaporate somewhat.  I upped the heat a bit, which caramelized everything nicely. A true winner!
Deeeelicious! I made Moroccan Spice Burgers on the grill this evening and used this raita to top it off. It was simply amazing. Thanks for sharing, I will use it countless times.
This is a very stiff dough, didn't rise much and not sweet enough. There has to be something missing or I have done something wrong. Anyone else try this recipe?
Very interesting, as this is the first time that I ever saw a Borsch recipe that does not contain any beets, as I always understood that Borsch was a beet soup.

Like Alan Leonetti, I'm a bit puzzled about the name of the soup because it does imply the presence of beets. On the other hand, a soup by any other name should taste as good, and if it tastes this good, who cares what it's called? The secret is in the lemon juice which imparts a nice zingy tartness. I microwaved the lemons 20 seconds before squeezing to get maximum juice production. A great cabbage soup!  (P.S. I did cut the cold water down to 1 cup for a thicker soup.)

This is one great tasting soup! A wonderful old cookbook from the library years ago allowed that not only did recipes for Borsch vary from county to country but from family to family - in some countries - simply another name for soup. Made as posted and these soup lovers here enjoyed this Cabbage Borsch. How good - another pot is in the planning. Thank you and thank your friend for sharing her mother's recipe ... this is going into my family favorites!

We absolutely enjoyed this dish -- loved the sweetness of the tomato juice and the added lemon juice.  I did not add a lot of meat to the dish, but I made up for it with some extra cabbage, carrots and potatoes.  Will definitely make this delicious borsch again. : )

being of Ukrainian/polish heritage..there is  Borscht (beet)..and Cabbage Borscht..also Root vegetable.Borscht.. I only make beet Borscht..but will defintely try this..my dad said my Gramma (ukrainian side) always made with cabbage..my gramma (maternal) polish always made beet borscht..huggzz
This is a quick and easy way to dress up refrigerated breadstick dough.  We served these as a side to soup and liked the extra Parmesan flavor.

Yes, I "twisted your arm" to post this gem of a recipe!  I'm honored to be the first review!  I made this when Mirj first described it in the Somersize recipes thread.  I used a small tub of whipped cream cheese with garlic and dill.  I also added a can of chopped mushroomus and a few healthy splashes of hot sauce.  This recipe is fantastic because it's exceptional in it's original form, yet the door is wide open for experimentation!  I've made this three times, and the last time I substituted frozen chopped broccoli for the spinach, and it was great!  Thanks Mirj for a legal, easy recipe!

This is so GOOD!  I cut back on the amounts, as I was only making it for myself, and really regret having done so - - I want more!  :)  I used fresh spinach and reduced the initial cooking time, and then only zapped for a couple of seconds with the cream cheese.  I totally forgot to add the hot pepper sauce, but will add it when I make this again tomorrow.  Thanks so much!
Fantabulous. Just the thing for a strep-throat sufferer [me]. I took Yooper's hint and used the flavored whipped cream cheese. Thanks Mirj for another winner!!

Oh Baby!  This is good!  I had some fresh spinach from my widdle biddy garden, steamed it and then added some soft creamed cheese, flavored with onions and chives.  The only thing is, I should have drained my spinach a little more before adding the creamed cheese.  My DH was out of town so it was just me and the kitties for this feast!  Lucky me!  A definite winner.  Does "Mr. Food" know about this one?

I was looking for an idea to use some leftover cooked swiss chard and used this recipe as my base. Didn't have enuf cream cheese, so added some feta and some velvetta.
Then with this leftover I used it in Cream of Spinach Soup 76808. I am the leftover queen!

This is just what we needed here in this house.Mark loved it. I did not add anything to it. However Mark did add his salt. OH my that I wish he would not add.
I did add my pepper. This is very good. I am not changing anything. 
Thank You.
Mirj, my husband and I absolutely LOVED this spinach preparation!  And it is so easy!  We love spinach, and we'll be having it alot more often now.  : )  Thanks!

I microwaved my fresh sp inach (no water) in baking dish, covered with plastic wrap for 2 minutes and stir in cream cheese with chives. It couldn't have been easier. I added some on top of plain cooked noodles, too.  I loved to but it didn't make the kids like spinach any better. Oh well, it's difficult to please everyone. 

Roxygirl in Colo.

I needed a leafy vegetable for Thanksgiving and believe in having one dish that's microwaved on that day so as not to compete for the oven and stovetop. I quadrupled this recipe, using 2 8-oz tubs of garlic-and-onion whipped cream cheese and adding a 6 oz bottle of sliced mushrooms. It fit the bill wonderfully and got compliments all round. Then I brought home the leftovers and gobbled up the rest right out of the bowl. A valuable and tasty time-saver that will go in my Standbys cookbook.
I really enjoyed this, Mirj. It was unbelievably quick & easy, & it was really good. Thanks for a great recipe.
This was a great last minute way to jazz up frozen spinach. I did end up adding some garlic to round out the flavor a bit. hanks so much for posting!
Excellent, for when you're looking for something quick.  I could've eaten the whole bowl myself!  Thanks!

I just realized I hadn't yet rated this delicious low-carb delight...  I was not a huge fan of spinach but this is a recipe that could convince me to eat spinach every day! My husband loves spinach so he is delighted that I found this. Thank you for this delicious recipe! I also added fresh grated parmesan on top once served.

This is just what I was looking for, a quick, easy, tasty recipe with spinach. I can't believe how good it came out when it was so easy to make! I followed the recipe exactly this time, next time I will play around and add garlic, and maybe some bacon bits. This really is great!

This was so easy, and really good! I used 16 oz of spinach and 5 oz of cream cheese. Six of us ate from that amount, but I really think I could have eaten more. I was worried about the dish being runny, but really the frozen spinach didn't have as much liquid as I thought. Although this is not as rich as my favorite creamed spinach, it is wonderful when I am tired and hungry.

Surprisingly delicious for such a simple recipe. The red pepper flakes give it the perfect amount of kick. DH, who doesn't even like spinach, ate two servings in no time flat. Took no time at all to make, and tasted like I put a lot of effort into it. YUM!
We used fat-free cream cheese, and flavor was awesome beyond reason. Rates five full Popeyes!
This was a nice quick side.  I drained some of the water from the spinach once it was cooked  before adding the cream cheese and I think that helped it not be so watery.
Quite nice and easy to make.  Thanks for sharing, CJAY.  :-)
This is a good and easy dessert to make.  I followed all the ingredients per recipe.  Made for Bargain Basement Game.
Made this over the weekend while camping on the lake with my family! This was amazing!!! Best cake I've ever made!
after  frying-put back in pan, steam squid in vingar--I like this cold or hot. The vingar  takes the fishy taste out, that is how my gandmother taught-they were from the island just off from Greece

Great name, great recipe, I love the simplicity and will have to tune it a bit to get a better looking result thanks 
S.F.

This was good. Due to apartment complex rules and weather, I was not able to grill the chicken.  I used chicken thigh that I skinned,  and baked them with the sauce and cheese and then poured them over the noodles. It was quite tasty. I have made this before without the extra cheese. I will do it this way more often. Thanks for a great recipe. Made for PAC '07
This was good but next time I will mix some mozzarella in with the noodles to make it cheesier. I also used leftover rotisserie chicken in this recipe and rotini noodles

ABSOLUTELY THE BEST!!!!! I have been trying to make a roll like this for a couple of years and I am no Betty Crocker! I followed the recipe exactly, with perfect results! All I can say is the first dozen was gone before we sat down for dinner! Thanks for a real winner!

These are the BEST!!!!!!!!!!!!!  I am so pleased with how they turned out.  I made them tonight to go with dinner and they were the most delicious rolls I have ever made.  They turned out light and fluffy and, well... perfect in every way!  A superior recipe!  I will make these often, as they are very easily put together...the bread machine does all the work!  Thanks for a new favorite!  I highly recommend these to anyone wanting to make an excellent dinner roll!  You won't be dissappointed!

The rolls turned out great on my second try(they were hocky pucks the first time) because if you follow the recipe exactly there is not enough rising time before making the rolls in step 2.  I put a 2 hour rising time in between step one & two and they turned out wonderful

Made these rolls a bunch of times now, everybody raved over them.  I must say that I cut down on the sugar to less than half the amount and didn't brush with honey as I didn't want them to be so sweet. I now also use about 3/4 cup of strong brown flour and the rest is white bread flour.  Thanks for posting such a super recipe!

I need a higher number to choose here for rating!! :)
This recipe is absolutely awesome! I couldn't believe my eyes when I opened up my bread maker after dough had risen, and to top that I was amazed how fast they rose before baking. If DH didn't know I was making these he would have sworn I brought these in the store. LOL   Thanks so much for posting this nice recipe.  Keeper in my book of breads!!!
Excellent.  I don't have a bread machine, so I just made them by hand.  Very delicious!  Thanks for posting.
I like yeast rolls so I'm going to try them and come back an let you know how they turned out.

Excellent roll recipe. I brushed half with the honey butter and half with regular butter when they came out of the oven.  I shaped into 12 rolls, because it says 12 servings and needed about 18 minutes bake time.  Also, I baked in the middle oven rack because with my electric oven, the coils burn things on top if they're too close.  Thanks much for posting!
Don't be fooled by how small they are when you divide them into rolls.  They are huge when they rise for the last time and extremely good.  My whole house smelled like baking bread.
Just like cafateria rolls!  We even subsituted 1 1/2 cups of whole wheat flour and they were still light, healthier, and just as good.

NOTE: This review is for my mom, who doesn't have a Zaar account, but will as soon as I get to her house.  

"These rolls were PERFECT!  What I'd been looking for.  My bread machine is in storage (they're remodeling) and I mixed them up by hand..just threw them together.  They were SO SOFT!  SO GOOD!  (she raved on and on!)  I am so happy I finally found a recipe I've been looking for!  Thanks!"  Now, I have to try them...and if you don't care, pass them on my readers with your permission.

Oh my gosh are these good.  Really, really good.  I have a favorite bread machine yeast roll that I make all the time and they are fabulous.  But these are better!!  Very close to Quincy's rolls, plus the honey butter.  Wow!! Thanks so much.  This is my new favorite yeast roll!!
Made these and we loved them. Will for sure be making these again. They sure impressed my husband's boss.

Very good rolls!  I subbed 1 c whole wheat flour for 1 cup of the bread flour and the results were just great!
