The flavor was just perfect!!!..my kids (11 & 16yrs) want to know why there isn't more??? gotta go, makin' another batch and printing this out for all my friends to try!!!
This was ok - dh liked it but 11 yr old thought it tasted "sour" - it could have been from the plain yogurt though...

Absolutely delish!  After I served this, I heard something I've never heard before:  "When's leftover night?"  This dish is so rich that half of it served my family of 4 big-eating adults.  A note: I used only 2 rolls of crackers and there was plenty.  I also decreased the butter to 3/4 cup.

I did not make the recipe as it was posted due to the reviews so it's hard to rate it correctly. I payed attention to the reviews and make adjustments accordingly and it came out really really good. My DH didn't even use ketchup or hot sauce like he does on everything because he said he didn't want to ruin the flavor. I read complaints about the fat content, so I marinated it in fatfree yogurt instead of sourcream, and I greased the pan with a little bit of oil instead of all that butter, then I only drizzled about 1/4 cup butter over the chicken instead of 1/2. I also read reviews that the crackers were too sweet, so I used half Ritz crackers, half bread crumbs. As for the spices, I replaced the 2 TBS terragon with Garlic Salt and Italian Seasoning/ Oregano, salt/pepper, and a touch of Cayenne pepper. I think we should use the herbs we like here. It Was Really Great. Thank you Steven for the recipe and thank you everyone for the reviews.  This is how you perfect a recipe for yourself!

Read all the reviews, used part Ritz, part saltines, and left them a bit chunky.  Used half the total butter, dredged individual strips that I had marinated in fat free yogurt- no sour cream here. Hate tarragon, used combo of garlic, herbes de provence, salt and pepper, cooked a bit longer.  Good, still very rich, even with the changes.  DH loved it.  I thought it was good, but falls short of great for me.  Was fast and super easy though.  I would make it again, with more garlic next time.

Sorry but Ritz crackers aren't available here in The Netherlands so " 1 Box Ritz crackers, 3 roll size " was a pretty useless measurement for me and I had to completely and totally guess the quantity of breadcrumbs. (I used approx 1.5 cups in the end)I read all the reviews, used 125g butter in total, halved the tarragon and upped the cooking time so that it became crispy and asked the 6 people at dinner to rate it... generally it was liked becuase indeed it wasn't dry and was tasty, but they agreed that it lacked the total "wow" we expected to get given the title of the recipe...  therefore I would have given it 3 stars, but DH who isn't a huge fan of chicken actually asked for it to go into my cookbook and for me to make it again, and that alone was worth the increase in rating to 4 stars.
Summary: nice enough,easy to make, would make again, everyone liked it but it wasn't nearly exceptional enough to rate a "5". Thanks for sharing it Steven :)

Totally TDF!  Couldn't believe I didn't rate this as I've been cooking this for a few years now.  It's a family favorite around here and my relatives often ask that I bring to potlucks & parties.  Yummy yummy yummy!

This recipe is definately a favorite of mine! This time I made it I didn't realize I was out of Tarragon & Marjoram until I was in the process of seasoning. So I used Mrs. Dash seasoning and a little bit more parmesan cheese instead. It turned out pretty good anyway. Great recipe for church dinner. Thanks for sharing!

Steve-  As the recipe stands my family would give your famous chicken 3 stars.  They felt it was too buttery so we would cut it back to 1/2 cup and half of the cracker crumbs.  We liked the flavor a lot but there was just too much butter floating in the dish.  They do want me to try it again making the adjustments though.  Thanks for the recipe. Paddles

This is definately to "die for".  It even tastes good the day after...cold!  I ate the leftovers for breakfast because I woke up craving them!  Cut back on the butter, and used different spices, but OMG it was good!

Followed recipe to a "T" - was awesome!!! Hubby told me rate it 6 STARS. Used Sour Cream, Chicken in a Biscuit & Marjoram, and would not change a thing about it.  Regarding butter, I didn't notice any greasiness or such. Was really a perfect recipe & weeknight meal. Easy & tasty. Thanks for posting!

This dish was excellent!  I will absolutely make this again.  I only used 2 rolls of crackers and I still had a bunch left over.  I just sprinkled the remainder over the top.  Also, I forgot the tarragon or marjoram, but I don't think it mattered much!
Very good. A little on the rich tasting side for me. But my family loved it, so I am giving it a higher star rating than I would just for myself. Thanks for the recipe!
I tried this out on a table full of guests and it was wonderful.  I doubled all the ingredients except the butter and only used 1/2 cup total butter.  Very impressive recipe with little effort!

This is OK.  It lacked flavor, unless you consider "fat" as a flavor.  It was a tad boring, I thought.  My husband liked it better than I did.  I followed other's advice and cut down the butter to 1/4 total and I can NOT imagine having more.  If you have picky eaters, this is a good choice.

This was very good!!  I used 1/2 cup of butter, Chicken in a bisquit crackers, marjoram, garlic
and plain yogurt.  Everyone loved this.  I will make again and perhaps season the chicken just a bit more. Thanks for posting!!!!

I haven't tried this exact recipe, but I make something close to it. In the sour cream you need to add worcestershire sauce, enough to turn it a beige color, maybe 2 tble. spoons, and some lemon juice, about 1 tbl. You will first dip breast into butter, coating well, then dip it into sour cream mixture, then roll in ritz crumbs or bread crumbs, pour remaining butter over each breast, it shouldn't be much.
No need for the parmesan cheese nor the tarragon. 
The breast are so moist. I have found that the frozen boneless skinless breast are the most tender.
yummy & easy.  this stayed nice and moist.  kids loved i-i too used only 1/2 cup butter total and it was good. thanks for the yummy recipe.

I didn't really care for this recipe I thought the Chicken was a little bland, I tried it again this time I use a mixture of sea salt and a very little course sugar and it was better, Maybe I'll try it with Chicken in a biscuit next time.

We loved this chicken....wow!!
I made one addition and added some garlic to the crumbs and boy, was it ever a big hit.
I'll be making this one again!
Thanks for posting!

Maybe not 'to die for', but very tasty. I used 1 cup crushed chicken-in-a-biscuit crackers mixed with 1 cup Italian breadcrumbs for the breading. I wasn't entirely sure if this recipe was calling for fresh or dried herbs and I noticed that some people said the flavor was too strong so I went with 2 tablespoons of fresh chopped marjoram (thinking they used dried and it came out stronger). I did cut the butter down to 1/2 cup and it was still too much. It kept the breading a little soggy. At any rate, it was easy; the chicken was moist and tender and the overall flavor was good. Thanks.
â€” Update -
Tried this again with ritz and tarragon instead of chicken-in-a-biscuit and marjoram and added 1 1/2 tsp garlic salt, 1/2 tsp each cayenne pepper and thyme to the mix as well. Definately liked the marjoram better, no real preference on the crackers. I used turkey this time which worked fine and cut the butter down to 2 tbsp which made it still soggy on the bottom, but crisper on top.
Loved the tarragon flavor! I followed the advise of some reviewers and sprayed my pan with cooking spray and cut the amount of butter in half.

This is outstanding! Don't leave the parmesan out - it gives it quite a flavor. I made this for the first time and everyone LOVED it. This is definitely a keeper. It is to die for - you become addicted to the flavor and want more and more.

DH and I had this for dinner tonight. Nice! We have a similar recipe that calls for Dijon mustard mixed in with the sour cream. Next time, I'll add some cayenne or mustard to spice it up a bit. All in all, though, this is a keeper. Thanks for sharing.
We didn't care for the flavoring of the Ritz crackers and the tarragon.  The chicken was very moist though.

I made this last night for dinner and boy is it good.  I doubled the recipe and used marjoram instead of the tarragon.( I was out)  We really liked this recipe.  I agree with the other reviewers about it being rich, but if only made in moderation....lol.  I will definately make this again, so simple yet so good.  Thank you.....Stephanie

My whole family loved this recipe and I have made it several times. The chicken turns our super moist and I love the flavor of the Chicken in A Biscuit crackers! My only complaint is that the bottom of the chicken turns out soggy. I have altered the amount of butter and with only 4 tbs. it tastes the same but less soggy. So I melt 4 tbs. and drizzle it over the top of the chicken before baking it. I don't put any butter into the bottom of the dish- this helps keep the coating crunchy!

We really liked this recipe.  Since we are on a lower calorie diet, we substituted the regular sour cream for low fat sour cream and sweet butter for "I Can't Believe It's Not Butter" and since we did not have tarragon or marjoram we used paprika.  Even with these substitutions, it was really delicious.  We will be making this many times to come.

I finally got around to making this dish.  I loved it, as written. Baked it a wee bit more for crispness and subbed "Smart Balance" for the butter. 
I like a mild dish and this fit the bill. Tarragon is a must.

I'm sorry to say that for my family this was not to die for.  I used the chicken in a biscuit crackers and cut down the amount of butter just to keep the bottom from being mushy and it was just bland.  Of course we have probably had our taste buds burned off by all the hot sauce we eat.  Will not try again.  T

My husband & I loved this recipe! I used plain yoghurt and wholemeal salada biscuits as i didn't have the other crackers. Also used mixed dried italian herbs and for a split second I thought i was eating a healthier version of KFC. This inspired me to search the KFC 'secret spices', and next time I make this I will substitute the cheese & herbs with the KFC secret spices!
Good. I added garlic. Served with rice and steamed broccoli. Thanks.

You have to give 5 stars to a recipe that you really go astray on and it still is super!  I thought I had gotten chicken out, instead I had thick pork chops.  Being short on time I thought, heck with it.  This should work on those too.  It did and it was darn good.  Juicy!!  I just pasted on the sour cream let em sit for an hour.  I used Ritz crackers the vegetable kind.  Did them in the oven for about the same amount of time turning them half way through.  Turned out great.  The coating was not real real crispy but browned nicely.  Thanks Steven, add pork chops to die for!

Just used 2 tbsp of butter and mixed cheddar cheese with parmesan.Put the chicken in a dish added the yoghurt and then tipped in the rest of the ingredients-it came out fab the top was crunchy and the sauce was lovely.
I made this yesterday and the name is right on.I used only 1/2 cup butter.

The whole family loved this juicy & tender dish!  I let 3 lbs. of chicken tenderloins & sour cream marinate in a ziploc bag for an hour.  I only had 2 rolls of the Ritz crackers...I crushed those & added some Italian seasoned bread crumbs & grilled chicken seasoning.  I didn't have Parmesan cheese, so I used mozzarella.  To cut down on prep time, I layered the bottom with 1/2 cup of butter and a few crumbs.  I then layed the chicken on top of that, followed by the mozzarella, bread crumbs & butter.  I cooked this for 45 minutes and it came out perfect!

the meat was really nice and the taste was OK on the top, although I would add some salt - but there was way too much butter and it made the cracker really soggy on the bottom of the chicken. so next time I will try to reduce the sour cream and be very careful with the amount of butter I use...
I have made this dish twice now. I let the chicken marinate overnight in the sour cream. I also added just a little bit of seasoning to the Ritz crackers. All in all, excellent
HIGH fat content. Tender but the fat content was out of control-mild flavored but good

I'm not leaving stars since I switched it up a bit, using only enough butter to coat the bottom of the pan. This recipe was VERY tasty, giving the chicken a nice tang. Also, didn't marinate the chicken (no time), but plan on doing so next time. Yum, yum!

I switched this around a little bit to use what I had on hand.  I took some individually frozen chicken breasts and cut them into strips, cooked them on the stove top until almost done.  Then I added the leftover ranch dip we had (ranch salad dressing and sour cream) and poured it on top, combined some crushed Townhouse crackers with some parsley and parm cheese and 3 Tbs melted butter.  I stuck the whole thing in the oven for 10 minutes, then broiled it for about 4 minutes to really crisp up the crackers.  
This was fantastic- I ended up making the recipe the way it is written  about a week later, and Dh preferred the ranch flavor, so I will be doing that from now on.  Thanks so much for posting!
i made this dinner for some friends everyone loved it even my honey

I read all the reviews before attempting this dish. I added tobasco sauce to the sour cream, marinated it for two hours, sprinkled it with garlic salt before rolling in Ritz and I used the roasted vegetable flavor Ritz. Also, I cut the amount of butter in half and it was plenty. 
That said, this recipe was rated a "keeper" by DH, my 9 year old DD said it was great(and she came back and ate it cold for snack) my 8 year old Ds said it was good, and my 7 year old DD said she didn't like the taste. I thought it was good but next time I will spice it up a bit more and maybe try the Chicken in a biscuit crackers.
All in all, we will be making this recipe again.

Excellent!  I cut the butter to about 4 TBS and used 4 large chicken breasts sliced into strips.  used reduced fat parm. cheese and FF sour cream.  I also substituted 2 TBS Italian seasoning for the tarragon.  We really enjoyed it with green beans and potato rolls.  Thanks!
Good.

I give this recipe ten stars for taste and maybe 3 for texture of breading. The chicken was amazingly tender and moist ( I used tenders which always dry out) but the underside of the breading was soggy. I halved the butter and even though I drained the pan twice, there was still to much. Take my advice, grease your pan well and use maybe a 1/2 of stick total butter. I don't favor the spices used so I left those out and in place added a teaspoon of garlic powder to my crumbs along with a good dose of pepper. I will definitely make this again with less butter, Thanks!

We loved this recipe!  I adjusted a few things.  I halved the butter, used bread crumbs instead of Ritz, used garlic powder for seasoning and used cream of mushroom soup with chili powder mixed in instead of sour cream.  So I guess I kind of made it my own recipe, but it was based on this one.  My husband loved it and I will definitely be making it again.
Huge hit with my family.  Even my 2-year-old loved it!!!!!

Made this for the family I worked for and they requested it again tonight!!  It's super easy. They didn't have sour cream or yogurt so I used ranch dressing instead w/ a lil garlic powder added and it was SO GOOD!! Used breadcrumbs for the coating and served w/ steamed veg and alfredo noodles - delish! Thanks for sharing!

This was really good.  However, I did cut the butter down like everyone suggested.  I also felt like it was lacking a bit of kick.  I used thyme, paprika, garlic, freshly ground black pepper flakes and salt insted of tarragon, because I was out.  I also used bread crumbs, since I didn't have any ritz on hand.  I think next time I will use the ritz cracker.  I bet the buttery taste helps kick it up.  I will also use the tarragon next time I make it.  It turned out pretty good though.

This was good although the fat content is rather scary.  I tried to cut down on some of the fat content.  I only used 1/4 cup of butter, 1/8 for the bottom and 1/8  for the top and think that if I ever made this again I would forgo it completely as it isn't necessary to the dish.  I also used low fat sour cream.  I added garlic powder, pepper and onion powder to the ritz cracker mix as well as I thought it may be bland otherwise.  As I said, I would make this again with even more modifications and perhaps try with a thicker yogurt next time.  It is a promising base that makes the chicken super moist.  Thanks for posting.

This is a great quick & easy recipe! I didn't have time to marinate as long as suggested and used less crackers and butter than it called for, but everything still turned out perfectly moist and flavorful.

Prepared 2 large breasts, sliced in half length-wise.  Marinated in sour cream for about 2 hours, then  dredged in plain breadcrumbs with some Panko, parmesan, garlic powder, onion flakes and tarragon (as suggested by other reviewers).  I did not melt butter in the bottom of the casserole -- just sprayed heavily with Pam Butter, and topped with 2 TBSP melted butter. This was tender, flavorful, and moist.  Thanks, Steve , for posting a tasty chicken dish !

Oh, this was definitely worth it!  I used chicken thighs, as that was what we had on hand.  I also added poultry seasoning, salt and pepper to the tarragon.  I also used only about half of a stick of butter.  It was moist and delicious but not soggy.
very good

This was good and very moist, but the chicken needed seasoning like onion powder or something.  Next time I'll season the chicken before marinating.  I'll also add a can of fried onion rings to the cracker crumbs.  Also, I had a ton of cracker crumbs left over, so I'll only use 2 tubes.  I reduced the butter to only 2 tb and drizzled it over the top of the crumbs and I used low fat sour cream.  Thanks!
Well, we REALLY enjoyed this chicken.  It was moist and yummy.  We had leftovers which were great cold in a salad.  Will add this to my dinner rotation.  Thanks for a great recipe!

My DH loved this recipe and told me I could make it for him "anytime".  I used a mix of breast and thigh, since he likes only dark meat.  I cut back on the crackers and the butter, but I think I could cut back on the butter even more.  I used marjoram for the seasoning, but I think I would prefer oregano and maybe some garlic or onion powder.  I certainly will make this again.  My husband thinks the recipe should be a six- or seven-star!  Thanks for a great recipe!

This was good, but just had too much of a sweet flavor to me. It was very crunchy, but I cringed using all that butter, so if I make it again I will cut back on the butter and maybe not use sweet butter, or add some garlic or ranch seasonoing to the crackers instead.  Overall a good recipe, but we will tweek it to our tastes. Thanks!

This was just ok for us.  I was expecting/hoping for a WOW.  It was good, but not great.  Made as directed.  It's always fun to try new recipes even if they don't work out for me, so thanks for sharing.
A++! We used whole chicken breasts and it was fantastic. Tasted so great. It's a keeper!

I would give this a 10 if I could.  I had to improvise a bit.  I only had 1 package wheat ritz and 1 package of saltines.  I crushed them all together and used oregano in place of the tarragon.   I did the rest the same.  My husband came very close to giving this a 10 - which he very, very rarely does!  Thanks for the keeper!

I made this dish for the first time and it was fabulous!! I used whole wheat crackers, low fat sour cream. and used the whole chicken breast instead of cutting it into strips. Very, Very moist chicken!! I made extra and heated it up the next day and it was still very most and alot of flavor. My teenage son and his friend couldn't get enough of it and didn't believe the coating was Ritz crackers! A definite KEEPER!!

Very tasty, and easy. The chicken pieces were moist, the coating was flavorful, with the tarragon giving a unique exotic touch. The one cup of butter almost made me pass this by, but I'm glad I didn't - DH & DS make this a keeper. As another reviewer suggested, I only used 2T butter, nonfat s. cream, & whole wheat Ritz - these worked out great. One thing - I used less than half of the crumb mixture & of course had to toss it since it had come in contact with raw meat. One and a half rolls (5-6 oz.) would have been plenty. But then you may want to reduce the parm. cheese & tarragon to reflect this change.

great recipe!  i read the reviews and here's what i did decided to do differently:  i cut the chicken into thin strips, i used the chicken in a biscuit crackers that i highly seasoned with pepper, garlic powder, chicken boullion granules, cayenne and tarragon, instead of using 1/2 the butter on the bottom of the dish i just sprayed with pam, i did use the 1/2 cup of melted butter to pour on the cracker crust, but i think next time i might use the whole cup of butter on top (terrible, i know)!!  i did need to broil a few minutes to brown up the crust.  i think next time i will spread the strips out on 2 baking sheets instead of have everything all crammed in a casserole dish, i think it made it a little soggy.  however, everyone loved this dish.  even the leftovers were delish reheated in the oven the next day!  i really loved the flavors of the cracker and tarragon crust with the sour cream.  thanks steven!!

I am re-rating! This can be modified in so many ways--sometimes I use wheat thins, chicken-in-biskit, or whatever crackers I have on hand.  I do recommend still cutting back on the butter.  Choose your own favorite herbs to add, or go with a more flavored cracker.

We loved it made just the way it was posted.  I wouldn't change a thing in this recipe!  We had it with baked potatoes and coleslaw for a very enjoyable meal!  I love the rich buttery taste from the Ritz crackers and the cheese adds so much flavor.  This is a winner!
Wow, this was awesome! I'm pleasantly surprised!
Awesome chicken!
Delicious!  The chicken was so moist and flavorful!  Thanks
Its ok. I used italian bread crumbs. Sprayed the bottom of the pan with Pam. It's not one of my favorites.

Loved this, although I did make it following MizzNezz's suggestions: reduce butter to 1/2 cup, reduce tarragon to 1 T, reduce crackers to 1 1/2 sleeves, add 1 t salt, 1/2 t pepper, 1/2 t cayenne pepper, 1/2 t thyme.  This is very moist chicken & flavorful.

I doubled the recipe to feed my guests and then followed Mizz Nezz's reductions and doubled them.  I used tarragon instead of marjoram and I have to tell you it was a hit all over the place!!  My company raved about it all through dinner.  Served with Garlic Whipped Mashed Potatoes and Corn in Butter Sauce it was MMmm Good!

Steven~Fantastic recipe the chicken came out beautifully crunchy on the outside and so moist inside
thankyou for posting this great recipe

I used light sour cream, a different combo of spices (smoked paprika, thyme, salt, & pepper), and only about 1/2 cup butter. It still came out a little greasy - I think you could cut back the butter even more. I'm a veggie so I didn't try it myself, but the BF thought it was great, even better when he added some more fresh-ground pepper. Hint for easy dredging: Crush the Ritz crackers, spices, and parmesan in a ZIploc bag, then just throw the chicken in there and shake the bag, two or three pieces at a time. Less mess!

Really disappointed with this recipe- hoped it would be better. Only used half the butter- but still very greasy & heavy. Chicken wasn't even crispy after 45 minutes. But the flavor was good albeit soggy. Sorry.

WOW>>>WOW>>>WOW! Thanks so much for posting this! It is incredible. One reviewer said this was bad???? NO way Iv'e eaten and made chicken a million was and this is now my all time favorite! I will make this forever! thank you SOOOOOOOOO much for a keeper!

I read the other comments after I made and ate this. I used the Chicken in a Biscuit crackers and made it as written except I knew that 2 tablespoons of Taragon was too much for my tastes and eyeballed what I put in. We all agreed that this recipe is a keeper with minor adjustments. Next cut the butter to 4 tablespoons or so and just pour on the top. For the bottom of the pan I will use PAM. I intend to keep tinkering with this recipe until I get it right to our liking. The taste was fantastasic and the chicken was so moist.
6/8/10 I remade this recipe last night.  I made the changes above.  I think I am going to cut the butter all together next time.

I found this recipe on this site years ago and make it for company and special occasions. It always receives raves, and although it does contain a good amount of butter, I have always prepared it without modifying it in any way, usually using Marjoram. I believe the crackers add to the distnict flavor of this recipe and the fact that it isn't crispy doesn't matter, it's delcious as well as very easy to prepare.

World famous, to die for?  C,mon Steven, this recipe was tasty, but not all that.  Too many reviewers modified by spraying the bottom of the pan and slightly drizzling the chicken with butter.  I did too, and am glad it was suggested.  On the plus side, this is easy to make, the chicken turns out tender and probably most cooks have all ingredients on hand.  I am looking forward to trying some of Steven's other recipes--they sound interesting.
I didn't have time to marinate the chicken for an hour so I dipped it in the sour cream and laid it in the bowl with the broken crackers & butter on top. Came out delicious!
I made this using bread crumbs and basil sooooooo good! I added some seasonings though to both the sour cream and crumbs mixture.

We really enjoyed this chicken dish. I did cut the amount of butter in half and used poultry seasoning ( not fans of taragon in the house). I knew going in that this was going to be a really rich dish. Since we generally eat healthy, a once in a while splurge is okay. To the reviewer who commented that this is a heart attack waiting to happen, if you are so concerned with it being unhealthy, why did you make it? My main gripe is the comment that "the only one who enjoyed it lives outside and eats out of a bowl" is really nasty. It does not make you cleaver, just snarky. Shame on you. This site does not need nasty!!!

Don't make this recipe if you're dieting or want a low-fat meal - it's definitely not THAT!  But, it was one of the best "not good for you" chicken recipes I've ever made.  I cut the butter in half, increased the cooking time to 50 minutes and turned the chicken over half way through to brown both sides.  My hubby went back for seconds.  I'm using the left overs for chicken taco's tonight - hate to waste them!

I had to post a review because this was so good.  I just made an account to do so.  My husband hates sour cream so I did not tell him what was in the recipe until after he raved about how good it was.  I just had random boxes of crackers in the cupboard that I mixed together.  I think next time I am going to use goldfish crackers.
These were really good...had such a delicious taste!  I will for sure make again!  I did only use 1 cube of butter and it was quite sufficient.
My family LOVED this! It was easy and delicious! Thanks for sharing

Yum!!! This chicken is terrific! I made it last night and got rave reviews from everybody. I served it with buttered noodles and fresh green beans. It will definately be a regular on my table. You know, when I see 5 star reviews and then a one star review, I wonder how this is possible. Maybe the one star reviewer left out a crucial ingredient? Like the chicken?
Followed this recipe - exactly as written - TWICE.  Result - Powdery, grainy, bland.  I'd have given this recipe less stars if I could.

Love those sweet potatoes, but I did make this for a small potluck! I was a little unsure about how the spinach would work here, but the completed salad was surprisingly satisfying! Thanks for sharing the recipe! [Tagged, made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in the current Pick A Chef]

I used this recipe when I had way too many cucumbers that needed to be re-purposed. I loved the thin slices with the mandolin, but I only had time to press them twice (I used paper towels instead of wax paper to get them more dry), and they were still a little soggy. I also added green peppers, diced, and omitted the dill b/c of by boyfriend's extreme aversion to it. For the dressing, I used equal parts mayo/greek yogurt/sour cream and added some acidity with lemon juice and a dash of white vinegar. The spicy garlic flavor made this dish refreshingly different from other cucumber salad recipes - overall pretty darn tasty!

I like this recipe as a flour-free option. I was able to make it with ingredients I had on hand, by substituting the red onions for onion powder and using plain yogurt in lieu of sour cream. I think I needed either more heat and/or oil to make them crispier, but they were still tasty and did the trick. I will adjust the amounts next time so they have more of a fried texture closer to traditional potato latkes of which I am accustomed.
Nice change. Made pretty much as directed, served topped with powdered sugar. Made for ZWT7, Pacific Islands.

This was really good.  The macadamia nuts (which I so love!) and coconut give it a nice tropical touch, and it dresses up plain French Toast rather nicely.  But I had a lot of trouble pefecting the cooking process.  With the first, the bread was fine but the nutty topping burned.  The second, the nutty layer was toasted nicely but the bread itself was hardly cooked.  This is a recipe I'll try a few times so I get it right, because it really is a good recipe.  Thanks, Lainey6605.  Made for ZWT7, Mischief Makers.

What a nice sweet start to the day, close your eyes, add a gentle warm breeze and you will transported to the Islands. The coconut and macadamia nuts are the prefect crunchy crust for the soft sweet Hawaiian bread. Made as written. Thanks so much for the post.
I really gobbled this up it was so delicious!  It was also very pretty plated.

Pretty much made this as given, although I did leave off the cream & seeds! Just the two of us to eat it, & it was just as satisfying the second time around! Really enjoyed the garlic & thyme combo! Thanks for posting the recipe! [Made & reviewed for one of my adoptees in this Spring's round of Pick A Chef]

Excellent! One of the best couscous recipes I've tried yet, although I had no orange juice concentrate but only orange juice. It was still awesome. To be gluten free, I used rice couscous which worked beautifully. Thanks so much for sharing this gem!
Made for N*A*M*E travels to Morocco 11/2012

Very good!  I served these pastry triangles with butterscotch ripple ice-cream & whipped cream for Easter dessert - very rich.  Everyone loved them!  This was my first attempt at phyllo so they weren't the prettiest triangles to look at but I still managed to impress my family.

I am "cooking out of my pantry" this week, while we get ready for a trip with the family... i had a package of phyllo dough in the freezer and thought i'd make a dessert... i was all out of coconut?  but i chopped up some almonds - i only had one baking square of unsweetened chocolate so i subbed 3 T cocoa powder and 1 T melted butter for each of the other squares - and mixed in a good dollop of sugar :) - they turned out really really good... a little adult i thought since the chocolate wasn't as sweet as it could have been, but my children gobbled them up and my husband loved them.  I dusted them all with powdered sugar and they were a sweet treat :)

Lovely lunch ! I used roast beef cold cuts and left out the sprouts, personal preference, DH dosen't care for them. and I added some dejon mustard and used whole wheat pita and no fat ranch dressing. Very good and crunchy! thanks for posting.

Absolutely yummy!  I just added about 3 tablespoons of honey to the apple juice, and we had a great dinner.  I served it with plain rice, and there was lots of gravy/juice for the rice to soak up!  Unfortunately, there were no leftovers.  I may have to treble the recipe next time...
Excellent, easy and quick way to serve chicken. I followed the recipe exactly with good results and we all loved this dish.
A little splash of apple brandy braces up the flavor something wonderful.

My family and I loved this chicken dish. The sauce is bitchin'. The flavor of chicken and apples is a new discovery for me and one that I find extremely yummy.Thanks Dorothy. You are so right, this is a wonderful fall recipe.

Delicious recipe! Very quick and easy to make, too. I used apple juice not cider. I halved the recipe to serve two, but kept the juice/vinegar/cornstarch the same so that there would be lots of sauce. Very good taste, I'll be making this again.

A quick and easy dish that presents itself (and tastes) quite nicely. I think it's perfect as is, but my husband thought mustard would lend a touch more flavor and salt to the sauce. I served it with Miller's Chicken Mashed Potatoes (17415).

I was in the mood for a real fall kind of dinner since it was cold and dreary outside.  This was exactly what I was looking for!  It has a great fall flavor.  The only problem I had was in getting enough sauce when I mixed in the corn starch.  I think I just wasn't carefull enough when I remover the food from the pan, so I think I scooped out a lot of the juice that should have been left in the pan to make the gravy.  It was still a great dinner!  Thanks

I made this for Thanksgiving. WOW!! Nurse Di, this is another one of your outstanding recipes The color was a most beautiful pink. Had a predominantly creamy texture but the nuts provided crunch. My family raved. Will make this again for Christmas. Thanks :)

This frozen salad was outstanding. Had a sweet-tart flavor and a luscious creamy texture. The cranberry flavor was the perfect accompaniment for our pork dinner. Kids and adults all liked this at my house. Thanks for this one.

This was very easy to make and had a pretty, festive pink color. We almost liked the little taste tests of the unfrozen version better; kind of a cranberry ambrosia...might try leaving it unfrozen next time. :) The tart side seemed a bit strong, but overall it was a great recipe. Thanks!

Loved it - reminds me of a frozen salad that I had lost the recipe for - maybe this is it!  The flavors and textures blend together really well, and make a delicious (kind of healthy if you use fat-free milk and Cool Whip, which I did) dessert/salad.

I was so happy to find this recipe which my Grandma called Frozen Fruit Yummy. It is my favorite childhood Thanksgiving memory! I used walnuts instead of pecans and added an 8 oz package of softened cream cheese! I also froze these in colorful muffin papers just like my grandma. 
Yummy and delicious!!
I love this recipe!  It is a nice addition for a holiday dessert table.  I prefer it slightly thawed, the flavors and textures are a great combo.

This was just ok for us. It was quick and easy but somewhat lacking in flavor, I thought. Apples and onions together didn't cut it for my kids at all. With so many recipes out there to try, I probably won't make this again.

Wow.....If I do say so myself, this dinner was great! I made this last night for my son and new girlfriend and they both gobbled it up! I also served a mixture of oven roasted veggies....yum! I could almost hear my son purring! Hubby commented that it was good but I didn't make enough!  So I'll have to increase the quantity next time! Only change I made was the apple cider...I didn't have any.  So I used white wine....I added that and a few capers to the sauce for more zip, threw in the apple and onion mixture after the sauce thickened, added the chicken to absorb some of these flavours...and wow! Outstanding meal!  Thanks, Derf.....this meal is much too good just for the fall.....it's a year round winner!
Really tasty with great flavours. I used apple juice and served with creamy mashed potatoes and green beans.
Very good.  I added some garlic.  Didn't have as much sauce as I would have preferred.  Will try it again with more liquid and a few splashes of tabasco.  Thanks!
Love this sauce. The chicken is moist and tender with a browned outside--just right! Made for the Christmas Spelling Bee in Cooking Photos.

Very good dish - my whole family enjoyed it very much.  Quick and easy to make which is perfect for a busy weekday. Next time I will cook the onions just a bit longer other than that won't change a thing.

This recipe is awesome! Really simple and really yummy. Everyone in my family loved it. Just make sure you warn everyone that it's apple and not potatoes! my brother took a bite expecting potatoes and was so shocked he couldn't eat any more of the apples!

This was a nice change of pace recipe. I cut the chicken down to  serve one and the sauce to serve two. This is a recipe I'll tinker with. I did add a splash of balsamic vinegar at the end to give it a little more bite.

The flavors in this dish were really delicious. I used an Empire and a Macoun apple, and followed the directions as they were. The only issue I have with the recipe is that the chicken was quite tough. I had to cook it for longer than the additional 7 minutes after browning, and they weren't especially large or thick breasts. It was still a tinge pink when we cut into it to eat, and not as tender as I would have hoped. I might broil the chicken next time instead of essentially steaming it to see if I can get a nice tender chicken to go with this delightful sauce.
This is such a wonderful recipe! The vinegar gives the sauce a really interesting twang. I will definitely be making this again! Thanks so much for sharing!
Everyone in my family loved this recipe including my very pick 2 year old! Thank you so much for posting this.
This was just ok, I would reduce the vinegar to 1tsp or possibly 1/2tsp if using tart apples.  Also, the Golden Delicious got fairly mushy, though Granny Smiths held up well.

Delicious, idiot-proof recipe!
I am NO chef, but this one turned out brilliantly!
(It was a good way to use up some apples I had left over that were a bit past their prime...)
Great leftovers too!

This was so easy yet so delicious.  The flavors blended great together.  I'll bet this would be good with pork chops, too.  I used Golden Delicious and they fell apart somewhat but no on cared.  Thanks for a keeper!

Very delicious, Derf.  The only complaint I have, is that it didn't make enough apple gravy.  (Maybe I cooked too long :()  Even so, I will fix this again, using different apples each time.  Thnx for sharing, Derf.  Made for Comfort Cafe Snow Queen Chalet Jan 2010.

This recepie is a HIT!
Very fast to prepare and has great taste! We were looking for healthy new ways to make chicken and this is certainly one we will be repeating!

Great recipe, add a little spice by adding a cinnamon stick, pinch of clove, and a pinch of nutmeg when making the sauce. Use a firm apple like Granny Smith, MacIntosh or Cortland Best to use a sweet onion like a Vidalia. Shallots or Leeks work too, instead of onion

I made this a couple of years ago when that issue was published and just thought of it when going through old magazines. It was pretty good, not the most flavorful meal in the world, but we added parmesan cheese to it and it was good. Might have to make it again soon!

Good crackers that are much like saltines, but don't break as easily.  To get them crispy and browned, I did cook them almost 20 minutes.  Recipe makes about 10 dozen crackers 1/8 to 3/16 inches thick.  I used an ungreased cookie sheet, and they did not stick.  The second time I made these, I substituted 2 cups cornmeal and whole wheat flour for the plain flour, and added 3 tbs sugar.  These turned out well, too!  For a theme party, I will make them again and cut with different shaped cookie cutters.  They are sturdy enough to use for thick spreads or for dipping.  Thanks Love4, for sharing this recipe.

Made these tonight because I ran out of Saltines... good recipe! I quartered it and they still came out okay. They tasted a little bland, but I only wanted them to eat with peanut butter, anyway. Thanks for the quick and easy recipe!

Great basic cracker recipe.  All of the other recipes I have used turn out a crackers that is incredibly hard.... you can hardly chew it.  This one is perfect.  I added 3 tablespoons of soda and spices.  You can add any kind of spice such as garlic, onion powder, hot spice, dill, caraway seeds and etc.  Oh and I also substituted 1 cup of the flour with masa flour.  They are a great snacking cracker.  Thanks!!
These were great. I halved the recipe and put in food processor using oil instead of the shortening. A definite keeper.

I gave this 3 stars b/c although my DD liked these, they were not crispy and took forever for her to chew. I do like the idea of making my own crackers and knowing what goes in them!

I added a little twist and pureed some veggies and added them to the dough (I used the milk as my liquid in the blender). A great way to add some more veggies in the diet! 

Also, next time I will put the salt directly in the batter, instead of sprinkling on top. And a trick I figured out (if you like the salt on top) is you can sprinkle the salt on the cookie sheet BEFORE you put the crackers on it. I found that the salt I sprinkled on there just fell off b/c the dough wasn't very sticky. Since salt doesn't melt and burn like sugar you don't have to try to remove the excess before baking. 

Thanks for the recipe :)

These are so cool! I followed the advice of some fellow reviewers and added some sugar and subbed a cup of cornmeal. I didn't have proper measuring instruments so had to estimate a lot, and we also added some spices. What we ended up with, though, was something that tasted like a cross between corn chips and Ritz crackers. I will be making this often! Thank you for sharing!

really yummy!! i doubt I'll buy store crackers again especially since this recipe is so easy to "play" with and adapt. Instead of sprinkling the salt on top I mixed some seasoned salt in with the flour and it came out great!!

Great recipe. I solved the salt sticking problem by dusting the dough with coarse salt and rolling it into the dough lightly before I cut it into crackers. Works great. Be careful they cook fast.
They taste great and it was a simple dough to make.

Easy, fast and tasty!  I used about half coconut oil and half butter for the shortening. I made two trays with just salt, one tray with lemon pepper and one with salt/granulated garlic.  I think the garlic ones were the best, then the plain ones and then the lemon pepper, which would have better if I had used some salt with it. The crackers took about 12 minutes in my convection oven.  Thank you for sharing this recipe!

I made these with 1 cup whole wheat flour and the rest white flour. I also used almond milk, and they turned out beautifully. The dough was easy to handle and they taste much like ritz crackers, probably because I used butter flavored shortening. Great recipe, thx for sharing!

They taste okay, but were not crisp like saltines. I remember making homemade crackers a few years back and there was no lard or shortening in that old recipe. Wish I could find it. I wound up making breakfast biscuits with the rest of the dough for the crackers. Turned out great. This recipe has the same ingredients as my biscuit recipe. I think this recipe would make nice "chicken in a biscuit" crackers because they are not crisp....more along the texture of cookies but not hard like a crisp cookie. I will let them sit over night and see how they are in the morning. I might try this recipe again sometime with no shortening in it. Thanks for the recipe! Great try!
I added about 1c of flaxseed meal to this recipe, and used pink Himalayan salt, and, whoa, delisioso, I have to say!
My mother made these when I was a child. I now get requests for them every Christmas. Very rich. My mother (and I) used a bit of the drained cherry juice, rather than orange juice.

We love mixed bean soup.(15 bean or whatever)I more than Trippled this recipe. Made it up in collander so I could mix them up real good then put them in a 1/2 gallon jar. Did the same with the spices, put it into a small jar. I used  a lot of odds and ends of beans that I had small amounts of.Some that are not list in the recipe,Cramberry beans  for one. Thank you so much for posting , will have to try your bean soup recipe.

This is a great bean soup mix. I didn't have some of the beans so I just added more of the ones I had on hand. I also didn't have dried peppers but added real green peppers and onions to the soup itself when made. Great gift to make for friends and family. 
Thanks for sharing the recipe.
I reviewed the recipe separately, but here I just want to add my note that I had to double each of the beans in order to fill a 1 quart mason jar.

Great bean soup mix, and great gift (my friends enjoyed it, too).  I did not use large limas, but substitued red beans (for christmas color), and added some barley.  I layered the beans (as in photo) and found that for quart size jars, I needed to use 5-6 tblps per layer, but only 2-3 tblsp per layer for the pint size jars.  As gifts, these were a big hit for Christmas 2008--thanks so much for posting this gift "recipe" (soup reviewed separately).

This is like no other sweet potato dish I've ever tried. The combined flavors are surprising, amazing and each ingredient complements the next beautifully. I love your technique of soaking the sweet potatoes... Brilliant. Thanks for another great recipe, ChefPisces... from Pisces Moon Chef Aries with a Cancer ascendant... hehe

DH kept nodding his head, he was too busy eating to tell me what he thought! Finally, he said this is a 10 star dish! I cut the pork crosswise, but... I think I should have cut it lenghtwise after cutting in quarters. I didn't have cherry tomatoes (couldn't find them at the store) so picked up grape tomatoes and left them whole. Served with  hot (spicy) green chile salsa, warmed tortilla's, sour cream and recipe #41168 on the side. Great dish that should be tried by all. Thanks, Lilladyc for posting.

I was just about finished with this review and it just disappeared! Once again, thisa is an easy to follow recipe. The only thing I'd do differently would be to cut back on the chili powder  a little. My hubby doresn't hand out compliments very often, but he said these were awesome, but it was a little spicy also. I'll be making this often, Mary thatnk you for sharing this!
Delicious baked beans!  I love bacon in baked beans and also loved the smoky-spicy flavor of the chili in these.  These easy-to-make beans will be a bbq staple at our house - thanks for sharing!
Excellent! I'll use a little less olive oil next time, but this is a repeat recipe.  Don't skimp on the tomatoes, they are critical.  Thank you!

This is a WOW recipe! It can be fixed so many ways. True to the Zaar tradition I "messed with it" a little. I used Mirj's sun dried tomatoes instead of fresh, chopped the spinach in the food processor used homemade spinach and basil pesto and sliced some kalamata olives to mix in also. I made it in the morning and chilled it until supper time and served it with some french bread and fresh fruit - it was delicious! This is a "doer again" as my husband says. Thanks, Carole in Orlando

Made one substitution in this recipe, in that I used OJ instead of water or ice & also used a large frozen banana, & enjoyed this drink along with pancakes for a satisfying breakfast! [Tagged, made & reviewed in Beverage Tag]

Tagged for Beverage Swap Feb 2009.  This is really good!  I love the taste of the banana mixed in but my juicer was a pain to clean out. i will use my blender next time, just did not feel like lugging in from the garage. I will make this again however as it gives me all my fruits for the morning.   I also added in cruched ice after the juicer blend.  I cn see this as a start off for many juices, incorporating spinach, giner, carrots, or a number of veggies. Thank you!

So easy to make, and delicious!  I did add a bit of garlic, (can't help myself), and used some mozzarella and cheddar mixed.  Also, I increased the amount of the meat to satisfy a teenage boy!  I didn't add salt while cooking the pasta, so I found I needed to add it to the finished dish in the skillet.  Great quick and easy recipe....and you are right....leftovers are great!  Made for Newest Zaar Tag.

This recipe is so simple but the taste is unbelievable.  So yummy.  Even if it's jar pasta sauce.  I used a 4 cheese pasta sauce.  I used penne pasta.  I wasn't too sure about the sour cream and cheese mixed together.  But I did it and was surprised by the taste.  It was really good.  Thanks Pink :)  Made for 123 hit wonders
Sister Mercy Good...I need a heart pill!  There, I said it.  Oh, I made one little mistake and stirred in the sour cream.

Oh this is good! I used ground round, added minced garlic and onion powder, a 26 ounce can of Hunts Garlic and Herb spaghetti sauce, and omitted the water. The sour cream and cheese didnt look like enough when I mixed it but I had more then enough to top the pasta. Simmered for 8 minutes and the topping was creamy. Loved the zippy flavor of the topping, the pasta was perfect, and we enjoyed a lot! Made and reviewed for the Kittencals  European Forums - Europe on a Plate is in ITALY.

Delicious! I made this dish a couple times, the first time I made it almost exactly the way it says to, except I used Rotini Primavera (the colorful pasta) because the dish in the picture here just looked so....bland, so I thought I'd make it a little more colorful. Also I was only able to use 1 lb of ground beef as that was all I had but it turned out great.

2nd time I made this, last night, I did something a bit different. I still used Rotini Primavera as my pasta of choice, but I was unfortunately out of shredded cheddar cheese, and only had a bag of Shredded Mozzarella. I used Ragu's Roasted Garlic Parmesan sauce instead of spaghetti sauce. It was only a 12 oz jar so I added the 3/4 cup of water and also shook the jar remnants with a little more water in the jar to add to it. I ended up using 2 lbs of ground beef, and the whole bag of mozzarella (about 2 cups worth) and probably almost double the amount of sour cream needed.
It turned out even better than the first time I made it. It was so cheesy and delicious.

Overall, easy, delicious dish that is easy to add your own personal touch to.

Such a simple recipe with simple ingredients but it really made a big difference! I added 5 cheese garlic Texas toast with sauce spooned over the top to complete the meal and it was fabulous all together!
Pretty good and quick to fix. Made at the last minute for an unplanned meal. Thanks for the recipe!

Oh so good! I loved the 4 cheese Italian blend. DH doesn't like the texture of onions or green onions so I did have to use granulated onion which still gave it the yummy onion taste. I chose to mash and put in a medium casserole and kept them warm in the oven while the rest of dinner was being buttoned up. They held nicely. When I broiled my skins, I had to practically beat my DS back with a wooden spoon because he loves crispy skins! I seasoned them up a bit with seasoned salt before crisping. Cute idea serving the crisps on the side. *Made for PAC Spring 2010*

What a delightfully different pudding!  Made as directed except for using Splenda and threw in some raisins as you suggested.  This is so easy to put together and so delicious.  Thanks for sharing a keeper recipe.

I think this soup is very good. I did use small, rather than baby carrots - toddlers, perhaps? And also used homemade chicken stock. I had only Indian style curry powder, which included some flour, so I used about 1 1/2 tablespoons of that, with no other flour. (I think I could have used slightly less, but am quite happy with the soup, so maybe not.) I love cilantro anyway, but also think it is an important ingredient in this soup - the flavor went from just okay to really wonderful after it was added. Thank you very much for sharing this recipe.

Very simple soup to make that cooks up quickly.  I didn't have curry paste so I used 1 Tbsp of curry powder.  Also used chicken broth in place of vegetable stock.  I found the yogurt to round out the flavor nicely.
Delicious soup and so easy to make. I made as directed and mixed the yogurt in for a nice creamy texture and taste.

I made this with Cranberry chutney because I couldn't find any Mango chutney...this was the best glaze ever! The flavor combinations of the brown sugar, garlic, orange zest and chutney was perfect! This is the perfect way to dress up your ham. I'm going to keep this recipe and look for Mango chutney!
Thanks Mean for sharing another of your 5 star recipes!
I used this glaze on my Easter ham and man oh man was it fabulous.  Just the perfect sweetness to the salty ham.  Thanks MeanChef for yet another keeper.
I didn't think I'd like this better than my old tried and true maple syrup/rum glaze, but it is absolutely superb!

Despite my reluctance to give poor reviews, I am unable to recommend this recipe.  Given the source and the glowing comments, I took a chance.  Didn't work out.

Both the garlic flavor and the orange flavor were strong to the point of being overwhelming.  My guests were 'put off', to say the least.

Perhaps I should note that these are people who love and appreciate good food.  They have enjoyed several of Mean Chef's recipes enormously.  Sorry to say that this one just didn't work.

This is the recipe I am going to use for all my hams from now on. Since there are only 2 of us in the family. I used one of the boneless packed hams. This is not to be confused with "fully cooked spiral-cut smoked ham, on the bone". My recipe using a cheap cut was fantastic. I used Mango Chutney. Can not wait to try this with a good ham.Dh kept commenting, how this was one of the best hams he had ever had & he is an expert as my MIL knows how to pick & cook a ham! Thank you Mean Chef.

Could not resist trying this because I love mango.  I can't believe how many different kinds of mango chutney there are (most were the same brand, just different types).  I went with the major grey style (brand was Jaipur) when I noticed cloves floating in it.  Good choice.  No need to pay for a Honeybaked Ham again.  I did leave out the zest.  I used a smaller ham, but it was spiral cut on the bone even though there are only 2 of us because I think the bone adds flavor and ham freezes fine.  I am guessing highcotton used a different chutney because neither garlic nor orange overwhelmed.  I was concerned because the predominant smell while the ham cooked was mustard, but it was not an overpowering flavor at all.  I would use this glaze again.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.

This was heaven on a plate!  If you are looking for a slightly different, but richly flavored way to serve your ham, search no further.  I reluctantly spooned out the last of the home made chutney to make this, but it was well worth the sacrifice!
Excellent glaze, turned out great.  Will use again.  I might reduce the amount of mustard next time to 1/4 cup however.  The mango chutney was fantastic in this.

WAY too many mango chutney choices.  I had no idea.  I tried a mango ginger chutney but won't use it again; the ginger was too dominant. Even so, this was just delicious and I'm looking forward to exploring the world of chutney.
This was wonderful, Mean.  I  loved the fruty chutney mustard flavor on the ham.  Was a 5 star Yum!
This was a great glaze for ham; I did follow a few of the other posters advice and cut back the mustard to 1/4 cup and was very happy with the yummy results!

Am SURE you will agree, TRUE!
This recipe was GREAT on ham too!
Something different, something UNIQUE,
Hope your curiosity this recipe does peak!!!

I think this is a great recipe, but I also think the original author, Ina Garten, should be credited. The recipe was published in her book, "Barefoot Contessa Parties", copyrighted in 2002, and is shown often on the Food Network. Thanks for sharing the recipe, but let's do give credit for copyrighted recipes!

I chose this recipe because you can't go wrong with one of Ina's recipes. I usually just use the packet from Costco's spiral hams but this time I used a different brand of ham and was suspicious of the packet. I left out the orange peel (because my kids don't favor the flavor). I usually don't care that much about ham but tonight this ham was my favorite part of Easter dinner! It really has a delectable flavor (very classic and not just "preserves" tasting). The Dijon really balances the flavor and keeps it from being too sweet. I am going to be making this next week for my aunt (who does not favor sweet glazes for ham) and I bet she will really love it. Thanks Jeff, for posting my favorite ham glaze (won't go back to the packet). 

Roxygirl

The ham is still cooking, but the glaze is amazing!  I did a taste test, and could eat it right out of the blender, it was so tasty.

I substituted apple juice for oj (dietary sensitivities) and used Silver Palate Mango Chutney. I can wait for my family to try this ham!

Thanks for posting.
Was PERFECT for our Easter dinner. Can't WAIT for the leftovers tonight! Thanks, Jeff!
Wild rice cooks more slowly than regular rice. Thus, the regular rice was soggy.  I would like to try the recipe again, but next time I will add the regular rice after 20 minutes.
Found  this quite  good and very  filling.

I can't believe no one has rated this yet. Loved them. I adjusted the seasonings to suit our family's tastes and they turned out wonderfully. Thanks for sharing with the rest of us. Prepared some immediately; froze the rest & made it later.  Thank you.

Yay! Just like the 'sausage rolls' I used to get from bakeries back in my native Australia. I didn't need the egg to bind the mixture, it was just the right consistency. I made them into 6' long rolls, served with some ketchup and enjoyed every crumb. Cheers!

Very tasty indeed - The kids really enjoyed these.  Fortunately I had doubled the recipe...  Also added a couple of tablespoons of tomato paste along with the ketchup.  They've already been requested again!  Thanks for this recipe.
Party sausage rolls - yum

I omitted both eggs due to allergies. Meat never really sticks to the dough maybe due to this omission. The taste was ok, nothing special. They do freeze well, but the pork makes a bit too greasy. Won't be making these again, sorry.

Great tasting fruit salad! Loved the combo of PB & pineapple! Definitely a winner, at least for us! Another time, especially when I'm able to get a 'just right' fresh pineapple, I'd like to try that in place of the canned! Thanks for sharing the recipe! [Tagged & made in Please Review My Recipe]

This was surprisingly good for a recipe that you'd find just on the back of box.  I really like the peanut butter-pineapple juice dressing.  It tastes like a traditional Thai peanut sauce, but is far easier to make.  I served the salad with Thai fish cakes- the dishes paired perfectly. [Made & Reviewed for PRMR]
This was a yummy soup! I put the ingred. into my crockpot and cooked it that way, then froze in individual cups.  Now I have "fresh" soup whenever I want. Great recipe Pam!

A nice, basic recipe for pea soup, to which you could add just about anything. A little bacon takes my fancy! However, I did have a few "glitches" I had to sort out with the recipe. It needed 3 to 4 htimes as much water or otherwise the soup would have burned and it also took nearer 4 hours for the peas to cook. Maybe this is down to the type of split pea? Mine weren't old because I'd only bought them a couple weeks earlier. I also added a little bit of stock powder to the soup about halfway through cooking as I felt it was just a touch bland.
This is lovely.  I use green split peas and the colour is much nicer.  Also fresh onion, celery.

These were very juicy and flavorful burgers.  I sometimes find ground turkey to be very dry and lacking, but that can't be said for this recipe.  I did use ground turkey breast which made very sticky raw burgers, but they firmed up well in the frying pan.  My personal tastes felt that 1 cup of chopped peppers was a little much, but my pepper loving hubby really liked the flavor they added.  I served these on whole wheat buns with romaine lettuce, a slice of tomato and the tomatillo/avocado salsa.  It was a good balance of flavors and a recipe worth trying again.
Holy Huge Burgers.... These burgers are very very tasty and juicy and the best part is - there's no fat.... these are Good AND good for you... I highly recommend everyone give them a try.... YUMM
I would totally marry sweet tea. Actually I married a Louisianian~that might be close enough!  Made for My 3 Chefs.

Made for Zaar Cookbooks Tag.  These are excellent turkey burgers.  Very easy, low in fat and very tasty.  Because of a food allergy, I used 1/2 cup of oatmeal in place of the bread and they worked just fine. Have never sauteed veggies for a burger before ~ it really brings out their flavors.  Will be making these again.  Thanks for posting this SkinnieMinnie!

These are terrific! Sometimes turkey burgers are dry and lacking in flavor. This recipe provides the exact opposite. I really loved the flavor from the faijita seasoning and cooked veggies. Perfect! I couldn't find tomatilla salsa so I combined avocado, cilantro and chopped tomatoes instead.  Made for Healthy Choices tag game.
Delicious! I even skipped the tomato paste as I didn't have any on hand. Didn't add any salt either. I did melt white cheddar cheese on top at the end of cooking...very good!
Best burger ever. So tasty. They whole family loved it.

These calzones were absolutely delicious !! Made for a great lunch with just some Wickles Pickles and home made beets. This was such a fast lunch to put together. I had prepared everything in the morning and just popped it in the oven when I got to work. The only thing I changed was I used red peppers (just a taste preference) and I cut the recipe in half. We both loved them. The sauce was really good for these, I was surprised, I normally just go with a sweeter pizza dipping kind of sauce but the A1 really added a nice piquant taste.  Thanks for sharing your recipe Sweet Diva...will be making these again.

I marinated for 2 hours.  I think that may have been too long.  My steak came out tasting slightly like sausage.  The dipping sauce is good though...really enjoyed that.  I'd like to give it 3 1/2 stars because of the dipping sauce, but all diners voted either a 2 or 3 on the steak and majority ruled in this case.  Sorry.  Made for Newest Zaar Tag.

These lettuce wraps were great!  I marinated about 45 minutes and the meat was very flavorful and great with the dipping sauce.  I left out the onion and cilantro (personal pref) and we really enjoyed these wraps - thanks for sharing the recipe!

We love lettuce wraps and this was a really nice treat!  I only marinated the beef for 30 minutes and I did make some changes such as lowering the amount of soy sauce, vinegar and ginger.  We really enjoyed the sauce as well.  Thanks for the post!  Made for 1-2-3 Tag, February, 2012.
This is simple, quick, and delicious.  The shallot adds just the right amount of onion flavor, and the capers give it a satisfying saltiness. Thanks for posting; I really enjoyed this side dish.

This is a definate like.  I steamed the cauliflower in a steamer basket and followed the recipe as written.  My head of cauliflower may have been a little on the small side as I seemed to have quite a bit of vinaigrette left.  Made for ZWTIII.  Thanks Sharon!  See you soon.
This turns the normal boring cauli into a wonderful tasty dish. The capers really make this recipe. Easy to prepare and quick to make. Thank you Sharon :)

I made this for *Zaar World Tour III* yummy and healthy Cauliflower recipe and was easy to make.  Kept the recipe even added the cayenne peppers, Little Miss (DD) didn't eat this as likes her cauliflower dish plain but we enjoyed the jazzed up Cauliflower.  Thank you Sharon123

Wonderful!!  This had a marvelous flavor - and I found that the vinaigrette was not quite enough for one whole head of cauliflower so would double it in the future. (You have great recipes Sharon123)!

Made exactly as written, and I wouldn't change a thing!  Quick and easy to make, and for such strong individual ingredients, the final product had a really soft but distinctive flavour.  Yummy.  Thanks Sharon!
I made it for a Cousins Tapas Party and it was made exactly as written.  I'm so sad. There were no leftovers.  I can't wait to make another batch.  Thank you for a "great" recipe
The bomb!!!   So delicious!!!!!!!!!!
My 13 year old daughter made these and got rave reviews. She is adding it to her recipe collection!

This makes a yummy chicken salad! I used store bought prepared chicken and chopped it up. The only change I made was to add avocado in place of the mayo on the bread and added alfalfa sprouts for the crunch. Just lovely! Made for Football Pool 2013.

Easy to make roast lamb. The smell was divine when the clove and honey mixture was added. I felt like the flavours didnt permeate the meat very well, so will pour it over earlier next time I may it, thanks for posting.

Well everyone ate what was on their plate. This was totally different with the honey and cloves. On the cooking time I had a leg of lamb that was just over 1.8K and according o the thermoter it was well done in 1 hour 45 minut4es. I poured the the lemon juice mix and popped back in the oven for a further 20 minutes, even though the thermometer was reading well done 20 minutes and then transferred the cooked lamb to a plate and let rest. When carved it was not as welldone as expected which I really enjoyed (the the DH disagreed - this is a no baa man/guy). With the remaining pan juices (after draining fat) I made a gravy (fried of some flour and added som water to thicken - helped to take up the juices, at this point tasted so sweet and the DH suggested some rosemary sprigs (we have heaps growing in the garden) and simmered in the gravy worked a treat (for about 10 minutes) and then strained the lot (initiallly I had removed the cloves but would leave and then strain) and just strain and you have a sweet but very tasty gravy. Thank you Charlootte J, made for ZAAR Cokbook Tag.

I loved this recipe. I didn't use all of the salt or pepper in the recipe, it would be way too much, but I never use the amount of salt or pepper that a recipe calls for. Salt or pepper should be to your own taste.

My family loved it!! I doubled the recipe, and used evaporated milk and whole milk to replace the half-and-half I forgot to buy. :-) I kinda forgot the mushrooms also, but my kids don't like them anyway. :-) I used some uncooked chicken breasts I had, chopped them into small pieces and then sauteed them with seasoning and fresh garlic. Oh, and I added extra cheese!! Mmmm!
This would also be good with a bread crumb topping, but I just sprinkled the top with paprika for color this time.
This was very easy, tasty and versatile! I will definitely make this again and try it out with different meats, vegetables and cheeses. A keeper for sure!

Absoutely divine! We LOVED this, it made a wonderful Sunday Lunch for today! I followed this to the letter and was rewarded with moist and crispy chicken with a wonderful wine and lemon sauce. I cooked this in my woodburning stove for 2 hours, it was perfect. We ate this with steamed broccoli, carrots, garden peas, new potatoes and home-made stuffing. Made for Special Meals in the Photo's Forum and VERY much enjoyed thanks! A keeper for me! FT:-)

Well this wasn't an engagement roast chicken, but DH might have wanted to propose all over again, lol!!!  My chicken was almost 6 lbs so I cooked it a bit longer, but it was so flavorful and juicy, the whole family loved it.  I served it with mashed potatoes, gravy made from the drippings and corn.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!!  Made for 123 Tag Game.

Very different and good steak. I had the most fun smashing all the beans and peppercorns! I used a couple of strip steaks instead of the sirloin. I served this with some brown rice and a simple romaine salad. I am glad that I tried something new. It was a great special dinner for DH and myself. Made and Reviewed for Comfort Cafe - Java Jolt - Thanks! :)

As did the previous reviewer I used a New York Strip steak. There is lots of flavor here and if your a coffee fan you owe it to yourself to try this. I added a bit more salt after cooking and tasting. I must advise that if anyone who will be eating this has dentures or dental problems that you pound the coffee and pepper as fine as possible. My DH had a bad time with the small chunks getting under his upper plate and causing discomfort. I was thinking about the nice pepper pop from biting the broken corns and not poor DH and his teeth. OR, if you have folks with dental considerations make the steaks up to the point of adding the coffee beans and peppercorns and just leave them off. I was planning to grill outdoors but my great summer day turned into rain and I used the broiler giving it 2 mins on each side. Made for Photo Tag.
Lovely steak. I used strip steak for this recipe. Will make again.Made for 123 Hits.

Okay, I was about to post these as one of my recipes (got from Quick Cooking magazine) but decided to do a quick search to see if they were already listed and HERE THEY ARE!!!  These are soooooooooo good, you should be making these right now.  I brought these to the law firm where I work and one of the attorneys actually told me, absolute deadpan -- "This is the best thing I've ever eaten in my entire life" -- for real!  Yummy Yummy Yummy!  Try these!
These are great!  My kids (and my husband and I) really enjoyed them.  They would also be a good treat for a bake sale.
This dish was AWESOME. I didn't have lemons and substituted Green Peppers. It was so tasty. I followed the recipe exactly (other than the substitution).
Yum says it all..........wonderful flavor and the lemon shines thru beautifully.   Sometimes roast chicken can have an oily taste but ths is sharp and clear.   Thanks.......

Can I marry you, Scoutie?  Because this is some outstanding chicken - moist and bursting with flavor.  I added potatoes, as suggested, which were also very tasty.  And the gravy is divine!  I will never make a roast chicken any other way!

Delicious!  Cooked perfectly, moist and flavorful.  The sauce is very rich.  Looking forward to making soup tomorrow from the leftovers and adding the rest of the rich sauce to the stock.  Made for Best of 2012 game.

Excellent roast chicken! This was a wonderful cooking method and the results were perfect. I really loved the sweet onions surrounding the chicken. The gravy was great, too. I would only make one teeny change next time - I would omit the wine and instead double the chicken broth. I didn't care for the wine flavor in the gravy. That is definitely a personal preference though - not a reflection on the recipe. Roasting potatoes on a separate baking sheet is something else I will add in next time. Thank you for posting. I love Ina's recipes and this one was excellent. I'll be moving this recipe over to my best of the best file. Thanks!

simply amazing....I cooked two 5lb. birds at once and I'm glad I did! Th e chicken was roasted to perfection and the sauce just makes it out-of-this world. You can taste the wine, lemon, onion and garlic yet nothing over powers anything else. Delish, I can see how this could "seal the deal"!    *side note, I accidentally only bought 2 lemons even though I was doubling the recipe but this turned out just fine, as I think it would be too lemony for me- if I had had two lemons per bird as a opposed to two for each.

Was super excited to make this roast chicken. Chicken was amazing, nothing new, simple roast chicken.  However, the gravy was awful.  The bitterness of the lemon absolutely ruins this dish.  I Made it for my boyfriend and we both agreed the bitterness of the gravy was awful.

I am so happy I tried this recipe! It is a great staring point for someone who isn't too experienced with roasting chicken in the oven (I do most of my cooking on the grill or in a skillet). I didn't have a whole chicken so I did two large bone-in breasts (with skin) and 4 drumsticks. I definitely liked using the pieces (vs. a whole chicken) because they cooked quicker and you don't have to carve them prior to serving. I added large carrot chunks to the onion/lemon medley and they were awesome (they took on the flavor of the chicken wonderfully)!! The lemon flavor was too strong/bitter for me; I will either reduce it or omit it for next time. I will use the same amount of onions for roasting but probably wont serve as much with the stock/wine sauce; I think adding artichoke hearts with about 1/2 of the required amount of onion (plus a few tabs of butter) will make the sauce killer! I cant wait to try making "engagement chicken" again!
Your recipe are easy ... I enjoy cooking your recipe for guest Do u ever cook low sodium recipe
Made this exactly as written. Came out wonderfully. Loved the sauce.

Super easy super fast and great with veggies or potato chips. Kids thought I bought the dip premade.

This was a nice new way to eat broccoli.  I enjoyed the egg and corn in this salad. I think when I made it again, I'll add some sunflower seeds for some crunch, but I will be making it again!  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.
Difficult to put away, sorry to see them finished.

I would love to give these pecans a 5* but don't feel I can for the contest.  We didn't care for the flavor of the combination of spices. And there was barely enough seasoning mix to boil together without burning, making it difficult to coat the nuts thoroughly.  Sorry, I was disappointed in this recipe and hate to give it such a mediocre rating.

I bow before you my Chef's hat for this beautiful CAP recipe - CAP as in "Crunchy and Addictive Pecans!" That is what these nuts are all about - I bet nobody could eat just ONE! I made this on the 2nd of July for a small celebration at home and my friends' had a great time enjoying these nuts. Some of them even took the liberty of marching into my kitchen and making more! The little that remained was packed into boxes and they took it home for their family members. LOL. I guess they really went nuts over your nuts!Please note that I did omit the garlic powder as I didn't have that on hand because we never use powdered garlic; we always use fresh. So, I had to leave that out. Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly. Thank you, these nuts are indeed very nice. All the best for the contest! I wish you luck!!
Very easy recipe!  I used bulk pork sausage and it worked very well.  Would make this again for company since it makes a lot and tastes great!

Yum! I scaled this down to a half a cup yield and it scaled beautifully. My toddler is equally keen on them and I'll be lucky if these last 10 minutes.
I used real raw sugar rather than Splenda. Dead easy and delightful.
Good idea and I have certainly enjoyed it!

MMM MMM MMM!!! These are really good!! I used 1 cup roasted, salted peanuts instead of pecans and I omitted the cayenne pepper. I will definitely be making these again! Thanks for the recipe. It's a keeper!
Awesome! I try to keep my eyes open for low carb recipies and this is definitely a keeper. I didn't have any Splenda so I substituted Sugarlike, which is similar to Splenda but Maltitol based

I use Lorac's system, and only give 5 stars for recipes that blow my socks off and I never would have thought of in a million years!  This is one of them! Very Very good.  I added extra Cayenne to the dry coating mix  used to coat the nuts at the end (Yes, we like 'em hot).  I also used 1/2 pecans and 1/2 almonds, both are yummy.
